Now on the topic of audio, if you aren't using wireless Bluetooth headphones, there is still going to be a standard 3.5 mm headphone jack on the bottom as well. So yes, you are able to still plug in wired headphones or headsets. And similarly, aside from the two type-C ports, you will find access to some of the controls which are back lit. There is no more remote that's built into the armrest of the seats. So, everything is now controlled via this large touchscreen display, which works well enough for the most part. You can still see them in the dark. You can change the volume using these tactile buttons, as well as turn the entire screen on and off by pressing that key. And since again, it is an OLED display, everything goes completely dark when you turn it off and then on again if you want to use it, if you're trying to sleep, for example. And then similarly, you can actually access a button for turning on the light on top of the seat as well as calling the flight attendant. So all of those controls are now built into the in-flight entertainment uh buttons on the side here. Now in terms of the overall menu system, one of the other aspects that is going to be new and perhaps original to Panasonic solution is they have a flight tracker as a map that you can visualize when you are flying over different territories. And specifically, the mapping software here is called the Arc Moving Map. So, I do really like this new system. It felt very fancy, almost like a scene from Minority Report or maybe even The Matrix, uh, just because it's able to transition very smoothly between different views, including virtual perspectives as if you were looking directly in front of the plane, from the left to the right of the plane, underneath the plane. Now, all of the graphics here though are simulated over a kind of mapping software similar to maybe Google Maps, but it's not exactly onetoone real live feed coming from an actual camera, at least in the economy cabin experience. Uh, but still, it was interesting to have kind of a virtual map being displayed. Felt realistic enough to see if you were flying underneath a certain mountain range. And similar to Google Earth, you're able to interact with the screen using your fingers. It's a multi-touch enabled touchcreen. So, you can actually pinch in and pinch out to make the map larger and smaller. It felt pretty smooth and responsive during operation. Even though the specific frame rate or the refresh rate of the screen isn't necessarily stated by Panasonic, but yes, it is kind of fun to be able to freely move it around. It felt much more responsive versus the resistive plastic screens which have a lot of glare and they have to really force you to get in there with your fingers that we had on older inflight entertainment systems. Uh this is now finally a capacitive screen. Kind of feels like you're using a giant modern iPad flowing a lot more seamlessly. And if you are zoomed all the way out, it kind of reminds me of a scene from sci-fi films or threebody problem. And you can even see your position on Earth as it is reflected in the entire galaxy like a planetary simulation model which was neat to see. So plenty of perspectives. You can also leave it into an auto mode in which it will transition between the different perspectives of looking in front underneath the plane to the left or the right of plane. Uh even having some virtual windows that you can simulate on the display. And since it is large enough with a true OLED nature, when it is displaying blacks, everything is just completely dark. So it has a pretty convincing effect of kind of looking out into these different perspectives just from this monitor of what you are seeing as it's flying over space. So that view I do think is done relatively well by Panasonic and their software team. And you're able to see your position, how much duration is left until you arrive at your destination, the current speed that you're going, some of the basic stats like that. This is the software part that I think is perhaps the most interesting out of their solution compared to everything else still being relatively similar to other inflight entertainment systems that I've seen uh in the past, which is to say definitely not bad when it comes to watching movies, TV shows. Again, the smaller bezels as well as the OLED screen brightness, everything has been pretty satisfactory for just getting you a little bit more immersed in the entertainment that you are consuming. However, when it comes to the UI of navigating around the system, the carousel, all of that feels relatively familiar compared to other entertainment system screens that I've seen uh in the past. Hasn't really changed dramatically. You can swipe up and down through the carousel to go through other TV shows to sort by genres. Also listen to different music and albums that they have shared on there as well. And some tapandgo style, very basic, casual style puzzle games, more or less. There's nothing super crazy on here, but yeah, it's basically a grid system. Almost reminds me of something like a PlayStation interface or maybe a Windows Metro screen from back in the day, Windows phone of just swiping up and down to get through the different options on the touch screen. So, the flight map software, I think, is by comparison the more new aspect software-wise that I was surprised by. Now, it is worth noting though that not all of Iceland Air's planes have been retrofitted with this new Panasonic uh in-flight entertainment system. It just receives it on their A321 Neo designed for their longer hall flight. Now, if you have a shorter hop between Europe connecting through Iceland and then getting to somewhere else like the UK or getting to Sweden, maybe taking just uh around 2 hours or 3 hours, then those smaller planes have not yet been updated with their newer systems. they're still using the older maybe resistive touchscreen or maybe a smaller LCD screen. Typically, we see around 7 in to 8 in being the norm on economy class uh for most of those older planes versus again this being dramatically larger at 13 in with tiny bezels. It's definitely one of the first things you'll notice once you get on board. So, it was definitely interesting to check out and kind of got me curious to see what other airlines have started to update using a similar 4K system even on economy class. And it looks like there's a couple actually. United Airlines surprisingly here in the US is also updating to their 4K OLED screens also 13 in. the same product essentially also an economy cabin going forwards uh with the Boeing 787 Dreamliners receiving that updated interior and other carriers to follow suit include Air Canada Raida Air from the Middle East I believe as well as Iceland Air are the three other ones receiving it. Although as we saw from that press release, it looks like Iceland Air was the first to officially partner and roll it out from Panasonic. And this also comes off the tale of similarly last year we saw Hawaiian airlines renovate their in-flight systems by offering Starlink access to satellite Wi-Fi for free for flights that are going from the US over to Hawaii. So you can access internet even as you're flying without having to pay anything extra and having more reliable and pretty fast Wi-Fi connectivity as well. So, it's nice to see these subtle improvements start to roll out across even economy products as technology evolves and the cost becomes more accessible. We start to see more of these renovations going on. Now, honestly, I'm kind of surprised though to see United Airlines, Air Canada, and to some extent Iceland Air as well. The fact that these are some of the first to support it again is somewhat surprising in my opinion because Iceland Air for example is known to be slightly more cost effective versus many of the other carriers and then similarly Air Canada as well as United Airlines are definitely fullervice airlines but they're also pretty competitive on price usually. So I didn't really expect for these particular brands to be some of the first to update. I kind of expected them in fact to be maybe later down or last in line just because they tend to be more sensitive to pricing. But maybe they're trying to pull in new customers by improving their product and experience and so they're choosing to go with this versus some of the more premium names and brands like Delta. Not to mention other flag carriers, whether that's Emirates as well as Singapore Airlines is another kind of five-star airline. surprisingly aren't other examples I've made the list, but rather it's United Air Canada and Iceland Air which have more of this kind of stoic traditional image, at least in my opinion. And if you're into traveling and more of an age geek, you may know that another carrier that has been kind of a newcomer in the aviation space has been Starlux Airlines. But they've been making some splash on social media over the past uh 2 years or so after recently launching their flights from the US over to Asia as another competing option to other legacy carriers. And because they are a new airline, their planes are new as well. And they previously had some of the better performing hard products in economy, including 13in 4K screens. But what's interesting here is Starlux Airlines have chosen to go with IPS LCD screens instead of OLED screens, the newer type that's built by Panasonic that's starting to roll out now, maybe a year or so later after Starlux first started to pop up on the scene. And of course, it's unlikely that Starlux will be updating their fleet after just purchasing their planes not so long ago. But at the same time, LCD may be having a slightly longer shelf life or usage lifespan. If they are always displaying certain images on it, that might actually have it age better, ironically enough, compared to the more expensive and newer OLED panels that these other airlines have opted for instead. So maybe it's a blessing in disguise, but they are matching them when it comes to these older screens also being 13 in, also being 4K on the Starlux Fleet. And ultimately, it's kind of ridiculous to call them old since they're still pretty new in production for just around 2 years or so. But just a slight difference there when it comes to the screen technology type. So, there we have it. Kind of an unusual video in many ways. Again, it isn't like a typical consumer product review that you can purchase off the shelf, but more of an observation kind of sharing some of my experiences when it comes to that updated tech powered by Panasonic in the inflight entertainment systems that I was able to experience. Just wanted to kind of document and share some of my thoughts. But let me know, have you guys also experienced some of these recently renovated interiors, the inflight entertainment systems? Also, if you are interested in aviation related tech, feel free to share your thoughts. But for now, that's been our video. Thanks for watching here at OS Reviews.

And I won't be holding my breath that this measure will result in cheaper airfare. And I've tried those device holders, they are awful they dont hold tablets and they snap down so hard it can hurt you. Ideally I'd still like some form of setback infotainment. Maybe a hybrid approach with a smaller screen to view your flight info, maybe food and snack options, and airport info while still emphasizing customers stream their own entertainment. But I can't remember the last time airlines have done anything for the good of the customer.

yt_comments.author: @christopherzy
yt_comments.text: Taking the American A319 soon here and yeah don’t care for IFE on it what so ever, but this definitely won’t bring airfare down one bit.

yt_comments.author: @CM73878
yt_comments.text: United is changing course. Since 2019, under CEO Scott Kirby, the airline announced its “United Next” program: all new narrowbody aircraft (like the 737 MAX and Airbus A321neo) will come with seat-back screens. • The reasoning: • Competing with Delta and JetBlue, which advertise seat-back screens as a premium experience.

yt_comments.author: @VinniChannel
yt_comments.text: US Airways management had some influence on this decision. The old AA plans were to have IFE on smaller aircraft like 737/A320 family. They have even received some aircraft on this configuration.

yt_comments.author: @bennyattar8862
yt_comments.text: When I was a helluva lot younger I flew on routes operated by 747-200s. In those days and planes, IFE was a book. I still carry a book on every flight. I've been on 4 or 5 long haul flights where the IFE just wasn't working.

yt_comments.author: @skylineXpert
yt_comments.text: If people already use their phone for this then the IFE is ancient when you only need a stable wifi connection...

reviews.transcript_full:
While other US legacy carriers have sought 
to ensure inflight entertainment is present   on ALL their mainline aircraft, American 
Airlines has moved forward with more of an   austerity approach. Indeed, we’ve seen 
a reduction of seatback entertainment   across much of the fleet operating 
domestic services. Most recently,   the carrier opted to remove seatback screens from 
its A319s in its latest retrofit program. These   jets were the carrier's final short-to-medium 
haul aircraft equipped with the systems. It should go without saying that this 
move has been implemented to save costs. As you can guess, when compared to NO 
screens at all, inflight entertainment   systems cost money to install and upkeep, and 
licensing for the films and TV is not free. Furthermore, screens add additional weight,   thus contributing to greater fuel 
burn. From an operational perspective,   there’s a lot to lose by having the systems, 
and a lot to gain from removing them. American has begun retrofitting the 
cabins of over 30 legacy Airbus A319s.   This move is important because the 
legacy A319s were the last of the   carrier's short-to-medium-haul aircraft that 
were fitted with seatback entertainment. Thus, it won’t be long before American Airlines 
short and medium-haul passengers will lose all   hope of seatback entertainment. Of course, 
a notable exception occurs when widebody,   intercontinental jets are deployed domestically as 
a way to reposition for another long haul flight. There were 32 A319s received from 
2013 to 2015, with the airline's   other A319s having been inherited from 
US Airways and America West Airlines. The group of 32 are noteworthy as 
the only Sharklet-equipped A319s   that operate in the US. These will 
be American Airlines' first batch   of aircraft to be overhauled as part 
of its fleet retrofitting efforts. When it comes to the passenger experience, it will 
set American Airlines back from the competition,   as it will become the only US legacy carrier that   has no seatback entertainment on its 
short-to-medium-haul mainline aircraft.   Carriers like Delta and United have opted to 
continue seatback entertainment. These carrier   retrofits have focused on improving 
and installing seatback screens. It won't be a case of bringing a 
book or getting bored, however. As is a trend with some airlines, 
seatback entertainment will be   replaced by seatback device holders and 
passengers are able to stream content. This is available on smartphones,   tablets and laptops, although it may not 
work until the aircraft reaches 10,000 ft. There is also free Wi-Fi for T-Mobile customers   on certain plans, while connectivity 
can be accessed by others for a fee. To bring things full circle, American has 
taken a bet that customers won’t mind the   lack of seatback entertainment because they’ll 
choose the airline for other reasons - such as   connectivity to certain airports, or comfortable 
flight scheduling. IF this bet pays off,   then American will save money on acquiring, 
installing, and maintaining those screens.   And again, as mentioned, it will 
save on fuel with lighter aircraft. But what do YOU think of this 
decision by American? Is it a   move that will pay off? Or backfire? 
Let us know by leaving a comment.

It is currently 7:00 a.m. I am at the Sydney 
International Airport. Today I'm going to be   flying Asiana Airlines on a 10-hour flight 
in Economy from Sydney to Inchan Airport. You   might have heard of Asiana Airlines before. It 
is one of the two main Korean airlines. However,   did you know that they're going to be merging 
with Korean Air on the 17th of December, 2026,   which makes today's video interesting, if not 
slightly poignant, as this will be one of the   last times I will ever fly Asiana Airlines. 
Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.   Bye-bye. Once one of Korea's most recognizable 
airlines, it is now living on borrowed time. So   before the brand disappears, I wanted to find out 
is Asiana still worth flying? And so apart from a   little nostalgia trip today, I'm also going 
to be reviewing my entire flight experience   from check-in to the cabin to the service 
and the food. It's the current Q situation,   which is impressive given that we're about 4 and 
1/2 hours away from departure time. So, luckily,   I checked in online beforehand, which meant that I 
got to go on this much shorter, non-existent queue   instead of the normal queue, which meant that the 
check-in was a real breeze, and I was within the   waiting area for boarding within 20 minutes.

a check-in machine. I'm at the gate now to board,   and it looks like it's going to be a full 
flight today. So, while we're waiting to board,   here's a bit more info on this Korean Air and 
Asiana Airlines merger because I was just as   shocked as you when I found out this happened as 
Asiana has reportedly been financially struggling   for years. However, as the move combines 
Korea's two biggest international airlines,   regulators were worried about reduced competition 
and hence increased pricing, which is why it took   around 4 years for the final approvals to happen. 
The final approvals took place in December 2024.   However, Asiana has been allowed to continue 
operating independently during a transition   period from then right up to December 2026 where 
the full integration is expected to take place. Today I'm flying Asiana Airlines on their Boeing 
777-200, one of the older widebody aircrafts in   Asiana's longhaul fleet. Here we are in the 
economy cabin and it's a 3x3x3 configuration   and I have to say it definitely still felt 
like Asiana as I stepped on board from the   warm greeting of the crew and the branding of 
the aircraft. But now I'm going to be honest,   Boeing 777-200 is not the newest aircraft in the 
sky. So the cabin itself, while still superbly   clean, is looking a little bit old, but I mean 
I don't know if Asiana really has any incentive   to upgrade anything during this transition 
period. That being said, the cabin itself   felt reasonably spacious. Leg room was pretty

really does go to showcase how Asiana Airlines   pays attention to the little details. The airline 
also comes with an online entertainment system   that was packed with a decent movie selection. 
There's also a foldout tray table for the meals, a   seatback pocket with all the usual safety card and 
airline literature. But perhaps more importantly,   there's also charging ports and powerpoint for 
you to either recharge your phone or to be able   to charge your laptop during your flight. All in 
all, all the main things that you would expect and   care about in a longhaul economy flight were 
there. After being warmly welcome on board,   the captain came on with his usual welcome 
announcement and off we went. And once we   reached cruising altitude, it was now time for the 
food, which I have to say has always been one of   my highlights when it comes to Asiana Airlines, 
because let me tell you, the Korean food on board   is actually pretty darn amazing. And in fact, is 
one of the key reasons why I've always preferred   to fly Asiana Airlines over Korean Air. For this 
flight, I went with a Bibbop, which comes as a set   that looks a little bit like this. And if you're 
not sure how to put it all together, not to worry.   It comes with a cute little instruction card. 
I won't walk you through this step by step of   course, but I will say that this unsurprisingly 
was really delicious. A fact that by the way   remained consistent on the way back with their sam 
aka Korean beef bogi and rice wrapped in a leaf.   All this cuteness put aside, one of the things 
that I'm going to miss about Asiana Airlines the   most is how they proudly highlight Korean food. 
I remember having their food way back when I   flew them for the first time and found it to be 
a great pre-introduction to Korean food and has   been a big reason as to why I am now obsessed with 
not just Korean food but with everything related   to Korean culture. And as it was a 10-hour flight, 
we were also served a second meal, which for the   flight from Sydney to Inchon was a spicy fish with 
vegetables and rice. It was equally as delicious. I want to start this next part by saying that 
everybody's going to have different things that   are important to them on a flight. And yes, 
Korean Air is probably going to have newer   aircrafts and equally as good customer service, 
but I am personally going to miss the food on   Asiana Airlines. And that is why to me Asiana 
will always trump Korean Air. I also did a bit   of research before my flight and Asiana pricing 
for direct flights is still very competitive. And   so whether you're looking to fly Asiana for the 
last time for nostalgia sake or this video has   made you curious to try them out before they go 
away for good, it is definitely worth it. But if   you're an Asiana fan like me or a frequent flyer, 
you're probably curious what exactly is going to   change. What do we know so far? I also did a 
bit of research after I got back and here are   some confirmed changes that you can expect after 
December 2026. One is that the Asiana Airlines   brand will completely disappear and be integrated 
under the Korean Air brand. The Asiana frequent   fly program is also under the Star Alliance, but 
that will no longer be so after December 2026,   switching its alliance membership to Sky Team 
as part of the merger. That is to say that the   Asiana Club program will also completely switch 
over to the Korean Air Sky Pass program. If you   are a frequent flyer and have miles under the 
Asiana Club, they will be recognized for up   to 10 years post December 2026 and can still be 
used right up to their expiry date. You can also,   by the way, choose to convert your Asiana Club 
miles into the Korean Air Sky Pass miles at any   point during this 10-year period, but you will not 
have a choice to only convert part of them. You   will have to convert all of it if you choose to 
do so. Regardless of whichever option you choose,   you will not be able to earn any Asiana club miles 
post December 2026. you'll obviously be earning   Korean Air Sky Pass miles instead. Further, if 
you're an elite member in one of the tiers in   the Asiana club, you'll be transitioned over to 
an equivalent in the Korean Air Sky Pass. Any   Star Alliance or what tickets booked will need 
to be completed by the day of the merger date,   regardless of when the ticket was purchased. 
Routes that you might be familiar with may also   disappear under this merger to obviously avoid 
duplicate and overlapping schedules between the   two airlines. And last, but certainly not least, 
if you do also fly with the budget arm of Asiana   Airlines, aka Air Busan and Air Soul, those will 
be integrated under Korean Air's budget arm,   aka Janet. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank

is still going to be around. But I do hope that   you find value in today's video and if you have,

With the salmon glistening and the chocolates glistening, Alaska Airlines is serving its inaugural flight today and I just happened to upgrade myself. Our flight today is AS1503, a completely full flight operated on registration N538AS, a 14-year-old Boeing 737-800 taking us further than any commercial flight out of Boise has before. And to celebrate, our aircraft features the Star Wars livery and more importantly, the latest in what Alaska Airlines has to offer in their hard product. While still a kind gesture, not the most riveting way to welcome a new route. Still better than Avelo and Spirit and Sun Country though. I ended up choosing the roast beef and rice with leafy greens and red peppers. The dish also came with a side of cold sliced veggies and hummus, as well as a tasty chocolate cake. actually better than their old 2-2-2?  Everyone always wants a modern all aisle access 
flatbed, for the record, myself included. But,   this was the first time that I’ve ever sat 
in those traditional lie flat seats followed   by a tight squeeze of a staggered seat just 2 
hours later and well, I have opinions to share.  By the way, the price that I paid for this and 
every flight I take is always in the description.  Let me welcome any of you who may be new to the 
channel, my name is Kevin. I’m here to give you   a self-funded and honest look at some of the 
best- and some of the not so best- airlines and   hotels in the world, which I’ve been bringing 
to you full time for the past four years.   Check out my hundreds of videos, scan 
the QR code or click the link in the   description to learn more about how I do 
things. Let’s get into the trip report.  I just arrived here in Santiago from Sao Paulo 
and when I say “just” I mean seconds ago and now   I need to high tail it through what honestly felt 
like a never ending maze from the new additions   here at Santiago’s international airport. 
Editions that Google Earth hasn’t even added yet.  I was meant to have around a 2 hour layover. 
Short, but relaxed and was really looking   forward to visiting the LATAM lounge since I 
love their lounge in Sao Paulo and this one   is meant to be even better. But, the winds 
over the Andes today were extreme and so   we had to take a very out of the way route to 
get here, adding an hour to that first flight   and meaning that I needed to walk directly to 
my next gate after passing through security.  As I arrived they were already pre-boarding 
so I was glad I decided to come straight here.  Tonight we’d be hitching a ride on a 7 
year old 787-9 of which Latam group has   27 of with 19 more on the way- along with 
10 787-8s. This flight was originally sold   showing the older configuration 2-2-2 
seating as you saw in my last video,   but around a week prior to the flight, the 
seating was updated to the newer layout.  I should mention though, while today’s layout is a 
very modern seat, LATAM has also revealed a third   layout featuring seats with doors which they 
begun installing, I believe to eventually   replace both of these existing layouts.
Like I said, multi national airlines with   fleets spread out over five countries 
can get a bit complicated at times.  Stepping on board I was warmly greeted and 
quickly found one of my favorite cabin designs   flying these days. I had previously reviewed 
this product- and I use air quotes around this   product because on the 777s, especially in the 
bulkheads, the layout is wildly more spacious.  On board our 787 tonight, all of the finishes 
that I loved from that 777 are the same here,   from the really satisfying squishy interior of 
the shell, to the red leather accents and even   what I swear is real stone on the side tables. 
It’s one of the classiest cabins you can find.  If you’re enjoying the video and would like to 
support the channel there are many ways you can   do so. A quick like on the video and subscribe 
helps videos with the algorithm. You could join   my Youtube Memberships to get early access to some 
videos and access to all of my Community Posts or   you could check out my Patreon where I post the 
most and can help out if you have travel related   questions. Whatever you do, thanks for doing it.
Next to you you have an open storage area with a   small integrated closed area what is built 
like a tank and really satisfying to click   close. The build quality of it makes me wonder 
if it was originally meant to have a lock,   which would have been pretty cool.
Controls, remotes and outlets are   thoughtfully laid out and easy to use and access.
The seat itself though is quite narrow, as is the   aisle to access the window side seats. Generally- 
tight as it may be- I can fit my size 12 foot in   this space, but that wasn’t happening today.
Same as my previous flight, no pre departure   drinks were served but there were 
bottles of water at each seat.  The foot cubby is quite shallow but tall and 
doesn’t have space under it to stow anything.  To get fully situated you’re going 
to need to macgyver it in this seat.  So about what I was saying. Of course, it 
is wonderful to have your own private space   and I have sat in these staggered lie 
flat seats more times than I can count,   some of those times on other airlines on 787s but 
here they were clearly trying to pack these seats   in as tightly as possible. I’m 6’ tall or 181cm 
and while I was seated it was one of those cases   where both of my knees were touching parts of the 
seat and the monitor just felt needlessly close.  I checked the seatmaps of ANA and EVA air who both 
use similar seats on their 787s- both of which,   especially EVA felt extremely roomy 
and they all look to be fitting the   same amount of seats in the same space- 
so, I’m not sure what was going on here.  Anyway, it’s less a complaint and more just 
an open question about the pros and cons of   certain 2-2-2 seats vs certain all aisle access 
seats. The safety video began and we pushed back.  The first drink service started 
promptly after take off, but first   let’s take a look at the comfort items on board.
First up, love a really good quality and cushy   pair of slippers- that along with a great pillow 
are investments I wish more airlines would make,   they can really make a good flight great.
Luckily, LATAM got the message and the pillow   was fantastic in size and fluff- nearly 
as good as Iberia’s but not quite there.  There’s a duvet style blanket in 
the bag as well, one that is soft   and cozy and a good weight as well.
Finally there’s also a mattress pad   which I’ll show you in action in a bit, but 
for now, another creative storage solution.  The drink cart came down the aisle and 
I had a glass of Sauvignon Blanc along   with a sad bowl of cold and somewhat stale nuts.
Here’s a look at the full menu. Prior to take off   orders were taken and I went for the special dish 
of the day, part of their Sabores que Transportan   or flavors that transport a series of local 
inspired dishes created by locally renowned   chefs- a type of program I love to see on board 
any airline, I’ll blindly order whatever they   recommend. Unfortunately when I did order it, it 
had already sold out, so I went with the beef.  Luckily, shortly after take off my 
very friendly member of crew came   by and let me know she found one for me and 
it turned into the highlight of the flight.  The full meal is served all at once which 
is standard for Latam. For the starter   there was thinly sliced Chilean Abalone with 
lemon and potato salad and a green salad.  The main dish, which to their credit looked 
incredibly similar to the photo in the menu   was Smoked pork tenderloin with smashed Chancado 
potatoes with paprika oil, caramelized apples and   plums. Give me pork and apples together and I’m 
there for it all day and this was no exception.   Overall I’d say the dish was lighter in flavor 
than I was expecting but was still a delight to   eat. I can’t tell you how refreshing it is to try 
something truly new on an airplane of all places.  That was finished off with a Dulce de Lech Mousse 
with Chocolate Ganache and brownie chunks which   was perfectly indulgent and a great finish to 
the meal. Overall, the full meal gets a 9/10.  I know some don’t like full tray services 
but for a late departure like this,   I thought it was a good way to go. My tray 
in the last row was cleared just an hour and   25 minutes after take off, leaving plenty 
of time for sleep on this 10 hour flight.  The entertainment on board was decent with 
over 200 movies on offer from all types   of genres as well as a great newest 
generation moving map. Quality noise   canceling headphone were available as well.
Here’s the bed in full flat mode. It is a bit   of a tight squeeze around the knees 
but it gets the job done. At least   that food cubby is tall enough to not also 
restrict you in that direction. That said,   this is not a seat I can comfortably 
sleep in as a flat bed as I’m not   part of the mummy sleeping crowd.
The sleeping pad was thin but very   nice and squishy foam which even while sitting 
up made for a much more comfortable surface.  I enjoyed a few hours of wine assisted half 
reclined sleep and came to as we were approaching   Florida, just before the sun began to come up.
Let’s take a look at the amenity kit and   get ready for the breakfast service.
I loved the kit. These and the smaller   kits offered on my previous flight are both from 
the same artist collection of kits that they   had rotating through different designs. While I 
don’t need socks or ear plugs or stuff like that,   the number one thing I look for in a good 
kit is whether it’s practical to use again   and this surely, for something, is.
Bathrooms on board were sparse but   kept mostly clean throughout the flight.  The cabin was woken up around 80 minutes prior 
to landing and I was served around 15 minutes   later. A much appreciated efficient service again. 
LATAM really understands what important on these   overnight flights that often stay in the same time 
zone. There’s no need for jetlag if you can get a   decent sleep and LATAM’s service allows for that.
For breakfast there was a choice of scrambled   eggs, a ham and cheese selection or crepes with 
dulce de leche and strawberries. Now, crepes   or pancakes are something I never order unless 
necessary for breakfast on a flight- but also,   I have a rule which requires me to order anything 
that ever has dulce de leche- a rule I adopted   many years ago during my time in Argentina.
Well, today it was a mistake. The dulce de leche,   it can do no harm, was good, even the 
overheated nearly burnt part. But,   the crepes turned into a globbual of sticky hot 
dough as the individual layers fused together.  I also had some yogurt, a small fruit plate 
and… ⅓ of a muffin? Are we rationing muffins   now? Overall, the breakfast gets a 6/10.
Service on board was exactly what I want on   an overnight flight. Friendly and efficient 
during meal services and hiding in between   them for all I care. I also appreciate that 
they never locked the dimmers on the windows.  This flight on it’s own I’d say is 
a 7, but averaged out with my other   LATAM flights I think keeping them at a 6 is fair.  A gorgeous morning approach over 
Sandy Hook and into JFK is coming up.  So, LATAM is a solid airline and I wouldn’t 
hesitate for a moment on flying them again-   though I would be on the lookout 
for their new seats or at least   their 777s which was vastly more comfortable.  So I really do hope you enjoyed this wonderful 
flight with me today. If you did, please be sure   to click that like button and subscribe with 
notifications on so you don’t miss my weekly   flight and resort reviews. I’ll see you next time 
for my final installment from Punta Cana for a   video that I honestly didn’t want to 
make which sounded really tempting to   watch. You’ll understand when you see. As 
always, thanks for watching until the end.

reviews.transcript_full: Did you know South America is home to some surprisingly solid business class products? Take Laten for example. They even run a rare fifth freedom roads between Oakuckland and Sydney and many of their 77s feature a comfortable triple 2 layout. While a cabin refresh is on the horizon, this seat will still be flying for a few more years, which makes it worth a closer look. Honestly, I came away more impressed than I expected on one of South America's largest airline. Stick around because I'm about to show you exactly what you're in for when you fly latam business class. [Music] Latam doesn't have its own lounge in this airport. So they send all their business class and highle elite status holders to this strata lounge. But here's the deal, it's also a contract lounge. Many other airlines are also sending their worthy passengers into this lounge. And to top it off, you can also enter with a priority pass. That said, this shr lounge is a pretty decent stop if you also have priority pass access. It's a step up from your standard priority pass lounge. A nice spot to take a breather, grab a seat, and even freshen up with a shower. [Music] There's enough room to relax. The Wi-Fi is reliable. And while the food and drink selections won't wow you, it covers the basics just fine. [Music] If you want a deeper dive, I've got a full tour on my second channel, Sweet Flyer Plus, where I break down the seating, food, and amenities. And I've also heard that Latam's own lounges in South America are pretty solid. So, I'm willing to trust that they keep a higher standard on their own lounges. Bottom line, it's functional, comfortable, but not a destination lounge. It's perfect for a quick recharge. Though I wouldn't plan a long layover here. [Music] If you are constantly traveling and hate checking in your belongings, then you will need a good carry-on luggage. Check out the one by Level 8 that I've been using for the past few trips over here. It is made with aluminum, keeping it lightweight and sturdy and the wheels are buttery smooth. The luggage doesn't have zipper but TSA approved locks which are way more secured. It comes with three colors, black, gray, and blue. So, if you are a road warrior like myself, then you will love the Level 8 luggage. The best part is the price is super affordable for such a high quality luggage. So, I highly recommend you to go check it out. I'll leave all the info in the description below. Now, let's get back to the video. Now, let's talk about the flight itself. First impression, I love the visually pleasing colors in the cabin. It gives off a fresh and modern vibe compared to the darker designs you still see in some other carriers. That said, there is a slight privacy issue. The layout feels open, so you don't get that cocoon-like feeling you'll find with the newer business class suites. It's not a dealbreaker, but if you're sitting next to a stranger, you'll definitely notice it, and that makes sense. This is one of the most common seat designs from the 2010s. Back then this was the industry standard and you still see it flying today on airlines like Turkish Airline, Lo Polish and similar layouts can also be found in Qatar ANA and even Cafe A. If you have flown any of those carriers in the last decade, this setup will feel familiar. [Music] Comfortwise, honestly, I don't mind it. For short to medium hall flights, it's perfectly fine. But compared to today's suites with doors, yeah, you miss the extra privacy and space. [Music] [Music] [Music] Hey, [Music] hey, hey. [Music] I also appreciate that the airline provides an amenity kit to every passenger even though this is a short hall flight. [Music] Heat. Heat. [Music] The food, it was fine. Not memorable, but not bad either. It fill me up, and that's what really matters on a flight like this. [Music] What really stood out was the sleeping kit. The pillow and a duvet were of high quality, and that extra bit of comfort really makes a difference. [Music] [Music] The seat itself was comfy enough for this short hall flight. And I would say it would even hold up reasonably well on a long haul flight, especially if you're traveling with someone. But here's the catch. Many passengers, myself included, would still prefer a 121 configuration. The tighter triple 2 layout feels a little crammed, especially for solo travelers, and is the same issue Turkish Airlines faces with this design. Pairing that with the lack of a seat divider, the privacy takes another hit. Other than that, it's a solid product. The seat is comfortable, the bedding is excellent, and overall, it delivers a relaxing experience. So, where do I land? Punfully intended. For me, this flight earns a 14 out of 20. It's not perfect, but it strikes a decent balance between comfort and practicality with a few trade-offs you'll notice more on longer journeys. [Music] [Music]

reviews.transcript_full: [Music] Welcome back. In this video, we're stepping on board LAM Airlines in their new business class seat on a Boeing 767300 ER on our way from Lima, Peru to Atlanta in the USA. How does LATAM and this business class product stack up against other options? And is it worth flying? Stick with us and find out. Join us as we get on board one of the last 767s ever built in LATAM's newest business class product and embark from the brand new terminal at Jorge Chavez International Airport. [Music] Welcome to Travel at Random. We're Trevor and Ryan. This channel started out of a love of travel. We're here to share unbiased and self-funded trip reports, hotel and flight reviews, and travel advice. We hope we inspire your next getaway. Check out our playlist in the description and browse the channel. If you enjoy this video, please hit that like button and subscribe to keep up with our latest content. Thank you for watching. Now, let's fly. [Music] We're starting off today at Jorge Chavez International Airport in Lima, Peru. Serving about 23 million passengers annually. The airport recently completed construction of a brand new terminal which opened on the 1st of June 2025. While the new terminal is open, it's not exactly finished yet. If you've never been to Lima, one thing to know is that the traffic is terrible. This city of more than 11 million people has very limited mass transit and lacks major highways. The new airport terminal is not currently connected to public transit and traffic is routed over two temporary bridges. Traffic can be slow and congested, particularly at peak times. We had given ourselves plenty of time, but it still took about 90 minutes from our hotel in Mirror Flores to get to the terminal at 9:00 a.m. on a weekday. In fact, we were sitting for so long that Uber sent us a message to make sure we were okay. Once we made it to the terminal, things improved. Check-in is located on the upper level with LATAM on the far right side of the terminal. LAM Airlines has a premium check-in area at counters A11 through A15. There is a separate check-in room just past the counters for top tier status holders, including Delta Diamond, Platinum, and LATAM Platinum members. There are check-in lanes for Delta Silver, Gold, LATAM Gold, Gold Plus, and a separate queue for business class passengers. There are four concourses at the airport. the domestic B concourse on the lower level and three international concourses A, C, and D on the third level with check-in. Since this terminal is brand new, currently the only airside lounge is the club Lima. LOM is opening its own club in August of 2025, so we missed it by just a few weeks. The lounges are accessible to international passengers only. Priority Pass is accepted at the club or you can purchase a pass at reception for $55. This is the newest and largest The Club location at almost 20,000 square ft. It has the capacity for more than 450 guests and is designed to provide options for travelers of all kinds. It features relaxation areas, private meeting rooms, and an enclosed player area for children. The club is decorated with local Peruvian artwork and greenery. There are two small buffets on either side of the central bar. There are also drink stations at each buffet. We were in the club for breakfast and the options were basic. The buffet closer to check-in had more options available. There are showers in this lounge and you can reserve them with QR codes on each table. Wi-Fi was available. The speeds were pretty good. The club was comfortable and had plenty of space. It felt open and spacious, and we didn't have any trouble finding a seat. One note, our LATAM business class ticket did not get us entry, and the LATAM check-in agents did not even mention a lounge when we dropped off our bags. Our 7-hour flight today takes us a little over 3,000 m from Lima, Peru to Atlanta, Georgia in LAM Airlines premium business class cabin. LAM is in the process of refitting their planes with new interiors. The 767s, trip 7s, and some 787900s have these new business class seats. They are currently also deploying a new business class suite on their 787800s that feature a door. Lat's boarding process was a bit chaotic, and we started an hour before departure. Boarding for premium cabins is zone one and includes both business and premium economy passengers. There are only three zones in total. Everyone had to have their carry-on items searched prior to boarding, and they held us on the jet bridge for another 5 minutes before we were allowed to board. Boarding for all passengers was at the front of the plane, leading to a lot of foot traffic and liloos in the business class cabin. We saw several economy passengers stowing their bags in the business class overhead bins, and the flight attendants didn't seem to care. This is a Boeing 767300 ER with 20 business class seats and 213 economy seats. This aircraft also features 39 LATAM plus seats which feature additional legroom. The business class seats are arranged in a 1 121 staggered layout and all seats have direct aisle access. We are in seats 3A and 5A today which are the window seats closest to the windows. Even rows are closer to the aisle. Each seat has a 16-in touchscreen, USBA, and universal power plugs. The universal power plugs didn't get turned on on our flight, or they weren't working, unfortunately. The seat has a decent amount of storage space. There's a small closing compartment below an open area to the side of the seat. A goodiz counter with a real stone surface. [Music] The seat surface uses three-dimensional textiles to help improve air flow and temperature. The seat was a bit narrow, and I found that I often hit the seat controls with my elbow, causing my seat to move unintentionally. The seat has a pitch of 45 in and a width of 19 1/2 in and recines to a fully lay flat. As a bed, the seat was comfortable. I think more comfortable than as a seat where it was a little too flat and didn't have much lumbar support. The footwell was a bit tight, but as long as you lay on your back, Trevor found it comfortable, and it was long enough for him to lay completely down, even at 6'4 in. When in bed mode, it is a little difficult getting in and out of the seat. That's one of the problems with the 767. The cabin is narrower than newer aircraft models, so the seats tend to be a little tighter. There were accent lights above the literature holder and storage area and you can control their light level. There's also a reading light which you can adjust the brightness on. Waiting at our seats was a mattress topper, duvet and pillow. The linens were good quality, the pillow a decent size and the duvet was quite large also welcome. The amenity kits are eco-friendly and focus on sustainable materials throughout. The bags feature designs from South American artists. Inside the kit features a bamboo toothbrush, eye mask, socks, earplugs, a refreshening towel, lip balm, and hand cream. Push back was prompt, but the taxi and wait to depart took about 20 minutes. We took off to the south and quickly escaped the cloud cover. [Music] On board, the in-flight entertainment system is called LATAM Play. With over 300 movies and a thousand TV episodes, there's a decent selection available, and the system was responsive. There were also music and games available and a flight tracker. This aircraft did not have Wi-Fi. Some LATAM 767s have it installed and they're working to install Wi-Fi across the fleet. No pre-eparture drinks were offered, but they did take our meal orders on the ground. On this flight, there was a lunch service and a hot snack service just before landing. Just after takeoff, mixed nuts and sparkling wine were served. LATM has refocused their onboard dining experience recently and now provides Latin American focused meals with a focus on the local flavors of the departure point. For lunch, we both ordered the Amazonian shufa, which is a fried rice dish, and Luca mimoose for dessert. The starter was a take on a kowsa, a traditional Peruvian potato dish, although a bit deconstructed. The shrimp were fine, a little tough, but fine. Overall, this dish lacked flavor. The salad was literally three leaves of lettuce and a basic vinegarette. I guess it counts as a salad, but it could have just been a garnish at that point. The starter was fine, not great, not bad. The main dish was their signature dish from a local chef, Ilia Garcia, and it was great. It was flavorful, and anything with plantains is always a plus to us. The Luca Mimoose was light with some tart mango fruit bits on top and then cookie crumbles on the bottom. It was good, but the mango on top was what made this. Overall, the lunch was good. We're glad to see local flavors on board. And while the starter wasn't anything special, we did enjoy the rice dish. About 70 minutes before arrival, a snack service was served. It was a sandwich and a dessert. Trevor ordered the lentil burger and dol de leche pudding and a Coke Zero. I skipped the snack. Trevor said the sandwich was pretty good and had mozzarella, lettuce, and tomato on top of a lentil patty. It was served with potato chips and an ioli. The pudding was very light with a few cookie bits on top and fresh blueberries. Overall, the dish was decent and more than some carriers will offer on a flight of this length. For comparison, we flew Delta down to Peru and there was no second meal or snack service offered in business class. We arrived into Atlanta around 8:00 p.m. This was a completely daytime flight. [Music] Evenings are a bit busy at ATL, but we got a good sunset view as we taxi to our gate in the F concourse. [Music] We found this flight to be comfortable. I slept a good chunk of this flight since I wasn't feeling great. I found the bed to be long enough and the footwell decent, although I found it more comfortable to sleep on my side than my back due to the contours of the seat. Trevor felt like he could have slept, but it wouldn't have been the best sleep due to the space restrictions around his shoulders and legs. The service was good, the food was enjoyable, and had a unique flare to it. The flight attendants were present throughout the flight and were personable and friendly during service. I think this product is fine for a mediumh hall flight. We got a great fair for our trip and had a good experience. Would we fly LAM again? I'd say absolutely for a mediumh hall flight like this one. Our biggest complaint about service was the fairly indifferent LATAM ground staff in Lima. Once on board, the flight attendants were friendly. One important thing to note is that we booked this trip through Delta. Latam has a joint venture with Delta. And while LATAM is not part of the Sky Team Alliance, Delta medallions get many perks and benefits with LATAM. This includes priority boarding, check-in, etc. We also earn Delta miles and elite MQDs on this flight. Have you flown Latam? Let us know in the comments what you think of this airline. And don't forget to hit that like button and subscribe to keep up with our latest travels. Thank you for watching. We'll see you on the next adventure. [Music]

reviews.transcript_full:
Welcome back to Travel Expertos. Today we’ll be flying with Emirates in Business Class onboard the Boeing 777-300ER from Tokyo Haneda to Dubai on flight EK313. This flight is scheduled for just over 10 hours and will give us the chance to fully experience Emirates’ newer Boeing 777 Business Class product featuring direct aisle access, fully flat beds, premium dining, pajamas, lounge access, and one of the best entertainment systems in commercial aviation. In this full review, we’ll cover the entire experience from the chauffeur transfer through Tokyo, Haneda Airport Terminal 3, check-in, the Japan Airlines Sakura Lounge, boarding, seat 10A, dinner service, bed comfort, sleep quality, breakfast before arrival, and finally our arrival into Dubai before continuing our trip to Frankfurt onboard Emirates First Class. Let’s see how Emirates Business Class performs on this overnight flight from Japan to the Middle East. Our journey begins in central Tokyo with Emirates’ complimentary chauffeur drive service. One of the major advantages of flying Emirates Business Class is that the premium experience starts before you even reach the airport. Instead of navigating Tokyo’s busy evening transport system with luggage, Emirates provides a direct private transfer to Haneda Airport Terminal 3. Tokyo at night feels incredible from the back seat of the car. Soon enough we've reached Tokyo Haneda international airport. The drive to Haneda was smooth, comfortable, and surprisingly fast considering Tokyo traffic. We have now arrived at Tokyo Haneda Airport Terminal 3. Haneda is widely considered one of the best airports in the world thanks to its cleanliness, efficiency, modern design, and proximity to central Tokyo. Compared to Narita, Haneda is significantly more convenient, especially for premium passengers connecting quickly into the city. Tonight the terminal feels calm, modern, and extremely organized. Even during busy hours, the airport maintains a very quiet and premium atmosphere. Haneda was open in late of October 2010. We now head toward the Emirates check-in area for EK313 to Dubai.  Checkin counters were organized and split into First,Business,Premium Economy and Economy class The whole checkin process was well organized efficient and fast. After check-in, we continued through security and immigration. Haneda’s security process is extremely efficient compared to many major international airports. Even during evening departure waves, the airport moves passengers quickly without feeling chaotic. Once airside, we headed through the terminal toward the lounge area. Emirates Business Class passengers departing Haneda have access to the Japan Airlines Sakura Lounge, which is one of the more interesting partnerships in the Emirates network. As we walk through the airport you may notice how clean and spotless the terminal and airport actually is. Soon enough we reach Jal's Business Class lounge at Haneda. Japan Airlines Sakura lounge is located on the 4th floor (1floor above the terminal.) We are now inside the Japan Airlines Sakura Lounge. Food options included Japanese dishes, light snacks, bakery items, drinks, and self-service beverage stations. The lounge provides showers, changing rooms, and spotless bathrooms. The lounge has a very different atmosphere compared to Emirates’ own lounges in Dubai. Instead of flashy luxury, the focus here is calm design, efficiency, privacy, and Japanese hospitality. Large seating areas overlook the apron, offering excellent nighttime views of aircraft movements around Haneda. The lounge atmosphere is extremely quiet, making it a very good place to relax before an overnight departure. Compared to some overcrowded international lounges, this feels far more peaceful and refined. After spending some time here relaxing before the flight, it is now almost time to head toward Gate 144 for boarding. We are now leaving the lounge and heading toward Gate 144. Haneda’s terminal design is simple to navigate, and even the longer walks remain pleasant thanks to the modern architecture and clean layout. Waiting area is divided into Business and First class cabin together and Premium and Economy class together. Our flight is delayed due to bad weather on way to Tokyo, the plane has not even landed yet. Soon enough our plane arrived to our gate. reviews.transcript_full: Flying from Cebu to Hong Kong, most people choose Cebu Pacific because it's usually the cheaper option. But this time we decided to fly with Cathay Pacific instead. The ticket cost more, so the question is simple. Is the extra money actually worth it? If you're flying from Cebu to Hong Kong, you'll usually end up comparing these two airlines. Cathay Pacific is often more expensive, although the price difference can vary quite a bit depending on when you book. But first, Cebu Airport. Still my favorite airport in the Philippines. It's modern, spacious, clean, and has plenty of food options. Waiting for your flight here is actually enjoyable. Boarding was right on time for us. The staff were professional, everything was [music] organized, and the whole process felt smooth from the start to finish. The aircraft isn't brand new, but it feels very well maintained, clean, comfortable, and in great condition. This is the Airbus A330, a wide-body aircraft commonly used on longer routes. Inside, you get a two-four-two seating layout, which immediately feels more spacious than the narrow-body aircraft used by many budget airlines. By the way, I have a video about the Cebu Pacific aircraft, linked down below in the description if you want to check it out. The seat was comfortable, and the legroom was more than enough for this 3-hour flight. [music] You also get a personal entertainment screen with movies, TV shows, games, and a flight tracker. Headphones are included as well. So already it feels like a different experience compared to most budget carriers. Then came the food. She went for the chicken and rice, while I chose the seafood pasta. I'll be honest, seafood on an airplane is always a risk, but surprisingly, it was delicious, cheesy, flavorful, and I finished every bite. No regrets here. And unlike most budget airlines, the meal is already included in your ticket. Drinks are included, too. Soft drinks, such as or or I asked the cabin crew for a recommendation and ended up trying a Hong Kong craft beer. Really good. Definitely didn't expect that. You also get a fresh fruits and a Haagen-Dazs ice cream for dessert. Simple, but a very nice touch. After the meal service, the crew came back offering coffee, tea, and hot chocolate. They also mentioned that drinks were free flow throughout [music] the flight. Service overall was excellent, friendly, attentive, and professional throughout the flight. The flight itself was smooth and comfortable with flight time of around 3 hours. There's enough time to relax, watch a movie, enjoy the meal, or simply sit back and enjoy the ride. So, is Cathay Pacific worth paying more compared to Cebu Pacific? In my opinion, yes. You get better comfort, better service, included meals and drinks, in-flight entertainment, and an overall more premium travel experience. Is it essential for a 3-hour flight? Not necessarily. But, if you value comfort and want to start your Hong Kong trip on a better note, I think it's worth considering, especially if the schedule is more convenient for you. And that's what it's like flying Cathay Pacific from Cebu to Hong Kong. If you found this review helpful, consider subscribing. I regularly share hotel reviews, flight experiences, restaurants, and travel guides from around the Philippines and beyond. See you on the next adventure.

again Before landing I also checked out The rear lavatory on the aircraft Even after more than 10 hours It was still kept pretty clean There were also paper cups for brushing teeth But the space was definitely very tight Still for a 20 year old 777 The condition was actually quite well maintained Before landing in Chicago Let’s talk about the overall experience Even though this Boeing 777 is already quite old I still think the Sky Wider seat is pretty good After more than 10 hours in the air My knees didn’t feel too uncomfortable And the lower back support was better than expected JAL’s inflight service isn’t especially extensive But small details like the ingredient list Show that they are quite thoughtful At least you know clearly what you’re eating Without needing to ask the crew If you’re flying from Asia to North America And don’t want to pay extra for premium economy But still want a more comfortable seat I think JAL’s long haul economy class Is a very solid option What do our wedding with uncle and aunt. I'll also meet Vaishali and I'll tell her the whole truth. I've been living alone for many years. Not anymore. Now, we'll be together. And that's final. The body found in Gaurav's backyard was confirmed to be Sanjana's
through DNA matching. Gaurav faced murder charges
for Sanjana's death. Sanjana's uncle and aunt

is quite simple. Either both are happy, or neither is. It's important to end that relationship
right away. Because forcing
a broken relationship together is like trying to piece together
shards of glass. The relationship will shatter,
and it will be painful. Family, my people... If I say in Bollywood style,

in happiness or not, but they always support you
in difficulties. These are the relationships that
don't break even when they fracture. Always in life... think positive, think good, think wise. May all be blessed.
May I be blessed.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to San Juan, Puerto Rico. Our time in the sun is over and now we have to head back home. Today, we're going to be flying in first class on United. We'll be checking out their service on board a Boeing 737 MAX 9. Join us as we put one of United's newest first class cabins to the test. We'll evaluate the seat comfort, in-flight service, and overall value of United's premium cabin experience. This is also a dinner flight, so we're going to evaluate United's catering and see if it's any good. Plus, stick around and we'll tell you how much we paid for this flight so you can determine if it's worth the upgrade. Welcome to the capital of Puerto Rico, San Juan. We're starting today at Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport, airport code SJU. Puerto Rico is a US overseas territory located between the Dominican Republic and the US Virgin Islands. No passport is required if you're traveling from the mainland US. SJU is the busiest airport in the Caribbean with over 13 and 1/2 million passengers in 2025. The island is home to more than 3 million people. If you're flying out of San Juan, there's one thing you must do before you head to your airline check-in or TSA, and that is go to the USDA inspection. If you've ever flown out of Hawaii, you've probably seen this. Among other things, they're checking to make sure you're not taking any fresh fruits or vegetables or plants off the island. You'll see signs for this just inside the terminal. Make sure you complete this before heading to your airline to check in. With USDA inspection complete, let's head over to United. >> [music] >> Our first class ticket gets us access to the priority check-in line. Two 70-lb check bags are included with our ticket. The bag drop was a quick process and now it's off to security. If the lines are long, you can also walk over to the other terminal and use that checkpoint. All of the gates in San Juan are connected airside. After security, you're dropped into a duty-free store. Good to note, even if you're traveling back to the mainland, you can buy duty-free. Just like Delta and American, United does not provide lounge access on a domestic first class ticket. That wouldn't matter today because United does not have a lounge in San Juan. But there are a few Priority Pass and credit card lounge options at SJU. The Global Lounge Network operates two lounges, a small location near the JetBlue gates and a second location near the C gates. This is closer to American, United, Delta, and Southwest flights. Both of these accept Priority Pass. We reviewed one of those lounges in a previous video when we flew JetBlue Mint. We'll leave a link in the description if you want to check that out. Plus, now's a good time to click that like button and subscribe so you never miss one of our flight reviews. We missed the Escape Lounge last time we were here, so let's go check that out. This lounge is located near gate B2. >> [music] >> There are a few ways to access the Escape Lounge. You can access it with the American Express Platinum or Centurion card. Delta Reserve card members are also eligible if flying on a same-day Delta ticket. Amex card holders receive two complimentary guests. This lounge also sells day passes on a space-available basis for $55 per person. Upon arrival, there was a waitlist today, so I signed up. They text you when it's your turn to enter. Unfortunately, the wait today was only about 10 minutes. The Escape Lounge is open daily from 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. The lounge is located one level below the gates. It's not a large space, but it's nicely broken up into a few different seating areas. There's a bar across from the elevator and main staircase. It features a limited selection of complimentary alcohol and non-alcoholic drinks. Oddly, they didn't have any beer, which was disappointing since they advertised their partnership with a San Juan brewery. In the center of the lounge is a food buffet. It featured a decent mix of hot and cold items. The shredded meat was actually quite good. You can definitely find enough food here for a meal before a flight. There were several friendly staff walking around taking drink orders. This included coffee, tea, and water. The main coffee machine by the buffet was out of order. Seating is broken into a few different areas. There are dining tables and chairs near the buffet and tucked behind the elevator and staircase. Near the bar area was a sofa. Many of the seats were perfect for solo travelers and featured high walls for privacy. There were also pairs of seats together. It was tough to film since this lounge was quite busy most of our visit. There are three single user restrooms in this lounge and they were kept clean. There are no showers in this lounge. The lounge is at ground level and does offer a pretty good view of the nearby Southwest Airlines gate. There is Wi-Fi. It was easy to connect and speeds were very fast. So, this Escape Lounge isn't bad. It's a little small and there was a short wait to get in today. Now, it's about half empty. The only big problem is it's really warm. The air conditioning's not working, so they have some temporary units and looks like they've been here for a while, so I'm guessing it's always like this. Having been to all of the lounges at SJU, the Escape Lounge definitely had the best food, but the other lounges aren't bad options either and I think they had a better selection of drinks. >> [music] >> Our 3-hour and 30-minute flight today takes us 1,570 miles from San Juan, Puerto Rico to Washington Dulles Airport on board of Boeing 737 Max 9 in first class. Time to board our flight. United uses the B gates in San Juan. Boarding here can get a bit hectic as the gate areas are a bit crowded. We've said it before about United, but one of our biggest complaints with United's boarding process is that they board the 1K members well before zone one, even if they're not in first class. So, even if you're in zone one, you're going to be competing for overhead bin space with the 1Ks who got on before you. This can also mean you may be putting your bag in economy, which on a paid first class ticket is not an ideal situation. Boarding started right on time. On this 737 Max 9, there are 20 first class seats in a standard 2-2 layout. The aircraft also features 45 extra legroom economy seats and 114 standard economy seats in a 3-3 layout. I'm in 1B today, the bulkhead. This flight was completely full. One of the reasons we tend to avoid the bulkhead is there's no under seat storage. All personal items and bags must go in the overhead bin for takeoff and landing. Fortunately, there was enough overhead bin space on today's flight. The advantage of the bulkhead is that no one's going to recline into your space. Today, we're on a 2-year-old 737 Max 9 featuring United's new signature interior. Depending on what version of this plane you get, [music] you may or may not get an IFE screen. The older Max 9s don't have screens. The first class seats are 20 in wide with a pitch of 37 in. The legroom is good and on par with other domestic first class seats. The crew had all of the window shades closed to keep the cabin cool and the lights were very dim, so it was difficult to film the cabin upon boarding. Here's a shot of these seats from a previous trip we had on United's Max 9. The legroom in the bulkhead is decent. However, there are no cutouts at the bottom of the partition for your feet, so keep that in mind. We like to see individual air vents above. This is also where you'll find the reading light. There's a wide center armrest. At the front is a small table. Tucked between the seats is a space to hold a water bottle and the universal power outlet and USB-C port. Unfortunately, my outlet didn't work, but the USB-C port did. In front of the seat is a small storage pocket. This was large enough to hold a tablet. And under the center armrest is a small storage cubby. The bifold tray table pops out of the armrest. It was sturdy and it featured an integrated device holder. Under the armrest closer to the aisle is another storage compartment, large enough for a laptop or something skinny. The seats feature an adjustable headrest that goes both up and down and the wings fold in. Blankets were also passed out by the flight crew, which is a nice touch. Overall, the seat is comfortable with decent padding for our 3 and 1/2 hour flight. Pre-departure drinks of water or sparkling wine were offered, both in plastic cups. I had some water. We do wish United offered a full selection of pre-departure beverages like some other carriers. Boarding wrapped up and we pushed back from the gate a few minutes early. reviews.transcript_full: Hello everyone and welcome back to my Disneyland series. Today we are talking all about our experience flying Southwest Airlines. I've actually only ever flown Southwest my entire life. So when they announced they were getting rid of open seating and switching to assigned seats, I was really curious to see what the experience would be like. This trip was also our first time flying with four kids and traveling carry-on only, which honestly made me nervous. Especially because my son Asher is autistic. We were originally assigned one of the last boarding groups and Southwest no longer offers family boarding the way they used to. Thankfully things ended up going much smoother than I expected and I was really impressed with our experience. So if you're flying Southwest, traveling with kids, traveling with an autistic child, or just curious about their new boarding process, here's how everything went for us from check-in all the way through landing in California. One thing I really appreciate about Southwest Airlines is that families can check strollers and car seats for free. You can do this at the ticket counter before security or at the gate if you'd rather use the stroller throughout the airport. We gate checked ours so it would be waiting for us on the jet bridge as soon as we landed. Okay, now you've checked in, printed your boarding pass, made it through security and found your gate. It is now time to board your plane. As I mentioned earlier, our family had been assigned the last boarding group, group eight. Normally that wouldn't be a big deal at all, but for our family it was a little more complicated. I know some families actually prefer to board last with their young children and that just works better for them. For us, with Asher being autistic, we absolutely need that extra time to get him on board, familiarize with his seat, comfortable with the seatbelt, and to just adjust before there are too many people on board. Southwest no longer offers family boarding the way they used to. Instead they offer pre-boarding for customers with disabilities or anyone who needs additional boarding assistance. Even though Southwest states only one person will be able to accompany the disabled passenger, I just explained my 5-year-old is autistic and asked if we could pre-board. The gate agent immediately said yes. I then asked if our entire family would be able to board together since it was just me, my husband, and our four young children. I am so grateful they also said yes to that without hesitation. We had a backup plan just in case, but I'm so thankful they were able to accommodate all six of us this time. It changed the whole entire flight for us. I can't guarantee every family's experience will be the same as ours, but it never hurts to politely ask. Once boarding began, it was surprisingly quick. I had heard stories that assigned seating actually slowed down Southwest's boarding process, but that wasn't our experience at all, and both of our flights were completely full. The boarding process was very efficient, and I feel it was faster than when we would board with open seating. I think people choosing and changing their mind while on board made it take longer. Okay, now we are officially on the plane and ready to take off. Southwest is in the process of upgrading all of their planes. These upgrades will include extra legroom seats, USB ports in the seatback, adjustable headrests, and device holders above your tray table. I did not expect us to have an upgraded plane from Austin International Airport to LAX, but we got so lucky. And wow. These upgrades are amazing, okay? Like just outstanding. The standard seats felt like I had more legroom than in the past. The device holder was awesome. It held our Kindles, iPads, phones, and they were more eye-level versus having them much lower on your lap or on your tray table. And the adjustable headrests, oh my goodness. I slept so good with the headrests, and it was the first time ever on a plane that I did not need a neck pillow to sleep because they just supported my neck and head so well and were oh so comfortable. On flights 250 miles or more, you will be served complimentary graham crackers, pretzels, and drinks. Here's what you can get for free during your flight and here's what you can pay extra for if you would like an alcoholic beverage. Unfortunately, and this is like the only thing I wish Southwest would change, is this is the only food offerings on board no matter how long your flight is. I do wish they were heavier options available for purchase, maybe like a snack pack, fruit and cheese tray, or sandwich, or something like that. Southwest Airlines doesn't have screens in the back of their seats. They do offer tons of free movies, TV shows, and even live TV for their in-flight entertainment. They offer a great range of movies from classics to new releases like The Housemate, Wicked for Good, and Zootopia 2. To access the in-flight entertainment, just turn on airplane mode on your device, connect to Southwest Wi-Fi, and then open up your Southwest app and click on flight entertainment and it will guide you right through. Southwest also has just introduced free Wi-Fi for Rapid Rewards members. You can sign up for the Rapid Rewards for free on the Southwest website. You can then connect to the free Wi-Fi the same way as accessing the in-flight entertainment. Just sign in with your Rapid Rewards info and password when prompted, watch one quick ad, and then free Wi-Fi for the rest of your flight. Now, on the flight to California, the Wi-Fi was extremely slow and eventually stopped working altogether. So, I switched to their free movies and ended up watching Jurassic Park 2 until I fell asleep. The Wi-Fi seemed to work for simple things like if I needed to look something up on Google, but then trying to stream Hulu on it just did not work at all. It buffered a ton until it just cut out altogether. On the flight back from LA, the Wi-Fi just would not work at all even for simple web browsing. They also offer the option to buy Wi-Fi for $8 per device. We used this once on one of our previous flights years ago and I didn't notice any trouble at all with the paid Wi-Fi. It worked perfectly. Our flight attendants were great as they always are. They were friendly, very conversational with us and they gave us a lid and straw for the kids drinks that they ordered, which was a small gesture that made a big difference. So yeah, that was our experience flying Southwest Airlines to Disneyland. Overall, Southwest Airlines made what could have been a very stressful travel day feel smooth and effortless, especially traveling with four kids. The employees were incredibly kind and helpful and thankfully we had no major issues at all. So if you're thinking about flying Southwest, hopefully this gave you a little idea of what the experience is like. Thank you so much for watching. Next week we're finally getting into the actual Disneyland portion of this trip and I cannot wait to share that with you because this trip was absolutely incredible. Make sure you're subscribed if you'd like to follow along and I'll see you in the next one. Bye everyone. That was our journey as our first time traveling with four children on Southwest Airlines. If you made it this far, thanks so much for watching and subscribe to see our travel day and actual days at Disneyland next week.
