கொடுத்தாங்க. இந்த சப்பாத்தி சிக்கன் கறி வந்துட்டு டேஸ்ட் வந்துட்டு ரொம்பவே சூப்பரா இருந்துச்சு. அடுத்தது வந்துட்டு வெஜிடேரியன் ஆப்ஷன். சோ வெஜிடேரியன் ஆப்ஷன் பாத்தீங்கன்னா வந்துட்டு ஒரு சாம்பார் வடை ரவை மாதிரி ஒன்னு கொடுத்தாங்க. அப்புறம் ஒரு சப்பாத்தியும் கொடுத்தாங்க. இது டேஸ்ட் வந்துட்டு ரொம்பவே ஆவரேஜா இருந்துச்சுன்னுதான் சொல்லணும். ட்ரிங்க்ஸ் பாத்தீங்கன்னா வந்துட்டு ஆல்கஹாலிக் அண்ட் நான் ஆல்கஹாலிக் டிரிங்க்ஸ் அவைலபிள் நம்ம வாங்குனது வந்துட்டு ஒரு டயட் கோக்தான். ஓவரஆல் மீல்ஸ் வந்துட்டு நல்லாவே இருந்துச்சு. பபினிஷிங் டச்சுக்கு ஒரு மசாலா டீயும் வாங்குனோம். இந்த டீ வந்துட்டு ரொம்ப ரொம்ப தண்ணியாதான் இருக்கும். பட் டேஸ்ட் நல்லா இருந்தது. அடுத்தது கிரிஸ்பிளேயர் இன்போடைன்மென்ட் சிஸ்டம். சோ இந்த இன்போடைன்மென்ட் சிஸ்டம்ல ஓரளவுக்கு நிறையவே கலெக்ஷன் வச்சிருக்காங்க. தமிழ் மூவிஸ் அதுக்கப்புறம் வந்துட்டு ரீஜினல் ஹிந்தி, தெலுங்கு, மலையாளம் எல்லா மூவிஸுமே வந்துட்டு அவைலபிலா இருக்கு. அது போக நம்மஃிளைட் எங்க போகுதுனோ ட்ராக் பண்ணிக்கலாம். ரெஸ்ட்ரூம் பாத்தீங்கன்னா நீட்டாவே இருந்துச்சு. அது போக டென்டல் கிட்ஸுமே வந்துட்டு அவைலபிலா வச்சிருந்தாங்க. ஏன்னா இது ரொம்பவே ஏர்லி மார்னிங்ஃிளைட் நிறைய பேர் காலையில வந்திருப்பாங்க. சில பேர் வந்துட்டு ஏர்போர்ட்லே தங்கி இருந்திருப்பாங்க. அதனால வந்துட்டு சோ பிரஷ் இருக்காதுங்கிற பட்சத்துல அது வந்து டெண்டல் கிட்ட வந்து உள்ள ரெஸ்ட் ரூம்ல அவைலபிலா இருந்துச்சு. மத்தபடி நீட்டாவே இருந்துச்சுன்னுதான் சொல்லணும் ரெஸ்ட்ரூம். சோ ஓவரஆல் இந்தஃிளைட் வந்துட்டு உண்மையிலேயே வந்துட்டு கம்பர்டபிலா இருந்துச்சு. டோட்டல் ஜர்னி டைம் 4 ஹவர்ஸ் தான் நம்ம இப்ப பெங்களூருக்கு பக்கத்துல வந்தாச்சு. சோ லைவ் மேப்ல நம்மளுக்கு பார்த்தாலே தெரியுது பெங்களூர் இன்னும் வந்துட்டு ஜஸ்ட் பை மினிட்ஸ்தான் நம்ம பெங்களூர் ஏர்போர்ட்ல லேண்ட் ஆக போறோம். லோக்கல் டைம் பாத்தீங்கன்னா இப்போ 1020 am ஆன் டைம்கே வந்துட்டு பிளைட் [இசை] லேண்ட் பண்ணிட்டாங்க. சோ நம்ம இப்ப லேண்ட் ஆயிருக்கறது எந்தன்னு பாத்தீங்கன்னா பெங்களூரோட டெர்மினல் 2லதான். சோ பெங்களூர்ல ரெண்டு டெர்மினல் இருக்கு டெர்மினல் 1 டெர்மினல் 2 அதுல டெர்மினல் 2 தான் உண்மையிலேயே சூப்பரா இருக்கும். இன்டர்நேஷனல் பிளைட்ஸ் எல்லாமே வந்துட்டு இங்க இருந்துதான் வந்துட்டு டேக் ஆப் அண்ட் லேண்டிங் பண்ணுது. சோ இப்ப நம்ம பாக்குறதுதான் நம்மளோட airர்பஸ் A350 பிளைட் சிங்கப்பூர்ல இருந்து வந்து லேண்ட் ஆயிருக்கும். சோ இம்மிக்ிரேஷன் செக்யூரிட்டி எல்லாமே டக்குன்னு முடிச்சிட்டோம். இப்ப நீங்க பாக்குற டியூட்டி ஃப்ரீ ஷாப். சோ இது வந்துட்டு இந்த நம்மள அப்படியே பேக் எடுத்துட்டு போற வழியிலயே வந்துட்டு இருக்கும். சோ ஓவரஆல் இந்த எக்ஸ்பீரியன்ஸ் வந்துட்டு ரொம்பவே நல்லா இருந்துச்சு. சோ சிங்கப்பூர் ஏர்லைன்ஸ் வந்துட்டு சர்வீஸ்ும் சரிஃபுட்டம் சரி எல்லாமே நல்லா இருந்துச்சு. இந்த வீடியோ உங்களுக்கு புடிச்சிருக்கும்னு நினைக்கிறேன். புடிச்சிருந்தா கண்டிப்பா லைக் பண்ணி கமெண்ட் பண்ணுங்க. ஆம்

reviews.transcript_full:
Today we're flying on Swiss Airlines brand new 
premium economy on their A350-900 from Montreal   to Zurich. But this premium economy cabin 
is a little bit unconventional. So we'll   see how it feels on this flight along with the 
food, the service, and the overall experience.   More importantly, we will of course see 
if it's worth paying extra to upgrade   to premium economy from economy. But 
let's find out all this together on   today's flight. Our trip today starts 
off here at Montreal Trudeau airport. First, let's talk about check-in. Unfortunately, 
Swiss Premium Economy doesn't include dedicated   check-in, so we'll be using the same 
check-in counters or kiosks as economy. In terms of luggage, premium economy passengers 
get two pieces of luggage weighing 23 kg or   50 lbs each. Although, if you are flying on a 
premium economy light fare, you'll only get one   piece of check-in luggage, which is the same 
as economy comfort plus, green, or flex fares. Hi. So, I'm here at the lounge here in Montreal. 
And unfortunately, like most airlines, Swiss does   not provide premium economy passengers with lounge 
access. So, that is the reason why I'm not going   to show the lounge here in Montreal. But what 
I do want to mention is that if you are flying   from Zurich, you can actually purchase access 
passes for Swiss business lounges as well as their   arrival lounge. And that as a premium economy 
passenger, you can get a little bit of a discount   on those access passes. So, normally the Swiss 
business lounges in Zurich cost 49 Swiss Franks,   but as a premium economy passenger, you can
get it for 39 Swiss Francs, so 10 off. And   then the arrival lounge is normally 69 Swiss 
Francs, but as a premium economy passenger,   you can pick one up for 49 Swiss Francs, so 20 
off. I will also have an upcoming video on Swiss   Senses business class where I will be covering 
those lounges as part of the video so you can see   what the lounges in Zurich look like. I will link 
that video in the description box down below when   it is ready and you can check it out to see if the 
lounges are something that you interested in if   you wanted to get one of those access passes. But 
in the meantime, let's get to boarding because I   am super super excited to check out this new 
Swiss Senses Premium economy on their A350. Today we'll be boarding out of gate 61. And here's   just a quick little look at our 
A350 waiting for us at the gate. As a premium economy passenger,   you do get priority boarding. We'll board in 
group three after first class and business   class passengers. Whereas economy class 
will board in groups four through six. Okay. Now let's board this 
bird so we can talk about this   slightly unconventional premium economy cabin.  Our premium economy cabin today 
has 38 seats arranged in a 2-3-2 configuration.   Now I'm sitting in seat 25A which is next to 
the window on what would normally be the last   row of premium economy. But what's slightly 
unconventional about this particular cabin   is that there are actually two rows of economy 
seats behind the last row of premium economy.   Although the first row of these preferred economy 
seats seem to be blocked off for this particular   flight. There is no bulkhead or curtains 
that separate premium economy from these   two rows of economy. Although you can see here 
that they do have these smaller dividers that   hang from the ceiling. And then behind the 
wall is the remainder of the economy seats. These two row of economy seats that are in the 
same cabin as premium economy are considered   as preferred economy seats and come at 
an additional cost of $74.40 Canadian.   Okay, but let's talk about the premium economy 
seats, which are a hard shell fixed design with   a 39 inch or 99 cm pitch and a width of 19.5 inches or 
49.5 cm. By the way, the preferred economy seats   have the same pitch and width as the standard 
economy seats. They just benefit from quicker   disembarkcation due to being closer to the front 
of the plane. Premium economy seats also have this   privacy divider in between the headrests in case 
you want to avoid awkward eye contact with your   neighbor. There's also a double wide armrest in 
between the seats because again, we don't want   to have to interact with the neighbor if we 
don't have to. Underneath the center armrest,   you'll find wireless charging. And tucked in the 
back, there's also a USB A port. Up in front close   to the floor each person gets their own AC outlet 
as well as a 60W USB C charge port. You'll also get   a calf rest which pops up which is something that 
isn't available in the economy seats. As for the   tray table, it pops down from the seat right 
in front of you first as a half size and then   you can fold it out for a larger size. In terms 
of legroom space, this is what it looks like.   And underneath the seat in front of us, this is 
how much space you'll get to store your personal   items or to stretch your legs. Okay, so now 
let's talk about one of the biggest differences   between economy and premium economy, which is the 
recline. As I mentioned earlier, premium economy   has a fixed hard shell design. So the seats 
don't recline, which is nice because obviously   that means other people can't recline onto you. 
Basically, the cushions slide down like you see   here. And it's the equivalent of around 7 inches or 
17.8 cm. And here's just what the seats sliding   down look like from the top as well. In economy, 
the seats have a traditional recline where the   seat actually recines and it's around 5 inches or 12.7 
cm. Before takeoff, we're offered a welcome drink,   which was this non-alcoholic elderberry drink. 
It's light, slightly tart, but refreshing. And I seem to have lucked out once again because 
there is nobody sitting next to me on this flight. Once we're in the air, the crew gets 
started on service. But first, let's   take a look at the menus. Here's what the menu 
looks like for the main meal, which is dinner,   as well as the pre-arrival meal, which 
is breakfast. And then just on the back   here is the beverage menu, which includes 
both alcoholic and non-alcoholic options. The main meal arrives and I've chosen the seared 
beef tenderloin with a balsamic demi glace. But   first, let's talk about presentation. 
Everything is served on one tray and   the food is served on ceramic plates like you 
see here. In economy, you'll get disposable   food containers. You'll also get metal cutlery 
and premium economy wrapped in a napkin. And   although economy also gets metal cutlery, it 
comes in a paper envelope instead. Something   to note though is that for the second meal, 
the pre-arrival meal, economy gets disposable   cutlery and Premium Economy will continue to 
maintain the metal cutlery for both meals. All right, now back to the food. In terms of 
presentation, the beef tenderloin looked really   good, but it was slightly overcooked, so it was 
a bit tough. Not the worst I've had on a plane,   though. There was a side of potato gratin, and 
these potatoes were very buttery and fluffy.   We also got exactly three spears of asparagus 
that were overcooked, but they had good flavor at   least. There was also a green salad with sun-dried 
tomatoes and feta. And this came with an olive oil   balsamic dressing. There was also two dinner rolls, a 
fruit and cheese plate. And finally, for dessert,   there was this mango cranberry cheesecake. 
This was pretty good. Just the right amount   of creaminess and balance between the tart 
cranberry and the sweetness of the mango. Okay, now that dinner's done, let's take a look 
at the amenity kit. There are actually three   styles of amenity kit available. A plastic 
pouch, a metal tin, and a fabric pouch,   which you can see here. Each of these options 
comes in two different colors. Luckily,   I got the one in the tin. I think it looks much 
nicer than the plastic bag or the fabric one,   personally. Inside the amenity kit, there 
was a pair of earplugs, a pair of red socks,   and a dental kit. You'll also get a small bottle 
of water, but no slippers or anything like that. Okay, it's now time for the lavatory tour. 
Unfortunately, there are no dedicated lavatories   for premium economy passengers, and the closest 
ones are the four that are located at the front of   the economy cabin. In terms of amenities, you'll 
find some soaps, face spray, and lotion from   the brand Soeder in Swiss Airline's signature Alpine 
Valley scent, as well as some surface cleaner. And while the faucet is automatic, the garbage bin   lid unfortunately is not. So you will 
have to push it open with your hands. No foot pedal either, unfortunately. 
There is a full length mirror, though,   although I think I'd rather have an automatic 
garbage bin. All right, let's head back to our   seats now so we can check out the entertainment, 
the pre-arrival meal, as well as talk about cost.   Let's check out the headphones first, which are 
tucked away on the headphone holders in between   the seats. This is what the headphones look 
like. They are noise cancelling, and I found   them to be pretty good. They also had quite a bit 
of cushioning, so they were comfortable to wear. As for the inflight entertainment, you'll get 
a 15.6 inch or 39.6 cm 4K touchscreen display.   There is Bluetooth capability, so you can 
connect your own headphones or use your   device as a remote if you'd like as well. As 
for entertainment, there were over 200 movies,   250 TV shows, and roughly over 100 
or so music playlists, audiobooks,   and podcasts available. For those of you 
addicted to being online, there is Wi-Fi   available. Messaging is complimentary, but 
you'll have to cough up 25 Swiss Francs for   4 hours of full Wi-Fi or 35 Swiss Francs if 
you want the premium Wi-Fi. For me, though,   the best part of the in-flight entertainment 
are these installed cameras. Honestly, drone   users can suck it because who needs a drone when 
you got views like these 35,000 ft in the air? All right, now let's talk about the pillow, 
the blanket, and the comfortability of the   recline. Pillow is slightly smaller 
than your standard sized pillow, but it's   comfortable and that's what matters. As for 
the blanket, it comes in Swiss's signature red,   and it's actually quite nice. I found it 
kept me warm enough during the flight. Now, let's talk about the comfortability of 
the recline. When the seat is fully reclined,   or rather when the cushions are completely 
down and forward and the calf rest is up,   I found it to be decent but not great. It's pretty 
much on par with most premium economy seats in   terms of recline where you're kind of comfortable, 
but something still feels a little bit off. Okay, now before we get to the pre-arrival meal, 
as well as final thoughts on whether or not Swiss   Premium Economy is worth the upgrade, let's talk 
about how much all this cost. Okay, so as always,   let's talk about cost. But before we talk about 
the cost, I always have to put in my little   disclaimer that the prices I'm about to show you 
are just for this specific flight on this specific   day. If you are looking at prices, the prices that 
you might see might be higher or lower than the   prices I'm about to show you, just because that 
is the dynamic nature of pricing when it comes   to flights. All right, so now that my little 
disclaimer is out of the way, let's talk about   cost. The prices I am about to show you are round 
trip in Canadian dollars between Montreal and   Zurich. So, the cost of premium economy was around 
$3,900 Canadian. Economy was $2,411 Canadian. And   for reference, business class was $12,166 
Canadian. And I couldn't fit on the screen,   but first class was around $17,000 Canadian. 
Let me know what you think about those prices. It's now time for the pre-arrival 
meal, and there was only one option   available. It was a continental style 
breakfast with croissant, a bread roll,   a bowl of fruit, peach flavored yogurt, 
and some butter and strawberry jam. All right, as we start to land now in beautiful 
Zurich, let's talk about Swiss Airlines premium   economy and whether or not it's worth the cost 
to upgrade. While I do think their new premium   economy cabin looks great and is modern, 
given the lack of dedicated lavatories,   no lounge access, and overall soft product just 
being marginally better compared to economy,   I think that double the cost is a bit much for 
what they're offering. If the price had maybe   been around 30% more, it might be more 
worth it for me personally. Otherwise,   I'd probably just book those preferred economy 
seats for an extra $75 Canadian as I personally   prefer a more intimate cabin. But let me know what 
you think about Swiss's new premium economy. And   if you've enjoyed the video, please do like and 
subscribe so that we can fly together again soon.

reviews.transcript_full: [music] >> This is Japan Airlines new flagship aircraft featuring an entire brand new cabin experience. And today, I'm finally trying out Japan Airlines new business class on their Airbus A350-1000. [music] Japan Airlines operates from Terminal 3 at Haneda Airport, which handles most of the airport's international flights. For Japan Airlines business class passengers, the check-in area was located in section D. Japan Airlines has almost [music] a full self-service check-in system, even for premium passengers. This means you [music] need to check in at a self-service kiosk, print your boarding pass and luggage tags, and then proceed to the self-bag drop area. The process is quick and efficient, and everything runs smoothly. [music] That said, I personally still prefer a traditional staff check-in experience for business class. After check-in, the staff kindly directed me to the priority [music] security line, which I really appreciated, especially since the standard security queue was quite long. Flying Japan Airlines business class gives you access to several lounge options at Tokyo [music] Haneda Airport. Business class passengers can choose between the Japan Airlines Sakura Lounge, the Sakura Sky View Lounge, >> [music] >> and the Cathay Pacific Lounge, giving you plenty of choice before your flight. The Japan Airlines Sakura Lounge is the airline's main business class lounge at [music] Haneda. However, for this flight, I decided to visit the Sakura Sky View Lounge instead, [music] mainly because the main Sakura Lounge was extremely crowded. The Sakura Sky View Lounge >> [music] >> is essentially an overflow lounge for business class passengers, though the overall experience between the two is very similar. Both lounges offer nearly the same [music] selection of food and drinks. The main Sakura Lounge does have the advantage of shower [music] facilities, while the Sky View Lounge is generally quieter and offers even a better view of the airport. >> [music] >> When you enter the lounge and turn right, you first come into the main dining area. Whereas there's a buffet offering [music] both hot and cold dishes with a mix of Western and Japanese options, including the famous Japan Airlines signature curry. >> [music] >> In addition to the buffet, there's a small ala carte menu [music] available through the lounge app. You simply scan the QR code at the table, place your order, and the food is brought straight [music] to you. There's also good variety of seating here, including individual tables, chair tables, [music] and private booth. From this area, you also get some of the best views in the lounge. Further inside the lounge, it gets noticeably quieter with a more [music] relaxed seating area. There are also a few private phone booth room, as well as the locker room for storing your belongings. Our flight to London was departing from gate 113. As you expect in Japan, boarding started exactly on time. Group one was called first, which includes first class passengers and One World Emerald members. Business class passengers then boarded with group two. >> [music] >> As I stepped on board the A350, [music] you can immediately feel a level of privacy Japan Airlines new business class cabin offers. As I arrived at my seat, I immediately knew this was going to be a great flight. [music] Japan Airlines A350-1000 feature premium heavy business class cabin with a [music] total of 54 seats spread across two cabins in a one-to-one stagger configuration. There's a forward cabin with 20 seats [music] across five rows, and a larger rear cabin with 34 seats across nine rows. If you're traveling as a couple, it is worth noting that this product doesn't offer true couple seating. In the center section, seats are always separated by side table. So, even with the privacy divider lowered, you won't be sitting directly next to each other. The window seats is also staggered, [music] alternating being closer to the aisle or closer to the window. So, as I said, the best option is the true window seats. The one positioned closer to the window and further from the aisle. For this flight, I'm sitting in 3 Alpha, a bulkhead seat in the forward cabin and a true window seat. Japan Airlines use Safran Unity seats on its A350 business 1000 business class, and they're also the launch customer for this seat. Seat is very impressive, and I really like how they maximize the available space. There's also a surprising amount of storage, and the tech on this flight is truly top-notch. In front of the seat, you find a 24-in 4K IFE screen. >> [music] >> Next to it, it is a translucent sliding panel that's open to reveal a wardrobe, complete with a hanger. The design feels very Japanese and slightly inspired by traditional shoji screens. Beneath the wardrobe, there's also a dedicated shoe storage compartment. >> [music] >> I found this to be a real underrated feature and a clever, innovative storage solution that you don't often see on airlines. And underneath the IFE screen, there's a very spacious footwell. I found this to be one of the most spacious footwells [music] out there, and there's even extra space large enough to store a small bag or backpack underneath the footwell, too. >> [music] >> Business class seats are upholstered in airline's signature dark red fabric with leather detailing around the headrest. Speaking of the headrest, it can be adjusted for extra comfort and also feature built-in speakers, allowing for [music] headphone-free audio. The side console has a lot of useful features. Starting from the top, you find a reading light with three different lighting settings. Along with the small [music] enclosed storage compartment that's large enough for a water bottle or headphones. Below that, there's a large service area. The tabletop flips to reveal a shallow enclosed storage space with soft felt padding, perfect for items like your phone or passport. In addition to wireless charging on the counter, there's also a panel with universal [music] power outlet, USB A, and USB C outlets, plus a headphone jack. The IFE screen can be controlled using a remote, but since the screen is touchscreen, there's very little need to use it. Seat controls were just below the side table. They're fairly intuitive and have presets for full flat, lounging, full upright position, as well as lighting controls. There's also a specific button to adjust the headrest, which is useful for watching movies through the headphone-free system. [music] The tray table folds out from the side of the seat in a single large surface. It is sturdy and well-built. It can be quite tricky [music] and it always stows properly when you follow a specific sequence. I also didn't like that it could be pushed forward, so it's worth [music] keeping in mind to use the bathroom before the meals, since it's not easy to get out [music] once the table is in use. The seats also feature a door that extends up to 132 cm in height. [music] It can be easily opened and closed by hand. At 132 cm, the doors aren't quite high as Qatar Airways Qsuites [music] at 143, but they're still very close and well ahead of most other business class products. There's no individual air nozzles on this aircraft, so there's limited control over the temperature at your seat. That said, I found the overall cabin temperature [music] to be comfortable throughout the flight. This newer Airbus A350 comes with dimmable windows, similar to those on the Boeing 787 Dreamliner. However, they react much faster and can go fully blackout. Airbus also used touch-sensitive slider to control them, which feels much more modern and hygienic. Japan Airlines offer an impressive range of amenities in business class on long haul flights. >> [music] >> Waiting at each seat was a pillow and a blanket along with a pair of slippers that even includes a small shoehorn inside. There was also amenity kit, noise canceling headphones, the menu and a drink list for the flight as well as a large bottle of water. Passengers are also offered a set of pajamas to use during the flight. However, these are all the provides on loan. So, they need to be returned before landing and can't be taken home. Toward end of boarding, the crew came around with hot towels followed shortly by pre-departure drinks with a choice of orange juice or champagne. Drinks were served in a solid plastic glass rather than a real glass wear, which was a bit disappointing. Though, I heard this is due to safety regulation from Japanese aviation authorities. >> [music] >> If you like this video, please consider to click the like button and subscribe to our channel. >> [music] >> Your support help the channel grow so we can create even more videos. Thanks for your support. >> [music] [music] >> Around 40 minutes after take off, the crew came around to take meal orders. >> [music] >> Around 10 minutes later, drinks and canapés were served. The canapé consisted [music] of candied walnuts along with breadsticks and then dip. It was slightly a usual combination, though overall, it was just okay. Japan Airlines offers both Japanese [music] and a Western menu and they collaborate with a local chef to decide the dishes. And of course, I went with the Japanese option. The appetizer was served in a beautiful presented [music] bento box featuring a selection of Japanese small dishes. There were broad beans and [music] snap peas with sesame dressing, fried omelette, slow-cooked octopus, a shrimp dumpling with [music] mountain vegetables, scallops with seeweed and tomato, steamed abalone, grilled salmon with bamboo shoot, [music] and a Japanese chicken served with potato puree and soy sauce. I found it quite good, although some people might find traditional Japanese dishes a bit different from what they're [music] used to. My rating, 7 out of 10. Next up was the main course, which included stewed dishes and a selection of traditional Japanese items. The main course features deep-fried mebaro rockfish with grated ginger and asparagus, wagyu simmered in dashi broth [music] with soy sauce, and deep-fried tofu. It was also served with a block of rice wrapped in paper along with pickles and miso soup. [music] For me, the highlight was the curry and wagyu. Both were full of flavor and really tasty. [music] My rating, 10 out of 10. Lastly was dessert, a matcha bavaroise with azuki bean paste and soft [music] mochi. It was a great combination. The matcha and red bean worked really well together and it wasn't overly sweet. >> [music] >> The soft mochi added a nice chewy texture, which made it even better. My rating, >> [music] >> 8 out of 10. Business class passengers have access to three lavatories, all located in the center galley between the two business class cabins. The lavatories were a bit compact but well designed. [music] It featured a fold-down bench and most of the function were touch-free, which felt modern and hygienic. And of course, as you expect on Japanese airline, every lavatory comes equipped with a bidet. I also try out the pajamas and honestly, they felt like a bit like an oversized bath poncho. They may not be the most stylish, but they were comfortable. When converting into bed mode, the seat transforms into a fully flat bed measuring 200 cm in length. I found it to be comfortable wide around both shoulders and feet. Staggered business class seats often struggles from tight footwells, but because I was seated in a bulkhead seats, I had significantly more space. As you can see, the footwell was so large that I almost can't sleep inside it. The mattress cover isn't fitted and tends to slide around a little [music] during the flight, so it doesn't provide much extra padding. I noticed some passenger using mattress pad [music] when leaving the aircraft, so these appear to be available. Unfortunately, I wasn't offered one. And it's something that Japan Airlines could probably advertise a bit better. The amenity kit is provided by Hal Boney and come with a good selection of essentials. Inside, you'll find a toothbrush, hand cream, an eye mask, pocket tissues, and ear plugs. It also include Japan Airlines branded charging cable with both USB-C and lightning connectors. And it even comes with a small phone stand. Japan Airlines A350 business class has 24-in 4K screen. The taking interface are great, though unfortunately, the selection of movies and TV shows isn't huge. But it has a lovely map features >> [music] >> plus a tail camera, which is just about my favorite entertainment on any aircraft. Japan Airlines is one of the first airlines to offer three different ways to listen to the entertainment system. You can use the provided headphones, which I found to be decent, connect your own headphones >> [music] >> via Bluetooth, which was my preferred option, or use the built-in speakers >> [music] >> in the headrest. The speakers actually work surprisingly well. They were loud enough to enjoy movies and music [music] comfortably, yet didn't disturb other passengers around you. Japan Airlines also offer free Wi-Fi [music] in business class with no data caps. The airline usually provides all passengers with free [music] 1-hour Wi-Fi pass, while a 24-hour pass cost around 1880. I received a promotional code by email a few days before the flight, and if you [music] happen to miss that mail, you can also generate the code on board. That said, the process of actually connecting to the free Wi-Fi is surprisingly complicated. [music] It's not as simple as entering your name and the seat number. Instead, there's a pamphlet in your seat pocket that's walk you through the setups, [music] and it includes around 12 steps. On polar routes like this one, I often struggle to get Wi-Fi [music] working properly. This flight was no exception. There was a good selection of snacks and light meals available throughout the [music] flight. I decided to start something simple, so I tried Japan Airlines' original [music] fried chicken and a pork cutlet sandwich, a classic combination you often find at a combini in Japan. One feature that I love was that you don't need [music] to press the flight attendant call button to order food. Instead, you can place your order directly from the IFE screen, which [music] I found very convenient. As I expected, the fried chicken wasn't crispy, but I didn't really expect [music] it to be. It was tasty, and the presentation reminded me a lot ordering a famichiki [music] from FamilyMart. My rating, 9 out of 10. The pork cutlet [music] was quite good, but it was dry for my taste. My rating, 7 out of 10. The second inflight meal followed a dine-on-demand concept for the rest [music] of the flight. I think this is a great idea as it allows you to eat whenever you feel like. I went with the Japanese [music] washoku plate, which is served as a single course. It includes a grilled miso-flavored black cod as the main [music] dish along with a Japanese omelet. The side dish is simmered chicken [music] thigh with vegetables. And it also came with steamed rice and miso soup with white leek. Overall, it was a solid meal, [music] well presented, and nicely balanced, but nothing really stood out for me. My rating, 7/10. With this flight, I can finally cross Japan Airlines A350-1000 business class off my bucket list, and it truly lived up to the expectations. Overall, I would rate this experience among the best [music] in the world. There's a lot to like here. The Saffron Unity seat is spacious, well designed, and offers an impressive amount of storage. The take on board is also excellent. And it all comes together with a very strong soft product including great food and drinks, attentive service, [music] and thoughtful amenities. It is easily one of my favorite business class product, but how does it compare to ANA's room? For me, ANA's room still has the edge in terms of hard product. The seats are more spacious, but it lacks some of the tech >> [music] >> and storage solution that Japan Airlines has. On the soft product side, I also slightly give that advantage to ANA, especially in terms of service consistency. However, Japan Airlines does have one major advantage, the aircraft itself. The A350-1000 is a fantastic platform to fly. It's much quieter than the older aircraft, and the improved cabin pressurization makes the long-haul flight experience noticeably more comfortable. That said, both Japan Airlines and ANA are world-class products and you really can't go wrong with either. The best choice often comes down to price, schedule, and convenience. I flew Japan Airlines A350-1000 first class last year and it still stands out one of the best flight I ever taken. If you want to see what that was like, check out this video. We hope you enjoy watching our video and sharing our flight with Japan Airlines in business class on their A350-1000. Consider to like and subscribe to our channel and we look forward to bringing you more amazing content in the future. Until then, take care and see you next time.

reviews.transcript_full: O jeito mais barato de experimentar uma das melhores classes [música] executivas do mundo e também o mais confortável de viajar entre o Brasil e o Chile. Nesse vídeo [música] nós vamos viajar juntos aqui de Santiago para São Paulo na classe executiva da Turks Sharlines. Vamos lá. Chegou a hora de voltar pro Brasil. Faltam 2 horas meia pra partida do voo e acabei de chegar aqui no aeroporto de Santiago. A fila do chequinho da Turkish tá grande, mas da classe econômica, né? Da classe executiva tá bem mais tranquila. Eu já fiz o chequinho online pelo aplicativo da companhia. Vou viajar só com essa mochila pequena aqui com artigo pessoal. e a mala de mão. Mas mesmo assim eu passei aqui pelo balcão para fazer conferência dos documentos e imprimir um cartão de embarque. Eles colocaram essa identificação aqui na mala de mão e também conferiram um power bank que eu tô levando aqui na mochila pequena. Lembrando que as regras mudaram também mais rígidas. Inclusive eu fiz um vídeo aqui no canal só sobre isso. Se você quiser saber mais detalhes. Eu vou poder levar o meu powerbank no voo, mas não posso usar ele em momento nenhum, né? Muitas companhias aéreas estão proibindo o uso do powerbank aí durante a viagem e ele sempre tem que ficar à vista ali, né? Tipo no bolsão ali da da sua frente ou no item, no artigo pessoal, não pode nem colocar na mala que vai lá em cima do bagageiro, porque tem tido alguns casos de incêndio aí, então é por segurança mesmo. Passageiros da classe executiva da Turkish podem usar a sala Prime Class Pacífico aqui em Santiago, mas eu já adianto que não é uma sala muito grande. captions.text: Today we're flying on a ZIPAIR from Incheon to Narita,
to test the free Starlink Wi-Fi onboard.

reviews.transcript_full: Have you heard of Starlink Wi-Fi? Today we're flying on a ZIPAIR from Incheon to Narita, trying out the Starlink Wi-Fi above the sky. From this B787, to real Starlink speed tests. Let's find out together. Hello! Good morning from Incheon Airport Terminal 1. Today we're flying on ZIPAIR from Incheon to Tokyo Narita. Not 'Jin Air' of Korea, it's 'ZIPAIR' of Japan. ZIPAIR? Why is the name like this? The airline explains the meaning behind the name like this: It's said to come from the word 'zip', which means 'fast', and also means traveling through various zip codes. Pretty thoughtful branding… but to be honest… Many people would just think of a ZIP file at first. At least we'll never forget the name. ZIPAIR is an airline under Japan Airlines (JAL). A low-cost carrier specializing in medium- and long-haul routes. It operates as a separate LCC brand. Think of the relationship between ANA and Peach Aviation, or Singapore Airlines and Scoot. In the 2025 SKYTRAX rankings, ZIPAIR placed 4th among long-haul low-cost carriers. But honestly, the real reason I booked this flight is to test the free Starlink Wi-Fi onboard. It's SpaceX's satellite internet service. By placing small satellites in low Earth orbit, it provides internet access above the clouds. ZIPAIR already offered free Wi-Fi before, but starting May 8th this year, ZIPAIR installed Starlink on their entire fleet. So, let's get this trip started. ZIPAIR uses the K check-in counters. Today's flight is ZG046, departing at 12:55. The check-in counter opens at 09:55.  ZIPAIR doesn't offer self check-in yet, so if you have checked baggage, you'll need to visit the counter in person. I don't have checked luggage today, just one backpack to carry on. I heard ZIPAIR is pretty strict about the 7kg carry-on limit, so I weighed my bag, and it's 5.1kg. No problem. Heading to security now. Right in front of the K counters is a security check lane for Smart Pass users. Since May 28th, SmartPass-only lanes have expanded. In Terminal 1, they're at the west side of Gate 2 and the east side of Gate 5, which is here. In Terminal 2, they're at gates 1D, 2C, and 2D. I already registered for SmartPass, so let's go right away. It was 11:14 when I got on the move, and I'll see how long it'd take to duty-free area. I came through security check and immigration. and it's 11:26. Only 12 minutes! ZIPAIR is basically a low-cost carrier, which means you even need to buy a bottle of water. A bottle of water on board costs 2,500 KRW($1.63). I picked one up beforehand for 1,000 KRW($0.65) instead. Today's boarding gate is 107 at concourse. To get there, you take the shuttle train, which is basically an underground subway. From the center of Terminal 1, head down to the platform level. There's a platform on the left, and one on the right. Since the last train just left from the left platform, the next one should arrive on the right side. Trains alternate every 3.5 minutes between the two platforms. The display shows the countdown to the next train. Here's a small tip. Most people get crowd into the front doors, but instead, take the 3rd door from the back. Because after 3.5 minutes on the train, you'll be much closer to the exit. making for a faster walk to your gate. It will be helpful when you're running out of boarding time. But it still takes some time, so make sure to leave Terminal 1 at least 20 minutes before boarding. We are here, gate 107. ZIPAIR flights are usually assigned near here, between 107 and 113. and here's our ZIPAIR B787-8. ZIPAIR only operates B787-8, with 8 aircraft total. 6 of these were used ones from parent company JAL, while the other 2 are newly leased ones. Today's aircraft is one from JAL, about 14 years old. It's kind of old, but sill has Starlink Wi-Fi. Whereas most LCCs stick to narrow-body aircraft, packed tight with economy seats, this LCC flies a wide-body, which is pretty unusual. That's actually one of ZIPAIR's key differentiators. This aircraft has 290 seats total. From the 18 full-flat premium seats, to the 272 economy seats behind. ZIPAIR plans to introduce longer aircraft, the B787-9s in 2027. It seems like this airline is on a roll. Starlink is installed here. The layout is 3-3-3 with black leather seats. Even though the aircraft is fairly old, it looks like the seats are well-maintained. That's my seat, 50A. Seat pitch is about 31 inches. The passport just barely fit sideways. There's no IFE screen, on this Recaro CL3710 model. We have a USB port and a power outlet here, so you can plug in your charger. The headrest also adjusts up and down,  as well as side to side. We're pushing back now.  The B787's windows don't have physical shades, They're electronically dimmable. The window is set to the brightest setting, there's a noticeable yellow tint somehow. Let me adjust the color a bit. Please understand the tint is SO yellow that it's still a bit off. We are departing from Runway 33L. Let's go to Tokyo. You can dim the window this way. Press the button to adjust through 5 levels. and it gets dark slowly. Let's try connecting to the Starlink Wi-Fi. After joining the network, you scan the QR code in front to get online. There are many options, but let's check out the flight map first. It's powered by FlightPath 3D from Betria Interactive. Look The display quality is great and it's pretty responsive. You can check altitude, speed, distance, and time remaining, plus a 3D view of the aircraft and points of interest. For food, the options are pretty limited. Instant noodles, water, and a few drinks. The photos didn't load properly, which was a bit disappointing. There's also an entertainment section. You can watch a movie with your phone. As an AvGeek, Top Gun is a must. But subtitles were only in Chinese… with no option to change. I'll rather watch YouTube. Is the Wi-Fi speed actually good enough for YouTube? Let me play my video. Hey, zero buffering. Even when scrubbing forward, it handles it without a hitch. If you can watch YouTube like this at 40,000 feet, A long-haul flight would just fly by. Let's run a speed test on this Wi-Fi, whether it's worth the hype or not. I can see it's provided by SpaceX Starlink. (tesing Wi-Fi speed) For download, I got around 41 Mbps, and for upload, 26 Mbps. That's pretty fast enough for most uses! I even made a video call to my wife with zero lag. Let's take a quick look at the seat. The tray table folds in half. Personally, not my favorite design. Wait... what is this? Looks like something the previous passenger left behind… It's a return leg, so I understand, but it wasn't the cleanest. The seat pocket had a safety card, an electronics restriction notice,  and sick bags. That's about it. Here's the lavatory. Since it's a wide-body aircraft, it's quite spacious. There's a baby changing table, and what I thought was a coat hook, is actually an ashtray. Smoking is of course prohibited, yet by regulation, this has to be here. The toilet flush is sensor-activated, You can just wave your hand near it. Today we have 262 passengers out of 290 seats, a load factor of 90.3%. It's been 2 hours after departure, and we're getting ready to land. We'll be landing on Runway 34L at cloudy Narita shortly. Today we flew on ZIPAIR from ICN to NRT with Starlink on board. You know, there are many airlines flying between ICN–NRT, but very few fly a modern wide-body like B787, and ZIPAIR is the only one offering free Starlink Wi-Fi so far. That said, the cheapest option, Air Premia, includes 15kg of free checked baggage, while ZIPAIR charges around 40,000 KRW($26) extra for up to 23kg, So maybe it's worth factoring in baggage costs when comparing prices. The Starlink Wi-Fi was really fast and smooth. Many airlines are also gradually rolling out free Starlink Wi-Fi. Maybe soon, we won't need to tell our friends and family "taking off now, I'll message you when I land" anymore. If this video helped for your trip, a like and subscribe would be greatly appreciated. See you in the next video!

But today, I'm in economy, hosting 18.5 inches of seat width, one of the widest economy  seats owing to the sheer size of this aircraft.  Today's route is Singapore to Sydney on SQ-231, a red-eyed parting Singapore just passed  midnight with a total flight time of 7.5 hours.  Let's see what the A380 on Singapore Airlines actually feels like in the back of the bus.  Singapore Airlines operates out of Terminal 3 at Changi Airport.  In the world's best airport, 14 times by Skytrikes.  Checking counters are at Rho 3 and 4, with plenty of self-service kiosk if you want them.  I went to the desk as I wanted an actual boarding pass, not a floppy piece of paper from a  kiosk.  The entire process took about 10 minutes with the queue and if you're short on time,  the kiosk with automated backdrop make it even faster.  Not long after, I was ASI.  The transit area at Changi is its own thing entirely.  Food and beverage, luxury duty-free, liquor, versalaction is immense.  There are well-designed seating spaces everywhere you look from proper lounging areas to productivity  setups to dining.  It was passed 11pm and I wasn't feeling particularly hungry, so I found a quiet corner and said,  I love this airport.  It's the only one in the world where you genuinely don't feel like lounge access is necessary.  Today's departure gate is B7, roughly a 5-minute walk from the immigration area in Terminal  3.  If there's one thing that consistently gets brought up as a friction point at Changi,  it's the security screening that happens at the gate itself.  I got through security almost immediately only to be greeted by a packed seating area.  Fun fact, the aircraft taking me to Sydney tonight is on its first commercial flights of  the coming out of months of maintenance in Spain.  During an A380, an economy is a serious waiting game and the numbers explain why.  Business class alone is 78 passengers.  By the time you work through sweets, business, premium economy and however many economy zones  they have carved out, it makes you acutely aware of how far down the food chain you are.  The line moves slowly and I eventually made my way to 66h.  I selected this seat right before checking after spotting what looked like an empty row  on the seat map as it turns out the whole row was mine.  Having a whole row to yourself on a packed red-eye flight is like winning the lottery.  People call it the poor man's business class but I prefer the term make shift business  class.  After what seemed like a long-browling process I finally settled in and the first thing  waiting for me was the signature hot towel.  After 30 minutes of shuffling down an aisle with a couple hundred people, it's a huge  stress reliever.  The seat itself 32 inches of pitch and 18.5 inches of width.  Above average for economy and noticeably so at 178cm tall I had enough leg room.  The in-flight entertainment screen is 11 inches with an adjustable angle to touch response  is decent not laggy.  Load screen on the left you get a USB-A charging point, reading light controls, call button  and a two pin headphone jack.  On the subject of the provided headphones it's not the best.  If you can bring a blue-tooth transmitter that plugs into the two pin jack and pair it  straight to your airport.  The sound quality difference is significant and on a long flight it's worth it.  The new tray table has a vanity mirror built in, it's an odd placement but it's there  if you need it on the right there's a cup holder.  Useful between new service when you want somewhere to put a drink, standard blanket and  pillow provided, worth noting for window seat sleepers.  The A380 is so wide that the wall is too far to lean against.  Chris World is extremely well stocked.  Singapore Airlines updates their library regularly with the latest blockbusters.  You'd be hard pressed to fault it.  We push back slightly late.  The flight was intentionally delayed to allow some connecting passengers to make it.  Our estimate economy was around 85% full and we taxied out to it, run way zero to center  and took off into the moonlit skies.  Shortly after takeoff, refreshment service comments.  Two options were offered, mozzarella, mushroom pizza bar and margarita pizza bar, along with  coffee or tea, beer, soft drinks, wine and cocktails were available too.  I went with the margarita pizza bar and it delivered cheesy, good umami and the bread texture  was decent.  It's a great late night snack, just don't expect the quality of a naveli pizza.  After the crew made their rounds to clear the rubbish, I got comfortable in my makeshift  business class seat.  It was amazing.  And I wholeheartedly endorsed gaming the system to snack a whole row for free on empty flights.  Keep checking up to when checking closes.  Singapore Airlines offers complimentary wifi to every economy passenger, but only if you  tag your ticket to your Chris Flyer account during checking.  Speeds are solid for general browsing but don't expect to stream 4k videos on your phone.  On this front, airlines like Carter with Scarling have an edge.  Singapore Airlines is planning to upgrade their fleet with Starlink from 2027.  So this is only going to get better.  After the best economy sleep I've had, breakfast came around.  I went with the scrambled eggs with cheese and chicken sausage, accompanied by a fruit  platter, strawberry yogurt and a bread roll with butter.  Full beverage service was available with hot and cold options.  There are usually three options for mains on flight to Australia.  Western, Indian and an East Asian or Singaporean option.  The metal cutlery is a nice touch and its genius marketing on their part.  Research shows that the tactile experience of handling heavier items triggers a higher  perceived value.  For an economy meal, it was solid.  If they had offered the Singaporean fried carrot cake, I would have gone for that.  As new service wrapped up, we were fast approaching Sydney.  The crew prepped the cabin for landing and soon we were on approach.  Follow me on Singapore Airlines is one of the best in the industry.  It's not easy to differentiate an economy class, but there are some standout features  such as the hot towel service and above all, the crew.  I've flown an economy class on other five star carriers and while the hard product  is often comparable, the crew experience ends to fall short.  On Singapore Airlines, the crew is the difference maker.  It's what the brand has been built on and it's what keeps me coming back.  As I've mentioned in previous videos, the crew have the ability to straddle both eastern  formality and western casualness in a way that's unique to places like Singapore.  Beyond the product itself, what Singapore Airlines is really selling is trust.  You're buying the confidence that you'll be taken care of.  That if something goes wrong, it gets resolved quickly and competently.  That's why I would gladly pay a premium for Singapore Airlines economy.  If you would like to check out my return flight to Singapore in business class, that video  is up right now.  Drop a like and subscribe if this was off-value to you and I'll see you in the next one.

reviews.transcript_full: This wasn't just another Emirates Airbus A380 flight. It was my first flight from Dubai since the Middle East conflict. Today, I'm flying Emirates unique fifth freedom route from Dubai to Hong Kong via Bangkok, staying on board for both sectors to experience the entire journey from start to finish. The journey begins at Emirates dedicated first class check-in area in terminal 3. Separate from the main departure hall, it offers private check-in counters and a much more exclusive start to the journey. After check-in, it's through security before making my way to the Emirates first class lounge, one of the largest airline lounges in the world. There's plenty of seating, several dining areas, and a wide selection of food available throughout the day. Rather than feeling like a waiting area, it feels more like a premium hotel lounge where you can comfortably spend a few hours before boarding. >> Soon, it's time to board today's flight, an Emirates Airbus A380 operating the airline's unique fifth freedom route from Dubai to Hong Kong via Bangkok. Walking into the Airbus A380 first class cabin is always impressive. Even years after it entered service, it still feels spacious and elegant. I'll be staying on board for both sectors, giving us a chance to experience the complete journey from start to finish. Let's take a quick look around. The enclosed suites, warm wood finishes, and soft lighting create an atmosphere that's very different from most modern first class cabins. The suite offers plenty of personal space, intuitive controls, and useful storage. While just a few steps away is one of the aircraft's most iconic features, the onboard shower spa. It's something only the Airbus A380 can offer. And it remains one of the biggest reasons this aircraft continues to stand out. Once we're safely in the air, it's time to visit another signature feature of the Emirates Airbus A380, the onboard bar. Located at the rear of the upper deck, it completely changes the atmosphere of a long haul flight. On a flight of this length, that flexibility makes a noticeable difference. Back at my suite, the first meal begins with Emirates famous caviar service. Presentation has always been one of the airline's strengths, with every course arriving individually plated and carefully prepared. Instead, it's the combination of the suite, the shower, the bar, and the service that creates a complete first-class journey. A little later, it's finally time for the shower spa. Taking a shower at nearly 40,000 ft is still one of the most unique experiences in commercial aviation. And stepping back into your suite afterwards genuinely makes you feel refreshed before settling in for some rest. Making it easy to get several hours of proper sleep before the next sector. We arrive in Bangkok where transit passengers remain on board for around 90 minutes while the aircraft is prepared for the next flight. Giving you a chance to watch the cabin transition between two different flights without ever leaving your seat. Before long, we're pushing back once again, this time heading for Hong Kong. Pushback is right on schedule, and as the four engine Alliance engines power us down the runway, the takeoff feels smooth and incredibly refined, while cabin noise stays impressively low despite the aircraft's enormous size. The Airbus A380 reminds you why it's still loved by aviation enthusiasts. For the second meal, I decide to try the Arabic mezze, a classic Emirates option that always feels like the right choice when departing Dubai. Shortly afterwards, lunch is served, continuing the same relaxed service style that has been consistent throughout the journey. As we begin our descent into Hong Kong, it's clear why the Emirates Airbus A380 remains one of the airline's flagship experiences. Even after flying both sectors, the journey never feels repetitive because every part of the aircraft offers something different. Flying my first journey from Dubai since the Middle East conflict made this experience even more memorable. For anyone who enjoys aviation as much as luxury travel, this is still one of the most complete premium experiences you can have anywhere in the world.

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Saigon's Tan Son Nhat Airport, or as they say in Vietnamese... Mời mọi người đến Sân Bay Tân Sơn Nhất với Freddie I'm about to take a 2 hour flight from Saigon to Hanoi with Vietnam Airlines in their AIrbus A350 Premium Economy an exciting trip for 2 reasons: Firstly because this is the world's fourth busiest flight route with over 11 million passengers a year and about 70 flights a day flying between the two cities and secondly, because despite being a relatively short domestic route, Vietnam Airlines use their long haul Airbus A350s and Boeing 787s with lie-flat Business Class and Premium Economy on this route so you just need to check the aircraft type when booking, and you can get a very premium experience Also, Vietnam Airlines now use Terminal 3 at Tan Son Nhat Airport for domestic flights It just opened last year and is about a thousand times better than the old domestic terminal as you can see, it's nice and bright and open but this terminal is only used for domestic flights so there's not really much to do past security Now, if you're flying between Saigon and Hanoi then you actually have quite a few choices Vietnam Airlines of course, or Vietjet Air, the country's largest budget airline Then some smaller airlines like Bamboo Airways, Viettravel and Sun Phu Quoc In fact, just look at the ridiculous number of flights available to book in a single day... But my one word of advice as someone who's flown within Vietnam quite a few times, just choose Vietnam Airlines The hassle and delays you might experience with the likes of Vietjet is just not worth saving like $10 Of course Vietnam Airlines get delays too, but at least they'll take care of you Anywho, here's our plane for today, a 9.5 year old Airbus A350-900 painted with what I think is one of the best liveries of any airline... Since we were flying in Premium Economy today we boarded in group 2 out of 3 and it was pretty smooth, no staff checking bag weight or dimensions or anything like you would get on Vietjet Now before we step on board here are the stats and route map for today's flight departing 25 min late and arriving 15 min late, so pretty standard really and after probably 6 or 7 flights on Vietnamese airlines I don't think a single one has been on time So no surprises there Also here's the seat map for this aircraft we're flying today, and I should note This was a group booking for 5 people and I pre-booked these seats circled here but with no explanation they changed us to these seats at the back during check-in so that was annoying, and worst of all it meant I no longer had a window to film out of So I had to go to the gate desk and ask if there were any free windows and eventually got assigned 14A, which you'll see in a moment but first, friendly reminder to like and subscribe if you're enjoying the video so far! and here's my seat at the back of this 36 seat Premium Economy Cabin and you still get good recline despite it being next to a bulkhead The seat is spacious with 38" of seat pitch and has an extra wide middle armrest  and I've found that basically all Vietnam Airlines cabins look pretty dated with the drab colour heavy cushioning and lotus flowers embroidered on the fabric But honestly because the cushions are so thick and plush it makes their seats some of the comfiest of any airline I've flown also a little coat hook but disappointingly, the casing for both armrests seem to have fallen off and they shoddily repaired with duct tape here it was fine for me but unfortunately for my seatmate it made it so his table was pretty much impossible to get out so he ended up eating later in the flight with his tray on his lap There was a very good view of the engine out the window though and of course, a nice plush adjustable headrest You get a little foot rest too, though I've always found these to be pretty impractical to use also cleanliness is just adequate I guess but I do like the Lotus flower pattern on the seat, a nice touch as it's the national flower of Vietnam and also on the logo of Vietnam Airlines They hand a wet wipe out to everyone after boarding is complete and lastly, you get decent over-ear headphones with new ear covers handed out separately slightly annoying to install but good for hygiene at least Before we push back some fun adverts start, this one randomly for a company that makes industrial steel for the construction industry ,and they clearly have a large marketing budget Then as we push back the actual safety video started playing and it's quite entertaining, so here's that and some scenic views as we taxi to the runway... Surprisingly to me at least they do actually give you a meal in Premium Economy, A step up from Economy where it's just water and a snack Here it's a basic but tasty bánh mì, the best sandwich in the world plus some fresh fruit and a yoghurt drink You can also preorder bubble tea and pizza (which I did as I thought we wouldn't get fed) and it's surpsrisingly good value for aircraft food at something like 50k dong for a big bubble tea and 100k for half a pizza and this is the pizza in question, made by Pizza 4Ps, a popular high end pizza chain in Vietnam probably the best pizza I've ever had on a plane, but may that isn't saying much   considering how sad and soggy most airplane pizzas tend to be incidentally, sad and soggy is how I felt when walking for more than 5 minutes outside in  in the 35 degree heat of Vietnam, the bubble tea is good too And finally, a quick tour of the IFE system and if you've noticed I've magically changed to a different seat in Economy,  it's because I filmed this on a later flight, but everything is exactly the same and mainly the movie selection is surprisingly extensive better than many airlines in this region and they have all the standard tv, music and games available too The moving map is very detailed too, but the touch screen just feels a bit laggy There's also these little info cards about every airline in their fleet and some surprisingly good Vietnamese movies, so give them a go if you end up flying Vietnam Airlines some of the movies did have this annoying watermark though, but weirdly not all of them Also fun observation, this infamous sea is labelled as the East Sea, or Biển Đông if you know you know Very last of all, there is WiFi onboard, but the free plan is only 15 minutes But at 5 USD for messaging throughout the flight or 8 USD for full speed (basically half the flight) It is at least priced quite fairly Now on Vietnam Airlines you know it's almost time to land when the adverts start playing... and here we're treated to a standard chilli sauce ad, then slightly more weirdly an ad for another industrial steel company I do feel it slightly cheapens the experience when they play so many ads throughout the flight and definitely shows Vietnam Airlines isn't quite in the realm of premium airlines Like you wouldn't see Qatar Airways or Singapore Airlines advertising some fast food or something... Anyway, the sunset view coming in to land was fantastic so here is that to enjoy instead... So here we are arriving in Hanoi just a few minutes late which meant we got to enjoy a lovely sunset landing They love a bus gate at Hanoi Airport, but a benefit of being in a larger aircraft is that they  reserve jet bridges for them, saving a few minutes on disembarking Domestic arrivals here are pretty smooth so that's it for today's flight... Now on to my final review: and I'll give Vietnam Airlines a pretty solid 75% on this flight today the only thing I can really fault them on is the slightly shoddy condition of the seat and fact they changed our seat selection last minute, but everything else was great and  Premium Economy is something I think is well worth paying for on this route On my airline tierlist they keep their 7/10 rating, the same rank as British Airways Which I think is fair as they're both distinctly average airlines with occasional flairs of brilliance Now if you want something else to watch you can check out my review of Vietnam Airlines long haul Economy Class in their Boeing 787 from Hanoi to London This flight was kind of disappointing, and reinforces my average rating for Vietnam Airlines overall but they do have a few quirks that keep them interesting so thanks a lot for watching be sure to like and subscribe if you enjoyed, and maybe leave a comment too and lastly good bye!

reviews.transcript_full:
It’s not everyday that you get the chance to 
fly with a new airline - especially one that’s   consistently regarded as one of the best in 
the world. So, when I had the opportunity   to fly with All Nippon Airways on a domestic 
flight across Japan, I simply couldn’t pass   it up. Join me as we find out whether ANA 
really lives up to its stellar reputation. Hello and welcome to IH Aviation and Travel! I’m 
Ishan, and I share reviews of flights and hotels,   along with city guides, so you know 
exactly what to expect on your next trip. Today, we will be flying on All Nippon Airways, 
one of Japan’s two major full-service airlines,   from Osaka Itami Airport (ITM), which 
is the city centre airport in Osaka,   to Sapporo’s New Chitose Airport (CTS), the 
main gateway to Hokkaido in northern Japan. Both All Nippon Airways and its 
regional partner IBEX Airlines   operate from the South Terminal here at 
Osaka Itami Airport. The airline offers   both self-service check-in counters 
and traditional check-in counters. One thing I noticed was how thoughtfully 
designed even the weighing scales are. They   are almost at the floor height, so you don’t have 
to lift your heavy bags onto a raised platform.   It’s a small detail, but one that 
reflects the attention to practicality   and user experience that Japan is known for.
 While we take a look around the airport and   make our way to the gate, let me share 
a brief history of All Nippon Airways. All Nippon Airways, widely known as ANA, 
was founded on 27th December 1952 as Japan   Helicopter and Aeroplane Transports Company. 
Interestingly, the airline’s IATA code, NH,   originates from its original name, Nippon 
Helicopter. The airline launched helicopter   services in February 1953, before 
expanding into cargo operations,   with its first cargo flight operating 
between Osaka and Tokyo using a de   Havilland Dove aircraft. Passenger services 
on the same route began on 1st Febraury 1954. As the airline expanded across Japan, 
it was renamed All Nippon Airways   Company in December 1957. Just a 
few months later, in March 1958,   it merged with Far East Airlines, creating 
Japan’s largest private airline at the time. ANA continued to grow through the 1960s, 
merging with Fujita Airlines in 1963 and   introducing its first jet aircraft, 
the Boeing 727 trijet, in 1965. For many years, the government-owned Japan 
Airlines had a monopoly on scheduled international   flights. During this period, ANA was allowed 
to operate some international charter flights,   the first of which was from 
Tokyo to Hong Kong in 1971. That changed in 1986 when Japan Airlines’ 
monopoly on international flights came to   an end. ANA immediately launched scheduled 
international services to Guam on 3rd March,   followed by Los Angeles and 
Washington D.C. later that year.   This was followed by the addition of Beijing, 
Dalian, Hong Kong and Sydney in 1987,   Seoul in 1988, London and Saipan in 1989, Paris 
in 1990 and New York and Singapore in 1991. A major milestone came in 1999, when ANA joined 
the Star Alliance. Today, as of June 2026, ANA   operates a fleet of 244 aircraft, with 106 more on 
order, serving around 95 destinations worldwide. Here is our aircraft for today’s flight, a 
Boeing 787-9 registered Juliet Alpha - 936   Alpha, delivered brand-new to All Nippon 
Airways in October 2021. The aircraft is   configured for domestic operations, 
featuring 28 Premium Class seats in   a 2-2-2 configuration and 347 Economy 
Class seats arranged in a 3-3-3 layout. Can we just take a moment to appreciate 
how efficiently ANA handles the boarding   process? Our scheduled departure time 
was 1:55 PM. Boarding began at 1:30 PM,   and by 1:54 PM, the aircraft had already 
pushed back from the gate. That’s just 24   minutes to board a Boeing 787 and be ready 
for departure. It’s genuinely impressive. Another interesting thing is how ANA carries 
out the boarding process. Rather than calling   passengers by row numbers, boarding is 
done according to seat position. Window   seat passengers board first, followed by those in 
middle seats, and finally those in aisle seats. It keeps passengers from constantly 
getting up to let others into the   row, making the entire boarding process 
noticeably smoother and more efficient.   It’s such a simple idea, and I’m genuinely 
surprised why more airlines haven’t adopted it. 32A will be my home for the next hour and a half. Let’s take a closer look at the seat. 
In the front, there’s a crisp 13.3-inch   4K inflight entertainment screen, 
along with a standard tray table.   The legroom is excellent for a domestic flight, 
with ANA marketing a seat pitch of 31 inches.   Unfortunately, individual airvents are not 
available, but every seat comes equipped   with a USB-A port and universal power outlets. 
Inflight Wi-Fi by Panasonic is also available. The inflight entertainment system 
offers a good selection of movies,   tv shows and music, along with a 
dedicated section for children. The inflight map by Panasonic is really 
great, with multiple viewing modes,   such as cockpit view, right and 
left window views and many more. On domestic flights, ANA offers complimentary 
beverages. The options on this flight included   Mineral Water, Cola, Apple Juice, Hot Coffee, Beef 
Consomme and both Hot and Cold Japanese Green Tea. Service throughout the flight was fantastic. 
Although my interactions with the crew were   limited, they were consistently 
warm, courteous and welcoming. Overall, this was a fantastic flight. 
It departed and arrived on-time,   the aircraft was spotlessly clean, the 
inflight entertainment system was excellent,   the beverage service was perfectly adequate for 
a domestic flight, and the crew were outstanding. It was my first time flying with ANA, and after 
this experience, I can certainly understand why   the airline enjoys such a strong reputation. I’m 
already looking forward to trying one of their   international flights to see whether they deliver 
the same level of excellence on a longer journey. I hope you enjoyed this flight review 
today. If you did, please make sure to   like the video and subscribe to my channel for 
a new flight or hotel review every alternate   Saturday. I will see you next time for a hotel 
review.  If you have liked this video so far,   I would be grateful if you like, comment and 
subscribe to my channel. For those of you who   want a perfectly crafted itinerary, designed and 
personalized specifically for your next holiday,   I can actually build it for you. Alongside 
this channel, I run a custom travel advisory   company called Ishara Journeys. We take the 
guesswork out of every trip, tailoring every   single detail to your specific preferences, and 
I can manage the bookings as well. To know more   and get started on your trip planning, scan 
the QR code or visit www.isharajourneys.com.

reviews.transcript_full: सो इस टाइम बहुत से लोग परेशान हो रहे हैं जिन्होंने इंडिया से कनाडा या कनाडा से इंडिया फ्लाई करना है। सो भाई इस बार हमने ईटा में ट्रैवल किया है। ये एक इटालियन एयरलाइंस हैं। तो रोम में अपना लेओवर था 2 घंटे का। तो चलिए इस फ्लाइट का आपको एक्सपीरियंस बताता हूं कि क्या ये फ्लाइट इस टाइम स्पेशली दिल्ली ट्रंटो के रूट पे वन ऑफ द बेस्ट ऑप्शन है या नहीं। अब जैसे ही घर वालों को सी ऑफ करके बैगेज ड्रॉप ऑफ के लिए अंदर घुसा, तो हम सबको पता है सबसे बड़ा डर यही लगता है कि यार लाइन में कहीं 40-50 मिनट घंटा खड़ा ना होना पड़ जाए। बैगेज ड्रॉप ऑफ में तो टाइम लगा ही नहीं। 510 मिनट में ही फ्री हो गए। सो अभी तक का एक्सपीरियंस जो है सो फार सो गुड। इमीग्रेशन और सिक्योरिटी का भी सीन अलग ही चल रहा था भाई। 5 मिनट्स फॉर ड्रॉप ऑफ एंड 5 मिनट्स फॉर सिक्योरिटी। रात की फ्लाइट का यह फायदा है। बिल्कुल ही सन्नाटा बंदा ना बंदे की जात। उसके बाद भाई ड्यूटी फ्री में घूमता रहा। सिर्फ घूमता ही रहा। शॉपिंग-वपिंग कुछ नहीं करी और फाइनल कॉल का वेट किया कि लाइन में नहीं लगना भाई बोर्डिंग के लिए। दिस इज द लास्ट एंड फाइनल कॉल फॉर ऑल द रिमेनिंग ईटा एयर। तो इस प्लेन के बारे में ऑनलाइन रिव्यूज तो बहुत अच्छे पड़े थे कि ब्रांड न्यू प्लेेंस है ये एयर बस के। तो चलो अंदर चल के देखते हैं कि रिव्यूज आर रियल ऑर नॉट। यार सच में प्लेन तो बड़ा साफ-सुथरा निकला और फर्स्ट इंपैशंस भी बड़े खतरनाक थे। बट एक बार प्लेन को पहले टेक ऑफ करवा [संगीत] देते हैं। फिर करते हैं आगे बात। सो इस तरीके से भाई इंडिया से उड़ चले हैं परदेश की तरफ। बट नाउ आई वुड से कि भाई इंडिया सेकंड ओम लगता है और परदेश फर्स्ट ओम। यार फ्लाइट में पता ही नहीं चला कब सनराइज हो गया। देखो कितना खतरनाक व्यू आ रहा है और ऊपर सूरज भी दिख रहा है। सूरज ही लग रहा है ना? भाई साहब आप मानोगे नहीं। यह सूरज नहीं यह चंद्रमा है। यह देखो 17 Pro Max का कैमरा। मैंने एक्सपोज़र वगैरह सेट करके ज़ूम करके कि यह भाई चंद्रमा है, सूरज नहीं है। भाई साहब, क्या कैमरा है, यार। यूरोप की धरती के ऊपर हमने पहुंच चुके हैं। और बात करते हैं अब अंदर के सिंग एक्सपीरियंस की। ऑलमोस्ट सभी पैसेंजर्स की स्क्रीन्स वर्क कर रही थी। USB के भी दोनों ऑप्शन थे। आप नई वाली केबल लगा के भी अपना iPhone चार्ज कर सकते हो। और यार स्क्रीन की क्वालिटी ऐसे लग रहा है iPपैड चला रहा हूं सच में। इस तरीके का एक्सपीरियंस सिर्फ एमिरेट्स में या फिर ऐतिहाद में ही आया अभी तक। वरना एयर इंडिया की स्क्रीन तो भाई आधे टाइम चल ही नहीं रही होती थी और उंगलियां मार-मार के उसको चलाना पड़ता था। और अगर आपके पास पैसे थोड़े ज्यादा हो तो आप प्लेन में भी वाई-फाई पैकेज लेके इंटरनेट चला सकते हो। एंड जितने भी लेटेस्ट मूवीज हैं या टीवी शोज़ हैं उनके भी अच्छे खासे ऑप्शन दे रखे थे। गेम्स की भी कोई कमी नहीं थी। जितने भी पेरेंट्स थे ना जिनके बच्चे परेशान करते थे सबको उन्होंने गेम्स पे लगा रखा था प्लेन में। वाओ वाओ वाओ क्या बात है। इटली के पहाड़ तो बड़े खतरनाक लग रहे हैं। देखते हैं अब ले ओवर का एक्सपीरियंस कैसा रहता है। लैंडिंग की तैयारी चल रही थी। इटली में ना एग्रीकल्चर का बड़ा सुना था। तो ऊपर से देख के समझ आ गया अच्छे से कि भाई फार्मिंग वाला सीन ना यहां पे है खतरनाक। [संगीत] भाई फ्लाइट लैंड हो गई। एंड आई वुड से बहुत ही स्मूथ लैंडिंग थी इनकी। पीछे देखो सभी स्क्रीन्स चल रही है ना और प्लेन भी बड़ा नीट एंड क्लीन था यार। [संगीत] भाई साहब व्यू देखो यार ले ओवर के टाइम पे हम बाहर नहीं जा पाते तो मेरे को बड़ा अच्छा लगा कि इन्होंने रोड पे ही उतार दिया। तो फाइनली मैं कह सकता हूं कि रोम की हवा खा के आया हूं और पीछे प्लेन देखो भाई आसपास खड़े थे। बड़ा सही व्यू आ रहा था। यार सही है। पूरा एयरपोर्ट देखने को मिल रहा है। है ना? और ये खड़ा है कोलंबिया का प्लेन। क्या बात है। इस एयरलाइन की लैंडिंग बड़ी फेमस है। ऑफिशियली वेलकम टू रोम। चलो अब टाइम है। थोड़ा हाथ पैर खोलता हूं। फिर अपडेट देता हूं आपको। ट्रेन ने सीधा रनवे पे ही उतार दिया था। बस में लेके आए थे अंदर। और अंदर आने के बाद भी नेक्स्ट फ्लाइट का भी इन्होंने फ्लाइट उड़ने से 1 घंटे पहले बताया कि कौन से गेट पे जाना है। गेट पे जाके भी देखते हैं कि सीधा प्लेन डॉक हुआ है या फिर से बस में लेके जाएंगे। [संगीत] पिछला प्लेन भी साफ सुथरा था और यह भी एग्जैक्टली सेम मॉडल का प्लेन है। तो देखते हैं अंदर से भाई कोई सरप्राइजेस मिलते हैं या वैसा ही मस्त होने वाला है। [संगीत] फिर से उड़ चला। [संगीत] तो इस बार हम यूरोप के पहाड़ों को क्रॉस करके आगे निकलने वाले हैं। एमिरेट्स एतियाद की बराबरी ना हो सकती। ये [संगीत] देखो प्लास्टिक के स्पूनस मेरे को बहुत एलर्जी है इससे और खाना भी बड़ा ना काम चलाऊ सा ही था। इन्होंने जो इयरफोंस दिए थे उसकी शेप देख के मैं खुश हो गया था कि एप्पल जैसे हैं। फिट मस्त होंगे। बट साउंड क्वालिटी ऑलमोस्ट जीरो थी। यार हमारा प्लेन जो है ना 12 कि.मी. ऊपर चला गया था। क्या ये यूजुअल है क्या? वैसे जितना मैंने सुना है 33,000 फीट तक रहता है प्लेन है ना? तो ये 400 तक पहुंचा रखा था इन्होंने। सो फाइनली हम कनाडा पहुंच चुके हैं। बट लास्ट में थोड़ा सा काम खराब हो गया। तो 400 फीट से जब यह प्लेन नीचे आ रहा था, इस बार नीचे आते टाइम ना यह बहुत ज्यादा हिल रहा था, जर्की हो रहा था। एंड ऑलमोस्ट तीन बार मेरी वोमिटिंग होती [संगीत] बची और बची हुई कसर निकाल दी। फिर से इन्होंने रोड पे उतार के बस में लेके गए। भाई अब सोचो जिस बंदे को घबराहट हो रही है वो सोच रहा था मैं फाइनली जाके आराम से बैठूंगा। तब फिर बस में झटके देते देते लेके गए। बस यह प्लेेंस वगैरह को देख के मैं खुश हुए जा रहा था जिससे कि थोड़ा मूड मेरा सही हुआ। एयर कनाडा के प्लेेंस की ना यह यूनिक चीज है। देखो ब्लैक होती है इनकी विंड [संगीत] शील्ड। और उसके बाद एक चीज और खतरनाक दिख गई। ये क्या कारगो प्लेन था डबल डेकर A380 इस तरीके से अपने पहुंच गए एयरपोर्ट के बाहर और Uber करवाई अपनों ने इलेक्ट्रिक एनवायरमेंट बचाने के लिए नहीं सेम प्राइस पे हो रही थी इसलिए सो इस तरीके से पहुंच गए भाई अपने घर पे हालत आपको दिख ही रही होगी थकावट बहुत ज्यादा हो रखी है और जेट लैग से अभी तीन-चार दिन खराब भी होने वाले हैं आपको पता है तो कंक्लूजन पे बढ़ते हैं मेरे को पता है प्राइस भी सोच रहे होंगे कि आप यह टिकट करवाई कितने में मैंने तो लगभग $990 की पड़ी थी यह मेरे को कनेडियन लगभग ₹70,000 की। इस टाइम आप सबको पता है कि टिकट्स बहुत ज्यादा महंगी हो रखी है। सो आई थिंक ओवरऑल अगर आप बात करोगे वो घबराहट जो हुई थी उस इंसिडेंट को छोड़ दें और दूसरा आने वाले इंसिडेंट को छोड़ दें। उसके अलावा अगर अपने सोचे ₹70,000 में सिर्फ 2 घंटे के लेओवर के साथ पहली फ्लाइट जो थी वो 8 घंटे की थी। दूसरी फ्लाइट जो थी वो 9:30 घंटे की थी। तो अपने लगभग 20.5 घंटे में ट्रंटो पहुंच गए। सो आई थिंक इट वाज़ टोटली वर्थ इट। बट इसके अलावा एक और ऑप्शन है पॉलिश एयरलाइंस का एलओटी का वो इससे भी जल्दी पहुंचवा रही थी यूरोप ले ओवर में। सो वो भी फ्लाइट अगर आपको सही रेट में मिल रही हो तो वर्दिट हो सकती है। बट इसके अलावा जितनी भी फ्लाइट्स मैं देख रहा था सबका टाइम 23 घंटे या 24 घंटे से ज्यादा का ही था क्योंकि लेओवर बड़ा था उनका। सो अब आपके क्या थॉट्स हैं? आप कौन सी एयरलाइन में फ्लाई करने वाले हो या कितने में आपकी टिकट हुई है? आप भी अपना एक्सपीरियंस कमेंट सेक्शन में बता सकते हो। तो बाकी भी कनाडा वापस आ चुके हैं। बहुत सारा कंटेंट ऑन द वे है। मिलते हैं अपने नेक्स्ट वीडियो में। तब तक के लिए गुड बाय एंड टेक केयर।
