reviews.transcript_full: What's EVA Air's long haul economy actually like? After recently flying their excellent premium economy to Taipei, let's take a look at their standard economy. >> [music] >> Hello and welcome back to K S Aviation. Today, we're at Taipei Taoyuan International Airport getting ready to fly home on board EVA Air's flagship Boeing 777-300ER in economy class. We've got a long flight ahead of us, so let's get checked in. Here at TPE, [music] EVA Air exclusively uses Terminal 2. The airline has plenty of check-in counters, and [music] since they open around 2 and 1/2 hours before departure, there weren't any major lines. The entire process was quick, efficient, and friendly. After a quick security check, we are now airside. There's still nearly 2 hours until boarding, so I spent some time exploring TPE's brand new Terminal 3 North Concourse. After a bit of exploring, I made my way over to gate C6 where BR8 was boarding. A quick look at our aircraft for today, Bravo 16716, and it was finally time to head on board. >> Bye-bye. 66 >> If you'd like to see what EVA Air's business class is like, be sure to check out this video. And if you're interested in their premium economy, I've got a review on that as well. But for today, let's check out their economy. Welcome to seat 46 Kilo, a window seat located in the second row of EVA Air's economy cabin. EVA Air's 777 has three configurations. While the premium cabins remain mostly the same across all aircraft, economy varies. Newer 777s feature a 3-4-3 layout, while older aircraft like today's have a more spacious 3-3-3 configuration. This version features 221 Collins Aerospace Pinnacle seats spread across two cabins. Starting at the top, [music] we have a nicely padded four-way adjustable headrest. Moving down, the seat back and cushion are both comfortable, while the seat itself [music] measures 18 in wide. Turning around, the adjustable 10-in IFE screen features both a headphone jack and USB A port. As for the content, we'll take a closer look once we're in the air. [music] Below that is a large and sturdy bi-fold tray table. Underneath sits a spacious literature pocket containing the safety card, inflight magazine, and a small trash bag. Legroom is also very generous, which means I'll be very comfortable throughout the flight. Each seat is also equipped with a universal power outlet, which I found the charging speeds pretty fast. Soon, we were ready for departure. And with EVA Air's new safety video playing, it was time to go. While we taxi, let's talk about today's aircraft. Bravo 16716 is a 16.5-year-old Boeing 777-300ER. It first flew in November 2009 and was delivered to EVA Air the following month. Interestingly, this aircraft was involved in an incident in July of 2024. While operating a flight from Los Angeles to Taipei, the crew encountered an issue with engine number two and returned back [music] to LAX. The aircraft landed safely and later returned to service. Hopefully, we won't be repeating that experience today. Although, we may find out pretty soon as we're now lined up on the runway. >> [music] [music] [music] [music] >> Now that we're the air, let's take a look at the amenities. Waiting at each seat was a nice plush pillow along with a large soft blanket. I especially liked the texture of the blanket, which felt comfortable and cozy. Also provided were a pair of earbuds. While they're fairly standard, I appreciated the soft rubber tips, which made them fit very comfortably. While we wait for the meal service, let's check out the in-flight entertainment system. During takeoff, the glare from the sun actually revealed a fairly large scratch on the screen. Fortunately, it wasn't very noticeable once the display was turned on. The screen itself is actually quite responsive. When it comes to movies, EVA Air offers a large selection, including many new and popular titles. There's also a dedicated TV [music] and music section with many shows featuring full seasons and albums available to enjoy. One of my favorite features is the dedicated kids section, which is great for families traveling with children. Lastly, here's the flight map. It offers several different views and provides plenty of information throughout the flight. Unfortunately, there are no exterior cameras available. Overall, I quite like this in-flight entertainment system. It's responsive, easy to navigate, and does a great job of keeping me entertained throughout the flight. Around 25 minutes after takeoff, the cabin crew came around with a pre-meal snack consisting of mixed nuts, crackers, and a cup of [music] water. For some reason, it took another 30 minutes before the main meal service began. I'm not exactly sure why, but by that point, I was definitely starting to get a little hungry. Thankfully, the wait was worth it as the crew returned with many cards and [music] two meal options to choose from. The choices were Gambay barbecue karubi with steamed rice or spaghetti with seafood in a creamy mushroom sauce. If you don't know, Gambay is a well-known upscale restaurant here in Taiwan. [music] So, my choice was pretty obvious. The presentation of this meal honestly looks really nice. I especially like the individually packaged side dishes as they gave the meal [music] a more premium course-like feel. Along with that, the metal cutlery included [music] in the packet is a nice touch. And even the little tea mug feels surprisingly premium. I then got my drink of choice, an ice-cold Coke. Now, onto the food. Starting with the bread, it's nicely toasted and when paired with butter isn't dry at all. This small appetizer appears to be some noodles with slices of meat. Personally, I found it to be a little salty, but otherwise it was quite good. Next to that is a cup of fruit. For some [music] reason, EVA Air never fails to deliver when it comes to fruit. It's always sweet, juicy, and refreshing. Finally, it's time for the main dish. Starting from left to right, there are several layers of barbecue karubi served over steamed rice. On the right are some vegetables, including broccoli and bell pepper. Sitting on top is a piece of tamagoyaki, a Japanese-style folded omelet. This dish was actually really tasty. The beef was flavorful and remained surprisingly moist. In the corner were some kimchi along with a really [music] tasty green sauce, both of which added even more flavor to the meal. I then devoured the entire meal in no time, and it was finally time for dessert. Today's dessert appeared to be some sort of strawberry pudding topped with a small layer of jelly sauce. It's certainly an interesting choice, but at least EVA Air didn't skip dessert. Honestly, that was one of the best airplane meals I've had in a while. Everything was delicious, and I almost forgot I was eating an economy class meal. As the crew came around to collect my now completely empty tray, they also handed me a bottle of water. Hopefully, that'll keep me hydrated while I get some rest. After the meal, I decided to check out the restroom. Inside, you'll find a large changing table, two full-size mirrors, and a clean spacious layout. As for amenities, there was hand soap, lotion, and even a selection of scented sprays available for passengers to use. Moving over to the sink, it's decently sized and features adjustable water temperature. The water pressure was decent as well. Cups and napkins were also provided on the wall free for passengers to [music] use. The wooden floor was pretty clean, and any water visible on the floor was from me washing my hands, which I cleaned up afterwards. Overall, this is a nice lavatory with plenty of amenities and a surprisingly spacious feel. I then spent some time exploring the aircraft. Near the rear galley, I found an even larger lavatory, which offered noticeably more space than the one I just visited. Also located in the rear galley was a self-serve snack station, where passengers could help themselves to a selection of snacks throughout the flight. After a bit of exploring, I eventually headed back to my seat and noticed a couple of small issues. There was a minor crack near the tray table latch, along with some wear around it. Honestly, it didn't bother me too much, since it was purely [music] cosmetic and didn't affect the functionality of the seat at all. As the sun slowly began to set over the Pacific, [music] it seemed like the perfect time to see just how comfortable this seat would be for the [music] long flight ahead. Holding down the button on the armrest and leaning back, the seat reclines a fair amount. About half a window's worth. Combined with the generous legroom, I found it quite comfortable and had no trouble getting some rest. I actually ended up sleeping for around 4 hours. When I woke up, it was time for a mid-flight snack. Yes, EVA Air actually serves a snack between meals, which is always appreciated on a long-haul flight. Today's offering was a sandwich filled with tuna, lettuce, cheese, and tomato. It certainly looked appetizing and thankfully it tasted just as good. A cup of water was also handed out alongside it. After the snack, I decided to test out the Wi-Fi. During this flight, EVA Air was actually running a promotion that offered complimentary Wi-Fi to all passengers. After connecting, I ran a quick speed test. While the speeds were definitely on the slower side, I couldn't complain too much, considering it was completely free. At the end of the day, it's still better than having no Wi-Fi at all. By this point in the flight, there were only around 4 hours remaining. I spent some time getting a bit of work done, and before I knew it, the pre-arrival meal service was underway. Just like the first meal, there were two options to choose from. This time, the choices were a savory porridge with chicken and corn, or a vegetable frittata with bacon and roasted potatoes. Both sounded quite good, but I ultimately went with a porridge as I was in a mood for a lighter breakfast. A short while later, my tray arrived, and once again, the presentation looks quite nice. Included was the same bread roll as before, while the side containers held an appetizer and a serving of fresh fruit. The appetizer consisted of mushroom, seaweed, egg, and bell peppers. It was surprisingly flavorful and seasoned just right. Moving on to the main dish, it came with a packet of fish floss to mix into the porridge. Combined with the chicken and corn already in the porridge, it made for a very comforting breakfast. After a long flight, I especially appreciated having something warm and easy to eat. The flavors were excellent, and the corn added a nice burst of sweetness in every bite. Overall, I really enjoyed this breakfast. To finish things off, I dug into the fruit. Just like the first meal, it was sweet, juicy, and disappeared in no time. After the meal, I made another trip to the lavatory, and it was just as clean as before. It's great to see how well the cabin crew maintained it throughout the journey. Due to a strong weather system approaching San Francisco, we were set up to land on the 19th instead of the usual 28th, a less common approach into SFO. Eventually, it was time to land. After the announcements and the SFO welcome video played, the seatbelt sign was turned on once again. But before we get there, let's take a moment to rate this flight and talk about pricing. For today's 11-hour journey, I'll be rating this flight in five [music] categories: ground experience, seat, cabin crew, food, and amenities using the KSA Aviation International Economy Score. Starting with the ground experience, check-in was quick, friendly, and efficient, while boarding began right on time. There weren't [music] any long lines or issues throughout the process, earning four out of five stars. Next is the seat. Although there were a few small [music] cosmetic issues, the generous legroom, comfortable padding, and decent recline made this a great seat for a long-haul flight. 4.5 stars here. Moving on to the cabin crew, they were excellent throughout the whole flight. From the warm welcome on board to the efficient meal service and consistently clean lavatories, they did a fantastic job. Five stars here. Following that is the food. While the first meal service was a little slow, the quality of the food made up for it. Both meals were delicious, the fruit was consistently fresh, and the mid-flight snack was a welcome addition. Five stars. Lastly are the amenities. The IFE offered a vast selection of content, while the comfortable pillow, blanket, and scent sprays in the lavatories helped make the flight much more enjoyable, easily earning five stars. This means EVA Air's flight BR8 from Taipei to San Francisco earns a total of 23.5 out of 25 stars. And honestly, it's well deserved. The flight went by surprisingly quickly, and there was very little left to be desired. Lastly, before we touch down, let's talk about pricing. Due to the busy Christmas and New Year's travel season, I paid a total of $2,128 for the standard economy ticket. However, during non-peak travel periods, [music] fares for the same experience can be found for around $900, which makes this an excellent value for a long-haul flight. Anyways, we're now on short final, >> [music] >> so let's enjoy this rare approach into San Francisco. That was a pretty cool landing. After a quick taxi to the gate, it was time to deboard. Following a not-so-quick walk to customs, we finally made it to baggage claim. Baggage claim one. Soon enough, our bags started arriving, but that's when something went wrong. If you can't tell, there's a massive dent in my suitcase. So, let's see how EVA Air handles this situation. It's now been a couple of months since this flight, and I'm happy to say EVA Air repaired my suitcase completely free of charge. That's some excellent customer service. So, it looks like this flight has a happy ending after all. Although there was a small hiccup at the very end, the overall experience was outstanding. I thoroughly enjoyed this flight and would absolutely fly it again. I hope you all enjoyed this review. If you've flown EVA Air's economy before, let me know your experience down in the comments. Thank you so much for watching and I'll see you in the next one. Bye.

And that's the beauty. That's the real beauty of travel. That's why I love doing what I do. Like I said to you earlier and at the risk of trying not to get a bit upset, I lost my grandmother um she passed away um in quite quick circumstances which was really difficult. um she was my biggest um supporter and I haven't started the YouTube at that at that point. And um a little bit of Helen today has made me feel like, you know, my grandma is still here and um because she loved travel and just loves seeing new places and absolutely instilled in me the reason as to why I love travel and why I love flying so much. Um, so yeah, that today is the single reason why I love travel. And it proves to you that the best way to become a better person and the best way to learn is to immerse yourself in different cultures, travel the world, say yes to things you wouldn't normally say yes to, and spark conversations with people you wouldn't normally talk to. And that is the best way of living life to the full. I love it. Well, it doesn't rain, but it metaphorically pours aboard this AC91 flight to Sa Paulo. We're currently circling due to really quite heavy thunderstorms in the area and I've seen quite a lot of lightning, both sheet lightning and also fork lightning. So, uh, lots of stuff going off. In fact, this is probably going to be uh the, uh, seat belt sign coming on. Well, maybe not. Um, no real bumps now. We've got over those, but um, lots of lightning nonetheless. So, as we taxi to our gate in Sa Paulo, I think it's fair to say Air Canada absolutely delivered on AC91 today from start to finish. This felt like an all-star performance from the cabin crew. The service director, Ramy, alongside Mits and the rest of the team was simply superb throughout the entire flight. Warm, professional, attentive, and genuinely engaging. The kind of service that leaves a lasting impression long after the aircraft door opens. And that's even more impressive considering this was a relatively short hop by long haul standards and made even shorter by that pesky turbulence. One of the unexpected highlights today was also meeting Helen and then getting the chance to continue chatting on board. Hearing stories from her past and her own travels, journeys which in many ways have helped inspire and shape some of our future plans was genuinely special. Hopefully, we managed to leave her with a few tips of our own as well and not just a reduced champagne supply on board. But more than anything, this was one of those flights that you don't just review analytically, you actually feel it in your heart. The warmth, the atmosphere, the hospitality, it all came together to create something genuinely memorable. Air Canada, we came for business class and business class we got. Liking, sharing, and subscribing helps me more than you'll ever truly realize. So, thank you so much to those who've done it. And if you haven't subscribed, click the little icon and join me on a journey each week somewhere around the world.

reviews.transcript_full: Economy class was never meant to be luxurious. It only needs to do one thing well, make a 10, 12, sometimes 14-hour flight variable.  A seat that lets you sleep, a cabin that doesn't crush you into the person beside you.  Most major airlines manage this, most of the time, but some don't, not consistently, not across their entire fleet.  This is a ranking of the 10 full service airlines with the worst long haul economy products in 2026,  judged on seat comfort, cabin density, sleepability, fleet consistency, and entertainment.  Not safety crew or business class. Not because they're bad airlines, because on the wrong aircraft on the wrong day,  economy stops being tolerable. Let's start at 10.  10. Air France  Air France's newer Airbus A35900 is, by most measures, a modern and comfortable long haul economy seat.  The airline has invested seriously in its recent fleet and it shows. The problem isn't simply age.  It sits with Air France's high-density Boeing 777-300ER aircraft, configured for leisure routes,  where the economy cabin is stretched to its limit.  Personal space narrows considerably, and the gap between this configuration and the A350 experience  is significant. Even these co-con configured 777s have received newer seats and updated entertainment  systems in places. But the underlying 343 layout hasn't changed. The issue was never the age of the  seat. It's the density around it. Air France avoids ranking higher because most of its newer fleet  is genuinely competitive. The problem is simply that its oldest high-density leisure configured  777s remain common enough to keep it on the list. Better Aircraft Airbus A35900  Worst Aircraft High-Density Boeing 777-300ER leisure configuration  Who should still consider it? Travelers booking routes confirmed to operate the A350,  or those prioritizing Air France's broader network and pricing.  Number 9 takes the fleet lottery problem and adds one more variable, a cabin that barely varies  at all. Number 9 Kuwait Airways  Kuwait Airways is not a poorly maintained airline. Its Boeing 777-300ER fleet is relatively young,  and the newer Airbus A3-3800neo brings a noticeably more spacious, better laid-out economy cabin.  But the 777, which carries the bulk of the airline's long haul network, is configured in a dense 343  layout with narrow seats and limited recline, a combination that makes sleep difficult on overnight  sectors. In-flight entertainment on these aircraft also lags behind regional and international  competitors. Unlike several airlines on this list, the issue isn't an aging cabin. It's  that a relatively modern aircraft is still configured in a way that leaves economy feeling unnecessarily  cramped. Better Aircraft Airbus A3-3800neo Worst Aircraft  Boeing 777-300ER Who should still consider it? Passengers whose routes are confirmed on the A3-30neo,  or those for whom Kuwait Airways offers a meaningfully better routing or fare.  Number 8 is the opposite kind of problem. Not a fleet lottery, but a cabin that's uniformly firm  from front to back. Number 8, Lot Polish Airlines  LOT's long haul fleet is entirely made up of Boeing 787s, which sounds like a point in its favor.  Modern aircraft, consistent cabin, and in one sense it is, there's very little fleet variation  to worry about. The issue is what that consistent cabin actually offers.  The economy seat cushion is firm across the fleet. Entertainment content is limited compared  to larger legacy carriers, and the 787. Eight in particular runs a slightly tighter pitch than the  nine. Because the fleet is so uniform, there's little chance of getting a better aircraft.  This is simply the standard experience. Better aircraft. Boeing 787-9, marginally more pitch.  Worst aircraft. Boeing 787-8. Who should still consider it? Travelers connecting through Warsaw  on star alliance itineraries where LOT offers a convenient routing.  Number 7 is a case of an airline whose economy product simply hasn't kept pace with where it used  to lead. Number 7, Lufthansa. Lufthansa's newer Al-legress-equipped aircraft represent a real  step forward, and the airline's ongoing cabin overhaul is a legitimate sign of investment  in the years ahead. reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, in early February 2025! Heading toward Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport Terminal 2, which opened in 2018. Today, we're flying on China Southern Airlines flight CZ 381 from Guangzhou to Brisbane, Australia. China Southern, Asia's largest airline, operates a massive fleet of 700 aircraft—with Guangzhou as its main hub. Checking out the China Southern Lounge in the international departures area. It scores a 6 out of 10 — a bit small and cramped. China Southern operates a fleet of 20 Airbus A350-900 aircraft on long-haul routes to Europe and Australia. Our aircraft for tonight's flight to Brisbane: an Airbus A350-900 (registration: B-32AV), delivered in October 2022. Boarding for flight CZ 381 begins at 20:07 at gate A147, 48 minutes ahead of our scheduled departure. Stepping into China Southern's Airbus A350-900 Business Class cabin, featuring a 1-2-1 zigzag seating configuration. The cabin offers a total of 28 lie-flat beds, giving everyone direct aisle access. Settling into seat 9A. It's a window seat featuring a great privacy divider between the galley and the lie-flat bed. Aircraft doors close right on time at 20:42 as the safety video begins to play. An in-flight security officer — known as a "Fangbao" — is seated right behind me, equipped with a bodycam. Fangbaos stay with the plane at outstations like Brisbane and fly right back to China, which is why they are seated in Business Class. Pushback begins at 20:49, 6 minutes ahead of our scheduled 20:55 departure. Taxiing out to Guangzhou's Runway 01R, which stretches 3,600 meters (11,811 feet). Taking off from Guangzhou at 21:12 China Standard Time. It's a surprisingly chilly night for the tropics, sitting at just 10°C. At 7,300 km, this is a short route for the A350 (15,750 km max range) — making for a very light, easy takeoff roll. Goodbye Guangzhou and Mainland China! Listen to the magnificent roar of the Rolls-Royce Trent XWB engines, each capable of producing 84,000 lbf of max thrust. China Southern selected the Recaro CL6710 model for its Business Class cabin. The seat extends into a fully lie-flat bed reaching up to 208 cm (approx. 6'10") in length. The great-circle distance between Guangzhou and Brisbane is 7,062 km, with a scheduled gate-to-gate block time of 9 hours and 20 minutes. Dinner service begins 40 minutes after takeoff at 21:52, starting with an amuse-bouche. The appetizer cart arrives at 22:10, offering pork pâté with mango salad or a prawn and chicken salad alternative. Cruising smoothly directly over Manila, Philippines. The main course — a Western option of beef with potatoes — is served at 22:16. The dessert cart comes around at 22:41 with a choice of fresh fruit, cheese, or ice cream. The entire four-course dinner concludes by 22:52 — just 1 hour and 40 minutes after takeoff. That is remarkably swift service. Economy Class features 307 seats in a standard 3-3-3 layout. Note that Premium Economy is not available on this configuration. Checking out the IFE. There is a decent selection of Western movies, but it doesn't quite match Emirates or Singapore Airlines. At 00:57 — 4 hours and 45 minutes into the flight — we are just about to cross the equator over the Maluku Islands in the Halmahera Sea. Watch the latitude value in the lower right corner of the flight tracking app flip from positive to negative! With La Niña in full swing in early 2025, this equatorial region around Indonesia is packed with remarkably powerful thunderstorms. Cruising through a turbulent Intertropical Convergence Zone tonight over the Arafura Sea, right between Western New Guinea and Australia. The pilots are constantly navigating around severe thunderstorm cells over the Gulf of Carpentaria. Anyone getting Air France flight AF447 vibes? First signs of daylight approaching at 03:30 China Standard Time. Flying over Northern Queensland, Australia. Time to set our clocks 2 hours forward, transitioning from China Standard Time to Australian Eastern Standard Time. The cabin crew begins serving breakfast at 05:50 — a full 1 hour and 45 minutes before landing. That feels a bit too early. Once again, opting for the hot Western option featuring an omelette, sausages, and baked beans. Total sleep time is just 5 hours between the end of dinner and the start of breakfast—a bit too short for a proper rest. The seatbelt signs switch back on at 07:00, 35 minutes before arrival. Chinese regulations mandate that all seats must be fully upright at the top of descent, significantly cutting down on flatbed relaxation time. That said, the 5-minute mood lighting show to wake up the cabin is a really nice feature by China Southern. Cloudy skies outside. February brings the rainy season here during the Southern Hemisphere's summer. Flying over Bribie Island with a view looking out toward the Sunshine Coast. Moreton Island stands in the background as the aircraft makes a turn over Moreton Bay. Lining up for Brisbane's Runway 19R, which is 3,300 meters (10,827 feet) long. Welcome to Brisbane Airport, Queensland, Australia! It's now 07:35 Australian Eastern Standard Time, marking a total flight time of 8 hours and 23 minutes. Taxiing toward Brisbane Airport's International Terminal. Despite the early wake-up call, this was definitely a dream flight in a modern, luxurious Business Class product between two amazing destinations. With ongoing terminal modernizations, the immigration, customs, and biosecurity checkpoints were a bit of an unpleasant zoo. Stepping out into the warm, tropical Australian air here at the Brisbane Airport station. Catching the Gold Coast Line train from the airport down to Helensvale, which takes around 90 minutes. Queensland Rail trains operate on a distinct narrow-gauge system (1,067 mm). Transferring at Helensvale to the G:link tram to reach our final destination: Surfers Paradise. Enjoy some beach impressions from the Gold Coast, stretching from Surfers Paradise down to Tweed Heads! What do you think about China Southern Airlines, especially their long-haul premium product? Let me know in the comments below. Thanks for watching! Please subscribe to my channel, doc7austin's DreamlinerCentral.

reviews.transcript_full: [music] [music] >> Hey everyone and welcome to Hong Kong International Airport. This afternoon we are flying business class on Cathay Pacific to mainland China. When people think China, they think Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen, but today we are going to Chongqing, which is actually the largest city by population and total area. Of course, as business class passengers, we do also get access to the Cathay lounges, so please do subscribe to see the review of these soon. For passengers in transit, Hong Kong Airport offers cultural experience workshops between gates 32 and 34. Check out the Hong Kong Airport website for the current schedule and timings. Today we are doing some coloring of Chinese herbal tea signs, which I totally messed up. Despite the outcome, it was a good experience to pass time, and I hope you have better luck and better skills than me. What I love about Hong Kong Airport is its big open spaces and windows for plane spotting. It's approaching boarding time for us soon, so let's make our way to the gates. Today we will depart from gate 68 at 1:35 p.m. and our flight number is CX928. Outside our aircraft is an Airbus A330-300 registered as Bravo-Hotel-Lima-Mike. This aircraft is 25.4 years old and still going strong. Our journey to Chongqing will take around 2 hours as we travel to the center of China. Boarding was taken very seriously by the ground staff, and they strictly arranged passengers into the correct lanes. Of course, in business class, we were placed at the priority area, and soon it's time for boarding. >> Get a flight to your right. >> Okay, thank you. Welcome on board Cathay Pacific flight CX 928. After being greeted by a few cabin crew, I was shown to my seat 14K. I was actually the first passenger to board and seats in business class have a pitch of 45 in and a width of 21 in. Pretty spacious, if you ask me. In total, there are 24 Recaro CL 5510 seats in business class arranged in a 2-2-2 configuration. Welcome drinks were offered and we both got orange juice. As passengers got settled in, the business class menu was handed out. Let's take a look. The first two pages provide today's main lunch options. For desserts, we have a selection of Haagen-Dazs ice cream. The wines list is pretty good with a couple of selections from around the world. Finally, we end with beverages, which includes juices, coffees, and teas. Hot towels were also provided to freshen up and pillows and blankets were also provided. In addition, each passenger will receive a bottle of water and Cathay Pacific slippers. In front, we have a 12.1 in in-flight entertainment system, which is rather outdated. The colors are pretty washed out and we will take a closer look later. To control this dinosaur, there is an optional handheld controller under the armrest cover. Power options are excellent with two USB-C and power points between the seats. Finally, a quality pair of headphones are provided. Next to me are two windows and looking outside, we are in front of the right-hand side engine. As the pilots make their introductions, I couldn't help but notice the distinctive Australian accent, which I found to be common on Cathay flights. Let me know in the comments below if that is your experience as well, but for now, it's time to depart for Chongqing. >> After takeoff, let's look at the flight map which provides a good amount of information including altitude, time to destination, and speed. The map is customizable. However, performance-wise though, you can tell the unit's age as it is pretty laggy. Moving on to other parts of the units, there are of course movies and TV shows available in many categories. Next, music is available in several languages and genres if you want to sit back and chill. If you're taking kids for this trip, there is a dedicated kids section for movies, TV shows, music, and games. The Gate A shop with many items is available to browse in addition to the paper booklets. For games, there are about 15 titles to choose from including puzzle, sports, and strategy. Lastly, there is an information page which provides extra details including arrival information and weather forecasts. That's it for the IFE, and now looking at the seat controls, there are buttons to adjust the seat recline and leg rest. The recline amount is 9.5 in backwards and when extended the leg rest provide excellent comforts. The tray table is pretty unique and is found in front of you. Simply pull it out and extend as required. You can leave it in the half open position which provides a slim surface with two cup holders or you can fully extend it which provides a very large area. An Airbus A330 safety card is also provided to all passengers along with the Cathay in flights magazine. Lunch service was soon conducted after reaching cruise and the cabin crew came around and took our meal selections. Today I chose the grilled lamb rack with thyme and rosemary sauce. Stepping through each of the items the main meal looks fantastic and includes vegetables and potato gratin. For sides we have tuna, egg and vegetables as well as fresh fruits. For drinks I got the signature Cathay delights and a glass of water was also provided. Finally bread was given as an optional extra and of course you will have a full set of metal cutlery. Doing some taste testing the lamb main meal was absolutely delicious and the tuna was equally impressive. All ingredients were fresh including the fruits which were crunchy and sweets. To finish premium Häagen-Dazs ice cream was served which was excellent. Moving into the laboratory there is a single one available for business class passengers at the front of the aircraft. Inside everything was fully stocked but otherwise nothing really special stands out and the space is still pretty small. So after a very relaxing hour it's time to make our approach into Chongqing. As we descend let's go through today's ratings. First up is the cabin crew who were fantastic on this flights. From the moment of entry and then being personally greeted by name when I was seated I was was well looked after for the entire journey. They were very genuine and cheerful, and I have to make a special mention also to the ground staff who were equally excellent. Without their strict organization, I wouldn't have been able to board first and be the first person to arrive on the aircraft. This category therefore gets a perfect 10. Next for food and drinks, I found the meal items to be delicious and of high quality. I enjoyed all items and found the portions to be reasonable. There is plenty of choice also, so I'm giving this a 9.5 out of 10. Moving to comforts, the seats are certainly comfortable and spacious. However, these are unfortunately the only positives I can find. I would say the biggest let down is the in-flight entertainment units, which is archaic, slow, and has poor color and below average visibility. There is also a crack on the screen and the entire seat is screaming for an upgrade. Thankfully, Cathay will be upgrading these with the Aria Studio at the end of 2026, which will provide lay-flat seats and also fix all of these issues. The free Wi-Fi is certainly handy, but until the upgrade, this current business class product is definitely lacking. I'm sure Cathay is well aware of this, so unfortunately, at this time, this category only gets a five out of 10. Next for hygiene, the cabin was extremely clean from the tray table down to the carpets. My only thoughts are that the lavatory could have been cleaner in general. Nothing too serious, so this gets a strong 9.5 out of 10. Finally, for timeliness, we are on track to land at 3:45 p.m. This is 25 minutes earlier than scheduled, which is excellent. So, this category gets a perfect 10 as no surprise. Summing everything up, we get a final score of 8.8 out of 10. The food and service was world-class. However, the hard product is out of date and I'm glad it is due for upgrade later this year. >> [music] [music] >> Welcome to Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport. I hope everyone enjoyed the review as we arrive in China's cyberpunk city. Do you love aviation and traveling? If so, please remember to subscribe before leaving to ensure you don't miss out on future videos. Thank you for watching today. Let me know your thoughts in the comments below and be sure to leave a like. Take care and see you next time.

reviews.transcript_full: Planning a trip to Asia?  Korean Air is one of the leading airlines connecting North America with destinations across  South Korea, Japan, China, Southeast Asia, and beyond.  Korean Air offers non-stop service from several major cities in the United States and Canada,  making travel to Asia convenient and accessible.  Most journeys connect through Seoul, Incheon Airport, known for efficient transfers, clear  signage, and a traveler-friendly layout.  If your itinerary includes more than one destination in Asia, Korean Air's extensive regional  network can make planning easier.  Economy class is known for comfortable seating, adjustable headrest, and generosity legroom  on many long haul aircraft.  Meals and beverages are included, with both Korean and international menu options available  on many flights.  Long haul aircraft feature personal entertainment screens, with movies, TV shows, music, and  games.  USB charging is also available on many aircraft.  Blankets, pillows, and headphones are typically provided to help make long journeys more comfortable.  Korean Air is a strong option for travelers heading to Seoul, Tokyo, Osaka, Bangkok,  Manila, Ho Chi Minh City, and many other destinations throughout Asia.  For more airline reviews and helpful travel tips for economical international flights,  stay tuned with ASAP Tickets.

reviews.transcript_full: Greetings everyone from Kuala lumpur international airport. Thank you for joining us! Today we're experiencing Singapore Airlines business class on their shortest route, from Kuala Lumpur to Singapore. Singapore Airline deliver outstanding service—whether it's the cabin setup, the meals, or the overall service. So, can they still keep up the great service? Let's check it out together. This is the T1 Satellite Building. It's got this round design, and the gates are spread out in four different directions. There's no Singapore Airlines-operated lounge at Kuala Lumpur airport. Singapore Airlines runs at least 8 daily services,they are always full. Crazy busy! This 5.3‑year‑old Airbus A350‑900 will be taking me to Singapore. The crew's smiles gave me an instant sense of warmth as I boarded. This seat is pretty much the standard now for Singapore Airlines business class. You'll see it on most of their A350s and 787s. There are 40 seats in business class, from row 11 to row 21, with 4 seats per row. Only 40 minutes in the air, but they've still got a pillow and blanket set out for you, nice touch. Small sliding storage with USB and power， ideal for phone, earphones,or other little items. Touchscreen panel for all the controls. Lights, seat adjustment, IFE switch – everything's there. And the icons are so clear, you can't really mess it up." I've got to say, legroom is limited. When I lie flat and bend my knees, always touch the sides. For just rest, fine. But for a longer fligt, that would get uncomfortabl a little. Clever and thoughtful, love this design. Adjustable reading light. The headrest is soft and resilient. The pillow is so fluffy. The tray table is placed right below the screen, so it's really easy to use. And it fits in perfectly with the overall design of the seat. But the only downside is that it takes up a bit of legroom. Welcome drinks included orange juice, apple juice, and water. But since it was breakfast time, no champagne was offered. The crew brought another hot towel. Honestly, that woke me right up. Ambient lighting and reading light on and off. When you're sleeping or just don't want to be disturbed, you can press this button. The flight was so short that the seatbelt sign actually went off just five minutes after takeoff. Honestly, I thought it'd just be a bottle of water and a sandwich – but nope, they brought out a proper light meal and drinks too.  Option one is Japanese-style soba, a light noodle dish. Loved the texture of the noodles - nice and springy. So flavorful.  Option two is a Malaysian-style salad. Fresh ingredients, looks so healthy! Cheers, everyone! Now, let's see how this seat transforms into a bed. Fully flat, great privacy around the head. The only downside is the limited legroom. Full cabin view with Business class. So, do you think this 40‑minute business class flight is worth it? How would you rate the overall experience? Feel free to leave your comments! Looking forward to our next journey together, see you next time !

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to the X-Pro Stay Channel.  Today, we are taking you along on Turkish Airlines flight 1888 Taka's from Vienna to Istanbul,  flying on the spacious Airbus A330.  If you're curious about the airport lounge experience in Vienna before we take off,  make sure to check out the dedicated lounge video right here on our channel.  Honestly, the flight was absolutely fantastic from start to finish.  Right after boarding, it was great to see that we received comfortable pillows, blankets,  and our own complimentary headphones for the flight.  As we cruised, I explored the Inflite Entertainment System.  The movie selection is massive, featuring everything from the latest blockbusters and  popular animations to a great mix of music and TV shows.  There is easily enough content to keep you entertained for hours.  Another huge highlight was the onboard catering.  For such a short flight, we actually had a choice between two different hot meals.  Turkish Airlines is truly amazing for this, because getting a proper, delicious meal in  economy class is a rare luxury these days. During the flight, I also visited the  lavatory and was really pleased to see how nicely clean and well maintained it was,  complete with good quality hand soap and lotion. It's always a big plus when an airline keeps  up with cleanliness mid-flight.  The only minor detail that didn't work was the connecting gate info screen,  which was supposed to display our transfer gates for Istanbul Airport.  Luckily, navigating the beautiful Istanbul terminal upon arrival was still very smooth.  To wrap things up, this Turkish Airlines flight from Vienna to Istanbul on the Airbus A330  was an absolute pleasure. From the great comfort pillows and headphones provided at the start,  to the spotless lavatory and the massive movie selection, they really know how to take care  of their passengers. Plus, getting a choice of two delicious hot meals on such a short economy flight  is something you rarely see these days. Despite the minor glitch with the connecting gate screen,  I highly recommend flying with them. Thank you for watching, and don't forget to subscribe to  XproStay for more travel reviews.

reviews.transcript_full: Some of the world's best airlines are based in Asia. But when you actually look closely, they're not all excellent for the same reason. And some win simply because they operate the newest, most consistent aircraft in the sky. This ranking looks at what passengers actually experience in 2026, [music] from the seats and service to fleet consistency, network strength, and overall value. One note before we start. Airlines like Qatar Airways, Emirates, [music] and Etihad are not included here. They operate on a different model entirely and deserve their own separate ranking. This is about Asia's full-service carriers, from Tokyo to Singapore, from Seoul to Taipei. Let's begin with number 10. Number 10, Thai Airways. At number 10 is Thai Airways, a carrier that has spent the last few years rebuilding itself >> [music] >> into something more focused. Flying out of Bangkok, it still carries one of the most recognizable senses of [music] hospitality in the region. Unhurried service and food that routinely ranks among the best in Asian aviation, with curries and regional dishes that feel like part of the identity rather than an afterthought. Since its restructuring, the fleet is tighter [music] and operations have visibly improved compared to a decade ago. But Thai Airways still trails the airlines above it in one key area, consistency. Aircraft swaps remain common enough that passengers can book one cabin experience and receive another. And the airline does not currently offer a true standalone premium economy product comparable to the dedicated cabins offered by the airlines higher on this list. It's an airline built on charm and cuisine, recovering steadily, but not yet operating with the precision of the carriers ranked above it. Number nine, Malaysia Airlines. Number nine is Malaysia Airlines, a full-service carrier in the middle of real modernization. Operating from Kuala Lumpur and holding One World membership, Malaysia Airlines offers genuine hospitality in the cabin, something reviewers repeatedly point to, along with a signature satay service that has become something of a calling card. That push includes new A330 neo aircraft with updated cabins and suites, a meaningful step forward. The issue is what it's replacing. Older A330 business class seating that varies significantly in layout and comfort from flight to flight, meaning your experience can depend heavily on which aircraft shows up at the gate. And like Thai Airways, Malaysia Airlines does not currently offer a true stand-alone premium economy product. The space between economy and business remains thin. What you get is a carrier with real hospitality and a modernization plan in motion, but one that hasn't yet closed the gap with Asia's most consistent operators. Number eight, Vietnam Airlines. At number eight, Vietnam Airlines might be the most underrated long-haul carrier in this entire ranking. Operating out of Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, its long-haul operation is built primarily around the Airbus A350 and Boeing 787, with very few older wide-bodies affecting the overall fleet. That matters because it means passengers get contemporary cabins nearly every time they fly long-haul. Vietnam Airlines also offers a true premium economy product on its 787, [music] nine, and A350 aircraft, a dedicated cabin rather than a repackaged economy seat. And it prices its long-haul routes to Europe and Australia competitively enough that it reliably over-delivers on value. Where it falls of the airlines above it is in the ground and in the finer points of service [music] consistency. Check-in lines in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City can be chaotic. And the polish that defines carriers like Japan Airlines or Singapore Airlines isn't quite there yet. But as a long-haul value proposition with modern hardware, Vietnam Airlines earns its place here. Number seven. Starlux Airlines. Number seven belongs to Starlux, the most exciting new airline in Asia and arguably the hardest one to rank. Based in Taipei, Starlux operates an extraordinarily young fleet, among the newest anywhere in the world, built around the Airbus A350. And it shows in every part of the cabin. The in-flight entertainment is sharp. The seat design is considered down to the material choices. And the overall aesthetic feels closer to a design studio than a traditional airline. Passenger reviews have been overwhelmingly positive since [music] launch, and it's easy to see why. Everything about the experience feels deliberate. So why isn't it higher? Scale and time. Starlux still operates a limited route network. It isn't part of a major global alliance, and its small fleet means that any single aircraft issue can ripple through the schedule in a way it wouldn't for a larger carrier. It also simply hasn't been flying long enough to build the kind of track record the airlines above it have spent decades earning. It's an airline built on where aviation is heading rather than where it's been. But it needs more time and more aircraft before it can compete with the network strength of the carriers ranked above it. Six, EVA Air. Starlux may be Taipei's newest carrier, but the city's other major airline has been quietly excellent for years. At number six, EVA Air rarely dominates headlines, but it outperforms expectations almost every time. EVA is known for cabins that feel clean in the literal sense. Spotless, well-maintained, unfussy. Its Royal Laurel business class is one of the most respected products in the region. And its true premium economy cabin, found mainly on the 777-300ER and select 787-9 aircraft, has long been considered a benchmark for the category. EVA's standing across the Pacific is particularly strong, built over years of dependable service on routes connecting Taiwan [music] to North America. What keeps it from climbing higher is size and a certain restraint. Its overall network is smaller than Singapore Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Korean Air, ANA, or Japan Airlines, even though it maintains strong service across North America and key European gateways. EVA also tends to improve quietly rather than boldly. Cabins get upgraded steadily, but it's rarely the airline setting the trend. EVA Air isn't trying to be everywhere. It's trying to be reliable everywhere it flies, and on that measure, it rarely disappoints. Number five. Korean Air. Number five is Korean Air. A carrier whose real strength lies in scale. Korean Air calls Incheon home. Economy class is often praised for generous space, and the food, bibimbap in particular, has become something of [music] a signature. In business class, Korean Air's newer prestige suites represent a significant step forward in privacy and cabin [music] design, while the airline continues modernizing its long-haul fleet. Where Korean Air still trails the airlines above it is cabin consistency. That seat, branded Sky Wider, has become something of a favorite among frequent flyers. Its premium economy cabin builds on that same philosophy and is widely regarded as one of the best in the industry. [music] On the newest A350-1000 aircraft, JAL's flagship cabins bring that same attention to detail to business and first class, paired with food and service that regularly draws praise. The catch is that word, when. The Room isn't fleet-wide, and passengers booking business class on an older 787 will find a noticeably different, less private product. That inconsistency across aircraft is the one thing keeping ANA from climbing into the top two. Everything else about the airline is close to flawless. Number two, Cathay Pacific. At number [music] two, Cathay Pacific is the strongest comeback story among Asia's elite carriers. Hong Kong remains Cathay's [music] base, and the airline has spent the past few years rebuilding both its network and its reputation. And by most measures, it succeeded. Its economy class experience is frequently singled out as best in class. And on the ground, The Pier and The Wing lounges remain among the finest business class lounges anywhere in the world, spacious, calm, genuinely designed for long layovers, rather than just brief stops. In the air, Cathay's new Aria Suite is rolling out across its long-haul [music] fleet, joining an already strong product on the A350 and 777. And the airline's recognition through 2025 and 2026 reflects real momentum. What keeps it just short of first place is something harder to quantify, warmth. Service on Cathay is polished and professional, but passengers and reviewers alike note that it doesn't carry quite the same emotional warmth as Japan Airlines, ANA, or Singapore Airlines. It's an airline doing almost everything right, just not with the same human touch as the very best. Number one, Singapore Airlines. And that brings us to number one, Singapore Airlines. It isn't always the cheapest option, and it's rarely the airline you choose to [music] save money. But cabin for cabin, route for route, it's the most complete airline in Asia. Based at Changi, Singapore Airlines delivers a version of consistency [music] that few competitors can match. Economy class is comfortable and well executed across the fleet. Premium economy holds up as one of the strongest in the region. And business class, along with first class and suites where available, has defined the upper end of air travel for years. Its KrisWorld entertainment system remains one of the most extensive in the industry. And KrisFlyer members, membership is free to join, can access complimentary Wi-Fi, a small detail that adds up over a long flight. The trade-off is price. Singapore Airlines rarely competes on cost, and that premium is real. But what earns it the top spot [music] isn't any single seat or cabin. It's that the experience holds together across aircraft, across routes, across cabins, in a way no other airline on this list quite matches. No airline here is truly perfect. Singapore Airlines simply carries fewer compromises than anyone else. A list like this is never the final word. It's just an open box and you can put your things inside from the front, but this is not obvious. It was clear that a lot of people had tried to lift the lid. It is partially attached with Velcro. Food and drink are included in the fair with and without alcohol. The tray table comes out of the armrest. This one time when I opened it for the first time, I managed to get it out correctly. Every other time the table got stuck. You can angle the table so that in theory you can exit the seat even when the table is deployed, but I did not try that. The crew member greeted me by name and took my drink order. That feels premium. The breakfast tray comes with a default starter and side dishes. From top left to right, we have a chia bowl with pineapple, a couple of marinated olives, jam and butter for the bread, a fruit salad, and a selection of cheeses and smoked ham. The menu says specifically that the jam is homemade strawberry jam from Bodum, plus countryside butter from Trabzon. It's clear that Turkish Airlines takes a lot of pride in their food and its local origins. I somehow doubt that someone made this jam at home, but uh what do I know? We also get these cute salt and pepper shakers. For my drinks, I chose black tea and water. The teacup would have been better with a real handle instead of this paper sleeve. There were three choices for the main breakfast item. an omelette, a porridge, and then the one that I chose, gleame. This is a traditional grilled flat filow pastry filled with spinach and white cheese. This was a fantastic breakfast. Turkish Airlines has consistently great food on board, even in economy, by the way, and today was no exception. I finished off the meal with a Turkish coffee which came with a cookie and most importantly a Turkish delight. The in-flight entertainment is good and it's a modern system. The touchscreen remote worked really well. On the older A330 from the second flight, the remote was more old-fashioned. It had physical buttons and they were not very responsive. One problem on both versions of the aircraft is that the monitor, which also is not the biggest in the world, is too far away. It's a result of the seat design with all this leg room. The selection of titles on the if is pretty broad. However, it varies between aircraft. I started watching an episode of Dune Prophecy on one flight on the assumption that I could continue on the next flight back home. That last flight was on a narrowbody aircraft and it had fewer episodes. The episode I had started was not on that system. Turkish Airlines sensors the content on the if heavily. Certain themes result in muted audio and the blurring of a portion of the screen. I even saw this on the fairly mild HBO series Silicon Valley as well as the Kendrick Lamar album GNX. This censorship is ridiculous nonsense. Turkish Airlines, if you don't like a specific piece of media, then just don't load it onto the in-flight entertainment system. Censorship is not the answer. On the fairly unique content on the Turkish Airlines system, you can find the Quran as well as some educational content about Islamic life. The older A330 had some super retro ports around the inflight entertainment screen. If you know what these are for, please let me know in the comments. The headphones that Turkish Airlines provides are made by Audio Technica. That's a Japanese brand that makes professional audio gear. The headphones were pretty good. They have no active noise cancellation, but the passive noise cancellation just by virtue of being well padded did a lot of work. There is Wi-Fi on board. Theoretically, I should be able to log in to the Wi-Fi with the Turkish Airlines app on my phone. This is theoretically a good solution because I'm already logged in to my account on the app, but this did not work. There is both a USBA port and a universal power outlet at my seat. The universal outlet was impossible to access when I was seated. That's because it's located kind of behind me. I literally had to get on my knees in front of my seat to insert my charger. As for the lavatory, the most distinguishing feature is that there are some premium amenities in here. There is a liquid soap, a hand lotion, some scented diffuser thing that I don't know how it's called, and a perfume. My only complaint is that the tray was placed too near the wall so that there's no space for your hand above the soap pump. Luckily, the tray can be moved easily. These kinds of premium amenities are also in the economy class lavatory. By the way, the bed on the A330 may not be completely horizontal, but it does go flat. The main limitation is that if you have a person next to you, you will have to step over them if they're sleeping. On my flight, the seat next to me remained empty, so I had no issues. There's a pillow and they have blankets, but I didn't actually use the bed because this was a daytime flight. I had basically just woken up from the hotel. After the meal service, the crew handed out hazelnuts. I've seen this before. They really highlight the fact that hazelnuts are from Turkey. Overall, the service was friendly. When I boarded, the flight attendant personally walked me to the seat, and that feels premium. There are certainly airlines out there that have a more rigorous training program for the cabin crew. I would rather have good food and mediocre service than the other way around. And what Turkish Airlines does is perfectly acceptable. As we begin our descent into Istanbul airport, we're going to talk about the price in just a moment. If you've gotten value from my video, consider booking me for one of your corporate events. I've been performing stand-up comedy for almost a decade and I have a keynote called Leadership Lessons from the Comedy Club where I teach you some communication skills that they don't cover in your traditional presentation skills workshop. Learn more at marcuspresents.com. So now for the price. I booked this trip as a one-way ticket from Milano Malpenza to Dubai via Istanbul. I paid €434 for the base economy ticket. That's around $500 US. Then I upgraded both segments with my Turkish Airlines miles. The upgrade cost was $53,000. Those miles were going to expire by year end anyway, so it's hard to put a value to them. So when it comes to the value for money, I look at it from a different perspective instead. Turkish Airlines is the only airline I've tried that offers a lie flat bed on a widebody aircraft on an intra European flight. That's cool. That's unusual. I like it. Sure, the seat is not competitive with the state-of-the-art of business class today, but for a 3-hour flight, it doesn't have to be. Turkish Airlines also flies these routes with narrow bodies sometimes and then you just get a big recliner in business class. But even that is better than the Euro business with just an economy seat with a middle seat blocked. There's other aspects too like the huge modern airport at Istanbul. I'll talk more about that in the next video I will link to in just a moment. The food is consistently great on Turkish Airlines. And then there's the schedule. That's a real asset of Turkish Airlines. When both Whiz Air and Beyond cancelled my flights by offering a lot of connections between the Middle East and Europe, Turkish Airlines really saved the day. They had so many different connections available. First from Milan to Dubai and then back home, Dubai to Basil, Switzerland. It was easy to find good and convenient options, and the prices were reasonable even when I booked the return ticket just 4 days before departure. reviews.transcript_full: Today I'm trying out Etihad Airways' Airbus A380 First Class. A 10-hour flight from Abu Dhabi to Tokyo. Delicious meals. Onboard shower experience. Amenities and pajamas. Fully flat bed. Onboard lounge. New services. Please enjoy! I'm currently in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Etihad offers a free chauffeur service within the UAE. I will be taking the Etihad Chauffeur car. Mineral water and an in-flight magazine are provided in the car. The interior is luxurious and comfortable. Free Wi-Fi service is also available. Passengers can adjust the air conditioning in the car. I'm now heading to Zayed International Airport in Abu Dhabi. The free chauffeur service is available within the UAE, so transfers from Dubai to Zayed International Airport are also possible. We can see the futuristic airport building. By the way, the chauffeur service can be booked through the Etihad website. Arrived at the airport. The car has the words "Etihad Chauffeur" on it. This is the airport departure lobby. The check-in areas for First and Business Class are separate. This is the business class check-in area. Further inside is the first class check-in area. It says "The Residence & First". The Residence is a class beyond first class. Check-in is here. Drinks (water and Arabic coffee) and dates are served. A boarding pass case. This wasn't there before, so is it a new service? First class boarding pass. I went through a dedicated security checkpoint and entered the restricted area. Terminal A, where we are currently located, officially opened in November 2023. Approximately 3 billion US dollars were invested in the construction of the terminal. There are 163 shops and restaurants inside. Let's go to the Etihad lounge. There is a souk on the way. The entrance to the lounge is near gate C29. We are currently on the 3rd floor, so we will take the elevator to the 6th floor. The lounge is a three-story building, with floors 3, 5, and 6. The first class lounge is on the 6th floor. There are arabic coffee and dates. The coffee cups are made in the UAE. There are not many people in the first class lounge. We can see the parked airplanes from the panoramic windows. We're looking at the dining area. The buffet has a variety of dates, croissants, baklava, fruit, macarons, sweets, and light meals. Looks delicious. The drinks corner. Lemon iced tea and infused water. Dilmah tea from Sri Lanka. Earl Grey and other varieties. Coffee machine. Soft drinks such as cola. There is also an à la carte menu. We can enjoy gourmet dishes with wine. Three appetizers. Three soups. Seven main courses (more than on the plane). Six desserts. Soft drinks, coffee, and tea. The wine list. The champagne is a high-end one befitting first class. The wine menu is similar to the one on the plane. The champagne is Veuve Clicquot Ponsardin La Grande Dame Brut 2018. This champagne sells for about 215 USD outside of the airport. I ordered Robian Tahta. This is shrimp rice, an authentic Emirati dish from the UAE. The taste is not as strong as it looks. I’ll have the Robian Tahta topped with Dakous (spicy tomato sauce). I ordered only one item at the lounge, as I wanted to enjoy the meal on board. The lounge is a tranquil space with a luxurious atmosphere. At the very back is the relaxation area. You can rest in a quiet area with partitions. Daybeds and recliners are provided. There are three shower rooms in the First Class Lounge. Amenities such as toothbrushes are available upon request. Hair dryers are provided.  There is a toilet and a separate shower booth. a nice little nap, let's check out the all day   menu. I decided to order two classics. The first

yt_comments.author: @markjones2781
yt_comments.text: Hmm, The showers at the CX Pier Lounge are dark and tiny (I'm 190cm tall and fairly lean at 90kg). Moving about or even taking off your shoes is a challenge. The clammy humid air is suffocating. The showers at Changi are much better! As for the Aria Suite itself, despite its Instagram wow factor, it has many down sides. The IFE screen is just too damn big. It's like sitting in the front row of a cinema. The leg space/cubby hole is cramped and you can't swing the IFE screen out of the way like in the old cabin. Just what is the point of storages spaces so small you can't drop a handbag or whatever into? The wireless charging spot doesn't work in the real world of a moving/vibrating plane. There is no reading light! For those of us who still read books this is a tragedy. Finally, the door offers little privacy from people or crew walking up and down the isle and yet takes the claustrophobia level to an extreme. In summary, the Aria suite is a step backwards not forwards. Thankfully, the CX crews are simply fantastic and go some way to making up for the deficiencies of the new hard product.

Hi everyone.
This video is about my Cathay Pacific flight CX548  from Hong Kong to Tokyo in premium 
economy class First row window seat 30A.  This route is operated by the 
retrofitted Boeing 777-300ER aircrafts  equipped with the new premium economy 
class seats and the area suites.  Let's take a look at the retrofitted 
premium economy class cabin with me.  The scheduled departure time is 8:40am 
which makes it a popular connecting flight   for passengers arriving from Europe.
The cabin was quite empty this time.  Probably this reflects premium economy class is 
not quite attractive to short haul travelers.  The headset, the Cathay magazine and the safety 
instructions are in the storage space in front.  This space should also allow you 
to store a bottled water there.  The leg room in the bulkhead seat is 
generous which allows me to stretch my legs.  Although it may not be so 
important in this 3.5-hour flight.  The only weird part of this front row 
seat is the leg rest and the foot rest.  The leg rest does not rise high 
enough and thus the support is   not good even when I lowered the seat back.
I was so lucky that no one is sitting next   to me nor behind me so that I could show 
how the seat reclines to the full extent.  You can compare this to the leg rest in 
the seat in other rows as shown on Cathay's   promotional video.
Nevertheless,   I will still choose the extra personal space 
in bulkhead seats over the better leg rest.  Let's have a closer look at the headrest.
It can be adjusted in multiple ways to provide   a support that makes you feel most comfortable.
The leather-like material makes it looks more   elegant and highclass, and more 
importantly easier to clean.  Besides, the privacy wing provides added 
privacy when you are traveling on your own.  The reading light is also 
installed at the privacy wing.  Like the Airbus A350 premium economy class seat, 
there is a small storage space under the armrest.  The light is a very good improvement 
when the cabin lights were switched off.  In addition to the USB-C fast 
charging port under the armrest,   you can also find a USB-A charging 
port and universal power outlet.  The headset connector is also here 
under the cocktail mini table.  This is the headset provided 
in premium economy class.  Its noise cancelling effect is okay.
However, if you have big ears like me,   you may also find it is not quite 
comfortable to wear after a while.  It will be better if you bring your 
Bluetooth headset as it can now be   paired to the entertainment system.
The stunning 15.6-inch 4K screen   is fixed on the bulkhead.
As it is a bit far from   the seat for touch control, you can use 
the remote control to navigate the menu. Unlike the traditional remote control,   this one works like a trackpad, 
but it is quite intuitive to use.  The award-winning inflight entertainment 
system with new movies, TV series, podcasts,   and music added every month.
You will definitely find   something you're interested to watch.
Complimentary Wi-Fi is now offered to   cafe members in premium economy class.
However, if you entered other frequent   flyer membership at check-in, you 
cannot enjoy this offer like myself. Although you can find a cocktail 
mini table here, no welcome drink   was offered on this short haul flight.
There was also no hot towel service either.  Not a big deal. However, if Cathay wants 
to attract more revenue customers booking   premium economy class on short haul flights
These are actually some premium features   that customers would expect and 
it is not too costly to offer.  Here you can find your 
foldable table in the armrest.  As this flight departs before 
10:00 a.m., breakfast is served.  If it departs after 10:00 a.m. local time, 
nuts and drinks will be served before lunch.  There was no printed or onscreen menu, and the 
two breakfast choices are always dim sum set,   and egg and sausage.
As I had egg and   sausage on my flight from Manchester, 
I chose the dim sum set on this flight.  To be honest, breakfast in economy class 
and premium economy class are quite similar.  The only differences are croissant 
is served instead of white row   and food is served in stonewares.
Note that Prosecco is only   served in long haul flights.
Although the breakfast served on   this flight was nothing special, the late lunch or 
dinner served on my return flight was much better.  I had steak and mashed potato on 
the flight CX549 to Hong Kong.  If you have not tried dim sum before, these 
were actually quite tasty and worth a try.  The main dishes in premium economy 
class on Japan routes are similar   to that offered in business class.
Whereas on shorter routes like flights to   Shanghai, the same economy class menu was served.
On this route, try to pick a seat on   the left hand side.
If you're lucky that   the weather is fine, you will be able to see 
Mount Fuji when the flight approaches Tokyo.  This time I can barely spot 
it for a few seconds only.  Let me wrap up this short haul premium economy 
class experience with Cathay Pacific here.  First of all, the hardware, i.e. the seat 
is a big improvement. The big 4K TV and   the privacy wing are remarkably good.
I also love having the TV fixed on the   bulkhead instead of stowing under the armrest as 
I can still watch it during takeoff and landing.  This also makes it easier for passengers 
in the window seat to leave the seat.  About the service, to be honest, there was 
no notable difference from economy class   except the food was served in stonewares.
I was on this short haul premium economy class   only because I booked premium economy class 
return tickets from Manchester to Tokyo.  My honest opinion is that if I booked the short 
haul flight separately, I would definitely not   be paying the premium price for this slightly 
better seat for a duration of only 3.5 hours.  Last but not least, thank you very 
much for your time watching this video.  If you find it useful, please 
like and share this video.  Your subscription to my channel 
is also much appreciated.  Please enjoy the rest of the video for the 
approach to the Tokyo International Airport.
