reviews.transcript_full: In today's video, I take a gruelling 14 hour flight from Hong Kong to London in Cathay Pacific's brilliant Airbus A350-1000 Economy on what would actually end up being one of the best flights of my life so you'll find out why after flying over 60 airlines Cathay Pacific are one of my favourites and also I'll show you a useful trick which helped me get one of the best seats on the plane completely for free so buckle up and enjoy this Cathay Pacific Trip Report! and we start at an eye-wateringly early 5am in the morning in the impressive departure hall of Hong Kong Airport This is actually my first time flying Cathay Pacific Economy long haul, though back in 2018  I actually flew their Business Class from London to Tokyo via Hong Kong and remember those being some of the best flights of my life Just things like the cabin crew greeting me by name as I boarded and being able to order burgers in the middle of the flight not to mention that was my first time on an Airbus A350 too and the seat is really good plus their Business Class lounges in Hong Kong are probably the best in the world and up until that point in my life I'd only ever flown Business with British Airways and Virgin Atlantic which I don't think are bad airlines per se, but flying Cathay was just such an eye opener to what  a real world-class airline is like anyway, all that to say, I was exciting to be flying Cathay Pacific today, even if just in Economy... Hong Kong Airport is pretty good too, and I think is best summed up with the word efficiency though I feel like for an airport of this size there's actually not many shops or food and worryingly, the shopping area was filled with Labubu statues here I was thinking that trend had died down by now but clearly not in Hong Kong as you can see here, the airport is also pretty big, my gate happened to be all the way over here, literally the furthest you can get from the entrance so there was a lot of walking involved and I was lugging about fifteen kilograms of luggage so reaching the gate took a while and yes, that much carryon is vastly over their seven kilogram allowance... but they don't weigh bags at the gate, and I wanted to bring home a lot of souvenirs and snacks... anyway, now that the sun has started rising I have to say Hong Kong Airport is amazing for planespotting there are so many widebody aircraft here including a whole fleet of 747 cargo planes making it a feast for the eyes and the backdrop of skyscrapers and mountains makes for a lovely view in terms of seating though,  there isn't that much by each gate actually and I think if our plane was full then there wouldn't have been nearly enough seats for everyone Now here's our plane for today, a 7 year old Airbus A350-1000 registered B-LXI which had just arrived a few hours earlier from Boston it has 334 seats in total, 256 of which are Economy Class also this was the only one I caught on film but I got a great view of many cool takeoffs whilst I waited around for boarding to start and start it did, about 45 minutes before scheduled departure One way that Hong Kong Airport is living in the future is that they have these cool biometric gates so you don't even need to show your passport and boarding pass it just scans your face and lets you through after a few seconds hugely efficient and really speeds up boarding, not that that was necessary today as the flight probably wasn't even half full Now before we step on board here are the stats and route map for today's flight where we would actually take a pretty indirect route over North China around the Himalayas whilst avoiding Russia to land slightly early with a flight time of 13.5 hours, but about 15 hours actually sat on the plane due to a slightly delayed departure and as I alluded to in the intro, there's a good trick you can do with many airlines to find the best seat for free Cathay Pacific let you view the seat map online right up until departure I saw the best exit row seat 60K was actually still available, but cost £156 extra so I ignored it and thought I would be happy with the seat I'd been allocated 46K, this locked-in window seat but then the thought of spending 15 hours trapped by the window reminded me of this scene from White Lotus... So I went up to the gate agent, showed them the seat map and asked if I could have that exit row seat and to my surprise they did it for free very quickly so that was great you'll see how good this new seat was in a moment, but moral of the story is, just keep an eye on the online seat map and even if it's not an exit row you should be able to ask them to change you to the best seat available and even better, the two seats next to me ended up being empty too making this literally the best seating setup you can ask for in Economy Class obviously all this was largely due to the luck of having an empty flight,  but hey, I'm just reviewing my experience and this is just how it turned out now obviously legroom is fantastic and in this seat you get direct aisle access too and actually, the non-exit seats are also pretty good with 32" of seat pitch and 6" of recline the tv is a decent sized 11.1" too so overall it's a very competitive seat You get quite a nice soft pillow, no scratchy disposable cover here... and what is probably one of the better Economy Class blankets out there, soft and very large, plus I had 3 of them since my row was empty... a well padded adjustable headrest and a very nice wing view also something pretty rare to see in Economy Class these days, they actually give you a printed menu which first of all, just feels a bit more premium, but it's also nice being able to read it and decide what you want well ahead of time, rather than making an on the spot decision when the food cart comes round also the entire drinks menu is here, so you don't have to guess at what they have or don't have also they give everyone a water bottle after boarding, vital on a long flight like this and the headphones are actually pretty decent for Economy Class... though I've recently started using this Bluetooth transmitter instead which lets me connect my wireless headphones instead and makes for an infinitely better audio experience Amazon affiliate link in the description if you want one for yourself This is the new Naked Gun movie by the way, extremely stupid but I enjoyed it a lot and that brings me to the IFE System, which is actually really good so good in fact that Skytrax ranked them as having the best inflight entertainment of any airline in the world this year and they basically have everything you could want, loads of movies in many different languages a nice slick interface, tv shows, music, games quality of life things like airport guides and connecting gate info two external cameras in very high definition which I always enjoy watching... plus the inflight map is pretty good too they also have the full inflight menu here in addition to the paper menu handed out during boarding and the full Cathay Pacific Shop, which has a satisfying range of quality-looking branded merch Boarding finished very quickly due to how empty the flight was but of course, the pilot announced a 40 minute delay due to of course, air traffic restrictions over China which seems incredibly common due to how restricted China's airspace is and was mildly annoying, but we still ended up arriving 20 minutes early in London so it wasn't the end of the world and now here's the safety video, which I liked a lot,  makes me want to visit Hong Kong again and eat some claypot rice with a side of egg tart and milk tea After a bit of taxiing and some more waiting we were finally ready for takeoff and I definitely made the right seat choice as the view of Hong Kong on takeoff was jaw-dropping so get ready for that, coming up now... and here's something weird you can see here so genuinely curious if any pilots watching could explain... after fully raising the flaps the pilots lowered them again, only to raise them a few seconds later here they are going down after being fully raised... and here they are going up again... please leave a comment if you have any idea why? anyway, apart from that the views of Hong Kong taking off were incredible The contrast of the skyscrapers and mountains with the bay make for one of the coolest takeoff views in the world and hear you can see Guanzhou, which is just an absurdly big city and it has one of the busiest airports in the world which you can see here Pretty soon after takeoff breakfast was served, and the service was rapid due to how empty the plane was and I can report that this was easily the best airplane breakfast I've ever had mainly because they had proper dim sum and it was actually pretty good, which I've never seen on a plane before also metal cutlery make it feel fancy There was a prawn dumpling, a meatball thing and this yellow dumpling, all very tasty Then a well-seasoned congee which I mixed the meatball into They also give you a towelette, butter, jam and a bread roll which was actually warmed up then lastly a strawberry yoghurt, fresh fruit and orange juice to drink Then on top of all that I got a Hong Kong milk tea to drink which is pretty big in Hong Kong and also a unique thing offered by Cathay Pacific Another cool feature of the seat is they have a device holder built in not so useful on the exit row seat, but it's well placed here on the regular seats I got up to stretch my legs, and you can see here just how empty the plane was, back here I would say it was maybe only 20% full, with a lot of people just laying down on a full row and I'm aware Cathay took a very big hit after Covid, but I'm surprised they still seem to be struggling to fill planes Now for a loo review, toothbrush kits are available but I had to ask the crew for one and the toilets were kept clean throughout, with crew constantly going in to clean them Also, this is by far the biggest sink I can remember seeing in a plane toilet even when compared to most Business Class loos Another nice quality of life feature is they show you the flight timeline letting you know when to expect food and drinks services throughout the flight Halfway through the flight it was time for meal number two, and I got  sweet and sour pork with pineapple, rice and vegetables then for the starter a chicken and jicama salad, which I had to look up, apparently a jicama is a vegetable from Mexico then fruit, Haagen Dazs ice cream, and warm bread and butter to round things off and ginger ale to drink The cabin then stayed dark for the rest of the flight prety much, and I ended up watching Mulan If you get hungry or thirsty there's a drink and snack stand in the galley, plus you can just ask the crew to get you either cup noodles or a Hong Kong egg tart and I got an egg tart which was a nice mid-flight snack and all I needed as the two main meals were tasty and filling enough then right before landing the crew came round and handed out these Palmier biscuits which were also very nice so overall a fantastic flight when it came to food and Cathay Pacific clearly know how to  keep you well fed throughout a super long flight We then began our descent into a very overcast London which brings me to the very last feature of this review, the WiFi all I can really say is that it exists, and it was too expensive for me to bother trying it would be nice to see them catch up to many competitors who offer free WiFi Like Qatar Airways or British Airways but that's pretty much the only criticism I have for Cathay today... and now the landing... it was raining when we landed so the window instantly fogged up but to summarise, if you couldn't tell already, I just really like Cathay Pacific and they're probably my favourite airline and this super long haul flight confirmed that for me and as someone who mainly flies Oneworld Airlines, Cathay are my airline of choice when flying to Asia if the price is right also this was a personal record for me, it took maybe 4 minutes from stepping off the plane to passing through customs and there was no queue at all for immigration so that was very satisfying, and I just made a quick stop at M&S to buy these cookies,  which are the best in the world by the way, before heading home I used miles to pay for this flight and it cost a very reasonable 31,000 Avios plus £81 and sure, not everyone will be as lucky as me and get an almost empty flight to relax on but I'm just judging based on my experience on this flight so I'm giving Cathay an 82.5% and putting them up to a 10/10 on my airline tier list, the same rank as Singapore Airlines, who are maybe a bit better if I'm being completely objective but either way, I think Cathay have earned their place at the top of my list Now if you're looking for something else to watch then check out my recent review of Oman Air's Business Class a super underrated airline with one of the best Business seats out there and some fantastic food as well as part of this trip I also flew Oman Air's 787 Economy, and Cathay Pacific's short haul A330 and I have many more videos in the pipeline so don't forget to like and subscribe to stay up to date with all that! thanks a lot for watching and good bye!

Farrell and Australian pilot Sydney de Kantzow. The airline began with a single Douglas DC-3 aircraft nicknamed Betsy, flying routes between Hong Kong, Manila, Bangkok, and Singapore. reviews.transcript_full: Today I'm flying from Bangkok to Hong Kong on a Cathay Pacific Airbus A330 This plane is definitely on the more dated side and features the oldest cabin in Cathay's fleet but hopefully in this video you'll see why even when you're not in their most modern cabin Cathay Pacific still offer a very solid experience... I started off my journey by taking the airport train from the centre of Bangkok to Suvarnabhumi Airport which is quick and only cost me 15 Thai Baht, or about 35 British Pence In the airport itself it's huge and somewhat overcrowded, and this is actually my first time flying out of this airport so I can't say I'm that familiar with it but my overall review of it is that it's just fine The Cathay Check-in area is in the S Zone and 2 hours before departure there was barely any queue and check-in was very quick Impressive as Cathay operate about 7 flights a day from here, mostly on massive aircraft like the Boeing 777  or Airbus A330 I was on today Airport security was pretty slow as they seemed to be doing a secondary inspection on almost everyone me included, but I'm pretty sure that was because I had a big cake and some fruit in my bag so it was probably my own fault once through to the departure zone there are loads of shops and restaurants and these cute little cleaning robots but the whole place is laid out in a few long thin corridors absolutely crammed with people and it's a big building so walking anywhere takes a while  One cool thing I noticed though which I haven't seen at other airports is the departure board which says how long it takes to reach each gate, and the direction you need to go to get there anyway, I made it to our gate and whilst watching this Myanmar Airways plane our plane for today just happened to appear out of nowhere, what are the chances hey? and some more perfect timing, that's another Cathay Pacific plane taking off in the background as ours parks at the gate Today we're flying on an 18 year old Airbus A330-300 with 262 seats in total 223 of which are in Economy class, and the Airbus A330 is really the workhorse of Cathay's short haul fleet, with them operating 43 in total making them the largest operator of he type in the world and as these old planes age out, they'll eventually be replaced with the much newer Airbus A330neo It was soon my turn to board, and whilst walking down the jetbridge another Cathay A330 was pulling up alongside showing just how many flights they do to bangkok Now, before we step on board, here are the stats and route map for today's flight, where a 40 minute late departure would see us land 20 minutes late in Hong Kong and all the pilots said about the delay is it was due to Chinese airspace restrictions which I'm slightly dubious of as I feel every flight I've ever taken in or around China has said the same thing but in anycase, here is the plane's cabin, and as someone who always sits by the window the A330 is probably my favourite plane to fly thanks to its 2-4-2 layout I chose seat 61A here which was free to select and the thing I like about this plane is I only have to climb over one person to reach the aisle so it feels much less claustrophobic if you're in one of the window aisles like I was today Now looking at the seat itself, legroom is good with 32" of seat pitch, much better than the 29 or 30" you'll see on most narrowbody aircraft It has a nifty folding tray table which folds out like this Then a small storage shelf just above that... and a little drink holder so you can have a drink without needing the table down The screen is pretty small at 9", maybe one of the most noticeable flaw of this slightly dated cabin and as you'll see shortly, the touchscreen is pretty laggy, but it's still perfectly usable another noticeable thing is the seatback is actually quite short I'm only 5'6" and you can see my head pokes above the headrest, so taller people might need to crank the headrest all he way up to be comfortable The headphones meanwhile are some of the best I've used in Economy, also, the crew went through the cabin offering blankets, I didn't bother get one though and the seat back pocket has plenty of little storage pouches so very convenient Now for the TV, it has Cathay Pacific's award-winning IFE system with a really good selection of movies, tv and games in fact, it was rated the best entertainment system in the world by Skytrax in 2025 However, on the A330 the tv is a bit too old to run it properly, so you can see here it's just a bit slow and laggy not an issue on their newer planes but it is noticeable here, especially coupled with the small-ish screen we started pushing back about 30 minutes behind schedule and the safety video started playing so here's that... one of the better safety videos I've seen actually and shows a nice bit of Hong Kong culture Now getting ready for takeoff the sun was just about to set which made for some very scenic views,  so stay tuned for that coming up in a second... Despite being a short 2.5 hour flight, this is Asia we're flying in so of course we had a full meal service I can't remember exactly but I'm pretty sure this was pork noodles with warm bread,  a fruit bowl and their signature Haagen Dazs ice cream on the side Everything was good and it's just a solid service for a short haul flight plus you get actual metal cutlery and Haagen Dazs is a premium touch There's also an inflight magazine with some interesting articles in both Chinese and English, especially this one about the cats of Hong Kong and speaking of cats, here's mine, he wants you to like and subscribe to support the channel and help fund his ice cream addiction back to the magazine though, it has a cool route map which I always love to see and they have a bit about their fleet, which I amusingly noticed already includes the 777X even though it's been delayed for years with no end in sight last of all as we approach Hong Kong for landing, they do have inflight WiFi but you have to pay for it so I didn't bother Worth noting that Business, First and Diamond status passengers get it for free though anyway, here's the landing in a dark but somewhat light-polluted Hong Kong also I noticed as we were landing a big gap in the fencing and lighting around the runway and that was actually due the the Air ACT Boeing 747 which had crashed into the sea 2 weeks before this flight and I guess they hadn't rebuilt the fence at that point so you could still see the big gap So as we disembark the plane it's time for my final thoughts... Cathay Pacific just offer a very solid shorthaul experience on their Airbus A330 It might not be as snazzy and modern as their A321neo or A350  but it's comfortable and the inflight service is top notch the price was very competitive too, being about 20% cheaper than a similar time with Thai Airways and similar to budget airlines like Hong Kong Express when you factor in things like food, seat selection and baggage costs... So I'll just give them a solid 80% score accross the board and on my airline tier list they keep their spot as a 10/10 airline in my opinion,  mainly because in the past I've had some really good experiences with them and even though this flight wasn't perfect, it was still very solid for a short haul trip now if you want to see something that was a 10/10 experience then check out the flight I took after this one a 14 hour flight from Hong Kong to London in their Airbus A350-1000 Economy Class which was just an exceptional flight in every way I'll also have reviews of Oman Air, Jet2, Air Europa and Air France to name a few coming in the next few weeks so subscribe to keep up to date with that like and leave a comment if you enjoyed this video thanks a lot for watching and good bye

As passengers settle in, welcome drinks were served by the Cathay cabin crew and today I chose the orange juice. If you want to look outside, there are cameras at the front as well as on the vertical stabilizer. A final thing worth noting is the Cathay Shop, which is a digital catalog of items available to purchase on board. Looking at the extra seat controls, press firmly on the button and the indicated area will activate. As an example, the leg supports have been expanded, which provide a comfortable place to rest your legs. As you may have noticed, metal cutlery is provided, which is awesome. Moving around the tray, next we have the tuna and saffron salad, which was surprisingly good. For the fruit bowl, it was very fresh, sweet, and offered some variety. The cheese and crackers were tasty, as you would expect with cheese sourced from New Zealand. I forgot to mention, but if you want to see the entire menu for the flights, each premium economy passenger will receive a booklet. Here is tonight's full menu. After the tables were cleared, I went to take a look at the premium economy laboratories, which were kept clean. However, offers no difference over regular economy ones. As the hours go by and the sun travels across the west, day becomes night and the cabin descends into a very calm and quiet atmosphere. For the second meal service, I chose the steamed halibut fish with vegetables. This came with a side of fruits, and for drinks, I chose orange juice. Once again, I found this meal to be fantastic. Fast forward to around 40 minutes left, the cabin crew came around to prepare everyone for landing. As we make our way into Perth, let's go through today's ratings. reviews.transcript_full: Today I'm taking you on one of the longest flights I've done recently, flying Qantas from Sydney to Dallas on the Airbus A380. This was a long haul economy flight, and a lot of people ask me about it, and I took notes the entire way, so I can give you guys an honest review. Okay, before we get started, this flight came right after a cruise around New Zealand. So, I boarded the flight well rested and really curious to see if Qantas actually lives up to its reputation. Qantas gets a lot of hype, at least that's what I'm seeing, especially when it comes to their A380. And by the end of this video, I'm going to share whether I think it is deserved, plus three important watch outs you're going to want to know before you book this exact flight. So, I want to know if you've ever flown Qantas before. Drop your experience down in the comments. I'd love to see if your Qantas flight lived up to the hype, too. This was a Qantas Airbus A380 800 flying nonstop from Sydney, Australia, to Dallas/Fort Worth. The flight time was 15 hours and 25 minutes, and we departed about 20 minutes late, around 2:30 in the afternoon. So, you guys, this aircraft is massive. It is a full two-level plane, and it was not at capacity, which definitely impacted the experience. So, before boarding, I stopped off quickly at the Qantas First Lounge. I have One World Emerald status through American Airlines Executive Platinum, and the lounge was outstanding. And I don't always get access to the first lounges, so this was a real treat for me. I had a lovely lunch there, and I even got a complimentary 20-minute foot massage, which felt like a total luxury before such a long flight. So, I want to know if you're kind of a lounge person. Do you hit the lounge before a long flight? Which one do you like to go to, or are you kind of a person that just goes straight to the gate? I'm curious which approach that you prefer. So, boarding took place at gate eight in Sydney and it was very organized and well staffed. So, Qantas boards by number and the lower level of the aircraft actually boarded first, which made the boarding process really smooth and efficient and I was in that first group cuz I was on the bottom floor of the aircraft. My seat was actually 52H. It's an aisle seat at the front of the economy cabin on the lower level one row behind the bulkhead and right behind first class and kind of the galley. So, I had this entire row to myself, which meant I could enjoy the window for takeoff and if I wanted to to stretch out to nap throughout the flight. You guys, so good. I thought about choosing the bulkhead, which is like the front row in economy, but ultimately I didn't do that because the armrest don't lift up and the seats feel kind of tight and if you get really lucky and there's nobody else there, you can't lay across at all. I'm going to come back to that later when we talk about some of the watch outs here, but I just wanted to mention that. So, what do you prefer on long haul flights? Are you front of economy? Are you bulkhead, back of the plane? Are you first class, business class? Let me know your go-to spot. I'm usually an economy girl, but I love to try to get as close to the front of that cabin if I can. So, I was seated just in front of the wing near the engines, but the takeoff and landing were so smooth. We had zero turbulence at all and you guys, honestly, the seat belt sign, I think, was off for almost the entire 15-hour flight and the cabin on this aircraft is extremely quiet, which I had read was the case. It was so nice not to hear that constant, really loud, reverberating engine noise. And like I mentioned, I had those two windows I could kind of see halfway out each one of them, which was really nice. The cabin temperature was a little bit warm while we were on the ground in Sydney, but about an hour into the flight it kind of cooled down a little bit and stayed more comfortable throughout. As I would walk back to the restrooms, I did know that the uh noticed that the cabin got a little bit cooler. So, as you were going towards the back of the temperature came down a little bit. Now, the cabin noise level was really low, like I said, exactly what you'd expect on an A380 out of the aircraft itself. And one of the biggest positives on this aircraft was the seat recline. You guys, look at this. I mean, this is excellent. It makes a huge difference on a long-haul flight. You can really get that seat back. Now, charging in the seats was a little bit tricky. My US plug actually worked to charge, and I was really glad I brought a long cable because the charger's kind of down low between the seats close to the floor. Now, I didn't even find the USB port in the armrest until the very end of the flight, but the USB charging did not work on my seat, and I heard a lot of people saying that it did not work in their seat. So, it is best to pack a traditional charging setup with like a cable and actual, you know, little hub thingy just in case. Let's talk about entertainment. The in-flight entertainment system was okay, but nothing really special. It's controlled with a remote and the touchscreen option is available, but it worked really inconsistently and with a noticeable delay. In fact, I noticed people banging on their touchscreens to get them to work, and that is really unpleasant for the person in front of you. It feels like a thumping banging sound. So, I think this aircraft needs a little bit of repair. And compared to my recent Japan Airlines flight, the screen quality felt really small and pretty poor. With that said, though, there was actually a good selection of content, including movies from HBO, Paramount. They had Australian films, music, and lots more. I watched a full two movies and appreciated the first-run selection. I saw a lot of people watching a lot of movies on this particular flight. There was also a moving map that showed airspeed, altitude, like time to destination, and even a sky cam view from above the aircraft, which was really, really cool. And the system also very clearly displayed meal and drink options with detailed choices, which was great. So, how do you entertain yourself when you're flying? Are you like a a movie person? Do you listen to music on your own device? Do you use the seatback, or do you just try to conk out? I'm kind of trying to see what's most popular here. Now, the restrooms were a little larger than average, especially compared to like American Airlines, but smaller, I'd say, than Japan Airlines, but they were not cleaned a single time during the 15-hour flight. Yeah, they replaced the toilet paper, but trash overflowed, the floor became literally sticky, like your feet would stick and unstick when you walked in there, and the overall cleanliness really declined throughout the flight. I just couldn't believe it. The service overall was professional, but it was kind of, I guess you could say, minimal. The crew did their jobs, but there was no explanation of like restroom locations if you're in this cabin or that. There was really no overview of how the self-serve snacks worked. The captain said something about it for like 1 second, and there just wasn't a lot of proactive communication. And if I'm being honest, some of the interactions came off as a little bit snobby. >> [gasps] >> But then some of the crew were warm and friendly, so it was kind of a mixed bag. People are people, it's just the way it is. Now, let's talk about the food. I had high expectations for this. On the way to New Zealand, I flew American Airlines from Dallas to Auckland, and the snack that they gave me at mid-flight, you guys, it was like a raw stromboli, like they'd forgot to bake it. It was like raw dough. So, my expectations for Qantas were kind of high because I thought, well, I mean, it's got to be better than this, right? So, here's how everything worked. About 30 minutes into the flight, we were handed a bottle of water, which was great. A lot of times you're thirsty and you don't want to wait forever, followed immediately by a snack and beverage service. A very early dinner was served around 3:45. I mean, that's early if you're thinking the flight just took off. The main options were pumpkin tortellini, a beef with mustard gravy, or cold chicken salad along with a selection of Australian wines. I chose the beef. It was served hot, but it was fatty, it was kind of bland, and the gravy tasted like cheap brown gravy, not like a mustard gravy. The meal came with bread and cheese and crackers, but there was no salad or fruit. They gave us a dessert of an ice cream bar, which was really delicious, but I don't know, I just wasn't in the mood for it. In hindsight, I probably would have selected the salad main cuz I saw it and it looked really nice and tasty and fresh. Had like edamame in there, looked really good. There were also some self-serve snacks and drinks toward the back of the plane, but it was really easy to miss that because they didn't talk much about it, and the drinks were like put away. If you didn't know, you wouldn't be able to grab them. Later in the flight, there was a snack walk-through around 8:00 p.m. It was a little chicken toasty. Oh, I'm sorry. The snack walk-through was just like little packaged snacks and some waters. And then around 10:00 p.m., we got a chicken toasty, which tasted great. It was served hot and not raw like my weird American Airlines strong bully. Then they had a full breakfast before landing at 3:30 in the morning with a choice of your main could be frittata or fruit. Everybody then also got a muffin, coffee, and a yogurt pod on the little plate. That was great. I'm sorry, the coffee would have been on request, but the the yogurt and the muffin were included. The breakfast was decent and hearty, and the yogurt was really, really good. I'd say the coffee, though, was really bad. It was watery, lukewarm, so I ended up having to grab a coffee when I landed in the airport to trick my body into thinking, "Okay, it's like morning time." So, for those of you out there who fly a lot, I want to know what is the best or worst economy meal that you have ever had on a flight. Share it below. I really love to read the flight food stories. Now, for those watch-outs about this flight specifically from Sydney to Dallas. First, I would not recommend boarding the flight super hungry. The food is fine, but it's not especially filling or exciting, and timing kind of matters on a flight this long, so I would bring some snacks. Second, be very, very cautious when you're booking bulkhead seats, the ones up at the very front of the economy cabin. The seats are narrower, remember those armrests don't lift, and there is a lot of foot traffic and galley noise cuz you're right by the galley a lot of times. Also, if you see baby icons on the seat map, book those nearby rows carefully. They have these pull-down bassinets and a lot of times toddlers, babies, families are traditionally seated here. And in my experience, because these families sometimes will congregate here and sit here, the extra space in front of them means the kids are going to roam about, run about, and that can happen. On the flip side, if you are traveling with kids or as a family, this can be a great place for you to sit as long as you understand the front row armrests don't move, and your little ones cannot nap. I saw a family with a baby moving from the bulkhead to an empty row behind them because they couldn't let their baby nap. So, just something for you to be aware of. And this again has happened multiple times on my flights where the little ones are up front. So, if you want to sleep, I would not recommend booking at the front of the aircraft. I'm going to change my strategy on this. Now, the back of the lower deck of this aircraft actually tends to be really quiet, and you're not really sacrificing space. So, move yourself back there if you're going for quiet. Third, Qantas does not allow power banks, you guys. They mention it several times in their overhead announcements. So, you're supposed to rely on that in-seat power. You need to bring long charging cables or charging your phones and your devices might be really frustrating due to the location of the charging spots close to the floor, and your USB charging in your armrest may not work. All right, my overall thoughts on this, you guys, on the flight. I got to tell you, that seat recline alone makes this a good aircraft for long-haul flights. The flight was quiet. It was smooth. It was comfortable. But, beyond that, nothing truly wowed me about Qantas in this case. It's a solid experience, but it's not one that completely lives up to the hype. Now, if you want a comparison, be sure to check out my Japan Airlines flight review. That one is from Dallas to Haneda Airport, which is Tokyo. And also, for my adventures before this flight, be sure to watch my New Zealand cruise content, which I'm going to link to down below. Now, I want to hear from you. Would you fly Qantas again based on what you've heard? Comment yes or no, and tell me why. I'll be reading all your thoughts. And until next time, we'll see you on the high seas or in the friendly skies. Bye-bye.

reviews.transcript_full: Does Emirates really have one of the best economycl class products in the world? Buckle up because you're about to find out. Let's get started. [Music] Welcome to London Heathro Terminal 3. I'm very excited to fly the iconic Emirates A380 economy class to Dubai today and share this journey with you guys. Our journey today begins at the Emirates check-in area. Most passengers are asked to use these selfservice kiosks where you can print your own boarding pass and back tags. This area is super crowded and feels extremely chaotic. The infrastructure of Terminal 3 is pretty bad. Old, small, and with low ceilings. So, you can't fully blame Emirates for the check-in experience. Now, straight to security. Follow me. Security at Heathrow can be a test of patience, and today was no exception. Okay guys, time to head to the gate to board our Emirates flight EK32. Let's go. And here we have it. No introduction needed. The iconic Emirates A380 800. Have you ever flown on an A380? Let me know in the comments. Something I noticed is that everything is ready to guarantee an ontime departure. The cargo door is open. The tug is in position for push back. And there you have the crew getting to the aircraft from that back door. The Emirates lounge is conveniently located right next to the A380 gates, so you can maximize the time you spend at the lounge. Pre-boarding started around 80 minutes before departure. There are no boarding groups, so you can proceed as soon as the gate opens. Guys, look at that beautiful aircraft, isn't it? Did you know that Emirates has over 100 Airbus A380s in their fleet? It's by far the world's largest A380 operator. Very punctual boarding starting 50 minutes before departure. All passengers are called to board at the same time. Time to board this A380. Follow me. Today we have a lovely window seat in the front section of the lower deck. First impressions, amazing. It's easily the most luxurious and spacious economy seat in the skies. And here we have some goodies waiting for us. We have a small pillow, a blanket, and the if headphones. The Emirates economy class seat is very comfy and elegant. The texture of the seat is very soft and pleasant. The headrest is super plush and comfortable, and you can adjust the position and height like this. Speaking of comfort, this seat offers plenty of space for a long flight with a width of 18 in and a very generous pitch of 32 in. One more inch than most airlines. The armrest has the seat number over here, which is very handy. And here's the button to recline your seat to a maximum of 4 in. Economy seats are equipped with a 13 in HD touchscreen. There is also this remote with a touchcreen to control your IFB. You have a USB port over here to charge your devices and the port for your headphones. You will also find a power socket by the screen, which is a much better place than underneath your seat. Now, let's see what's inside the seat pocket. a 380 safety card, a guide to the entertainment and shopping on board, and a waste bag. Before push back, the crew came to deliver some special goodies for the kids on board. Okay, guys, it's time to fasten our seat belts and get ready for push back. Guys, if you enjoyed this video, drop a like now, share with your friends, and subscribe for more great content. Ready for takeoff. You might be surprised to hear that the A380 has the quietest cabin environment of any modern jet. It's even quieter than newer generation aircraft. The pillow provided is comfortable but relatively small and thin in line with what other airlines offer. The Emirates blanket is quite soft and warm and seems relatively new. Always great when you don't get a super worn out blanket, isn't it? And here we have the economy class headphones. These are the most comfortable headphones I've ever used in economy class. They are lightweight and the ear pads are very soft and comfortable. Now, let's explore the if Emirates is well known for having the most extensive entertainment catalog on board. The ice if is easy to navigate. It has an intuitive layout and the screen is very responsive. The selection of movies is endless, featuring hundreds of movies from all over the world, including recent releases. You can also enjoy loads of content from HBO, Paramount, Discovery, and more. But let me tell you, the coolest feature is live TV. You can watch live news and even live sports. Guys, I can already smell the food, so it's now time to pick a good movie for tonight. You can use this remote to control your screen and even watch content directly on it. In economy, the seats are very close to the screen, so I find this remote a bit redundant. Before dinner, the crew pop by to offer complimentary instant photos for families. Let's now take a look at the tray table. It's a classic economy class by folding table. Clean, stable, and adjustable. Oh, and here's a cup holder for your drinks. The dinner service was a bit slow. It took the crew over 2 hours to start serving dinner. Here we have it. I went for the chicken biryani and it looks pretty good, right? The tray is loaded with different things, but it's well presented and all fits nicely within the tray. As a starter, we have this potato salad, a bread roll, some cheddar cheese, crackers, and for dessert, we have this huge cookie with Belgian chocolate, a nice small chocolate, and a chocolate brownie topped with salted caramel. Emirates provides stainless steel cutlery in all travel classes which is lovely and a wet wipe is also provided. This biryani is excellent. The chicken is succulent, the rice is perfectly cooked and the spice level hits the mark perfectly. The potato salad is not my thing. Too much sauce. Dessert. Check this out, guys. The texture of the brownie is superb. Super fluffy and the caramel goes so well with it. I couldn't finish the cookie, but it's also of very high quality. I'm so full. Tea and coffee service started shortly after clearing out the trays. The flight time between London and Dubai is just over 6 hours and I didn't get any sleep despite the cabin being fairly quiet. I spent most of the journey enjoying the great selection of movies on board. The crew popped by multiple times to offer water and juice. Always much appreciated. Breakfast was served very early, two hours before arrival. I wasn't particularly hungry, and to be honest, the breakfast didn't look very appealing. You get this muffin, and you can choose a vegan or a cheese hot sandwich. I wonder why airlines don't serve more healthy options like some fruits and yogurt. That would make me so happy. So, how was my Emirates economy class flight? Overall, I'm super impressed with the experience. The airport experience wasn't the best, but not much you can do if you fly from Heath Terminal 3. The seat is excellent from the comfort and dimensions to the design. Small details like having a power socket right under the screen make a difference. Entertainment on board is amazing. Emirates clearly has the best I in disguise. I have mixed feelings about the food. The main meal was delicious and the quality and quantity of the food were spoton. Breakfast was very underwhelming though. The cabin environment was perfect. The aircraft was very clean and the crew were extremely welcoming and attentive. What do you guys think? Have you ever flown with Emirates? Leave a comment and let me know. And that's all for today, guys. I hope you enjoyed today's video. And if you did, check out the videos on screen. See you in the next one.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome back to the channel. Today we're flying Qatar Airways economy from Doha to Cape Town. We'll be trying their special meal options, Hindu and vegan. Are these meals worth choosing or is the regular menu the better option? Let's find out if the world's best economy class really lives up to the hype. As you arrive at Doha airport, you'll notice there are two entrances, one for premium class and one for economy. Hopefully, we'll get to review that business class experience sometime soon. But today, let's dive into the economy class journey and see what it has to [Music] offer. Doha airport is one of my favorite airports. second only to Singapore. As you enter, you're greeted by an enormous yellow teddy bear lounging under a giant lamp, an iconic sculpture here. It was actually created by Swiss artist Bers Fischer and was bought by a member of the Qatari royal family. The bear brings a playful touch to the airport's sleek design, making it memorable and unique for travelers. [Music] Dova airport is massive with huge open corridors leading right to the jet bridge. Let's take a quick look around the seat as we get settled in. [Music] We pulled back right on time and everything is running smoothly as we taxi to the runway. With the engines powering up, we're now ready for takeoff and on our way to Cape [Music] Town. The takeoff was smooth and we said goodbye to the brightly lit city of Doha below. If you ever have a layover of at least 6 hours, I highly recommend taking a transit tour of the city. It's a great way to get a quick taste of Doha, even if you don't have much time to explore. [Music] The Orex1 entertainment system on Qar Airways really stands out in the cabin. With over 4,000 options, there's no shortage of movies, TV shows, music, and games to choose from. The large, highresolution screens offer a sharp, vibrant display, making movie watching or gaming a pleasure. Navigating through the system is straightforward thanks to the intuitive interface, and I found the built-in controller easy to use. Whether you're in the mood for a blockbuster film or just some relaxing music, Orex 1 delivers a seamless entertainment experience that certainly helps pass the [Music] time. Please like, share, and subscribe the channel for more content. [Music] Dinner was served shortly after takeoff and I decided to go with the Hindu meal option which is a non-vegetarian Indian selection. The meal included a salad, the main course, dessert and bread. The bread unfortunately didn't impress me much. It lacked flavor. On the other hand, the salad was decent while the dessert was just okay. Nothing to write home about. The main course, however, was a pleasant surprise. It consisted of rice, dal, and chicken curry. The curry had a nice depth of flavor and was packed with surprisingly rich Indian spices, giving it an authentic touch that I didn't expect from an in-flight meal. Overall, while the bread and dessert didn't stand out, the main course certainly made up for it with its bold and flavorful taste. My wife tried the vegan meal, and that left a lot to be desired. While I appreciate the effort to cater to different dietary needs, the actual meal was underwhelming. The main course lacked variety with a somewhat repetitive flavor profile that leaned heavily on tomatobased dishes. The noodles were bland. The sides, like salad and fruit, were fresh, but overall, the meal didn't feel as satisfying as I'd hoped for a long haul flight. All right, here's a quick look at the restroom in Qatar Airways economy class. It's a pretty standard design, but it's kept clean and functional. You've got your basics: soap, lotion, even a light fragrance. Sometimes they actually do a good job keeping it stocked and fresh during the flight, which is definitely appreciated on a longer route like this one. And I'd say it's roomy enough to move around without feeling too cramped, which is a nice touch for economy class. A snack was served before landing, and I went with the Hindu meal option again. The taste was definitely on point, full of rich flavors and spices that I appreciated. However, the presentation left a lot to be desired. The meal was a bit messy to eat, and it wasn't as neatly arranged as I would have liked, which made it harder to enjoy without making a bit of a mess. While the taste was great, a cleaner presentation could have made the whole experience better. [Music] My wife went with the vegan option again, and this time it came with tofu and some other ingredients that we honestly couldn't identify. It definitely fell short of our expectations, but maybe that's because we're not true vegans. I imagine people who are more accustomed to vegan meals might appreciate it more, but for us, it just didn't hit the mark. My recommendation, unless you're a dedicated vegan, I'd say skip it. As we wrap up the flight, here's a quick recap of my experience with Qatar Airways economy class on this DOA to Cape Town journey. From the moment we boarded, the service was attentive, and the seat was surprisingly comfortable for longhaul travel. The entertainment system with its wide selection of movies, TV shows, and music helped pass the time effortlessly. The meals were a mixed bag. The Hindu meal was flavorful, though a bit messy in presentation, while the vegan option didn't quite meet expectations, especially for those not strictly vegan. Overall, Qatar Airways offers a solid economycl class product with excellent service and comfort. The food could use a bit of refinement, especially for special meal options, but the overall experience was good. I definitely recommend this airline if you're flying long haul, especially if you're looking for great in-flight entertainment and solid customer service. [Music]

reviews.transcript_full: Cathay Pacific is well regarded for its comfortable and high-quality economy class service, offering a solid experience for both short and long-haul flights. Seat comfort and legroom. Cathay Pacific offers a seat pitch of 31 to 32 inches and a seat width of 17.5 to 18 inches with seating arrangements in 3 to 4 to 3 or 2 to 4 to 2 configurations, depending on the aircraft. While legroom is adequate for most, taller passengers may feel a bit cramped. The seats feature moderate recline, adjustable headrests, and are equipped with pillows and blankets on long flights for added comfort. In-flight entertainment (IFE), the personalized screens, 10 to 12 inches, offer a wide selection of movies, TV shows, games, and music. Wi-Fi is available on many long-haul flights, though it's often pricey. Passengers also have access to USB charging ports and power outlets, ensuring devices stay charged throughout the flight. Food and beverage meals in economy class include a mix of Asian, Western, and vegetarian options with complimentary soft drinks, wine, and beer. Special meals, e.g., gluten-free, halal, can be requested 24 hours in advance. Overall, food quality is above average for economy class, and service is efficient. Service. Cathay Pacific's cabin crew is known for being friendly, attentive, and professional, making sure passengers are comfortable throughout the flight. Boarding is well organized with priority boarding for premium passengers. Cabin ambiance. The cabin is modern and clean with calming lighting and good air quality. Restrooms are regularly cleaned, and the overall atmosphere is conducive to relaxation, especially on long-haul flights. Baggage allowance. Economy class passengers are typically allowed one checked bag, up to 23 kg, and one carry-on bag, up to 7 kg. A small personal item is also permitted, offering enough space for most travelers' belongings. Final verdict. reviews.transcript_full: Today, I will show you what it is like to fly ANA on their premium economy product, including the seat, amenities, and everything else in between. But to start, we must go to where my journey begins, Tokyo Haneda Airport. Hello and welcome to Tokyo Haneda Airport, one of two major airports in the Tokyo Metro region. Out of the two, Haneda is the older one, having started operations back in 1931. Today, it boasts four asphalt runways, three passenger terminals, and connections to Japan's robust railway network and the Tokyo Monorail. Since I woke up a little later than I would have liked it this morning, I quickly go through security with just enough time to visit the ANA lounge. Let's head there now. Before I enter, I must preface that as a premium economy passenger, I'm only allowed to enter the regular ANA lounge. The suite lounge is reserved for first-class passengers, as well as ANA Diamond Service Members and lounge access card holders of ANA's Million Miler program. >> As I sit down to enjoy my view and eat my breakfast, I check my phone and realize it's time to go. If not, I will miss my flight. Speaking of my flight, let's take a quick look at our route for today. Today's 13-hour and 10-minute flight will see us leaving the Tokyo metro area and Japan as a whole to cross the Pacific before flying over Alaska and Canada to reach New York. We will reach a high of 37,000 ft and top out at a ground speed of around 550 kn. >> Hello. After getting on board, I pass business class and make my way to my seat, 25 Alpha. Let's take a quick look around our seat. The legroom is quite decent, coming in at 38 in or 97 cm of pitch. Stored in this wall-mounted pocket in front of you, you'll find slippers, headphones, a disposable paper bag, and a safety manual. By your armrest, you'll find two things: a small indent to put a drink, as well as a hidden table that folds out of the armrest itself. Moving upward to your right, you'll find an adjustable reading light. Here are the various controls for the seat's footrest and recline. Located here is the remote that controls the in-flight entertainment. More on that in a bit. Each seat has access to one international power outlet. Above the seat, you'll find individual air vents, as well as a personal reading light. And to your left, you'll find an adjustable window blind. Lastly, let's go over the miscellaneous stuff provided. We have a pillow and a blanket, an eye and face mask, and I can't go on without mentioning these two smaller storage areas located on the middle armrest. Overall, a solid seat with good amenities. Before long, we are pushing back and the safety video starts to play. At this time, I would also like to highlight the fact that 99.3% of all viewers of this channel aren't subscribed. So, hit that big red button if you haven't had the chance already. We are now ready for takeoff. Please make sure that your seats are securely fastened. Thank you. >> To start, the crew asked the passengers for a choice of drink and passed out a bag of snack mix. Now for the actual meal. I opted for the hash beef simmered in red wine with carrots, string beans, and pasta. Along with that, I got ANA's original bread and three other side dishes along with some frozen hard Häagen-Dazs ice cream for dessert. Real silverware was provided as well, which I really appreciate. But the food just kept on coming. A few hours later, I was served some sort of Japanese biscuit, another drink, and some cup ramen. Let's take a quick look at the bathrooms. Nothing special here, but nothing glaringly bad, either. Everything was well-stocked and things were in working order. >> As the sun rises over the Canadian prairies, let's take a closer look at the in-flight entertainment. Let's start with the most utilitarian function on it, the in-flight map. It works decently well and has everything you need to stay informed about your flight. Now to the actual entertainment. ANA has a decent selection of Western and Japanese movies and TV shows, as well as some other tourist-oriented videos about Japan. There is also a decent selection of audio programs and music to listen to, as well. If you, like me, have an interest in keeping up with current events, ANA has Sky Live News on standby just for you. Not exactly the thing that comes to mind when you think about staying informed, but I guess beggars can't be choosers. However, keep in mind there is also NHK and BBC available, but I'm not sure if these are live broadcasts. Time for some breakfast. I opted for the grilled fish served with fruit, yogurt, and some apple juice. >> As we descended to New York, what are my thoughts about ANA's premium economy product, and more importantly, what was the cost? Firstly, I really enjoyed myself on this flight. The seat was perfect for my needs, the in-flight entertainment had always something interesting to watch, and the food was quite good. The bathrooms were clean, and the cabin crew were very nice and attentive. The price, though, wasn't cheap. This flight was booked as a round trip, which totaled out at around $2,800. However, with all the extra bells and whistles that come with premium economy, including a better meal, select lounge access, dedicated check-in desks, and priority baggage over economy passengers, I think it is a viable option to consider if one has the extra money to spend.

Noise cancelling headphones are provided ensuring a great audio visual experience. Three, cabin experience. The premium economy cabin is separated from economy, providing a more private and quiet space. The cabin lighting is soothing and the service feels more personalized with a better crew to passenger ratio. Flyfi app highlight realtime flight tracker during your ANA premium economy journey. Enhance your experience with the FlyFi apps realtime flight tracker. You can monitor your flight's route, altitude, and speed in real time along with weather updates and estimated arrival time. It keeps you informed and engaged throughout your flight. Four, dining and beverages passengers are served a premium dining menu, including Japanese and Western options. Meals are elegantly presented with fresh ingredients and flavorful choices. Premium beverages, including wine, sake, and spirits are also available. Additional perks, premium economy passengers enjoy priority boarding, extra baggage allowance, and access to ANA's lounges at select airports, making the travel experience smoother and more luxurious.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to Plane Stuff! Today’s flight review will take us aboard Delta Air Lines newest fleet member, the A321neo, from Los Angeles to Minneapolis. In the next video I'll cover the onward flight on an almost 31 year old A320. Make sure to subscribe so you don't miss it! This is my first narrated video, or even video of this type in general, so it will probably be a little rough. Please do let me know what you think in the comments below so I can improve! Flight details can be found in the description, and I hope you enjoy! Welcome to LAX. It's very early in the morning and I've just been dropped off in front of Delta’s Terminal 3. LAX has 9 terminals in total, Delta occupies Terminal 2 and 3, although all check-ins for Delta now go through 3. I’m not checking bags on today's flight and already have my boarding pass, so I’m able to head straight to TSA, which is really quick at this time in the morning. It looks like we'll be going out of Gate 37B, so time to get walking! LAX is in the middle of a massive overhaul and work on terminal 3 was just completed shortly before filming. It feels very clean and roomy, although it has no moving walkways and some pretty long distances, which may be annoying to some. The food options here are a little limited, however all LAX terminals are now interconnected thanks to the ongoing overhaul... ...so you can always make the hike to other terminals for plenty more options. I decided to grab some snacks at this Hudson Nonstop, which uses cameras to track what you pick up and automatically charge you without the need for a cash register. Here is our aircraft today! N512DE. This aircraft was delivered to Delta in December 2022, making it just 8 months old at the time of filming. The A321neo is the newest member of Delta's ongoing fleet renewal... ...alongside the A220, A330neo, A350, newer 737-900s, and the upcoming 737 MAX, which are replacing or already have replaced many of Delta's older fleet members. One thing I didn't mention earlier about Terminal 3 is the music. The music here is pretty overwhelming, especially near the windows where I tend to sit. I think I can safely say this music just doesn't work at 7am, and even less so at 5am as I’ve previously experienced. Well after about an hour of enduring the music, it’s time to board. Delta boards in 10 groups. As with most full service carriers, Delta starts by boarding premium cabins and elite status holders... ...and after that they’ll move into the Main Cabin, which is split between status holders in Main 1, this will be our group, then Main 2 and 3, and finally Basic Economy. Gate Agent: In the general boarding lane I'd like to continue the boarding process by inviting Main 1, Main 1 welcome aboard. It looks like this aircraft has Delta's new free WIFI! We’ll check that out after takeoff. Delta A321neos currently have one seat layout, with a total of 194 seats. The front of the cabin has 20 of Delta's newest first class product, these are hard-shell recliners that are supposed to be a step up above their traditional counterparts. These seats do look really cool and I'd love to review them one day, but for now I'll have to direct you to this great review by Jeb Brooks! Behind first class, there are 42 Comfort+ seats, Delta's premium economy offering with more legroom, extra snacks, and dedicated overhead bin space. Finally in the back is the main cabin, with 132 seats. And here is our seat 30F... without a window. Well it looks like I got unlucky, and booked a windowless window seat. I normally check third party seat maps while booking, and this is the one time I slipped. This is exactly why I recommend you check out websites like seatmaps.com while selecting your seats to help avoid reclineless seats or windowless seats like this. I really wish airlines would just warn you if a seat lacks a window, I'm sure plenty of people out there wouldn’t shy away from such a seat... ...given how many I never even see open their window shades anyway. If Ryanair can get this right, I'd expect Delta to. Anyway, time to check out the seat! Overhead you will find the standard personal air vent, reading light, and flight attendant call button. The seatback features one of Delta's wonderful screens, which we will explore in a few minutes. Just below the screen you will find your headphone jack as well as a USB port. The seat also comes with a single piece full sized tray table. The Legroom is perfectly fine, for reference I am 6ft/1.8m tall. In between the seats in front of you, you will find universal power outlets, meaning there are two for every row of three seats. The seat also has a moderate amount of recline and an adjusting headrest. The seatback pocket is pretty big, and another safety card pocket is hidden inside. Speaking of the safety card, here is a quick look! After getting complementary earbuds, which are alright, it's time to take a look through the in flight entertainment system. First off, Delta seatback screens have a very clean flight tracker installed, which offer tons of viewing options, including the heads up display, which is my personal favorite. Next up, the screen has this nice list of all the aircraft types in Delta’s fleet. As well as an airport directory featuring terminal maps of major Delta hubs and their partner hubs. You will also find a link to the menu for today's flight on a QR code, as well as a WFI guide. Now for the main feature of the in-flight entertainment, the entertainment. Delta offers a massive selection of movies and tv shows, too big to scroll through in reasonable time.  I doubt most people will have a problem finding something to watch here. You can also find live news, music, games, and a kids section. If you prefer to use your personal device instead of the seatback screen, inflight entertainment can also be streamed to your device for free. Safety Video: …make sure your seatbelt is fastened, to fasten, insert the metal tip into the buckle and adjust the strap so it's low and tight across your lap. Safety Video: To release the belt, just lift the top of the buckle. Please remain seated with your seatbelt securely fastened... Time to push back! Thankfully the person sitting behind me said they didn't mind me filming out of the window just behind my seat, so I still got some cool views for you. If you’d like to skip the takeoff and head straight to the narrated part of this video, chapters are available below. Now that we are in the air, it’s time to check out the WIFI. Delta is in the process of rolling out free WIFI for SkyMiles members on domestic flights. You can tell if your aircraft has their new WIFI system by looking for that blue sticker next to the door we saw earlier as we entered. Getting access to that free WIFI is as simple as just logging into your SkyMiles account, and watching a quick ad. I'd say that's a pretty good deal! About 40 minutes after takeoff, a snack and beverage service arrived.  For snacks you have the choice between a small bag of Sunchips, a bag of salted almonds, a white chocolate granola bar, and the famous Biscoff cookies. I always ask for two items, and have yet to be disappointed! And here is the bathroom, this one is the rear right. There isn't anything special about it, being a little tight, and a little dirty just an hour into the flight. Well, without a window there isn't really much else for me to show you, as I didn't want to disturb the passengers behind me mid flight... ...so I'll check back in as we get closer to Minneapolis. About an hour before landing, the crew did a second quick service! I decided to just get another cookie. I really hope this screen isn't correct! And thankfully it wasn't, so time to get ready for landing! Flight Attendant: It's been our pleasure to have you on board with us today. Flight Attendant: To prepare for landing please ensure your seatbelt is fastened, your seatback and tray table are in their upright and locked... Flight Attendant: It's our pleasure to welcome you to Minneapolis-Saint Paul where the local time is 11:34, there has been a two hour time change. Flight Attendant: Please stay seated with your seatbelts fastened...  I really enjoyed my first time on a Delta A321neo, despite the lack of a window, which is partly on me anyway. Overall Delta offers a great service, and they have equipped their A321neos with very nice and comfortable seats... …and good quality in-flight entertainment systems that should hold up for years to come. Anyway welcome to Minneapolis-Saint Paul! I hope I'll see you in the second part of our journey, where, instead of a brand new aircraft, we'll be taking a nearly 31 year old A320! Please let me know what you thought of my first flight review in the comments! I know I have a lot to learn, but I still hope you could enjoy it, and will stick around for the next one!

reviews.transcript_full:
Tonight it's American Airlines turn 
to show us what they got for one of   their transpacific flights! We'll be flying 
from Tokyo to Dallas in Main Cabin Extra,   American's step-up economy product. We'll 
also see how the largest airline in the   world stacks up to some of the other 
transpacific flights we've seen on this   channel. Is Main Cabin Extra worth the extra 
cost? Come along and let's find out together! Good afternoon and welcome back to another video and welcome back to Haneda Airport terminal 3. Well,   we're getting close to the end of the year but
we still have time for a few more flights and   to start us off we'll be flying with American 
Airlines on a flight from Tokyo to Dallas. And   this is actually going to be my first time 
flying American on an international flight   outside North America so we'll see how their 
trans-pacific product is and compare to some   of the other airlines which we've experienced on 
the channel. We'll be flying in economy class on   one of their Dreamliners and the flight is set 
to depart at 6 p.m. So come along let's enjoy   American Airlines as we go from A to to A!  All right well arriving to the airport I headed to   the kiosks at the I check-in area which was 
being used by American. Earlier I checked in   online through the AA app so by the time I arrived at the airport I just had to drop off my bags and   the bag drop off lane took no more than a few 
moments. I should point out that I was headed   to Toronto so at baggage drop off I received an 
'international to International' sticker on my   passport which signified that I didn't have to collect and recheck my bag after US Passport control. With   the formalities out of the way I figure it was 
a good idea to step outside for a few moments   before heading through passport control on a 
pleasant early winter day. We even catch a Finnair Dreamliner! They have quite the interesting 
route due to the closed Russian airspace and   I recently found out that they were the first 
European airline to fly non-stop between Europe   and Japan. Did their non-stop flight to Japan 
begin in 1979,  '81, or '83? Leave your guess in the comments. EE: Terminal 3 used to be called the "Intl Terminal"
until T2 started accepting intl flights! Today we'll be departing from gate 145.   It's one of these lower level gates 
which exist only on the east side of   the terminal. Already waiting for us is 
our Dreamliner which will take us to DFW! We still had some time to kill and the good 
news is that gate 145 is not too far from the   food court so I figured I might as well. I went 
to the noodle outlet at the end and picked up   a tsukemen dish - one of my favorite noodle 
dishes in Japan! It's very similar to Ramen   with the main difference being the noodles and 
soup are separate and you dip one in the other.   There's a healthy serving of cold noodles 
alongside a warm broth with pork, nori and   green onions. A solid call and I can't believe 
it took me all these years to try this place out! By the time I returned to the gate boarding 
was well underway and look who's beside US! Air   Canada has since returned to using the B777
for their Toronto - Haneda route. That plane will beat   me to my final destination by about 6 hours. So is a detour through America worth it? Stay tuned and   find out! The only upgrade I purchased for this 
trip was Main Cabin Extra which gave me group   five boarding. It appears that Americans value 
higher boarding zones a little bit more than we do   north of the border. I really don't know why nine 
boarding zones are necessary but I digress. today   Today we'll be in seat 20J, an aisle seat on the emergency row which is dedicated to Main Cabin Extra passengers.   Passengers in this row can take advantage 
of the dedicated overhead storage bins as well. EE: Winter is a good time for aisle seats. Easy access to the aisle, and there's not too many sights due do darkness. Tonight we're on an almost 4-year-old 787 7-8 Dreamliner. American   has one configuration of this aircraft with 
234 seats across three cabins. Main Cabin Extra   and main cabin seats are in the same cabin but 
marketed as different products. There are seven   lavatories on board and it's important to 
note that there are none at the rear of the aircraft. It'll take about 10 
and 1/2 hours to reach Dallas.   and we'll be staying well south 
of Alaska as we cross the Pacific. EE: Footage of cabin is combination of AA176 and AA169 (LAX-HND) The economy cabin is laid out in a 3-3-3 seating 
configuration. Bulkhead monitors provide flight   information and messages throughout the flight. 
The cabin had a healthy blue glow during the   start of the flight and warm orange and reds 
towards the end. Main Cabin Extra are rows 10,   11, and 20 along with the centre seats of rows 12 through 18 so if you are after a window seat and   Main Cabin Extra you are limited to six possible 
options on the dash eight Dreamliner. The seats were   quite comfortable with an adjustable headrest. 
A pillow and blanket were provided for guests   which was advantageous as I thought they kept 
the cabin on the very chilly (read: freezing!) side. Of course one   benefit of the emergency row is the unlimited leg room at your disposal and you don't have to worry   about others in your row passing you when they 
want to get out. On the other hand no luggage can   be stored on the floor during taxi takeoff and 
landing so the dedicated bins come in especially   handy for the emergency row passengers. With no lavatories at the rear of the plane this area   was highly trafficked perhaps more than other 
Dreamliners particularly after the meal service   so I wouldn't recommend the aisle seat of the 
emergency row. The seats are slightly different   than the rest of the cabin housing a control 
panel on the one side. The IFE system pulls out   from under the armrest and you have to to press 
the tab to release it which took a few moments to   spot in the dim cabin. On my return trip I was in 
17D which I think is a better illustration of what   you get with Main Cabin Extra. The seatback has 
a large adjustable display. The lit pocket which   contained the safety card was just below with 
a table and pocket under that. You'll find the   power outlet at the base and the seat pitch is 35 
to 36 inches, about 5 in more than main cabin seats and   the extra bit of space is quite welcomed on these Long Haul flights. With the table extended you can   really get a sense of the extra space. To compare you can see how the table meets the armrest in the   regular main cabin seats over there overall. I was 
pleased with this seat more than the emergency exit   row and I thought the extra space was worth the 
added cost for Main Cabin Extra on these Long Haul flight. Wi-Fi is offered on the Dreamliners and is 
available for purchase at $23, about $30 Canadian   for the full flight it's in line with what I've 
seen on other airlines. With the AA app you can   also stream videos to your device which is useful if you have your own Bluetooth headphones. The app   is pretty extensive and worth downloading for 
your trip. It even has a track your bag feature   which provides peace of mind especially if 
you have connections. And as always I take a   moment to welcome new viewers to subscribe 
for continued travel and aviation related content:) About an hour after takeoff the dinner 
service commenced. The service started with a warm   oshibori... nice touch! The options were pork 
and rice or a shrimp pasta and I went with   the pork and rice which was a solid call. It came 
with a salad, a spinach side, and a lemon cake and   bonus points for providing a warm bun!
Everything was delicious and it was no chore   finishing every last bite. To accompany the meal 
I enjoyed a Goose Island IPA so cheers to another flight! ooo fresh! The IFE system on American is 
smooth and easy to operate. They have a   very extensive library in which to choose 
something to watch. One difference compared   to domestic flights is that there is no live 
TV available even when the plane is over the   US. Also one thing I think missing from the I 
system is a menu tab for the onboard service   many other airlines have this feature and 
I think it greatly benefits the guest!  And here's a look inside the lavatory closest to 
my seat considering there are no laboratories in   the rear the plane they were kept quite clean 
throughout the flight despite being heavily used. Don't let the darkness fool you it's early 
afternoon outside and plenty bright perfect time   for breakfast which was served with the last hour to go. The options were French toast toast or udon.   The hot meal was accompanied by some fresh fruit I wasn't particularly fond of the French toast   I thought it was on the dry side and no amount 
of syrup was going to save it but I did manage   to have a coffee with my breakfast ...or lunch ...or whatever you want to call this early afternoon meal. Overall this was a pleasant way to cross 
the Pacific the staff were kind and friendly   there was good entertainment and an abundance of food, snacks, and drinks. The flight was one   of five on a roundtrip ticket from Tokyo to 
Toronto and the price came out to C$1,368 which   includes the C$230 upgrade to main cabin extra. I thought the added of cost of main cabin extra was   worth it considering it was spread out over five 
flights. We also offset 613 tons (kg) of carbon for this flight. Landing in Dallas the passport control 
was much faster and better organized than when   I flew through Chicago a year ago. There's a 
dedicated line for US and Canadian [and PR] passport   holders which sped things up a bit. The ITI 
sticker on my passport did its job and my   bag was checked onto my next flight without 
me having to collect it at the carousel. So   as a Canadian would I fly them again well it 
depends! There is added time to your trip when   transferring through the states and another set 
of passport control but the flight was about 400   bucks cheaper compared to Air Canada. American is the largest airline in the world and they   simply have the size to provide a competitive 
price and times so if the price is right I'd   fly them again though I'd Try to snag a codeshare
flight with JAL through the American   website like I did last year. Anyways thanks 
for watching let me know what you thought   about the American Airlines transpacific 
product and I'll catch you in the next episode :)

yt_comments.author: @marekadboy
yt_comments.text: To any cabin crew reading this, if a passengers request you to fix their in-flight entertainment system and you can’t fix it for whatever reason then GO BACK to the passenger and explain the situation rather than waiting for them to ask you or your colleagues over and over again. It’s just a common courtesy and not a hard thing to do!! Passenger may not be happy but you have done what you can and they’ll appreciate it. Simples!!!! I had this several times hence why I am posting it here.

yt_comments.author: @JohnF677
yt_comments.text: I flew Omam Air earlier this year and it was absolutely useless. My IFE did not work for the entire of my first flight. They turned the IFE of over 30 minutes before landing on the second flight. On both flights the service was very slow with disinterested crew. After my experience and watching your video I will definitely be avoiding Oman Air in the future.

Shongshan airport in the city center which   serves some regional and domestic flights and

best in the world, just casually chilling here in   Taipei. I guess that tips my hat on this review.
