that are new to the channel. My name is Kevin and   I am the Flip Flop Traveller. I’m here to give you 
two honest videos each week about unique flights,   hotels and trains. This flight today was 
self funded, the price I paid is in the   description and Starlux has no idea who I am. 
So without further ado, let’s get into episode   316 and see what Starlux is really all about.
Here we are at Terminal 1. The airport has a   bit of a unique setup in that terminal one is over 
here on the right side and everything on the left   is terminal two, but they are all connected 
in what is in theory a continuous loop. Plus,   there’s a new terminal three being built as well- 
the concourses of which should be open by mid next   year with the full terminal opening in 2027.
Today is a pretty easy day here but I’ve seen   this place packed before, so they certainly need 
the breathing room with Starlux now added to the   mix. Last year Taoyuan saw around 35 million 
passengers, putting it in the same league as   the like of Tokyo Narita and Hanoi Noi Bai.
Here in terminal 1, Starlux has a single row   of check in desks- and there’s spiderman. 
They seem to be very much into the branding   collaborations. On their LAX flights, 
they even have LA Clippers branding.  I should mention that Starlux has a 
split operation now between the two   terminals and since my flight, Saigon and 
Da Nang’s flights have moved to Terminal 2,   while Hanoi and Phu Quoc stays here.
Let’s get through security and immigration   and head to the lounge, on the way, I can tell you 
about the level 9 drama that morphed into Starlux.  The current CEO of Starlux- Chang Kuo-Wei- used to 
work at EVA Airlines. He was a mechanic and then a   pilot and eventually made his way to be chairman, 
since you know, his father was the founder of   Evergreen Group. Chang became chairman of EVA in 
2013. Three years later, his father died and named   Chang as his successor as Chairman of Evergreen 
Group. This is when things got spicy. Problem was,   Chang was the youngest of his father’s sons, from 
his second marriage to boot. There was more a less   a coup that ensued at Evergreen and Chang was 
booted from the company. Within a few months,   he had the idea to create Starlux.
The name Starlux comes from the Chinese   character for Star, in honor of his father 
who navigated via the stars before GPS and   the Character for Universe, framing Chang’s 
own ambitions. In English, it became Starlux.  Let me pause that for a moment as we take a look 
at the lounge here in Terminal 1. It is small and   this is probably the weakest link of the entire 
Starlux network. That said, all of the longer   or more premium routes are now operating 
from Terminal 2 which has a larger lounge.  There was a small buffet selection on offer 
as well as a few a la cart items, from which   I chose the scallion bun and soy milk which was 
actually quite a stand out, all things considered.  I also loved the attention to small 
details- such as the ice on offer.  The only other big negative for this lounge 
is that the restrooms are a solid 100 meters   down the corridor outside of the lounge.
I know this isn’t ideal, but if the lounge   is ever too crowded, there’s a public lounge of 
sorts named the Airport Experience Zone which   looked surprisingly calm and comfortable.
I can never leave this airport   without mango tarts in hand.
So, obviously, Starlux is competing with China   Airlines, but much more so, with EVA. Their first 
flights were in late 2020, delayed due to COVID,   with the first three destinations being Da Nang, 
Penang and Macau. They’ve quickly expanded to   their current 26 destinations with 2 more on the 
way by the end of the year, with an impressive   operation to Japan and a stated goal of being a 
major player connecting southeast asia to the US.  One unique thing is that on their A350s,   which they have five of at the moment to fly to 
the US, they actually have a true first class,   something you won’t find at their competitors, 
as Starlux says they, “promise to commit to   luxury that Taiwan’s dominant carriers have 
lost sight of in recent years.” Still ironic,   they're talking about two great airlines. Also 
kinda cool that Chang flew the first A350 from   Toulous himself for the delivery flight.
They currently have 23 aircraft on   hand with 30 on order.
I got to the gate on time   but our aircraft didn’t. While the signs were

small group one. That said, there’s quite a bit   of speculation that Starlux may end up joining 
Oneworld alliance- especially since there’s also   speculation that Cathay may leave it. Then Taipei 
would be one of the only cities on earth serving   as a hub for all three alliances.

I stepped on board and there is one thing   that is like the finest crystal clear as soon 
as you step on board. This is an airline that   is here to impress- and I mean that both 
for the hard product and soft product.  The staff were enthusiastic, thoughtful and 
knowledgeable and that cabin was gorgeous.   The business class on these A321neos has just 
8 lie flat seats in a 2 x 2 configuration.  As I’ve said before, I’ve always liked 
these seats since in the seated position,   I think they’re pretty comfortable, even 
if they’re a bit narrow when lie flat.  But it’s all of the finishing details 
that make the difference here though.  From the leather trim, to the contrast stitching, 
and even things like the quality of the seatbelt-   it’s a very well designed product.
There’s a fully adjustable headrest   as well as a storage space over your 
shoulder with a universal outlet.  So we all know what happens if you click 
like on this video and subscribe to the   channel, but do you know what happens if you 
don’t? You may never see me again. So if you enjoy   this style of content, be sure to click all of 
the buttons. If you’re interested in a peak of the   inner workings of the channel or just need some 
travel advice- be sure to check out my Patreon.   Whatever you do, thanks for being here right now.  I was served a hot towel along with a 
really good cold pressed pineapple and   guava juice. I love creative- but not too 
creative- signature pre departure drinks.  Across, there’s a nice high resolution in 
flight monitor along with a good side foot   rest. The storage space under the foot rest 
is limited though. Also keep in mind the foot   rests for the bulkheads in this type of seat 
are around double the size of the other rows.  We pushed back and a very- shall 
we say different- safety video   began to play. Perhaps, not to Emirates taste.  We had an excruciatingly long taxi and wait in 
line for take off- at one point we were next in   line and it honestly felt like they just forgot 
about us. 72 minutes from push back to take off.  But it’s coming up now, 
along with the airport stats.  So before the meal begins, let’s take a look 
at the comforts and amenities on offer today.  The pillow is a decent size and 
quality- and freshly laundered.  Then there’s a fantastic blanket. At 
first glance it may look like a towel,   but it’s actually a super soft and fluffy blanket 
which thankfully doesn’t leave lint everywhere.  As for the headphones, they were noise canceling 
and quite good actually, but I think I actually   like the case even more than the headphones.
The tray table could be used fully   extended or folded in half.
Ok, let’s get into this really good   meal service. First, we will start off with an 
insanely comprehensive menu for a 3 hour flight.  Note that the prices in red are my addition 
to the graphic just to give you an idea of   the current retail price for each bottle.
As I said before, I love drinking wine   but my knowledge is limited, so I always 
appreciate wine lists that go into detail   about region, pairings and tasting notes.
Of course, I chose the Contemporary Asian   and Longtail Menu for my meal which 
honestly, even if I didn’t like it,   I would have loved it- and I’ll tell you why.
It’s clear, even for a single tray service,   they are trying to elevate the 
experience from the ground up.  For our meal today, we start with a Pineapple 
Pura Longtail and sparkling water. The starter is   Milkfish toast, Avocado, Daikon and Dill. Reading 
that, I had precisely zero idea what to expect,   but I think this is quite clever. 
It’s so elevated for in flight food,   but not at all fussy or difficult to serve.
For the main, we had USDA ANgus Beef Tenderloin,   Pineapple Rice, peanut and pickled kohlrabi.
So, when it comes to beef, let me tell you   how I know when a dish is really good. 
When I start taking little tiny bites.   I think I cut each of those slices into 2 or 
3 pieces. The pineapple rice was great too.  In East Asia, we are spoiled with the food 
offerings in business class on these regional   routes, but it’s worth pointing out that Starlux 
is the only airline in the region right now that   doesn’t follow the same exact format for 
meals. Small salad or cold meat appetizer,   plus hot preplated main and dessert. 
Cathay, ANA, JAL, EVA, China Airlines,   Korean Air, Asiana- it’s all the same 
format- and it’s generally all good,   but this is just another level. I’d be 
really curious to try Starlux’s catering   on long haul services- more on that in a bit.
Earlier I’d asked for a glass of the Reisling,   but the crew insisted that I allow them to chill 
it for a bit more time since it wasn’t properly   prepared- attention that I appreciated- so that 
came along with my dessert which was a Chocolate   Magao cake along with seasonal fresh fruit.
Entertainment on board- it’s just okay. I   have little doubt that it’ll improve 
overtime, but at the time there were   just around 150 movies on offer- along with 
a handful of TV shows with random episodes.  Loved the detailed map and in 
flight magazine though. There   was also in flight wifi which 
was free for Business Class.  And here we have the seat in full 
flat mode- definitely not needed on   this short day flight, but nice to have for sure.
So, how I ended up on this short Starlux flight.   Last year, Starlux announced a partnership with 
Alaska Airlines and then Alaska announced they’d   be selling Starlux tickets for points. Alaska 
communicated that there would be promotional   fares available for the first few months. The 
aviation world collectively freaked out and   everyone started trying to book. At that time, I 
had 43000 Alaska points. The had a promo to buy   more points and so I topped that up to 60000 
miles which would be enough for the Taipei   to LAX flight. I knew the points would take 2 
days to appear in my account, but it was fine,   Alaska advertised these fares would be 
available I believe from April until August.  Well wouldn’t you know they forgot to mention that 
each flight only had four seats available at that   price. By the time I went to book, everything 
was more than double the price. So in the end,   with my 60k alaska points, I got this 
flight, plus a longhaul LATAM flight,   decided to dump Alaska all together before 
they continued to devalue their program.  So yeah, I wanted a long 
haul flight- and I still do,   perhaps now even more so- and will 
keep my eyes open for them. That said,   this was a really nice first taste of what will 
clearly be a new major player in the market. Oh,   did I mention they even already began 
turning a profit last year? Yeah.  Ok, I’ll let you enjoy the rest of the approach 
into Saigon. The airport stats are coming up.  And so, that is that. We were late, the 
airport was mobbed but I was still on   cloud 9 so I didn’t even care. Starlux, 
I will be back- if you join Oneworld,   or any alliance frankly, I’ll be back often.
So I really hope you enjoyed this trip report   today. If you did, be sure to click the like 
button and subscribe with notifications on so   you don’t miss out on my twice weekly videos.

Today I'm flying with a giant which is 
literally unknown in the Western world.   It operates more than 800 aircraft and carries 
three times as many passengers as British Airways.   Yet it's much less known than many 
smaller airlines. This is China Eastern,   one of the China's "Big 3" airlines. But all 
that massive scale is still mostly busy serving   domestic routes. That's why internationally it 
flies rather low on the radar screen of many.   Exploring Chinese airlines and being a bit 
suspicious, I first went private. For starters,   I was really impressed by Hainan Airlines, smaller 
private carrier, of course, by Chinese standards   and arguably the best in China. Then I raised 
the stakes and flew First Class with Xiamen Air.   That was a really bizarre experience. As I gained 
more confidence, I moved to state-owned airlines,   starting with Air China. They passed, which 
is another way to tell I wasn't impressed.   But it was clear that efficiency was more 
important than experience. And today,   I'm very curious to test China Eastern. Let's see 
where I will land on my China aviation adventure.   One thing I can tell, it was quite an 
experience. Which one? You will find out soon.   Today's flight is Istanbul to Shanghai on China 
Eastern Airbus A330. It's 4,300 miles and almost   10 hours. And I'm flying from Istanbul Airport 
where it somehow feels I know every corner.   But I got myself thinking it's the first time 
I'm flying from here, not with Turkish Airlines.   That's definitely a hurdle for China Eastern to 
meet as the comparison bar for sure will be high.   Istanbul airport meets me with a familiar buzz, 
but I feel lost. I could navigate to fancy Turkish   business checkin zone with closed eyes. But where 
do I go with China Eastern? There are check-in   desks turned out to be actually at the very end 
of the terminal and very modest. But it worked.   There is life beyond Turkish indeed. Trying my 
luck with fast track, but not this time. Unlike   few other Sky Team airlines, China Eastern doesn't 
have a deal with airport operated IGA Fast Track.   So today we'll have to queue for immigration and 
security, which in Istanbul can take time. Well,   it's not uncommon for an airline to be squeezed 
in an airport dominated by another airline.   So no conclusions yet. Hope China Eastern will 
surprise me on board, which ultimately matters   more. Istanbul airport firmly sits on my list 
of the world's best airports. It feels more   like a giant luxury shopping mall than an actual 
airport. Now I'm to explore a different side of   it. The one that's not about Turkish Airlines. 
My aim is IGA lounge which serves Sky Team.   It's not hard to find, but once I come near, I 
start getting a vibe of a bus station. A bit of a   crowd, a bit of a chaos. All possible airlines are 
crammed in here with all the confusion it brings.   Inside you have more of the same. There are 
apparently different zones - dining, relax,   entertainment. But because of the crowds, 
everything feels pretty much the same:   busy, noisy, and chaotic. I'm circling around 
the lounge, looking for a quieter spot, like an   eagle looking for a prey. But ultimately decide 
to fly away as I concluded that having a beer   outside is still a better choice. So much for the 
lounge experience. Well, with another ground miss   the stakes are getting higher for China Eastern. 
They better get the flight right! Departing from   Istanbul is really two journeys in one. A flight 
itself and a walk to the gate which can take up   to 20 minutes. The airport is huge and there is no 
internal transportation, only your pair of legs.   I walk to the very end of the terminal and here 
I get the first surprise at the edge of nervous   tick. I see a China Southern plane. What??? 
But then I realized that the two flights are   boarding next to each other. That was a scare. 
The boarding is smooth, a pleasant contrast to   check-in and lounge hiccups, and I'm on my way 
to my today's ride, an Airbus A330. China Eastern   operates more than 50 of them. But this one 
is special. It has a modern 1-2-1 staggered   layout with 32 seats in business rather than usual 
outdated 2-2-2 layout they had since early 2000s   and still keep in a majority of their A330 fleet. 
There are only few of those new retrofitted planes   and I'm very eager to try it out. Well, 
China Eastern really made an effort here.   This might not be the state of the art business 
cabin, but it's a huge step forward from what   they used to have on their A330s before. This is 
a new generation cabin with fully lie-flat seats,   direct aisle access for all passengers and a fair 
level of privacy. But unlike some newer business   class products, it doesn't create that cocoon-like 
feeling - you still feel quite exposed. China   Eastern is using a well-known Thompson Vantage XL 
seat here. One of the early next generation seat   models that evolved business flying around 2010s. 
A very solid product which is also used by Delta,   SAS, and Quantas. But here China Eastern 
clearly got the off the rack basic model   with little or no customizations. The materials 
and finishes seem to be on the simpler side.   I'm somehow torn in making my mind about this 
cabin. For what China Eastern A330 used to be,   this is a major step forward, a modern, solid 
product. Can I call it best-in-class? Well,   not yet. It's a bit like when you come to Germany 
and you see that many taxes are E-class Mercedes.   Feels WOW at first. Then you get inside and you 
realize this is the bare bones model where you   don't have all the usual bells and whistles that 
give it a special experience. The form could be   excellent, but the content matters too. More here 
to explore, but now I'm switching to the service.   The usual rituals are followed properly. A 
wet towel and a pre-flight drink are here.   A good sign. A flight attendant brings a menu, 
which is not always the case on Chinese carriers.   On Air China and Xiamen, the menu was explained by 
the crew and details didn't go much further than   Western or Chinese. But China Eastern prepared its 
own challenge. It's a menu for a full year with   four different meal sets which are linked through 
color coding to four groups of non-consecutive   months. This is really not for an average 
mind! And I start feeling like a code breaker   deciphering Enigma. Finally, code is broken and 
I find the right section. For lunch, I will have   two choices of soups, four choices for main with 
a good mix of European, Chinese, Turkish, which   is actually thoughtful. And of course desserts. 
Then we should have something before the arrival.   But I can't figure out if this would be "Late 
Meal" or "Breakfast". I will handle this dilemma   when the time comes. On a single foldout of 
beverage menu, China Eastern manages to put   what takes 10 pages for others. Efficiency over 
fanciness. Interestingly, some wines are marked   First Class only. I was just feeling so proud of 
being a business class passenger and suddenly I'm   reminded that I'm still second tier, even if there 
is no first class on this plane at all. Finally,   I cannot hold a smile seeing very brief: whiskey, 
vodka, rum. Simple and to the point. You get it   for free. So why ask silly questions what brand it 
is? Enjoy the surprise. Overall, the menu sounds   right, but something tells me that reality might 
be slightly different with China Eastern. Well,   the new cabin showed me where a China Eastern 
is heading, while the menu well reminded where   they came from. Let's see how far they managed to 
get on this journey. We depart right on time. A   score for China Eastern. I have another glance at 
China Southern which almost gave me a heart attack   and also notice another Chinese carrier 
right next to it - Sichuan Airlines.   Might be a good idea for the next trip and 
a chance to try their atomic spicy cuisine.   Istanbul is a kingdom of Turkish Airlines and 
there are red and white tails are everywhere.   Turkish went a long way from being literally 
unknown to the larger world till early 2000s   to becoming a major player with massive 
network and award-winning service.   It's interesting what would be a journey 
of China Eastern. Despite its massive size,   to the rest of the world it's in a very similar 
position today what Turkish used to be in the   late '90s. For China Eastern, it all started in 
late 80s when China decided to break its state   aviation monopoly. And China's Big 3 was born. 
Air China in Beijing, China Southern in Guangzhou,   and China Eastern in Shanghai. All still 
government owned, but all went in their own ways.   Air China became flag carrier and a status symbol. 
China Southern focused heavily on domestic routes,   and China Eastern became an airline for Shanghai. 
It tried to balance focus on domestic markets   with international network and focus on business 
passengers. Later it acquired several regional   players and now has multiple hubs across China 
-- but it still remains a quintessential Shanghai   airline. Historically, China Eastern had what 
analysts call "inconsistent brand image",   while I would rather say they were blunt. 
Decent planes, but average cabins and comfort,   average service, and no any kind of distinctive 
positioning. In the last decades, they have been   investing heavily in planes while also trying to 
bring their service in line with their ambitions.   I can see that on a hardware side they did make 
a progress but I still need to be convinced   about the soft product and the upcoming 
lunch would be the best place to start.   I am fixing a tray table right away as if doing so 
can bring the food faster. It's adjustable which   is a plus but shaky and I struggle to understand 
the idea behind that strange curvy shape.   The usual continuation would be "a white cloth 
is served", but in our case, it's not a cloth,   but a paper towel. Which immediately brings the 
vibe of a cheap diner rather than an upscale   business class service. Attention to detail 
doesn't seem to be a virtue of China Eastern,   and this is something that they will 
keep reminding me for the next 8 hours.   Drinks come. I got a glass of Chilean Savignon 
from Frontera. A perfectly drinkable but clearly   no frills wine. Comes with mixed fruits and nuts 
in a very Chinese plastic pouch. Enjoy the nuts,   but could do without all the plastic. The 
meal itself starts with an appetizer and soup.   You can make your own judgment, but this is not 
something that impresses you just by its looks.   I wanted to give China Eastern their best 
chance by leaning towards Chinese cuisine,   which they should be most competent with, but it 
looks like they didn't appreciate my generosity.   I got a creamy fish soup, lukewarm and with fairly 
little flavor. The appetizer, according to menu,   was supposed to be grilled shrimp with smoked 
swordfish, but it looked like shrimps took a day   off and were swapped with salmon. The taste 
was okay, but clearly no time was wasted on   trying to present it better. Interestingly, China 
Eastern provides both western cutlery and Chinese   chopsticks, which is thoughtful. It's interesting 
how rays of customer focus come in some places,   but are totally blocked by clouds of practicality 
in the others. For the main course, I got chicken   Kung Pao with vegetables and steamed rice. By 
now, I don't expect too much from the looks.   The less expectations, the less disappointments. 
But what I got somehow went beyond. Either China   Eastern totally managed to re-imagine chicken 
Kung Pao the way no one could think before   or again the menu had some gaps with reality. 
Well, it was chicken in some kind of sweet sauce   and it was eatable. But I had Kung Pao in a 
food court few weeks ago and I have to tell   it was much better. What else? China Eastern is 
trying to serve a multicourse meal. So, we still   get fruits and mini cheeseplate. It's difficult 
to spoil those, but they still follow the model   China Eastern established earlier. They give the 
minimum possible option that would qualify for the   "We did it". The nice surprise though is an 
ice cream. We get a perfect Movenpick box   and this gets me in a better mood. Once the 
desserts come, I cannot hold my smile again.   It's not a Sacher Torte or some fancy pastry. It's 
a KitKat bar. Well, actually two of them. I love   KitKat, but this is yet another piece in China 
Eastern puzzle. It's all about doing the least   effort while still ticking the box. I don't know 
if this is the intent or just how things work out,   but this is how my experience with them is shaping 
out. I am done with the meal. It might not be   award winning, but it was quite big after all. 
Full stomach makes me more relaxed and hopefully   less picky. So, let's explore further the seat, 
amenities, and of course, entertainment. What you   immediately see is that seat is quite spacious. 
You also get a lot of space for your belongings.   There is a big console by the window where you 
can place your stuff as well as a decent storage   compartment. Power outlets are right by your 
hand: Universal and USB type A, no type-C though,   which hints that this is a little older generation 
of seats. The remote has a built-in screen,   which I always like as it allows you to track the 
route while watching something on the main screen.   The controls are usual, so nothing to decipher. 
What's good is that they are mirrored on a lower   panel, which you can reach when the seat is in lie 
flat position. You can argue about materials and   finishes, but from the practicality perspective, 
the seat definitely gets the job done.   But what about in-flight entertainment? The seats 
are equipped with an 18" HD touchscreen monitors.   Very similar to what Delta and Quantas are using. 
Not award winning these days, but definitely   competitive hardware. But let's see what's 
inside it. And here I'm up to a surprise. The   media content is extremely basic. There are barely 
some 20 international movie titles, mostly old and   somehow heavily skewed to cartoons and superhero 
movies. It is even worse with the series.   There are just few in English and none that I 
even remotely heard about. Here I start feeling   annoyed. I could put up with the food, but this is 
10 hours dayflight. You're in business and there   is nothing to watch. I'm sorry, China Eastern, 
but this is not how it works in 2026. Checking   the headphones largely loses its meaning by now as 
there is not much use for them. On other airlines,   I could brag why don't they have a branded pair or 
if Bose is better than Harmon Kardon, but here we   are in a class of its own. This is the most basic 
headphone set I have seen so far in business.   It's generally what others give you in economy 
on long haul. But strangely here it makes sense.   Since there is not much to watch, why splurge for 
expensive headphones? I'm annoyed, but I cannot   argue with the logic. My last chance to entertain 
myself on this flight is to figure out Wi-Fi.   It's a bit complicated and there are many 
clicks to make, but ultimately I get there.   Wi-Fi connected. This is much further than I got 
in last couple of flights with Chinese carriers.   It's really surprising that country which 
literally lives online on the ground is still   struggling to figure out internet in the sky. But 
there is a surprise here too. We have Wi-Fi. But   it doesn't mean we have internet. The connection 
is so slow that after 15 minutes I totally give   up. The only thing it was actually good for was to 
fill in the lending card for Chinese immigration.   As if trying to compensate for the lack 
of proper entertainment, China Eastern is   providing newspapers. A nice touch, but probably 
too late for me to learn Chinese, at least for   this flight. So, it looks like that for a change, 
I will have a flight where my mind is not going   to be bothered by movies, surfing web, or doing 
emails. Well, peace of mind is a luxury, too.   And here at China Eastern delivered in full, even 
if not asked for. Meanwhile, I noticed something   interesting. There is a small round module below 
the screen which looks suspiciously like a camera.   Is this a hello from a Big Brother or is crew 
keeping an eye on annoying airline reviewers?   I doubt it is a surveillance camera, but honestly, 
I have no idea what else it could be. So,   if anyone knows, please let me know. And finally, 
amenities. Pillow and blanket were already on the   seat from the start. They are big and functional, 
but there is no way to mistake them for Armani   Caza bedding on Etihad . This is more of a summer 
camp vibe. There is also a pouch with slippers.   Check. Amenities come in a small fabric pouch 
which does look quite authentic. Unfortunately,   the contents tell a different story. It is the 
purest form of business class basics. An eye mask,   comb, toothbrush, and ear plugs. Everything is 
double and triple wrapped and boxed in plastic.   Many airlines now turn a mini kits into 
collaborations with artists and fashion houses.   Here it almost looks like China Eastern cooperated 
with an Association of Plastic Producers.   I'm done with almost everything and at 
the absence of any decent entertainment,   my best option is to get some sleep. This is 
a red-eye flight. Still a daytime for me, but   will arrive early in the morning. So catching some 
sleep is not the worst idea. I'm checking if there   are any mini mattresses, but no luck. Well, not 
having entertainment and internet might have been   a blessing in disguise. I managed to get a decent 
sleep instead. And now ready to check out the   second meal service. Time-wise, breakfast would 
probably make much more sense, but we get what   China Eastern calls "Light meal". By now, I know 
that menu is more of a guideline than a guarantee.   Tuna salad somehow turned into grilled salmon, 
but I did get sauteed shrimps with veggie and   steamed rice. Salmon tasted like it was cooked a 
week ago, but shrimps were actually pretty good.   And somehow this light meal turned out to be 
better than the main meal earlier on. Wonder   if China Eastern kept the best till the landing 
as it's often the last impression that stays with   you. Now it's the time to conclude and to make a 
verdict. I came with low expectations and with all   the baggage of stereotypes about China state-owned 
airlines. Some of them China Eastern proved wrong,   but others unfortunately were still there. The 
airport experience was very basic, but I wouldn't   give it too much weight as it wasn't their own 
ground. Then the plane was a nice surprise.   instead of beating up an old-fashioned 2-2-2 
product, China Eastern had a proper 1-2-1 business   cabin. And even if I could pick things here and 
there on lack of customization, it's still a very   competitive product. Where they failed to deliver 
for me though is the service and attention to   experience. After all these years, China Eastern 
still seems to be all about transportation   rather than passenger experience, even in business 
class. Interestingly, I expected them to score   higher than more rigid and formal Air China. But 
strangely, Air China still provided a more premium   and satisfying feeling. The way I understand China 
Easter now is that they try to tick all the boxes,   but in the most formal and minimalist way. It's 
there, but it's not necessarily gives you an   experience. Poor in-flight entertainment options 
for international passengers, very weak internet,   bland food, and very little attention to all those 
small details here and there that ultimately give   you the experience. So, no surprise that I came 
up with 3+/5. China Eastern is clearly making an   effort to reinvent and to make themselves a global 
airline. And by its sheer size, it's as global   as it gets. But doing so, it prioritizes hardware 
over soft product. It invests billions into planes   but still fails to notice things that are beyond 
entertainment, service and passenger experience.   China Eastern got all the resources they need. 
But while they want to go global, it seems   that they find it difficult to go beyond what is 
needed to successfully compete at home. They are   still in soul searching if they really need to get 
serious about service or pumping up new planes and   frequencies will still do the job. So far, this 
is not something I would repeat except for testing   their flagship A350, but very curious to keep an 
eye if they will reinvent themselves in the next   years. The ambition is there, but I don't think 
the metal itself will get them where they want to

yt_comments.text: Not bad for a startup, but of course there are flaws: 1. No personal airvents 2. No universal power outlets in economy, I think only included in business class, which is a shame. 3. Weak Wi-Fi for a premium full service carrier that is digitally native (should have just stuck with StarLink) 4. Average lavatory, very ordinary, nothing special like Emirates Or Qatar Airways. 5. No onboard external cameras (forwards and downwards) QR and EK offer them on almost every aircraft and dreamliners are supposed to have them. 6. Safety Video seems to have used lots of AI and CGI (not necessarily a complaint but apparently some were bothered by it.) 7. Tray table cannot be extended, if seat in front reclines, can be difficult for the passenger. Some of the positives: 1. Very aesthetic mood lighting 2. Premium cabin with generous recline 3. Comfortable seats 4. Generous meal portions even for a short haul domestic flight 5. Massive screen (13.3inch for economy) with Wi-Fi (regardless of speed as some airlines don’t even offer it) and responsive. 6. Experienced staff, lots of former cabin crews from EK, QR, EY etc. 7. Metal cutlery provided, lavender scented hot towels, branded soaps and other little touches that make the experience much better 8. In-built headphones inside the headrests for passengers in premium economy and business class 9. Business elite is said to be even better than some airlines first class suites 10. Bluetooth pairing with personal headphones 11. One of the best in-flight map, interactive experience with the IfE, good content for a start-up, with games, music and much more. 12. Provided amenity kit for long haul travel Can still add much more Overall probably one of the best startups and there’s more postives than negatives. Thanks for the review and can’t wait for this airline to dominate the passenger experience in future travel.

got some sleep [Music] all right so it's currently almost 3 A.M and cabin line is turned on and it's time for a bit of breakfast didn't get much sleep it's expected though for me while packaged very playing bagel with a piece of ham wait and cheese and then some cream cheese in it does the job to [Music] cantaloupe two pieces of pineapple and one green thank you to our sweet pastry with blueberry finish my plate oh hey I don't turn down free food after eating I wanted to brush my teeth so I checked out of the lab only 787-9 Dreamliner you know what it feels relatively spacious in here compared to some of the other labs you can actually uh you know give my elbows up and down with that twisting side to side anyways we're about 45 minutes from Landing so there are other folks waiting to use I'll get in get out and get back to my seat it was soon announced we had begun our initial descent into Sao Paulo dropping below 10 000 feet it's time to summarize today's journey and my long-haul experience with latam before boarding I visited the Centurion lounge and found the food selection was limited and below the quality I expect from Amex I then tried to explore the Sky Deck at the Sky reviews.transcript_full: I am going to Turkey and for the first time ever I'm flying via Oman Air I've heard so many good things about the one air that I'm so excited to try it so come let's fly my flight out of Manila Philippines was scheduled at 7 45 a.m since I was at the airport three hours prior I had time to burn at the lounge Oman Air shares a common lounge with a few other airlines in Manila the food choices were limited but they had enough to tide me over until the full breakfast on board the plane upon sitting I was immediately offered a towel the food menu and the wine list good morning thank you allow me to give you this one hour menu for today including the white list welcome one more thank you very much while waiting for others to board I quickly checked out the other seats our flight has two legs with a two hour stop over at Muscat in Oman the business class of Oman Air had Apex suites with seats in two two configuration on the Boeing 7879 Apex Suites are known for being comfortable and spacious with a fully flatbed and a good body with and at five five setting up my feet could not even reach the foot rest the color palette of the cabin is in neutrals with sand Brown beige and white so the cabin looked clean and fresh one plus factor in the Apex Suites is that every passenger had aisle access I was sitting by the window and had no need to disturb my neighbor I had full privacy as between us was a privacy divider I could raise and lower using the controls beside the seat my seat was in row K and had three full windows on my right side as it was the morning flight we were not provided with a mattress pad I did have a plush pillow and a luxurious blanket before pushback I was offered individually wrapped dates [Music] Arabic coffee and my now favorite lemon mint Juice Plus nuts Once In The Air I looked through the wine list and chose to have champagne which was a great way to begin the eight and a half hour flight though it was a day flight I asked for pajamas and was provided with one along with the amenities kit the pajamas were made from cotton fabric so it was soft to the touch now the kit wasn't much it came in a pouch made from the same fabric and colors as the pajamas it has socks brush with comb earplugs and an eye mask [Music] on this flight I had no chance of getting hungry because the food just kept coming for starters I had smoked tuna with Tobiko and black caviar coriander cream cheese sumac cucumber onion cherry tomatoes crisp leaves and mango mint jelly tomato vinaigrette it was served with a variety of Breads and pastries plus butter and jam My Sweet Tooth could not be contained so for the mains I had the maple cinnamon french toast with berry compote Anglia sauce raspberries and toasted almonds one thing I didn't have to worry about was my gadgets losing power as next to my seat there was a universal power socket as well as two USB ports next to it is the headphone jack all the seat and divider controls were on the armrest while by my head where the reading light and a hook for the headphones the noise canceling headphones which came in a cloth pouch were decent and did the job my personal space had Ample Storage I put my medium sized bag under the footrest by the entertainment screen by my seat there are two small storages storing a water bottle and the headphones next to that is a literature pocket for the menus that could also hold a small tablet one thing I judge a flight by is the in-flight Entertainment System the lineup doesn't have to be extensive as long as the choices they do have are good Oman Air has my all-time favorite shows friends in The Big Bang Theory plus classic romantic movies so I was satisfied one thing though the entertainment remote control by the seat was not responsive and could do with an upgrade now it's time to check the lavatory the brand of the toiletries in the lavatory was abuage and from what I understand it is the luxury brand from Oman what made me happiest is that the toilet was equipped with a much needed b-day soon enough we touched down in Muscat Oman and since I am in Scott I am not not passing this opportunity to go into the first in business Lounge of Oman Air I heard it's golden literally and indeed it is gold is everywhere from the wall to the ceiling they also had a great selection of food and drinks they even had popcorn of course there's dates and more coffee they have a lot of space for passengers they have a family area nap rooms Lounge areas shower rooms and even a spa for the second leg of my flight I flew economy with a shorter flight of five hours it's your standard economy with simple blankets and pillows but upgraded because of ample legroom better seat angle recline a universal power socket and a seat jacket hook the lavatory had no amoage this time but it was clean overall flying Oman Air was a great experience but more than the bed and the food it was the people who made the biggest difference all their land and air crew members were attentive polite and seemed to genuinely enjoy serving great service and value for money that's Oman Air so I'm finally here in turkey and I must say that I enjoyed both legs of my flight so that's Istanbul the flight was comfortable and the service was amazing I love the food as well so I hope you enjoyed the flight with me until next time reviews.transcript_full:
Hello everyone, I’m Edin~ Today, I’m taking you from Taipei to Singapore~ This time, I’m flying on Starlux A330-900 in economy class I’m seated in 32K, near the No. 2 engine~ Engine View (Aviation enthusiasts’ favourite!!) A blanket and pillow are already prepared at the seat. The headrest has multi-angle adjustments. There’s a TV in front, with space below for small items. Under the TV, there’s a USB port and headphone jack. Meal tray~ Legroom when sitting upright (I’m 177cm tall)~ Underneath, there are headphones and a stack of documents (the black bag on the right is mine). In the middle, there’s a shared Type-C/international charging port with the adjacent seat. In-flight magazine, Wi-Fi access card, safety card, and airsickness bag. The in-flight entertainment system offers a variety of movies, TV shows, music, and games from different countries. There’s a decent selection, and most are fairly recent. You can also check the menu on the screen. There were two meal options that day (I chose beef pasta). Meals can be pre-selected online. Starlux offers signature drinks in collaboration with local bars (not available on the short Taipei-Hong Kong route).
This flight offered the Sci-Fi Cosmos signature drink. Of course, standard drinks are also available~ Now for the aviation enthusiast’s favorite section – the flight map!! It can be viewed from multiple angles! For convenience, you can connect wireless Bluetooth headphones to the TV. It’s meal time! This time, it’s beef in tomato sauce with long pasta~ Overall, I found the taste to be very high quality.
The beef had a great balance of fat and lean meat, with excellent texture! If I had to nitpick, I’d wish they offered ice cream. Sci-Fi Cosmos drink paired with a movie! Drinks in blue plus blue skies and white clouds outside ^^ Snapping a photo for the memories~ All Starlux flights offer free Wi-Fi for text messaging.
Just connect to the plane’s Wi-Fi, enter your email, and agree to the terms. Lavatory Visit There’s a green plant~ Moisturizing spray/lotion. Overall, it’s clean and tidy! About an hour before landing, they offered snacks and drinks (peach juice). In summary, I found this flight experience very comfortable and enjoyable. The hardware was nearly flawless.The only minor issue is that the window could be cleaner... On the software side, the meal exceeded expectations in taste.
The cabin crew worked very efficient too. The entire journey was very smooth, and I hope to try other international routes in the future~ Have you ever flown with Starlux Airlines?
What’s your opinion of them? Let me know in the comments! Thanks for watching, see you in the next video, bye bye!

reviews.transcript_full: For many travelers, Emirates and Dubai long seemed like a sure bit.  A global hub, a vast route network and the A380 have the symbol of comfortable flying.  However, recent regional tensions have led to a more critical view of things.  From what is currently apparent, what I saw and based on feedback from my community,  the onboard product has not been downgraded. reviews.transcript_full: In today's video, I'm flying business class from JFK to Lima with LATAM Airlines in one of their Boeing 767-300s. I'll be taking you through every part of my experience and towards the end, I'll share exactly how much I paid for this flight and whether I think this business class product is worth it. But before we get started, don't forget to give this video a thumbs-up. And if you enjoy content like this, consider subscribing to the channel and hitting that bell button so you get notified when I upload a brand new video. And with that out of the way, let's get started. This journey begins at JFK, where LATAM has a dedicated check-in line for business class passengers. The staff member checking me in was very polite and informative. She explained all the perks of flying in business class with LATAM, which includes access to the Delta One Lounge here in JFK and a dedicated security line. However, aside from that, there wasn't anything particularly special. No separate seating area or special pre-boarding zone. Still, the process was quick, friendly, and efficient. This is the private security entrance that leads directly into the Delta One Lounge, which means you can skip the regular lines altogether. >> Right off the bat, I have to say that the Delta One Lounge here at JFK is phenomenal. It's incredibly spacious and beautifully designed. Even during peak hours, it never felt crowded. There's a massive buffet offering a variety of options. I was able to enjoy breakfast and lunch here. And everything I tried was delicious. But what really sets this lounge apart is the ala carte dining area, where you can order gourmet dishes freshly prepared to your liking. Something that truly elevates the experience. There are multiple work pods, plenty of charging stations, and even spa-like amenities. The showers were outstanding, clean, modern, and stocked with high-end toiletries. The only minor issue was that the water temperature fluctuated a bit. But I'm honestly just nitpicking here. You've also got a full-service bar, multiple drink stations, spotless restrooms, and great views of the planes. In short, this lounge is as close to perfection as it gets. But before I knew it, it was boarding time. So, let's make our way over to the gate. The Boeing 767-300 I'll be flying in today has a staggered 1-2-1 configuration, which means that everyone in business class has direct aisle access, but the window seats alternate between being closer to the window and farther from the window. In this flight, I'll be in seat 3L. This seat has a clean, modern look with a subtle gray and red color scheme that I really like. Waiting for me at my seat was a full bedding set with a pillow, duvet, and mattress pad, all nicely packaged like a sleeping bag. There's also a menu, a bottle of water, a pair of slippers, and an amenity kit, which we'll check out later. And you get noise-canceling headphones, too. There's also a reading light and a universal power outlet along with a USB port. The IFE remote control can be found in its own little compartment here, close by to the seat controls. And there is some storage space, but I don't think it's enough. I do, however, like that there's a rail guard for the open storage space. It does a good job at keeping everything you place there from moving or falling off. However, there was no storage space under the footwell. And here's the tray table. The window seats that are closer to the window provide a good amount of privacy. You're not in a closed suite, but unless you lean forward, you can't really see your neighbors. And I appreciated the adjustable armrest, which adds a bit of shoulder space when you're lying flat. That said, this seat does feel a bit tight, and the footwell is extremely narrow, which makes moving around, especially when sleeping, pretty tricky. I also noticed some visible wear and tear on the surfaces. Still, it's functional and comfortable enough for a mid to long-haul flight like this. Soon after reaching cruising altitudes, service started with a warm towel, followed by a welcome drink and some nuts. The menu offered a great variety, plenty of drinks, multiple main courses, and options for various dietary preferences. >> I chose the ravioli, which was nicely presented and tasted good, though it wasn't particularly memorable. The main downside was that all the courses were served at once, which takes away from that refined multi-course dining feel. Also, the drink glasses were a bit dirty, which is a real letdown, especially in business class. Unfortunately, the restroom was easily the weakest part of this flight. It was incredibly cramped and the sink didn't drain properly. Furthermore, there were no special amenities, just soap. Definitely below what you'd expect in business class. Each passenger received an amenity kit designed by one of various South American artists that collaborate with LATAM. On this flight, I got one by Judy Kaufman. These amenity kits are reusable and collectible, which adds a fun touch to it. Inside, you'll find earplugs, an eye mask, lip balm, hand cream, socks, a bamboo toothbrush, and toothpaste. Most of them from Feito Brasil, a luxury Brazilian brand that specializes in artisanal, vegan, and sustainable cosmetic products. It's great to see that LATAM puts real thought into the design and eco-friendliness of these kits. Also, them coming in multiple designs is somewhat unique and makes you want to collect them all. The in-flight entertainment setup was actually quite nice. The screen was perfectly sized for the distance from the seat. It was responsive and had a solid mix of movies and TV shows, both new and classic titles. The noise-canceling headphones worked very well, and so did the remote control, although getting it out of its holder was a bit awkward. Unfortunately, there was no Wi-Fi on this flight, not even for purchase, which is a big miss in 2025. And the moving map wasn't available, either. Still, the system performed well overall and kept me entertained throughout the flight. When it came time to rest, I put the seat into bed mode. The pillow and duvet were super plush and comfortable, and the cabin was kept at a pleasant temperature throughout the flight. Unfortunately, the sleeping experience itself wasn't great. The seat felt narrow, and the foot well made it almost impossible to turn your body. The lowering right armrest does give you a bit more space, but overall, I wouldn't say this bed setup is very comfortable. About an hour and a half before landing, the pre-landing meal was served. There was a choice between a roast beef sandwich or a falafel burger, with dessert options of chocolate ganache or seasonal fruit. I chose the roast beef sandwich, which came with chips and the chocolate ganache. It was okay, edible but far from impressive, and presentation was pretty basic. The cash price for this business class flight with LATAM Airlines I took in late May of 2025 was around $2,000, but instead of paying cash, I redeemed 50,000 Virgin Atlantic points and paid $55.80 in taxes and fees. But thanks to a 30% transfer bonus from American Express, I only had to transfer around 39,000 MR points. With that bonus, my redemption value came out to be about 5 cents per point. A fantastic deal, especially for an 8-hour international business class flight that includes Delta One Lounge access. But now, let's see how I'd rate this business class experience with LATAM Airlines. The ground experience. The ground experience gets an 8 out of 10. The standout elements here were definitely the priority security line and access to the Delta One Lounge, both of which made the pre-flight experience feel truly premium and stress-free. However, aside from those highlights, the rest of the ground experience, including check-in, boarding, and arrival, felt pretty standard and didn't really offer anything above what you'd normally expect. The seat and cabin. The seat and cabin gets a 6 out of 10. The seat itself is decent and visually appealing, with a good level of privacy and a comfortable cabin environment overall, but in bed mode, the space feels tight and the narrow footwell makes it difficult to get comfortable. On top of that, the onboard restroom was a major weak point, cramped and lacking in amenities, definitely below business class expectations. The onboard dining. The onboard dining gets a 6 out of 10. There's a solid foundation here with a good variety of options and meals that are decent in both taste and presentation. However, a few execution issues really hold this back, things like the dining service style and the poor cleanliness of the glassware. The IFE and amenities. The IFE and amenities get a 7 out of 10. There are definitely some strong points here, especially with the amenity kit, which is both stylish and thoughtfully designed, and the overall entertainment system, which offers a good selection of content. But the biggest drawback is the lack of Wi-Fi, which is a major miss for a long-haul business class flight today. Limited storage space at the seat is another small downside. The onboard service. The onboard service gets a seven out of 10. The crew was friendly, professional, and did their job well throughout the flight. That said, the service felt more reactive than proactive, and there weren't many personalized touches that made the experience feel truly special or memorable. Averaging everything out gives this business class experience with LATAM Airlines an overall score of 6.8 out of 10. It isn't among the elite products, but it's a solid and mostly comfortable way to travel, especially when you factor in the amazing Delta One Lounge access and the great redemption value using points. The seat could use an update, and the food and restrooms definitely have room for improvement, but for an overnight 8-hour flight to South America, I'd say it's absolutely worth it and would fly in this business class product again, especially if booked with points. But ladies and gentlemen, that is just my opinion. What do you think of LATAM's business class product? Would you fly it, or would you fly to South America with another airline? Let me know in the comments section below. But for now, I just want to say thank you so much for watching, and I will see you in the next one. Take care.

reviews.transcript_full: KLM once used to be our favorite airline, but recent experiences have not been great. We haven't tried our economy product in a while, so we are curious to find out if flying standard economy with them is still worth it and if they live up to their own slogan, travel well. So, let's have a look at our full flight experience including an emergency landing and one a very questionable food item. We're flying to Bangkok and our journey starts at Amsterdam Schiphol Airport. We booked an economy standard ticket and that includes one piece of check-in luggage of maximum 23 kg and free seat selection upon check-in. Since we're flying economy, there are no further perks for us, which means we entertained ourselves by walking over this glass floor luggage belt. Last time we flew with KLM, we were in premium economy, which was fine, but not amazing. And especially the breakfast eggs were terrible. So, here's hoping we don't have to deal with those again. All right, let's go and experience economy standard. Time for our flight and here we are boarding the Boeing 777-200, which is set up in a 3-4-3 configuration. It's a full flight and we were seated apart because we wanted to get the full economy standard experience and did not pay for advanced seat selection. Also, because our ticket includes free seat selection during check-in, we figured if we were the first to check-in, we could still select two seats next to each other. We were wrong. Despite the seat map showing lots of availability mere minutes before check-in, the only option to be seated together the second check-in opened were paid seats. A little strange if you ask us, but okay. A very kind solo passenger offered to switch seats, which was a win-win situation since these seats are a lot less wide than we remember and are definitely not made for people with broad shoulders. Remember this solo passenger for later though. So, let's have a look at the seats. When you enter the plane, there's a blanket and basic pillow waiting for you. We have to say the pillow and the blanket feel a bit cheap and especially the pillow is not very comfortable. As for the legroom, it's pretty standard with 79 cm and when the person in front of you reclines, there's still luckily a bit of space left. The seat also comes with a split fold-out table and there's an adjustable headrest. For charging your device, you can either use the USB-A port integrated in the screen or the power outlet below the seat, but it seems that it doesn't get cleaned that often. Now, let's get ready for takeoff and continue our review in disguise. Shortly after takeoff, we received a wet towel and a headset. So, up until that point, you could not watch anything on your screen if you forgot to bring your own. We suspect it's because boarding started later than planned, but we're not sure. Let us know in the comments if you know if this is always the case with KLM. Speaking of the entertainment system, I have to say we were pretty impressed with it and dare I say it, it's one of the better ones we've experienced in economy recently. The home screen nicely shows a timeline of what you can expect during the flight. There's also a pretty good selection of entertainment. You can find the in-flight drinks menu and of course the most important part, a working in-flight map. Yay! To help us celebrate having a good in-flight map, make sure to like this video and subscribe to our channel. Aside from that, there's also free Wi-Fi on board that allows for messaging and emails. If you need more internet capabilities, you do have to pay for it. Before we move on to the food, let's quickly check out the toilets. There's only hand soap available though and no moisturizer creams that other airlines sometimes have. Time for our first meal, which was dinner. And we had the option to choose between the classic chicken or pasta. So, of course, we chose both. As for the sides, there were some peppers stuffed with cream cheese, a mystery dip that was definitely not mayo, some olives and sun-dried tomatoes, and finally, a bread roll. Taste-wise, I'm not sure what to say, except that we recommend the chicken over the pasta. And yeah, don't come to this flight hungry. Right after the meal service, something unexpected happened. Shortly after we were up in the air, a flight attendant noticed that a passenger was feeling unwell, and then someone yelled if there was a doctor on board. And remember that kind solo traveler offering to switch seats? Turns out that person is a doctor and rushed to help immediately. After some time, it was decided that we were going to have to make an emergency medical landing, and that's why we were now heading to Istanbul instead of Bangkok. To be able to do so, the plane started dumping fuel to get ready for landing. We never experienced an emergency landing before, and we really hope that the person in question has made a full recovery in the meantime. We have to say, it made for an impressive sight, though, and Istanbul by night looks very beautiful from above. Once the plane got a whole lot lighter, we made our descent, and once we made it, we awaited the medical staff to do their thing and take away the sick passenger. After refueling, we quickly left again for Bangkok, and the whole situation only took about 1 and 1/2 hours or so, which was very impressive. With the plane safely back in the air and most people trying to sleep, it was time for the dessert portion of the meal, and a brownie. The timing was very unfortunate, because everyone was trying to sleep and these things have the loudest wrappers imaginable. Then finally after some sleep and with only 2 and 1/2 hours of the flight left, it was time for breakfast. We were lucky to not have the dreaded eggs again, but we're not sure if what we got instead is any better. Dear viewer, behold the KLM breakfast. A cup of sour fruit, strawberry yogurt, and what's that? Oh yes, it's a Dutch pastry snack known as a cheese roll or kaasbroodje. Only eaten for breakfast by those who are either under 21 or hungover or both. With the Dutch travelers, you can count on some nostalgia and our love for greasy savory pastries, but to serve this for breakfast to an international audience even is definitely a choice and not a very good one if you ask us. Especially because the cheese roll wasn't executed that well. It was just very fatty and greasy and not something you want to start your morning with. So with a disappointing breakfast done and after 12 plus hours of flying, it was finally time to land >> [music] >> in Bangkok. With us safely arriving at Suvarnabhumi International Airport, it's time to have a look at what we paid for this eventful flight and if we think KLM is still worth it. For a direct flight from Amsterdam to Bangkok, we paid 950 euros per person for a return ticket including one piece of check-in luggage and so-called free seat selection during check-in. Although, I wouldn't attach too much value to that. As for the emergency landing, this was obviously not planned, but was handled very well by the cabin crew who were attentive overall. The in-flight entertainment system was good, too, but the food was honestly very sad, and especially the breakfast is a poor showing. The seats have also become very thin and narrow, and the overall cleanliness is debatable. It seems that KLM is dealing with some sort of identity crisis where its most recent campaign slogan "Travel Well" alludes to flying with a good experience, whilst their pricing and ancillary revenue strategies creams low-cost carrier, but without the fares to match it. So, while the flight was pretty okay and definitely not the worst we've experienced in economy, it's also not worth it to pay a whole lot extra for, since the experience as a whole is just mediocre at best. Oh, well, at least it was a direct flight. Well, sort of. If you want to see what flying premium economy with KLM is like, click here, and otherwise, thank you so much for watching. Bye.

Having the spare tray table next to me was very useful. The crew then came around with a hot drink service and I got myself a coffee. And they've gone all out on branding here with a purple red air cup and even a red air sugar packet. After the meal and drink service is complete, I got myself settled in to relaxing and watching the in-flight entertainment. I asked my Patreon WhatsApp group this question whilst in flight, but I'd be interested in getting your views, too, on recline etiquette. I'm usually personally of the view that in economy on a daytime flight, it can be a bit harsh to recline onto the person behind you. On this particular flight though, there was no one behind me and the plane was almost empty. But not long after take-off, someone moved into the seat directly behind me despite dozens of empty rows being available. It's perfectly cool to just recline the entire flight into that person under those circumstances, right? And this was a comfortable seat to relax in, helped by a really excellent pillow and blanket. In fact, this pillow might be the nicest and softest I've ever had in economy. And although the blanket was relatively thin, that was also really soft, too. I'd say the crew spent most of the flight in the rear galley, but they did come through the cabin a few times with water and to clear tray tables. And they were also very friendly when I went back to ask for a Diet Pepsi at one point. An hour 45 before landing, the crew came around for what I thought would be the second meal service, but was actually just a snack. An option of popcorn or ice cream and a drink service soon followed. As nice as the ice cream was, I have to admit I was a little disappointed not to get something a little more substantial. But, not everyone eats as much as I do, and ultimately it's not the longest flight in the world. >> [music] >> And in fairness, this ice cream is better than what I was served on Emirates for a similar length of flight, for example. So, I paid 1,127 for this, and that's a return trip, economy on the outbound, premium on the return. About the same price for both of those, so the economy outbound was a similar price to the premium economy return. So, it feels like the pricey side for an economy flight of this length. The seat has been great. Obviously, I've got the advantage here of being in basically four months business class with the row to myself. But, even without that, it's a comfortable enough seat. And it is worth just calling out again how good the inflight entertainment system is in this seat. So, if you are looking to just relax and watch a few films for a few hours on a flight, they are a good option. The one bad side about it, I'd say, is the tray table. So, people end up just slamming them shut all the time, which obviously then is quite annoying for the person in the seat in front. Food on board has been good, probably on the higher end of economy, but you know, nothing that will blow you away. Probably not a big enough differentiator to make Riyadh Air stand out or anything, especially when they're also not serving alcohol, which I know will be a big issue for some. And the crew, every interaction I've had with them, they've been really friendly, and I think they provide a good economy level service. Although, obviously, a few areas I've highlighted where that could be improved upon a bit. Now, would I fly them again? Well, if the fare is good, or if I could guarantee a flight as quiet as this one. But, I do think pricing probably needs to be a little bit better for me to rush to go with them again. One thing that would help with pricing would be reward flights. Riyadh Air do have their own reward points that you can earn, but you can't currently use it to book flights just yet. There is also talk of a partnership with airlines like Virgin Atlantic, and I'd certainly consider them a good option for a Virgin points redemption if that comes to fruition. The offering is consistent and excellent on both.  Unfortunately, we were disappointed that this amenity kit did not come with an eye mask.  Now for the tech. Both aircraft give you a universal AC power outlet and a USB-A  port at every seat, so keeping your devices juiced up is no problem.  The provided headphones are also a real step up from the cheap air buds you get in economy.

reviews.transcript_full:
Today, we’re flying Singapore Airlines Business Class
aboard an Airbus A350 from Brussels to Singapore The video features the complete Singapore Airlines Business 
Class experience (cabin, seat, meals, amenities, entertainment)  The video also features the spectacular landing 
in a thunderstorm at Singapore Changi Airport Welcome to Brussels Airport in Belgium
for today’s Business Class flight on Singapore Airlines Singapore Airlines has dedicated Business Class 
check-in counters at Brussels Airport Long lines snake through security and passport control Before the flight, it’s time to relax in 'The View' Lounge The lounge is located in Pier B,
just past security and passport control Seating areas are arranged for both comfort and privacy There are plenty of charging points and
work tables for business travelers The lounge's decor is simple yet stylish, 
with warm wood tones and soft lighting The natural light and design make it a pleasant place to wait A self-serve bar includes wine, beer, and a range of soft drinks The lounge's large windows overlook the tarmac A buffet area offers a selection
of snacks, salads, and hot dishes During the morning, you’ll find pastries, fruit, and yogurt Later in the day, sandwiches, soup, & Belgian waffles are served Showers are available for passengers
who want to freshen up before a long flight It’s time to head to the gate for boarding This is the Singapore Airlines A350 that will fly us to Singapore The aircraft has registration number 9V-SMO (built in 2017) Singapore Airlines has 65 Airbus A350s
(the world's largest fleet of 350s) Singapore Airlines operates several versions of the A350,
including the A350-900ULR ('ultra-long-range' model) Singapore Airlines was the A350-900ULR's launch customer
and remains the only airline to operate it Singapore Airlines’ A350-900ULR operates the world’s longest
scheduled commercial nonstop route (Singapore to New York) The A350 is one of the quietest jets in the sky The A350’s sleek carbon-fiber design also makes 
it lighter and more fuel-efficient The A350’s wings are elegantly curved
and flexible, improving aerodynamics It’s time to board the aircraft Singapore Airlines’ A350 features 42 Business Class seats The seats are spread over two cabins
and arranged in a 1-2-1 layout A larger cabin in the front of the plane
holds the bulk of the Business Class seats (26 in total) The remaining 16 seats are located in a smaller
and more intimate Business Class cabin over the wings The cabin design was created by James Parker Associated,
the company that also created the interiors of the Orient Express  Center seats include a partition screen
that can be raised for extra privacy All seats along the windows are single seats Singapore Airlines' Business Class seat 
is one of the widest seats in the sky Seat pitch is 153 cm (60 inches), and width is 71 cm (28 inches) The crew welcomes passengers with a drink and hot towel The pilot welcomes the passengers Singapore Airlines’ hospitality is
world-renowned, and it’s easy to see why Once boarding is complete, the safety video is shown It’s a beautifully produced film (not just a safety briefing) The video blends essential safety instructions
with Singapore’s cultural landmarks The famous Singapore Girl gracefully
guides passengers through each instruction Her presence symbolizes the airline’s
heritage of service and professionalism We’re leaving the gate (on time departure at 12 pm) Brussels Airport has three runways:
one north-south and two parallel east-west runways Singapore Airlines’ A350s are powered by
Rolls-Royce Trent XWB engines Have you ever flown with Singapore Airlines?
If so, what was your experience? Leave a comment Let’s explore Singapore Airlines’ A350 Business Class seat A reading light sits at eye level for easy use during night flights Seat adjustments are made through
a control panel in the armrest by the aisle In front of the seat is a large 18-inch HD screen A small compartment with vanity mirror sits beside the screen The entertainment screen can be tilted The seat features a large ottoman (foot rest) A console next to the seat holds another reading light,
the power outlets and some storage space Next to the console sits the handheld remote
for the inflight entertainment system A storage box in the armrest is perfect
for a bottle of water or small personal items The tray table is stored in the armrest
and can be adjusted in height and position The bulkhead seats in rows 11 & 19 feature full-width ottomans In the other seats, the footwell is tucked
diagonally into the side of the seat ahead When the seat converts into a bed,
your legs extend into this angled cubby In Singapore Airlines' Business Class, amenity kits 
are available upon request rather than automatically provided The amenity kit is designed in collaboration with
Le Labo, the boutique fragrance house from New York The kit holds a selection of
Le Labo Bergamote 22 skincare essentials Singapore Airlines sometimes gives Business Class 
passengers a collectible plush bear as a keepsake Slippers, socks and eye-masks are offered A large pillow and soft duvet are provided Noise-cancelling headphones are provided,
ensuring an immersive experience Flying through high clouds shows just how fast we’re moving Let’s explore the inflight menu Singapore Airlines partners with world-class chefs
to create its Business and First Class menus The airline’s “Book the Cook” service lets passengers
pre-select main courses before departure Canape : Singapore chicken satay,
with onion, cucumber, and spicy peanut sauce Cocktail: Singapore Sling Appetizer: Vitello Tonnato (thinly sliced veal), with creamy
tuna sauce, capers, tomato, caviars and snow pea tendril Main course: classic beef stew in beer sauce,
Brussels sprouts, carrots, shallot and roasted grenaille potatoes Dessert: Oreo ice cream, raspberry bavarois
and a selection of cheese and sliced fresh fruits Singapore Airlines' Airbus A350 features 
three lavatories for Business Class passengers Payot hand lotion and facial mist
are available in the lavatories during the flight We can enjoy some beautiful views along the way The IFE system is controlled using a handheld remote Called KrisWorld, Singapore Airlines' IFE system includes
hundreds of movies, TV shows, and curated playlists Singapore Airlines offers its Business Class passengers
complimentary onboard Wi-Fi during the entire flight The flight can be tracked
in real-time using an interactive 3D map The sun sets as we fly over Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan A light bite is served mid-flight: vegetarian rice noodles,
with lettuce, black mushrooms, and Chinese greens Snacks are also available in the galley throughout the flight It’s time for some rest:
the cabin crew assists in setting up the bed When fully flat, the bed measures 198 cm or 78 inches in length I am lucky during this flight: one seat can be used for sitting,
while the other is fully converted into my bed The full-width ottoman of the bulkhead seat allows
for a natural sleeping position and unrestricted legroom A few hours later: we're crossing the Bay of Bengal As dawn approaches, the cabin lighting
gradually brightens to mimic sunrise Breakfast starts with a selection of sliced fresh fruits,
Bircher muesli, flavored yoghurt, and assorted bread rolls Main breakfast course: Dutch mini fluffy pancakes
with pineapple compote, strawberry and butter We're encountering some moderate turbulence near Phuket Turbulence can feel unsettling, 
but the plane is designed to handle it safely How do you feel about turbulence — calm or anxious? I’m a nervous flyer, but it helps  
to be on a reputable airline like Singapore Airlines A crew member, curious about my blog, shared 
this lovely note before we landed We’re approaching the Singapore Airlines airspace Unfortunately, thunderstorms are building up
over Singapore, so we have to circle before landing The sky over Singapore is stormy as we approach the airport Thunder rumbles in the distance,
and lightning flashes across the clouds Singapore Airlines is one of the world’s most awarded airlines Singapore Airlines' story began in 1947
when Malayan Airways operated its very first flight The airline was founded with a twin-engined Airspeed Consul In 1966, it became Malaysia-Singapore Airlines, known as MSA When MSA split in 1972, two national carriers were born:
Malaysia Airlines and Singapore Airlines Singapore Airlines quickly established
itself as a global carrier with high standards The airline built a reputation for reliability and premium comfort Singapore Airlines has often led the way in aviation innovation It was the first airline to offer free headsets,
choice of meals, and drinks in Economy Class In 2007, Singapore Airlines was the launch customer
for the Airbus A380, the world’s largest passenger aircraft The carrier is part of the Star Alliance network,
connecting passengers to over 1,000 destinations The company’s commitment to quality extends
beyond its cabins — to training, safety, and sustainability The Singapore Airlines brand stands for
precision, warmth, and world-class service Would you be scared to land in a thunderstorm? Despite the storm, the aircraft touches
down smoothly on the wet runway Thank you for watching this
Singapore Airlines A350 Business Class flight
