reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Zurich Airport in Switzerland. Today, I'm flying with Etihad Airways to Abu Dhabi. I've flown with them several times in economy class, I'm excited to finally experience their business class product. In the future, I will also be reviewing Emirates and Qatar Airways, so let's go and see how good Etihad is first! Zurich Airport is the main gateway to Switzerland. I travelled with Air Serbia from Belgrade the night before and arrived here at 7:55 pm. Since it was relatively late, and I wanted to maximise my lounge use for my Etihad flight the next day, I stayed at the transit hotel. The hotel offers single, double, and triple rooms, as well as couches, and can be booked for periods ranging from 3 hours to overnight, depending on your budget and transit time. Switzerland is a notably expensive country. It cost me 120 Swiss francs for an overnight stay in this single room. In addition to the bed, the room is equipped with reading lights, charging ports, a desk, a TV, a sink, and a kettle. There’s no ensuite bathroom; they’re shared with other guests. Nevertheless, the place is well-maintained, and the shower water is warm with good pressure. As an avgeek, all of these inconveniences and high costs were forgiven when I opened the curtains. This is quite a unique view. The transit hotel is in Terminal D, and my flight to Abu Dhabi departs from Terminal E. To get there, I had to take a short ride on the Skymetro, a driverless automated people mover. Terminal E, also known as the midfield terminal, is exclusively dedicated to non-Schengen international flights. Being a standalone terminal, it is installed with floor-to-ceiling windows on all sides of the building, providing abundant natural light and impressive views of the apron. The bench chairs don’t have armrests, making them perfect for napping if you have an overnight layover and don’t want to pay for a hotel room. Zurich Airport is the hub for Swiss International Air Lines. As such, it operates three lounges at Terminal E. The Swiss First Lounge is open to Star Alliance first-class passengers and HON Circle members, the Senator Lounge is designated for Star Alliance Gold members, and the Business Lounge is accessible for Star Alliance business class passengers. Alongside the Swiss Air lounges, there are two third-party lounges and an Emirates Lounge. Anticipating that Etihad, not being a Star Alliance member, would direct me to either the Aspire or Primeclass lounges, I was surprised by a special arrangement Etihad made with Swiss, allowing me to use the Swiss Business Lounge instead. The Swiss Business and Senator Lounge share a common reception desk. The Senator Lounge is marginally superior. Therefore, I tried to enter using my Star Alliance Gold status. Unfortunately, I was still directed to the Business Lounge as Etihad isn’t a Star Alliance airline. I have to say, even the business lounge is quite amazing. Upon entering, you’ll find a map that helps first-time visitors navigate the available facilities. While lacking a whisky bar, there’s a self-serve mini bar offering a diverse selection of spirits, wines, beers, fizzy drinks, and water. Adjacent to the bar is a cold buffet station offering fruits, cold meats, salads, cheeses and also different condiments, and bread. I must note that the choices are not overly expansive; it’s similar to a Qantas Club in Australia. However, there’s a live chef station where you can order eggs cooked to your liking. In the middle of the lounge, there are wines, chocolates, more fruits, and coffee machines. Covering an area of 1200 square metres and a capacity of 200 seats, the business lounge has many seating options, including bar stools, dining tables, and couches, accommodating both business and leisure travellers. Additionally, there are a few semi-enclosed workstations, ideal for making phone calls and completing tasks before the flight. For those facing a long layover, towards the back of the lounge, there’s a quiet area with day beds. I ended up picking a seat next to the window. Zurich Airport’s busiest route is to London Heathrow; consequently, there are both European and UK-type power plugs next to my seat—an impressive attention to detail. Given the limited food options, I grabbed two Swiss chocolates, which were amazing, and ordered an omelette from the live cooking station, it tasted pretty ordinary. However, my eyes were quickly drawn to the outdoor terrace. In addition to offering some fresh air, the terrace presents spectacular views of the apron, takeoffs and landings on the runways, and the Swiss Alps in the distance. Moreover, there are even binoculars for scoping out planes on the far side of the airport. Lastly, private showers are available. Despite the limited food choices, this is still one of my all-time favourite business-class lounges. There’s so much natural light throughout the lounge, even in the toilets, and the outdoor terrace makes the views unbeatable. For those without lounge access, Zurich Airport has established two observation decks, one at Terminal B and the other is here in Terminal E. Positioned at the western end of the terminal and in the centre of Zurich Airport’s three runways,  this observation deck gives you a 270-degree view of the airport. There are free-to-use binoculars that provide close-up views of all airport activities, and various play areas add an element of fun for children. Zurich Airport is certainly a heaven for avgeeks and plane spotters. The aircraft that will be taking me to Abu Dhabi today is a Boeing 787-9. Currently, Etihad’s fleet comprises 30 787-9s, with some having first class and others with only business and economy class. Furthermore, the airline has three new aircraft with a fresh interior and cabin design on order and is expected to join the fleet soon. Boarding commenced 45 minutes before departure. This aircraft is in a 2-class layout. At the front are 28 Etihad Business Studios in a 1-2-1 configuration. Based on the Zodiac platform, these business class seats are arranged in an alternating forward/rearward staggered pattern. The best seats for solo travellers are the forward-facing window seats, providing more privacy as they are closer to the window and less exposed to the aisle. In the centre section, the forward-facing rows are ideal for couples travelling together, as the seats are positioned right next to one another. Each business class passenger has access to a large overhead bin. I chose seat 10K, a forward-facing seat in the second last row. Although these seats share a strikingly similar footprint with Qatar’s Q-suites, they lack the sliding door, making them feel less private. An Acqua di Parma amenity kit was already on my seat when I boarded, and the crew offered me a choice of water, orange juice, Champagne, or lemon mint juice as soon as I settled in. My seat wasn’t particularly clean. There were small flies crawling on the windows, fluff above the air vent, and around the control buttons. Once everyone was on board, the crew handed me a menu and a hot wet towel, which I found perfect for wiping the surfaces around my seat. Welcome aboard Etihad Airways flight EY74 bound to Abu Dhabi.  Our flight today will take us a flight time of 5h35m, initially we are expected to climb to 37,000ft, and a final cruising altitude of 39,000ft. Seats 9C and 9H are definitely the ones to avoid, as they are rear-facing and lack windows. The business class cabin is pretty full today, with around six empty seats toward the back. Now, let’s dive into the seat’s features. The seat has a width of 22 inches and plenty of legroom. A blanket is placed on the footwell, and there’s a small storage area below. Next to the TV, there’s a small reading light, a coat hook, and an exceptionally solid and sturdy tray table. Above this table, there are two USB ports for charging small devices, a remote for controlling the TV, and an all-in-one touch-sensitive control screen. Along the edge of the table is another seat-control strip, allowing one to easily control the essential functions while lying down. This screen is available in both Arabic and English. I can use it to control the electronic window shades, the massage function, the seat cushion firmness, the seat’s recline, the lights around me, and the ‘do not disturb’ button. In addition to the overhead reading light, there’s a lamp next to my seat, which, in my opinion, adds a luxurious elegance to Etihad’s business class product. Under the lamp, you can find a magazine holder, a universal power plug, and a hidden storage space where a bottle of water and headphones are placed. The plane is equipped with Wi-Fi, and there are two packages. The $2.99 text package only allows you to send text messages on social media, while the $9.99 package enables unlimited internet access for the entire flight. If you are an Etihad Guest member, which is free to join, you can get the text package for free. With this package, I couldn’t refresh my Instagram feed, but I successfully sent a message on Messenger. I later decided to purchase the full $9.99 plan. The speed was fast enough for me to upload instagram stories and watch a few videos on YouTube. While attempting to connect to the internet, the crew kindly offered me a drink and some warm nuts. As the 13th-best airline in the world, according to Skytrax rankings, Etihad has a massive range of beverages in business class. There are six choices of teas, various types of hot and iced coffee, four mocktails, some premium mixers, soft drinks, juice, and water. Printed on a separate piece of paper is a wine list featuring Bellini, Champagne, wines from all over the world, different spirits, liquors, and beers. The Butterfly Effect mocktail is such a beautiful drink—refreshing and fragrant without being too sweet. It’s definitely one of my favourite mocktails I’ve had in the sky. In the meantime, the crew also took my lunch order. Etihad allows its business class passengers to dine anytime they want, but the crew do try to encourage everyone to eat soon after takeoff. The menu features some all-day snack items and a full à la carte meal choices. The service was indeed on the slower side. The crew served from the front to the back. It took about an hour from taking my order to being served the entrée. I was starving. Each meal comes with a seasonal salad with olive oil, balsamic vinegar, and Etihad’s signature duo bread. For starters, I chose Cecina beef. Etihad partnered with Armani/Casa tableware in December 2022. The vibrant green, white, and black colours truly make the dishes stand out. The new cutleries also look stunning. This Spanish-cured, paper-thin beef tastes delectable, with a slight nuttiness, melt-in-the-mouth tenderness, and a hint of smoke. Accompanied with tomatoes and olives, it’s a well-balanced dish. Benefiting from Etihad’s partnership with Virgin Australia, I’ve had the chance to visit Etihad’s first lounge in Abu Dhabi, even when travelling in Economy. One dish I consistently enjoyed there was the beef tenderloin. So, on this occasion, I decided to try it on the plane. Considering the initial cooking is done in a central kitchen on the ground, serving a perfect reheated steak in-flight is not an easy feat. My steak was cooked to “well-done”, which isn’t typically how I like it, but thankfully, with the generous amount of mushroom sauce, the meat didn’t taste dry at all. Furthermore, I have never had poached apples in my steak before; surprisingly, the sweetness of the apple worked well with the sauce. To finish, I opted for the Häagen-Dazs ice cream; there were three flavours available: vanilla, strawberry, and chocolate. We are now already halfway through our journey. There are two lavatories for the 28 business class passengers, both at the front of the plane. There’s no cologne or body lotion here, as everyone was already given an amenity kit. “Acqua di Parma” is an Italian luxury lifestyle company that produces fragrances, skincare, and other scented products. In this beautiful faux leather bag, there’s cologne, hand cream, as well as sanitising wipes, hand sanitiser, a dental kit, socks, an eye mask, and earplugs. Let’s now take a look at the inflight entertainment system. The TV screen is 18 inches in size. As an airline that flies to over 70 destinations around the globe, I was surprised to find that the system only has two languages. The screen displays a comprehensive list of all available beverages on board. Although I couldn’t just order my drinks with a simple touch of a button, it was still nice to see what they have without having to refer to the paper menu. Regarding the movie selection, it may not be as extensive as that of Emirates, Cathay, or Turkish Airlines, there are still numerous choices available. There are also TV series, live TV, music, games, podcasts, radios, weather forecasts, and a live newsfeed. And of course, you can check out the flight path as well. If the main screen is too far to reach, you can use the touch-sensitive remote to make your selections. In addition, you can use the remote to check out the flight path while watching a movie on the main screen. There are still 2 hours left until landing. As expected, the seat can be converted into a fully flat bed. The rear-facing seats can extend into a 75.7-inch-long bed, yet my forward-facing seat is 80.5 inches long. I’m 6’1’, and my toes can’t reach the wall.  The narrow footwell limited the space for my legs, but I still find it comfortable. And the 22-inch seat width provides ample room for my arms and shoulders. If I have to say something negative, without a sliding door, I still feel quite exposed when lying down. Despite the lack of mattress pad on this daytime flight, a luxuriously soft and warm Armani/Casa duvet is still available. I couldn’t work out the brand of the headphones, but they did an excellent job of filtering out the aircraft noise. If you're flying with us in Business or First, you are welcome to refresh in our arrivals lounge. This is where you'll meet your pre-booked Etihad chauffeur. I had an uninterrupted 1-hour nap. For those starting or concluding their journey in Abu Dhabi, all first-class, The Residence, and certain eligible fare-class Business class passengers can enjoy a complimentary chauffeur service to and from the airport. If your fare qualifies, the booking option will appear on the app, and the chauffeur can transport you to any location within the UAE. In general, it was a pleasant flight. Other than the slightly dirty seat I discovered at boarding, I was thoroughly satisfied with everything else. I love all the fancy touchscreens. The crew were nice and friendly, and I enjoyed all the dishes that I ordered; they were healthy, tasty, and the portions were generous. The seats are less private than Qatar’s Q-suite, but they are way better than the 2-3-2 layout found on the Emirates Boeing 777s. I would certainly fly with Etihad again. In fact, tomorrow, I’ll be flying on their A350-1000 aircraft, which features their current newest business class product, complete with individual sliding doors for enhanced privacy! I’ll tell you all about that experience in my next video. A very good evening to you ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to Abu Dhabi. The local time here is 6:55 in the evening. This video was filmed in June when Etihad still operated from the old Terminal 3 instead of the midfield Terminal A at Abu Dhabi Airport. My plane was parked at a remote gate. Business class passengers were provided with a dedicated shuttle bus to the arrivals hall. Welcome to Abu Dhabi; once through immigration, the Etihad arrivals lounge was just before the exit. It offered several beverages, snacks, and private shower suites. For those who had arranged a chauffeur service, when you’re ready to leave, the staff would accompany you to your vehicle, ensuring a seamless transition to your next destination!! It truly adds a delightful touch to the conclusion of the Etihad business class journey. Thank you so much for watching! If you found this video interesting, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more flight and train reviews! See you all in my next video!

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Istanbul! I have two flights coming up today. First, I’ll be flying with Turkish Airlines to Helsinki. After that, I’ll be flying in Finnair’s brand new A350 business class to Singapore. This is my entire itinerary: Istanbul - Helsinki - Singapore, then Hong Kong! The total duration comes close to 52 hours. This exciting journey gives me the chance to enjoy business class services with three different airlines, all at a low cost of AU$2200. I consider this an absolute bargain, so let the adventure begin! Istanbul has two major airports. The New Istanbul Airport, opened in 2018, handles most of the city’s international traffic. Being the hub for Turkish Airlines, there’s a dedicated entry for the airline’s business and elite-level frequent flyers. I booked all my flights on Finnair’s website, but as my first flight was with Turkish Airlines, I had to check in with them. This airport is one of my favourites in the world. The international departures area resembles a giant shopping mall! Sam Chui thinks the terminal is too big, but I find it to be of a good size, getting to the furthest gate takes no more than 20 minutes. The Turkish Airlines business lounge is quite exceptional. Each chef has a dedicated cooking station, and the food is prepared right in front of you. For eligible passengers with long layovers in Istanbul, Turkish Airlines provides free hotel rooms in the city, and the lounge also offers private rooms and showers. My flight to Helsinki this morning is on a Turkish Airlines A321neo. There are five rows in business class with seats arranged in a 2-2 configuration. They have a sleek, modern design. The small divider adds a bit of privacy to the seat. There’s a universal power plug and USB port below the armrest. The 13-inch high-definition touchscreen is packed with entertainment options, including a collection of 659 movies for you to choose from! Turkish Airlines is known for its excellent in-flight catering. For this 3-hour flight, I was offered a watermelon and cheese appetiser, along with three main meal options. The plating is vibrant, and the food, as always, showcases the best of Turkish cuisine. The 3-hour flight went by quickly, and welcome to Helsinki! Helsinki is renowned for striking a harmonious balance between urban sophistication and serene landscapes. This Finnish capital is the perfect gateway for international visitors eager to chase the enchanting Northern Lights or the midnight sun in the nation’s Lapland region. Ladies and gentlemen, and dear children, we hope that you had a pleasant flight. As a Star Alliance member, thank you for flying with Turkish Airlines, Scandinavian Airlines, and Finnair's codeshare flight. We would like to say goodbye and hope to meet you again. Helsinki-Vantaa is the busiest airport in Finland. It’s the hub for Finnair, a member of the Oneworld alliance. Despite not being as busy as other major European hubs like Heathrow, Charles de Gaulle, or Frankfurt, its smaller size makes it one of Europe’s easiest and most pleasant transfer airports. Of course, there are duty-free shops, restaurants, and cafes for you to pass the time. My flight to Singapore is 13 hours away. While I could leave the airport and explore the city,  I decided remain airside and check out the two Finnair lounges in the non-Schengen zone. The Business Class Lounge is open to Oneworld Sapphire frequent flyers and business class passengers. Meanwhile, the Platinum Wing Lounge stands as an exclusive oasis for Oneworld Emerald frequent flyers. Upon entering, you’ll find luggage lockers, eliminating the need to drag your suitcase around the lounge. The lounge is divided into several separate spaces for working, relaxing, and dining, with distinctive Nordic design elements seamlessly integrated throughout. The upscale bar is really impressive, the shelves are stocked with vintage champagne, spirits, wines, and beers from local and international markets. The bartender is well-versed in creating signature cocktails as well as barista-style coffees. When I requested a fruity mocktail, the bartender prepared a delightful blueberry drink that tasted amazing. Since the Platinum Wing is only open to a handful of qualified passengers, it never gets crowded. Instead of exuding a business atmosphere, this lounge makes me feel as if I were at home. The couch-style chairs are incredibly comfortable, and nearly every seat is equipped with power plugs. For those who enjoy conversing with their travel partners, there are tables and stools behind the bar. And the working area provides seats fitted with small tables and lamps. Toward the far end of the lounge is the main dining area. The tables and chairs have a casual Ikea vibe, aligning with the overall homely atmosphere of the lounge. On every table, there’s an à la carte menu showcasing the month’s featured dishes. Additionally, there’s a dessert table with fruit, petit fours, cheeses, and a buffet station offering Nordic delicacies and Asian-inspired treats. I particularly appreciate the vibrant colours of the dishes, and the open kitchen at the back gives you a glimpse into the meal preparation process. I ordered the grilled salmon from the à la carte menu. It was delicious. And later decided to sample the reindeer burger from the menu! It was cooked nicely. The patty is a combination of smoked reindeer and beef, it tasted just like a classic hamburger, nothing special. Behind the dining room curtain hides a rather spacious, quiet area. This dark-blue-themed section emulates a living room, with numerous couches to cosy up in. For a flagship lounge, there has to be showers. There are three private shower rooms accessible on a first-come, first-use basis. You can reserve one for 30 minutes using the control pad. Once booked a vacant room, the door automatically unlocks. The shower room features a tasteful colour scheme of navy and grey, and you’ll find organic hand wash, creams, and various premium amenities at your disposal. The shower cubicle is generously sized and includes a rainfall and handheld showerhead. The most distinctive feature of the Platinum Wing is the sauna. In Finland, saunas are an integral part of the culture and hold deep significance. In the dressing room, there’s a vanity table, lockers, towels, and showers. The sauna can accommodate 4-5 people at a time. Since someone was already inside, I refrained from filming it. Here’s a picture I found on the internet. In general, the Platinum Wing is one of the most remarkable lounges I’ve ever visited. Unfortunately, it currently only opens from 10:30 am to 5:30 pm, which coincides with the departure time of most of Finnair’s long-haul flights. At 5:30 pm, I was asked to relocate to the business lounge next door. The business lounge is accessible to Oneworld business class passengers and Sapphire-level frequent flyers. There are luggage lockers at the entrance. Now, this place resembles more of an airport lounge than a cozy living room, it’s more ordinary, but the facilities remain largely similar. Upon entering, you’ll find a self-service beverage station stocked with beers, soft drinks, and tea bags. The seating looks a bit simpler but remains comfortable. The space is considerably larger, with a seating capacity of 450 people, compared to just 155 in the Platinum Wing. The buffet offers similar food, including salads, hot meals, side dishes, soup, snacks, and desserts, although there’s no à la carte menu. Behind the main dining area, there’s a circular bar. It’s not always staffed, therefore you can pour your own wines and mix drinks. I appreciate these wall-enclosed seats that provide both privacy and comfort. Once more, nearly all seats have power plugs nearby. While there’s no sauna, you can still take a shower before your flight. Can you guess the current time? Does this look like 6 pm to you? Well, surprise — it’s actually 10:21 pm. The sunset is expected at 10:46 pm, and sunrise at 3:53 am. This video was filmed in mid-June. Due to Helsinki’s geographical location, in June, the sun only briefly dips below the horizon before rising again. To me, this is quite phenomenal! Finnair’s long-haul fleet comprises 8 A330-300s and 17 A350-900s. They are undergoing gradual refurbishment, with plans to install the new business, premium economy, and economy class seats on all these aircraft by early 2024. The plane that will take me to Singapore is a refurbished 3-class 278-seat A350. It’s now 12:30 am, and the sun will rise again in just 3 hours. Yet remarkably, the sky remains anything but dark! Boarding commenced 35 minutes before departure. Welcome aboard! Finnair’s new business class is arranged in a 1-2-1 configuration, featuring Collin’s AirLounge seats. I love the dark blue colour, and it’s certainly one of the widest business seats I’ve seen. For optimal privacy and an excellent view of the engine during daytime, I picked seat 8A, located in the last row of the main cabin. The most unique design of the seat is that it’s not reclinable. The seat-back seamlessly blends with the sidewall, forming a semi-enclosed cocoon-like structure designed to resemble a piece of classic Nordic furniture rather than a simple airline seat. Once I settled in, the crew offered me a choice of still or sparkling water, champagne, or Finnair’s signature blueberry juice, which quickly became my favourite drink throughout the flight. Cabin crew arm the doors and cross check... We pushed back on time, and I couldn’t tell whether this is a sunset or sunrise! Helsinki-Vantaa Airport has three runways. This morning, we took off from runway 22R, then executed a left-hand turn over the city before continuing across the Gulf of Finland towards Tallinn, Estonia. As we headed south, the sky gradually darkened. Once the seatbelt sign was turned off, the crew handed me a wet towel to refresh myself. A meal will be served shortly. In the meantime, let’s take a closer look at the AirLounge seat! At the front, there’s a big high-definition entertainment screen. A mattress pad, a quilt, and a pair of slippers are neatly placed in the foot nook. I always appreciate having a small compartment like this so I can store small loose items here instead of having to always reach for my backpack. The left armrest doubles as a large table with a built-in wireless charging pad. There are buttons to control the leg rest, lights, and call the flight attendant. There’s another tray table that folds out to become a sizeable dining table or desk for work. Apart from the overhead reading light, there’s an adjustable lamp positioned near my shoulder to ensure ample lighting around my seat on a night flight like this. Beneath the lamp, there’s another concealed compartment where I found the remote control for the entertainment screen, a noise-cancelling headphone, and both USB type A and type C sockets. I also spotted a universal power plug near my feet, which I had missed earlier. The concept of the AirLounge is to offer both personal space and freedom to move, allowing me to relax in the most comfortable position. Furthermore, the two firm pillows on my seat make me feel like I’m lounging on a couch. Finnair does not have a dine-on-demand service in Business Class. Instead, long-haul flights typically include a main meal after takeoff and a lighter second meal a few hours before landing. A paper menu was given to us while we were on the ground, and you can find it on your entertainment screen too. To ensure your preferred choice is available, Finnair suggests that passengers pre-order their main meals online on long-haul flights from Helsinki. In terms of drinks, there’s a good selection of wines, beers, cocktails, and other non-alcoholic beverages. I must say, I love the presentation of the meal, each dish looks colourful and beautifully plated, and strikes a great balance between meat and vegetables. To begin, there are two cold plates. The thinly sliced beef is tender with a slightly caramelised exterior.  The citrusy ponzu sauce creates a delightful contrast that tantalises the taste buds. Instead of serving the typical green leaf salad found on many other airlines, the second cold plate is a creamy mustard potato salad. The green pea puree brings a burst of freshness and sweetness to my palate. Moving on to the main dish, the pork belly delivers a lavish and indulgent protein. The meat was well marinated in the sauce and was cooked thoroughly. It melted in my mouth instantaneously. Overall, all three dishes were incredibly delicious and maintained a high standard. I couldn’t fault anything. Aside from the cheese, there are two dessert options. Seeing that I was filming the flight, the crew warmly offered me both. I appreciate the petite portions they provide, as I assume most passengers, including myself, would prefer a lighter treat after a large and satisfying meal. The meal service concluded just 70 minutes after takeoff, which is remarkably swift. Shortly after that, the crew dimmed the lights to enable passengers to settle down for sleep. An amenity kit is provided in business class, featuring lip balms, facial cream, earplugs, and eye masks. The slippers in the foot nook come in two sizes, and the large size fits my feet perfectly. When it’s time to rest, you can press this button to elevate the leg rest, transforming the entire seat into a fully flat bed. The crew then kindly offered to make the bed for me. Now you can see how wide the seat is. The bed is long, I’m 6’1” or 186cm tall, and I couldn’t reach the end of the foot nook. Before I sleep, let me quickly show you Finnair’s redesigned inflight entertainment system. The touchscreen is 18 inches in size and offers eight languages. I love this timeline on the home screen, showing the time in both Helsinki and Singapore, the scheduled meal times, and the recommended sleep time. A quick glance would let passengers easily keep track of their flight progress. In terms of entertainment, there are movies, TV series, music, and games. There are 100 popular movies to choose from. The flight map proves that the Earth is not flat! If you select the explore mode, you can zoom in and out of the map. I find this to be a perfect way to enhance my geography knowledge. The aircraft is equipped with satellite Wi-Fi, which is free for the first hour for business and Finnair Gold frequent flyers and for the entire duration of the flight for Finnair’s platinum members. Other passengers can purchase internet access using a credit card or Finnair points. I connected with my free 1-hour pass, and the speed was fast enough to upload stories on my Instagram. It’s been 24 hours since I last slept. I had to get up at 3am for my flight from Istanbul to Helsinki yesterday morning. So, goodnight! I woke up after having a solid 3.5-hour nap. The quilt is fairly warm and soft, and my legs have plenty of space to move around. We are currently flying over the Caspian Sea and are still over 7.5 hours away from Singapore. There are three lavatories for the 43 business class passengers. I love this disinfectant spray so that I can wipe the toilet seat. As we are flying eastward, it’s now daytime outside. While there isn’t any eau de toilette or cologne,  the hand wash and body lotion are produced in Finland, and I love their scent. I then took a stroll to door 2. The crew has set up a small snack bar here where you can help yourself to water and a range of snacks. Feeling a bit peckish, I grabbed a pack of gummies and chips. In business class, Finnair provides noise-cancelling headphones, this pair effectively lowered the cabin noise, I was satisfied with them. After finishing my snack, I felt sleepy again, so I took another nap, only waking up 3 hours later. The time between the two meals is about 10 hours, which I find to be a really lengthy gap. Breakfast was still 2 hours away, and I began feeling quite hungry. I asked the crew if they had any more substantial snacks, such as a sandwich. Unfortunately, they didn’t have any, but they kindly offered me some fresh fruits. I decided to stay awake from this point on, as I was concerned that if I slept now, I might struggle to sleep tonight when the plane landed at 7:30 pm. We are finally only 2 hours away from landing. It’s 12 o’clock in Helsinki and 5 pm in Singapore. I find it amusing to have breakfast at nearly dinner time. Unless you have pre-ordered a dietary meal, there’s only one choice for everyone. It’s a typical Western breakfast consisting of bread, scrambled eggs, hash browns, baked beans, spinach, cold cuts of meat, fresh fruits, and yogurt. To complete the meal, I enjoyed a cup of cappuccino. As we begin our descent into Singapore, I’d like to share my thoughts on this flight. I genuinely admire Finnair’s innovative spirit: being the world’s first and only airline to offer non-reclining seats in business class is a bold move, and I must say I’m quite impressed. The contoured shell design provides exceptional privacy, creating a sense of being in a private suite. The spacious seat gives me ample room to sleep and stretch out. The dining experience, both in the lounge and onboard, was delightful. However, the absence of substantial snacks left me hungry between the meals. I believe, well, judging from their accents, the cabin crew were all based in Singapore. They were warm, polite, and professional, addressing me by my last name throughout the flight. Starting this October, Qantas Airways, the flag carrier of Australia, will be wet leasing two of Finnair's A330 aircraft for routes between Sydney and Bangkok, as well as Sydney and Singapore. I'm eagerly anticipating the opportunity to fly on this exceptional product again! Furthermore, I think getting three business class flights for AU$2200 was definitely a steal. A warm welcome to Singapore ladies and gentlemen. On behalf of all of us onboard Finnair, and the oneworld alliance, I hope you have enjoyed your stay with us. Thank you, goodbye, and we look forward to seeing you again soon onboard Finnair. Welcome to Singapore! Finnair uses Terminal 1 at Changi Airport, which provides convenient connections with its Oneworld partners. The arrival time is perfectly aligned for an onward Qantas flight to Australia. My next flight with Cathay Pacific to Hong Kong will depart in 17 hours. I decided to enter Singapore and stay at the Crowne Plaza, which offers fantastic views of Terminal 3 and the runway, as well as convenient access to Jewel Changi Airport Shopping Complex. I’ll tell you more about it in my next video! Thank you so much for watching! If you found this video interesting, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more flight and train reviews. See you again soon!

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Jakarta! Today I’m going to travel on the Argo Bromo Anggrek, Indonesia’s most prestigious rail service to Surabaya. Introduced in 2018, the Exectuive Luxury Class on this train only has 18 lavishly designed lie-flat seats in each carriage. I’m excited to find out what this 8hr journey will look like! Let’s go! Jakarta is the capital city of Indonesia, situated on the northwest coast of the island of Java. The Greater Jakarta region has a population of over 33 million, making it one of the most densely populated metropolitan areas in the world. The city is investing heavily in public transport infrastructures to reduce road congestion. There are several rail terminuses in the city. Jakarta Kota is the historic terminus, the current building was constructed in 1929. It handled most of the intercity trains to and from the capital until 2014. At the moment, it is used mainly by commuter trains and two long-distance trains. Most executive and business class trains currently commence their journeys from Gambir station, and economy class trains use the Pesar Senen station. Expected to be fully operational in October this year, Halim station will be the terminal for Southeast Asia’s first high-speed rail line, linking Jakarta to Bandung. Trains on this line can reach speeds of up to 350 km/h. All these stations are easily accessible by commuter trains, except for Gambir Station. It’s on the Bogor line. However, due to limited platform space, the Bogor trains do not stop here. Therefore, passengers needing to catch a train at Gambir must find their own way to the station. I used the ride-sharing app Grab to get here. The Argo Bromo Anggrek is long regarded as Indonesia’s most prestigious train. The name “Argo Bromo” was derived from the famous Bromo volcano in East Java. "Anggrek" means orchid. There are four train services operating under this name, travelling between Jakarta and Surabaya each day: one daytime service and one overnight service, departing from both cities. Gambir Station has three floors, the rail tracks are located on the top floor. Mornings are the busiest period. There is hardly any seating space on the ground level. So, unless you’re here to film a review, it’s best not to arrive too early.  There are a few options to purchase a train ticket: go to the station, visit certain convenience stores, or buy online through the official Indonesian railways website. However, the website only accepts Indonesian bank cards. As such, I purchased mine through a third party, ticket.com. Currently, bookings open 45 days before departure. The website charges a small commission, around AU$2.5. I was able to select a seat, and the whole process was straightforward. After making the payment, they will send you a barcode. They have a mobile app where you can check your bookings. On the day of travel, you must head to one of these kiosks and scan the barcode to print out the ticket. To access the platforms, you can either present the staff with the ticket and a photo ID, or you can enter by scanning your face. The new technology doesn’t seem to be widely embraced by locals yet. Once you’re inside, you’ll find toilets and prayer rooms. And on the second floor, there are more convenience stores. The station has four platforms, and my train will depart from platform two this morning. Based on my observation, it appears that most long-distance trains departing from Gambir are hauled by this type of locomotive: The GE CM20EMP is a double-cabin, diesel-electric locomotive introduced in 2013. The engines and bodies are manufactured by General Electric in the United States, while the bogies were built locally in Indonesia. They are now the workhorses of the Indonesian Railways. Here comes the 8:20 am Argo Bromo Anggrek! It arrived just 15 minutes before departure. As expected, the locomotive is the GE CM20EMP, followed by a power van, a single executive luxury sleeper carriage and nine executive class carriages with a dining car in the middle. Notably, this stands as the most opulent non-tourist train in Indonesia, there’s no business or economy class onboard. The executive carriage looks like this. There are two toilets at the rear, one for males and one for females. The seats are arranged in a 2-2 configuration and are rotatable, allowing them to face the direction of travel. Under the windows, there are European-type power plugs, and the seats can recline by about 30 degrees. The legroom is quite generous. Welcome to the executive luxury class. There’s a dedicated train attendant who warmly greets everyone on board. The seats are in a 1-1 configuration, with nine on each side. They resemble the reverse herringbone business class seats found on planes. Since the seats are not rotatable, half of them do not face the direction of travel. I chose seat 4A, which does indeed face forward. While Indonesia used to have trains with proper sleepers, they were all retired in 1995. Therefore, this is the finest bed you can find on an Indonesian train today. No matter which class you travel in, the luggage allowance is strictly 20kg per person, and there’s a good reason for it. The carriage lacks luggage storage space, you can only place large bags either behind the last row of seats or on the overhead luggage racks. We departed Gambir Station right on the dot. The Argo Bromo Anggrek is the fastest train between Jakarta and Surabaya. It only makes four stops in between, covering a distance of 725 km in 8 hours and 5 minutes. Other trains typically take up to 10-15 hours for the same route. Our next stop is over 2 hours away. The dedicated executive luxury class attendant just served everyone a glass of apple juice. This is Manggarai Station. It currently serves as an interchange station between Jakarta’s two commuter lines and the Soekarno-Hatta Airport Rail Link. As you can see, part of the station is still under construction. Once completed in 2025, the fully expanded multi-level Manggarai Station will become Indonesia’s largest station, replacing Gambir as the terminus for long-distance trains. Around 35 minutes after our departure, we arrived at Cikarang, located on the outskirts of Greater Jakarta. It’s the terminus of the Cikarang Loop Line commuter trains and is the end of the electrified rail line. From this point onward, I will be able to enjoy the lush greenery of the Javanese countryside. Introduced in 2018, the Executive luxury class is a relatively new experience in Indonesia. Let’s take a closer look at the seat’s features. At the front, there’s a small Android-based entertainment screen. Beneath the foot nook, there’s a blanket. This space is large enough to store a small bag. Within easy reach, there’s a small rubbish bin. The left armrest is equipped with a built-in cup holder, and there’s an additional storage area that’s perfect for a laptop or magazines. The seat is upholstered in leather, and a movable headrest adds to the comfort. Adjacent to my seat, there’s a lockable small compartment featuring a mirror and a USB port inside. It’s designed for storing valuable personal items, unfortunately, keys were not provided to lock it. There’s another power plug and USB port below this compartment. Noise-cancelling headphones are supplied for use with the entertainment screen, and an eye-mask is available for those who wish to nap. A built-in control panel is situated on the right armrest, featuring buttons for adjusting the seat, a remote control for the TV screen, a crew call button, and a switch for the reading light. A tray table is stored inside the armrest. This video was filmed on 31 May 2023, when masks were still mandatory on all public transport across Indonesia. Thankfully the government has now relaxed the mask rules. Although there isn’t a blackout curtain to completely block out daylight, there’s a semi-transparent blind to help filter out the sun. The Wi-Fi sticker on the window frame is hard to miss. For the review, I decided to give the Wi-Fi a try. However, it didn’t work on my first attempt. The entertainment screen is also Wi-Fi enabled. But that didn’t work either. The screen is a touch screen and provides several language options. Let’s take a look at the movie collection. Surprisingly, there’s quite a diverse selection of movies available, far more than I expected. Aside from movies, there are games, music, live TV and radio. The map icon displays the train’s current location, but the screen seems to struggle to load it. The map likely requires an internet connection to load. Lastly, I came across a food menu. Given that the train has a dining car, I assume this menu displays what’s available for purchase on board. The tenderloin steak looks particularly delicious! About an hour after departing Gambir, a complimentary breakfast was served,  accompanied by a choice of tea or coffee. The meal was presented in a paper box and included bread, a bottle of water, a mango pudding, a pack prawn crackers, some fried rice, a piece of chicken, and a fried egg. The portion size was notably generous. Fried rice is called “Nasi Goreng” in Indonesia. The rice is flavoured with sweet soy sauce and mixed with sambal, giving it a spicy taste. I enjoyed it. The cutlery pack only contains a spoon and a fork, making cutting through the chicken with them impossible. Although the meat was cold and dry, it had been marinated with a blend of aromatic spices and seasonings, it tasted really good. Overall I enjoyed my breakfast. If it had been plated on fine bone china and provided with metal cutlery, I would say it is of the same quality as an airline business class meal. I decided to give the Wi-Fi another try. This time, the login page appeared, and after providing my email and signing in, I finally managed to connect to the internet. The Wi-Fi speed was pretty fast. My Facebook feed refreshed instantly, and I could watch YouTube videos without interruptions. Dear passengers, in a moment, we will arrive at Cirebon Station. For those of you who will end their trip at Cirebon Station, Please prepare yourself, check you luggage and belongings, make sure that nothing is left behind. For your safety, it is forbidden to open the train door, before the train completely stops. Thank you for choosing train services from Indonesian Railway Company. See you on your next trip! We have arrived at our first stop, Cirebon. The train only stops here briefly. Therefore there’s no time to get out and stretch your legs. Cirebon is the sole coastal city in West Java, situated just 40 kilometres from the provincial border with Central Java. As a result, the city’s history has been shaped by the influences of both Javanese and Sundanese cultures, resulting in a diverse and vibrant cultural landscape. Let’s take a look at the toilet in the executive luxury class. Due to the fewer number of passengers, there’s only one unisex toilet in this carriage. It’s very spacious and remarkably clean. It’s fully equipped with essentials, including toilet paper, hand wash, and paper towels. I like the water plant decoration. Behind the mirrors, there’s a window that keeps the area ventilated. With not much else to do, I decided to lie down for a while. After playing around with the control buttons, I finally managed to adjust the seat to a 170-degree position, which is nearly fully flat. Even though Indonesia is located right on the equator and doesn’t experience winter, the provided blanket is a welcome addition as the air conditioning can get a bit chilly. Being 6’1” or 186 cm tall, the bed is just long enough for me to stretch out fully. While it would be even better if they provided a pillow, the bed is comfortable enough for an 8-hour journey, whether it’s during the daytime or nighttime. Dear passengers, in a moment, we will arrive at Pekalongan Station. For those of you who will end their trip at Pekalongan Station, please prepare yourself... The train maintains a speed between 90 - 120 km/h for most of the journey, swiftly passing through numerous small towns. Around halfway through the trip, near Plabuan Station, the train briefly runs right next to the coastline, providing a stunning view of the ocean. Semarang, the largest city in Central Java, has an estimated population of over 1.6 million. It is an important regional centre, acting as the primary hub between Jakarta and Surabaya. Opened in 1868, Semarang Tawang Station is the oldest major railway station in Indonesia still in operation. Nearly all trains that go through the North Java line stop at this station. During our 5-minute stop, you can see workers using this valuable time to perform some work on my carriage’s roof. Since I received a delicious breakfast in the morning, I assumed that lunch would be included in my ticket as well. However, it’s now 1:40 pm, and I just saw the train staff coming through the aisles selling snacks and drinks. I guess I’ll have to arrange my own lunch then. Let’s visit the lounge car and see if I can get the steak. After walking through several executive class carriages, I reached the dining car located in the middle of the train. The kitchen takes up half of the space in this carriage, and the other half is a dining area with face-to-face seats. There are power plugs under the tables. Alright, the menu is different from what I saw, there’s no steak available. Instead, they offer a variety of hot Indonesian dishes. The pictures of the dishes look quite appetising. In addition to the meals, there are many snacks and drinks. Indonesia is largely a Muslim country. Alcohol is not served on board. I expected the hot meal to be of the same quality as my breakfast. I ordered a Nasi Rendang Padang for 40,000 Indonesian rupiahs and coconut water for 15,000 rupiahs. The prices are very affordable. Here it comes! The packaging isn’t the same as breakfast, but the picture on the lid still looks quite appealing. After opening it up, it turns out the meal is not freshly cooked. The meal weighs 346 grams, the rice is wrapped in paper, and all the other ingredients are prepackaged. There are spicy potatoes, a piece of beef, some chilli paste, and green vegetables. “Nasi” means rice in Indonesian, and “Rendang Padang” is an authentic style of slow-cooked beef stew that originates from the Padang region. The chilli paste is a nice addition to mix with the rice. Once again, cutting through the beef with just a spoon was quite challenging. Personally, I think this is a disgrace to Padang: the beef tastes like a piece of jerky, it’s really dry and hard to chew. Unfortunately, the dehydrated green vegetables are tasteless and inedible. Overall, I came to the dining car with high expectations but left feeling greatly disappointed. Dear passengers, in a moment, we will arrive at Bojonegoro Station. For those of you who will end their trip at Bojonegoro Station, please prepare yourself... So that was the last stop we made before reaching Surabaya. Here are my thoughts about this trip. First, let’s talk about the things I liked: the train was punctual, it departed Jakarta on time and arrived in Surabaya a few minutes early. The seat is comfortable, and is equipped with all the amenities I needed. Furthermore, I was never tired of the scenery, no matter when I looked outside, it was always beautiful. Before arriving in Surabaya, the carriage attendant handed me a hot towel to freshen up. And the things I don’t like: the staff served an excellent breakfast in the first hour of the journey, but then there’s nothing else for the remaining 7 hours—no food, no snacks, and not even a drink. I paid 1,145,000 Indonesian rupiahs for this trip, that is almost 50% more than the price of a 90-minute economy-class flight between Jakarta and Surabaya. I wish they could offer a proper lunch meal to the luxury sleeper passengers. The tracks on this line are narrow gauge and old, making the ride very bumpy. Additionally, on the journey from Jakarta to Surabaya, the sleeper carriage is at the front, and the train driver frequently honks the horn. Overall, I would rate this trip 7/10. Surabaya is the capital of East Java and the second-largest city in Indonesia. While this city might not be widely recognised by international tourists, it holds a significant place in the hearts of Indonesians as the “City of Heroes.” The Heroes Monument in the city centre stands as a prominent landmark, commemorating the Battle of Surabaya and honouring the bravery, resilience, and sacrifice of the city’s inhabitants during Indonesia’s struggle for independence in the late 1940s. Surabaya has two major railway stations, both situated in the heart of the city. The Argo Bromo Anggrek terminates at Surabaya Pasarturi Station, which serves as the final stop for all trains arriving from the northern and western parts of Java. Thank you so much for watching! If you found this video interesting, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more train and flight reviews. See you all in my next video!

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Kuala Lumpur international airport. I've been to Malaysia quite a few times in the past, but I never get to fly with Malaysia Airlines. This morning, thanks to Oman Air, I'm finally going to fly with them to Bali Denpasar on an A330 aircraft. Hopefully, it'll be a great experience. Let's go! Welcome to Malaysia! I arrived here 12 hours ago after flying with Oman Air. As I booked both the Oman Air and the Malaysia Airlines flight under the same PNR, my bag was through-checked from Muscat to Bali. This allowed me to stay within the transit area and skip the immigration. Kuala Lumpur International Airport is Malaysia's main international airport, situated roughly 45 kilometres south of the city. It served more than 62 million passengers in 2019, making it the 21st busiest airport globally. The airport has two terminals, terminal 2, also known as KLIA 2 is a purpose-built terminal for budget airlines. It's the hub for Air Asia and Air Asia X. The main terminal building, also known as KLIA main or KLIA 1, along with a satellite terminal, handles most of the airport's domestic and international flights. It's the primary hub for Malaysia Airlines. As you can see, the satellite building offers a variety of amenities, including restaurants, cafes, duty-free shops, lounges, and prayer rooms. To move between the main terminal and the satellite building, passengers can ride the aero train. The satellite building also houses a transit hotel named Sama Sama Express KLIA. Due to the confusing signage, it took me a bit of time to find it. It's actually situated just before Gate C5. The hotel has 80 rooms, each with a private bathroom and a king-sized bed. My room was impeccably clean, and most importantly, it boasted a fantastic view of the apron. You can book the room for 6, 9 or 12 hours. My 12-hour stay cost me 386 Malaysian ringgit. The price is reasonable. Malaysia Airlines is a member of the Oneworld Alliance, its international flagship lounge is called the Golden Lounge Satellite, located above the aero train platforms. This lounge complex is shared between first-class and business-class passengers, with the entry to the first-class lounge on the right and the business-class lounge on the left. Flying in business class tomorrow gives me access to the business lounge. Being a Qantas Platinum Frequent Flyer with Oneworld Emerald status, I have access to the first-class lounge as well. Although not overly spacious, the lounge features plenty of comfortable seating and stunning apron views during the day. The self-serve counter provides alcoholic beverages, soft drinks, water, coffee, and tea.  Other amenities include toilets, prayer rooms, a napping area, and individual shower suites. There's no food available in the main seating area, instead, there's a small restaurant offering a la carte dining. Featuring only 13 tables in this room, the space fills up quickly. During my visit, I had to wait for half an hour before finally securing a table. While the menu is not the most extensive, it stills offer several options for each course. To start, I opted for their signature OX Tail soup, and I must say, it was worth my half-hour wait to get in here. The broth was rich and flavourful, and the meat on the ox tail was tender. Malaysians are known for their skill in cooking chicken, it is a staple protein in Malaysian cuisine. For my main course I chose the boneless roasted chicken, which had crispy skin and moist meat. Both the chicken and the noodles below were complemented by the tangy and slightly spicy mustard sauce,  this is another flavourful dish. The chicken alone was already very filling, so I decided to skip the dessert. In general, what I appreciate about the first-class lounge is its peaceful atmosphere and the a la carte menu that showcases local Malaysian cuisine. Now, let's take a look at the business class lounge. Passengers with a business class ticket from any Oneworld airline and Oneworld Sapphire tiered frequent flyers flying in Economy can enter this lounge free of charge. This place is much larger than the first-class lounge. I was particularly impressed by the food selections here. While it may not offer the fine-dining experience of the first-class lounge next door, the buffet is expansive and varied. The menu changes seasonally. It typically features local Malaysian dishes such as Nasi Lemak, Chicken Satay, Curry Laksa, and Beef Rendang, and international options like salads, sandwiches, soups and pasta dishes. In addition, there's an assortment of cakes, pastries, and fresh fruit. After a few hours of decent sleep, I checked out of my hotel room and returned to the Golden Lounge for a quick breakfast before my flight. I went directly to the business lounge this time, as it had a more comprehensive food selection. Although it was busier than the previous night, I was still able to find an empty table. By the way, the business lounge also has napping rooms, prayer rooms, and showers. As of November 2022, Malaysia Airlines has a fleet of 69 aircraft comprising of 42 Boeing 737-800, 6 A350-900, 15 A330-300, and 6 A330-200. At the time of filming, the airline operates three daily flights between Kuala Lumpur and Denpasar, utilising a combination of Boeing 737 and A330 aircraft. Similar to Singapore Changi Airport, security screening is carried out at the boarding gate, so please make sure you allocate sufficient time for boarding. My flight this morning is operated by an Airbus A330-300, which features 27 business class and 263 economy class seats. Malaysia Airlines uses Thompson Aero's Vantage model business seats on their a330 and a350s. They are arranged in a combination of 1-2-2 and 1-2-1 configurations. The seats on the right-hand side of the cabin are all single, those in the middle are double, and those on the left are a mix of single and double seats. Additionally, there are two rows of 2-4-2 configured extra-legroom economy class seats behind the business cabin before door 2. I particularly like this seat design as it caters to both solo travellers and couples. For this flight, I selected seat 6K, which is a throne seat. There is a lot more surface space around my seat compared to the double seats behind. Once I had taken my seat, the cabin crew offered me a glass of juice and a cold towel. Moments later, the cabin manager walked to every seat and greeted everyone by their last names. There are two lavatories assigned for the 27 business passengers. Despite the short flight, each lavatory is stocked with body and hand lotion, eau de toilette and toothpicks. Kuala Lumpur International Airport has 3 runways, and today we'll be using the east runway. Now let's take a closer look at my seat. I noticed a coat hook situated beside the entertainment screen. There are several storage places surrounding the seat, including a spacious area under the window enough to fit my camera bag and the provided blanket. On the opposite side of my seat, there's a hidden compartment with a vanity mirror. There are two control panels for adjusting the seat's position, activating the massage function and turning on the overhead reading light. Adjacent to the armrest, there's a USB-port, a headphone jack, a remote for the entertainment screen, and an adjustable reading light. A universal power socket and the safety card holder are positioned near my leg. The seat has a width of 20 inches, which is on the narrower side, and the pitch is 43 inches. Overall, while Malaysia Airlines' Vantage-based seats are not the most luxurious option on the market, they do offer all the features that a business traveller would anticipate. The product ticked all my boxes. Shortly after takeoff, the crew commenced lunch service. A menu was handed to me when the plane was on the ground. There are three choices for the main course, and I opted for the Nasi Lemak. As of 2020, the estimated Muslim population in Malaysia is 63.5%. Although there aren't any alcoholic beverages listed on the menu, a bottle of red, white and champagne were displayed on the drink trolley. Accompanying the main course were a selection of pastries, including crustless white toast, croissant, and banana cake. The champagne served onboard was produced by Philipponnat, it has a retail price of $82 per bottle in Australia. Nasi Lemak is often considered the national dish of Malaysia, it is a popular meal enjoyed at any time of the day. The dish typically comes with cucumber slices, a hard-boiled egg, fried anchovies, and roasted peanuts. The proteins in this dish can be varied, but chicken, beef, and prawns are typically the most common options. A spicy chilli paste known as sambal is added to enhance the dish's flavour. The prawns are big and tasted fresh and succulent. However, the highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the sambal, which boasted a perfect blend of spicy, sweet, and savoury flavours. Pairing the rice with this sauce was simply delectable. Instead of using the boiled egg, Malaysia Airlines used the omelette, which was nothing special. In general I was absolutely delighted with this dish, I have no doubt that this is the most delicious Nasi Lemak one could have in the air! Let's have a look at the inflight entertainment system. In the pocket below, there is a very basic noise-cancelling headphone. The 16" HD screen is a touchscreen, and you can also control it with the remote. The system is available in both English and Malay and offers a decent selection of movies, including recent releases, and TV shows. And of course, you can check out the flight path as well. We are currently just 57 minutes from Denpasar, and the plane will begin its descent in less than 20 minutes. As expected, each seat can be converted into a fully-flat bed. The bed length is 76 inches, which should be long enough for most people. The biggest drawback of my "throne" seat is its narrow foot nook compared to other business class seats, resulting in limited space for foot movement while lying down. Despite this, this bed is still relatively comfortable for those flying long-haul. In summary, this flight was fantastic. While their business class seats may not be the latest and the greatest, from ample storage space and power outlets to a comfortable lie-flat bed and direct aisle access, the seat still has everything I needed. What impressed me the most, however, was Malaysia Airlines' exceptional soft product. The crew members were all friendly, professional, and energetic, with smiles on their faces throughout the flight. And let's not forget about the Golden Lounge in Kuala Lumpur, which is undoubtedly one of the best airport lounges in Southeast Asia. Thank you for joining me on this flight to Denpasar, Indonesia. I hope you found this review informative and enjoyable. If you did, please give this video a thumbs up and subscribe to my channel for more flight and train reviews. In my next video, I'll be in Yerevan, Armenia, taking a journey on a state-of-the-art Russian-built night train from Armenia across to Georgia. Stay tuned and see you then!

reviews.transcript_full: Hello and welcome to Muscat, the capital of Oman. Today I’m going to fly with Oman Air to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. This airline is expected to officially join the oneworld alliance in 2024 and I’ve read good things about them on the internet. But what are they really like? Let’s go and find out together! Oman is a middle-eastern country located in the southeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula. It’s known for its diverse landscapes, including stunning coastlines, rugged mountains, and vast deserts. The capital city Muscat is renowned for its historic landmarks, vibrant markets, and beautiful architecture. The Omani people are also known to be one of the most welcoming people in the world. Muscat International Airport is the main airport serving Muscat. It’s the hub of the nation’s flag carrier Oman Air, which offers flights to destinations throughout the Middle East, Asia, Europe, and Africa. The airport has undergone several expansions and renovations since its establishment in 1973. In 2018, a new state-of-the-art passenger terminal was opened to increase the airport’s capacity and enhance the passenger experience. It covers a space of 580,000 sqm and features 45 boarding gates. The luxurious experience of flying in Oman Air’s business or first class commences as soon as you step foot in the airport. Located on the departures level, there is a specialised entry for business and first class passengers, which leads to Oman Air’s dedicated check-in area. Upon entering, a porter immediately offered to take care of my suitcase, and I was directed to one of the empty check-in counters. The process was fast, smooth, and straightforward. Today, I am flying with Oman Air to Kuala Lumpur and then continuing on to Denpasar with Malaysia Airlines. I received my boarding pass for both flights, and my bag was also through-checked. After obtaining my boarding pass, I proceeded through the private immigration and security line, where the wait was minimal. Once airside, the terminal is divided into three concourses: A, B, and C, with a large central section for duty-free shops and restaurants. The airport’s layout is similar to Hamad International Airport in Doha, Qatar, but on a smaller scale. There are ample signs throughout the terminal to assist travellers in finding their gates. Above the main departure level, you can find a transit hotel and several lounges. Among them is Oman Air’s flagship first and business class lounge. Beyond the impressive golden metal doors lies the joint lounge complex, with the entrance to the business class lounge on the left and the first class lounge on the right. Adjacent to the reception desk, you’ll find a model of Oman Air’s latest addition to its fleet, the Boeing 787-9. Additionally, there is a sign that lists all of the features at this lounge. This place is massive, it has the capacity to accommodate 500 people across the span of two levels. Starting in 2024, I believe OneWorld Emerald and Sapphire tiered frequent flyers flying in Economy should be at least eligible to use the business class lounge. Oman Air is among the few Middle Eastern airlines that serve alcohol on board, and their lounge is no exception.  The bar offers an extensive selection of wines and spirits to cater to passengers’ preferences. The lounge also features a terrace that extends beyond the floor-to-ceiling windows, providing a stunning view of the airfield. However, the outdoor area is not accessible to passengers. There are two main dining areas with mirrored layouts. While heading towards the bar, I caught a glimpse of the first dining area, and here’s the second one. It is currently closed as it only opens when the first dining area is filled to capacity. Deeper into the lounge, you will find toilets, shower facilities, and a prayer room. Additionally, there is a sleeping room that features several day beds separated by curtains, allowing travellers to catch a quick nap. I particularly admire this feature, and I hope that Qantas will consider incorporating it into its international lounges in the future. The upper level of the lounge features a spa section. In terms of the facilities, this is definitely one of the best lounges I’ve ever visited. It’s spacious, modern, clean, relaxing and well-equipped with everything I need. With my quick tour complete, I’m excited to head to the main dining area for a quick breakfast before boarding! The food and beverage selection was nothing short of remarkable. Let’s start with the drinks section, the semi-circular buffet features self-service coffee machines, various teas, authentic Omani coffee, soft drinks and water. On the opposite end of the buffet, there’s an array of refreshing juices. When it comes to food, the options are abundant, ranging from fruits, cheeses, cold cuts, cakes, cereals, and bread. There are several hot dishes as well, including the omelette, fried noodles, and meat. Overall I was truly impressed with the variety and quality of the food here. As of February 2023, Oman Air operates a fleet of 50 aircraft, ranging from Boeing 737-800, -900ER, and Max 8 to Boeing 787-8,-9 and Airbus A330-300 and -200. All aircraft feature business and Economy, with first class service being only available on selected A330-300 and Boeing 787-9, and Oman Air is planning to gradually phase out first class entirely. Boarding for my flight to Kuala Lumpur commenced an hour before departure, the aircraft operating this flight is an Airbus A330-200. There are 4 of them in the fleet. Each is equipped with 30 Collins Aerospace Apex business suites and 196 economy-class seats. The seats in business are in a 2-2-2 configuration, they’re Oman Air’s newest product. There are 5 rows in total, the forward cabin has three rows, and there are another 2 rows behind door 2. I picked seat 12K, which is in the last row in the forward cabin. I’m usually not a fan of the 2-2-2 configured business class due to the lack of privacy and the lack of direct aisle access for window seats. However, on this aircraft, each window seat is installed slightly ahead of the aisle seat, allowing for a direct path to the aisle. Additionally, there’s a partition that goes up between the two seats, creating a mini-suite for the window seat. Within a few moments of taking my seat, the cabin crew presented me with a choice of cold or hot towel followed by a choice of lemon mint or orange juice. After just five minutes, they returned with some dates and Omani coffee. With such excellent service, I knew it was going to be a wonderful flight! Muscat Airport has two runways, but only one of them is currently operational. Today, we will be taking off from the new runway, then make a U-turn and head east towards Kuala Lumpur. Sitting on the right-hand side of the plane will give me a bird’s eye view of the airport and Muscat City. Let’s take a closer look at the features of the business class seat. There are no overhead storage bins in the middle of the cabin, creating a more spacious feeling. There is ample space under the ottoman to store a backpack. The seat has a pitch of 82 inches and a width of 22 inches, providing plenty of legroom. There are two additional exposed storage areas for personal belongings, as well as a magazine holder with a wine list, a remote for the entertainment screen,  two USB ports, one headphone jack, and a universal power plug under the central armrest. The tray-table is hidden inside the armrest. And the other armrest has buttons to control the seat’s recline, leg rest position, and massage function. As anticipated, the seat can be transformed into a fully-flat bed that spans 77.5 inches in length. On the ottoman, the crew has placed a seat cover, a blanket and a pair of noise-cancelling headphones. The headphones work fine, but nothing special. Oman Air is not a dry airline, from the wine list, you can see it offers champagne, red and white wines, dessert wine and other alcoholic beverages. It’s nice to see that a South Australian wine has made to the list. Not long after the seat-belt sign was turned off, the crew served me some mixed cold nuts. I requested a glass of coke, and the crew also suggested a glass of the Champagne Lallier Blanc de Blancs, which retails for $75 a bottle in Australia. The 17-inch entertainment screen is controlled solely by this touch-sensitive remote. The screen is clear and well-positioned. The system comes in both Arabic and English. You can check out the forward and downward view of the aircraft fed live by the two exterior cameras, look at the flight path powered by GeoFusion, play games, purchase duty-free items and choose from a wide selection of movies and TV shows. With so many options, I have plenty to keep me entertained throughout the flight. There are three lavatories exclusively for the 30 business class passengers. The amenities include a hand cream, perfume, cologne and dental kits. What I like the most though, is that there’s a window here! This truly makes it a “loo with a view” and I love it! About 90 minutes after take off at 10:40 Oman time, the crew started serving lunch. Theoretically, I should be able to check out the menu from the entertainment screen, but it didn’t work on my flight. I was informed by the crew that there are four choices for the appetiser and three for the main course. I really like the thoughtful design of the plate and the shape of the salt and pepper shakers, which reflect Oman’s mountainous and rugged terrain. From my memory, the appetiser menu included four options: fruit, yogurt, scallops, and Arabic mezze. I was disappointed to discover that the scallop dish only had a single seared scallop along with some tender fish chunks. Nevertheless, the flavours of the seafood were delicately enhanced by a blend of herbs and spices, and I still found the dish satisfying. For the main course, passengers can choose from chicken kofta, fish with yellow rice and vegetarian. The fish dish appears to be a traditional Omani dish, and although the crew was unsure of the specific type of fish, they believe it may be emperor fish. The portion size was quite generous, the fish was fresh, and the rice had absorbed the flavourful sauce from the fish above. Overall the whole main course was healthy, colourful and tasty. The lunch is just two course, dessert was not offered, I didn’t mind it as the filling main course left me little room for anything else. We are now just 4 hours from Kuala Lumpur. While individual amenity kit was not offered,  I was pleased that the bedding was still provided on this day flight, so I could take a conformable nap. I’m sure the crew would be more than happy to set up the bed for me, I noticed that other passengers were doing it themselves so I did the same. Being situated away from the aisle, the window seat provides a heightened sense of privacy. Once the seat is fully reclined, you have the option to either sit up to watch a movie or lie down for a nap. I found both positions to be comfortable. Additionally, there is a reading light located above the headphone hook for those who prefer to do some light reading. The entertainment screen, remote screen, and the light above the ottoman can all be turned off for a more restful sleep. Approximately 90 minutes before landing, there was a small snack service. It includes some freshly cut fruits with cookies and a cup of tea. The idea of serving fruit is perfect, they’re not greasy, not too filling but refreshing. There’s a 4h time difference between Muscat and Kuala Lumpur, it’s already 8pm in Malaysia. Oman Air’s hard product, from dedicated check-in and massive lounge to modern business suites and comfortable beds, is on par with other major Gulf and Asian carriers. The cabin crew are some of the best I’ve ever encountered. They’re friendly, professional, and accommodating. With Oman Air joining the OneWorld alliance in 2024, I would definitely fly with them again in the future. I actually flew on their B737-800 from Cairo to Muscat yesterday and I will be flying on Malaysia Airline’s A330-300 to Bali tomorrow. I booked all three flights on Oman Air’s official website, and these business-class flights cost me just $1300.  Welcome to Kuala Lumpur International Airport! The hub of Malaysia Airlines, a member of the OneWorld Alliance. Thank you so much for watching, if you found this video interesting, please hit the like button and subscribe to my channel for more flight and train reviews. My flight to Bali is leaving in 13 hours, I decided not to go through immigration, instead, I booked a room at the transit hotel, and as a Qantas platinum frequent flyer, I spent a few hours at Malaysia Airline’s flagship Golden Lounge. Please stay tuned for my next video, where I'll show you more about these experiences. See you there!
