reviews.transcript_full:
Welcome on this Air France Business Class
flight in an Airbus A330 from Paris to St Martin (Caribbean) The video features the full Air France Business Class
experience, from seating & meals to amenities & bedding This Air France Business Class video also includes
the A330’s landing at St Martin’s iconic Princess Juliana Airport Our journey starts at Charles de Gaulle Airport in Paris,
Europe's third busiest airport (after Istanbul and Heathrow)  Unfortunately, my Air France Business Class 'light' ticket does
not include access to the lounge for some pre-flight relaxation We’re taken by bus to the remote aircraft stand This is the Air France Airbus A330-200 that will
fly us to St Martin (aircraft registration number F-GZCN) Air France has 11 Airbus A330s in its
long-haul fleet with an average age of 22 years The Air France Business Class on the Airbus A330
features 36 seats spread over six rows in a 2-2-2 layout There are two Business Class cabins: a front cabin
with 24 seats (4 rows) and a rear cabin with 12 seats (2 rows) The Air France A330 Business Class cabin has a sleek look 4A is my seat for the 9 hour flight to St Martin Air France installed Equinox 2D Business Class
seats by Stelia Aerospace on its Airbus A330 fleet The Air France Business Class seat on the A330
has a pitch of 78 inch (198 cm) and a width of 22 inch (56 cm) A retractable screen provides privacy between seats I’ll take a detailed tour of the 
Air France Business Class seat after takeoff A hot towel is provided to refresh a little Air France’s safety video is an elegant and stylish movie We’re leaving the aircraft stand at 10 am (on-time departure) Air France’s A330s are powered by General Electric engines  Air France’s A330-200s are being replaced
by the next-generation and larger Airbus A350-900s Let’s have a look at the Air France A330 Business Class seat Each Business Class seat features a large TV screen,
with a storage cabinet and footrest underneath  Directly next to to the seat’s head rest is a small
cubby for storing headphones, water and small items The power plug and passenger service unit
(remote control for IFE) are within easy reach The arm rest houses a large tray table Let's have a look at the Air France Business Class amenities The Air France Business Class kit contains the following items:
a dental kit, earplugs, eye mask, socks, and Clarins cosmetics A soft microfiber pillow and a warm blanket
are offered to all Business Class passengers All Air France's Business Class passengers get slippers Air France branded noise-cancelling headphones are provided  One hour into the flight, we're leaving Europe behind us
and will now fly over the Atlantic Ocean for the next 8 hours  I am a very nervous flyer, especially over the ocean Are you also scared of flying over the ocean? Leave a comment As we start the Atlantic crossing, the Air France crew
hands out the Business Class menus for the inflight meals Appetizer: cream of smoked sweetcorn soup,
girolle mushrooms and toasted buckwheat Air France also serves its Business Class passengers
crepes fourrées (stuffed pancakes) during the aperitif Starter: Camargue red rice, sweet potato,
and rainbow trout salad with raspberry vinaigrette Main course: beef chuck, peanut sauce, celery, Taggiasca olives Mustard in grains from the prestigious moutardier 
Edmond Fallot in Dijon is served with the beef  Cantal, Fourme d’Ambert, & Chabichou du Poitou cheeses Dessert: crispy hazelnut and caramel cake Air France's Airbus A330 is equipped with
two lavatories for the 36 Business Class passengers The Air France Business Class seat on the A330 can be
reclined into a fully flat bed with a lenght of 197 cm (77 inches)   Have you ever flown in Air France Business Class?
If so, what was your experience? Leave a comment Air France’s inflight entertainment system
offers a wide variety of movies, shows, music and games Snacks & drinks are available in the galley during the flight A light meal is served 90 minutes prior to landing Smoked salmon, tangy creamy sauce, 
pearl pasta with vegetables, and orange & pink grapefruit The Air France A330 pilot addresses
the passengers as we are approaching St Martin’s airspace There's a lot of traffic at St Martin airport, and we
have to circle for 30 minutes before starting our descend  We get some great views of the Caribbean during the descent St Martin has one of the world’s most scenic airport landings Maho Beach on St Martin is famous for being
next to the international airport, right at the end of the runway Thanks for flying with me in Air France Business Class Don't forget to like, comment,
and subscribe for more flight reviews!

article_quotes.text: Airlines Soar with Embedded IFE: The Key to Profit and Passenger Satisfaction - APEX > News > Thought Leadership & Brand Pictured: United Airlines’ Economy Plus seating, featuring embedded in-flight entertainment.

Photo via United Airlines In a fiercely competitive industry, airlines investing in embedded in-flight entertainment (IFE) systems dominate, capturing the lion’s share of profits and achieving top customer satisfaction and Net Promoter Scores.

Airlines like Aeromexico, Air Canada, Delta, Emirates, JetBlue, Qatar, Singapore, United, and many others prioritize passenger experience using advanced IFE systems, leading to increased revenues and customer loyalty.
United Airlines’ shift regarding seatback IFE in the past few years exemplifies this strategy’s effectiveness.
As United CEO Scott Kirby remarked last week , “[In 2016,] I was president of American, and we were putting seatback entertainment systems on every one of our airplanes.

Celebrating over 30 years of IFE leadership, Emirates’ SVP Retail, IFE & Connectivity Patrick Brannelly echoed similar sentiments on the importance of IFE to passenger satisfaction: “When Emirates introduced personal screens on every seatback in 1992, it was considered a massive industry innovation.
By the end of this decade, leading low-cost carriers (LCC) and ultra-low-cost carriers (ULCC) will likely incorporate embedded IFE screens nearly as thin and light as seatback plastic.
A shot of the screen that allows passengers to pair their personal devices with their seatback IFE screen.

The Comoda-Materia Pack seat is equipped with 16-inch Astrova monitors, while Elemento features 13.3-inch Astrova monitor s.
This demonstrates the effective use of lightweight, flexible Astrova OLED screens to improve the passenger experience while meeting challenging design and certification requirements.
The cooperation with Panasonic began in July 2023, and within 12 months, the seats with integrated IFE were successfully certified in a short lead time for both Comoda – Materia Pack and Elemento.
This partnership marks a significant achievement for Geven, showcasing our commitment to innovation and passenger comfort.

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome to Dubai International airport, terminal 3 Today we are going to fly Emirates on its iconic Airbus A380 in economy class to the French Riviera  Dubai airport terminal 3 is Emirates massive hub, it starts to show its age but it's still a great airport In a few years Emirates will leave DXB airport to move to its new hub, Dubai Al Maktoum DWC  The duty free offers a wide range of shopping possibilities from luxury boutiques to cheap souvenirs It even has a wide choice of alcohol Our flight to Nice will depart from gate A5 Passengers are pre boarded to a massive waiting zone located downstairs from where they will board the plane This massive area can accommodate all the passengers of an A380 and allows a smooth boarding process Our todays Airbus A380 is A6-EDO, assembled in Toulouse (France) in 2010 And here we are on board the massive A380 lower deck cabin, equipped with a full economy class layout This is actually an old generation cabin still equipped with older seats and no Premium Economy cabin The desert dunes design is still present with the dunes painted on the walls This is going to be our seat for the next seven hours despite of showing its age the cabin is very comfortable and  feels very spacious   Especially today as the flight will be half empty and no-one will be seated on my row of seat As on all Airbus A380 this old seat is quite wide and with a good legroom this good old IFE screen is of a decent size but has some reflection at daylight Some avgeek goodies are for sale on our seat we get a basic pillow as well as a warm and thick blanket and this pair of rectangular shaped headphones seats are equipped with a  universal PC power outlet as well as a USB charging port and a double audio jack our flight to Nice will take 6 hours and 30 minutes Let's now use our old school remote control to explore our IFE screen as we climb to our cruising altitude the cabin crew offer us our on board menu on this morning flight we will be served a breakfast followed by a lunch and as we fly over Kuwait, the breakfast is served toasted eggs and cheddar in a kind of sandwich Let's now have a tour of our A380, starting from the rear where a massive crew rest takes all the central rows at the very front this is where the new premium economy cabin would be located if this plane was retrofitted To me, nothing can beat this view... notice those water displayers located next to each lavatories, a feature a have only seen on Emirates A380 Basra, Iraq as the flight is almost empty we all get a full row to lay down, it's even better than being upstairs in business strangely as we are still in the middle of our way we are woken up for the lunch service a very generous and well presented tray on which I chose chicken with mashed potatoes as a main dish Antibes old town

yt_comments.author: @Espa889
yt_comments.text: Flew with them recently. The food was amazing. The staff were bitchy as you can expect. I said to one flight attendant "can you please put my bag in the compartment I'm too short". She gave me a look of stone, and rudely shoved it hard into the compartment. Obviously thought "I'm too pretty for this job". There was a nice Australian flight attendant. But this was weird. There were 3 open seats, with 3 more open seats in front of them. Someone called it "reserve seats" whatever that is supposed to mean..this Australian flight attendant, for some weird reason, took a liking to this Indian couple. They asked about the 6 open seats. She told them "yeah you guys can sit there". She was all chatty and smiley with them. The husband then took 3 seats for himself, and the wife took 3 seats in front of him..I just thought the whole thing was really weird. Sorry, but where do you get off just roaming a plane looking for open seats? And the flight attendant just giggles and says "yeah sure guys!" Not fair to other passengers. We don't want to see that kind of favouritism. But the food was really amazing, there was free internet on the first flight ( starlink ) and I could charge my phone on the plane ❤

The bedroom & iconic Four Seasons bed

reviews.transcript_full: This is one of the most affordable luxury hotels we've reviewed so far and it's a Four Seasons no less. But while the price is impressive, does the hotel itself meet the excellence that we associate with the Four Seasons brand? Does a lower price equal lower standards or should the Four Seasons quality be upheld regardless of price and location? Come along for our complete review of the highs and lows of the Four Seasons Singapore and to see if it makes our list [music] of our top 10 favorite hotels worldwide. Welcome. yt_comments.text: I did some research on Emirates registrations and what cabins you can roughly expect for all of them. The # will resemble [insert letter] For the A380s, registrations with “A6-ED#,” you will see the oldest cabins, which come with the most dated cabins and features the oldest and smallest IFE system within the A380s. For A380s registered “A6-EE#,” you will mostly see the cabin that was featured in the flight from Brisbane to Dubai: The “middle class” cabin which comes with the 10” black bezel IFE screen based on the eX3 (or maybe eX1?) platform. But there are a few “A6-EE#” cabins with the very old cabin seen in all “A6-ED#,” like A6-EEA featured in the video. For A380s registered “A6-EO#,” it gets complicated. From what I can tell, most with “A6-EO#” feature the same cabins as most of the “A6-EE#” registration. But there are some “A6-EO#” registrations that offer the newest cabins with the 13.3” IFE screens. A6-EOT is a good example, while A6-EOZ actually has the 2 class cabin, again with the newest 13.3” screens. For A380s registered “A6-EU#,” you will see most, if not all 4 class A380s with this registration have the new cabins with 13.3” IFE screens, but no premium economy class. Again, there are a few “A6-EU#” registrations that are 2 class configured and also have the new cabins. Actually, all 2 class configured A380s have the newest cabin type. Finally, for A380s registered “A6-EV#,” they feature the newest of the new cabins, including offering a premium economy cabin. Those are all the A380s, but I also did research on the 777 cabins! Most 777s registered “A6-EC#” and “A6-EG#” feature the old cabins with the 9” eX2 screens. There are a few that have the 10 inch IFE screens. 777s registered “A6-EB#” feature THE OLDEST cabins, even older than the A380s with “A6-ED#,” “A6-EC#,” and “A6-EG#.” The IFEs are older than the eX2. “A6-EB#” cabins feature the same system you see on Qatar’s A330s. 777s registered “A6-EN#” feature the “middle class” cabins with the 10” IFE screens. 777s registered “A6-EP#” feature the new cabins with 13.3” IFE screens, but not the newest game changer first class. 777s registered “A6-EQ#” are the newest, featuring their newest cabins AND the game changer first class. Some of them also see the new business class as well. Finally, all 777-200LRs which feature “A6-EW#” registrations have the same cabins you saw on the flight to Vienna. Hopefully this breakdown was helpful! This took a while to research 😅

only paid 12,400 mil Plus €65 in taxes and fees which is a bargain that's why I always recommend you sign up for frequent flyer programs even if you don't travel too frequently as sometimes you can earn just enough miles for these discounted trips two more things you can also earn miles on flying blue for example through booking accommodations via booking.com where you get two Flying Blue miles for each Euro spend and what I particularly love about flying blue is that the short hul connections into Amsterdam and Paris for those long haul flights are free so whether I book from Amsterdam to Shanghai or Vienna to Shanghai or from a tiny airport like Gratz the route costs the same amount of Miles anyway for this good of a deal I'm more than willing to suffer through a Transit at shiple airport the key reason why the airport is so bothersome is its layout as all passenger flows converge in this central part of the terminal resulting in some annoyingly crowded sections furthermore walking distances can be quite big today's Transit was 1.2 km and while I don't take an issue in that I know passengers with reduced Mobility are going to have a hard time in Amsterdam but here we are KL 895 indust Shanghai pong did you know all of km's flight numbers to China have the number eight in it Shanghai is 895 Beijing is 897 Taipei is 807 and Hong Kong got the coveted number 888 that's because the number eight is a lucky number in Chinese mythology as its name sounds similar to the word for prosperity and the number 88 slightly resembles the character for double Joy meanwhile the number four is an unlucky number as it sounds like death which is why the number doesn't appear in any of km's flight numbers to China this will be our right to Shanghai today Papa Hotel Bravo Quebec kilo a 2005 build 7200 ours like this one at a neighboring gate is labeled as km Asia so km is the last overseas carrier to still have an Asia division back in the 1990s when China and Taiwan refused to allow airlines flying to one of them to Falls of flight to the other a lot of airlines established second carriers to circumvent these rules there was a Swiss Air Asia an Air France AI a British Asia Airways and so on but with these restrictions lifted a long time ago all Airlines gradually got rid of their Asia divisions with the exception of KM I tried very hard to figure out why they did not just keep it but even still deliberately kept it around when they got a new livery in recent years and while researching I stumbled on a lot of wild theories that don't hold up and plenty of poorly researched block posts that simply contain factual inaccuracies such as this one by simple flying while also not answering the question as to why km Asia is still a thing nowadays they claim that km Asia planes never operate flights into mainland China well um okay let's give them the benefit of of the doubt and assume that changed after they published the article how difficult would it have been for them to fact check this claim well simply go to any plan spotting website put in KLM Asia mainland China and let's pick like the 2000s and voila km Asia planes have been operating to both mainland China and Taiwan for a long time like for decades and that makes it even harder to answer the question as to why it still exists today because it doesn't seem to make a difference so I did the last thing I thought would help me I reached out to km and asked them and I kid you not the Press Department referenced that simple flying article and told me they don't have anything to add to that you know the article that has stuff in it that's just wrong which they likely took from Wikipedia because there It also says that km Asia planes don't fly to Mainland China which is not and has not been true for at least 20 years so while we are unable to get a reliable answer as to why km Asia is still around in 2024 let's focus on what we do know km Asia branded PLS also do not reference the Dutch monarchy the abbreviation KLM stands forat matap which translated basically means Royal Dutch Airlines and that is an officially approved Title by the Dutch royal family with KM Asia having been a different legal entity back in the days they were not able to use the word Royal and also emitted the crown in its logo instead you may find this company name written in traditional Chinese characters I.E in the kind of written Chinese common in Taiwan and Hong Kong that says Netherlands Asia Airways km Asia currently has a fleet of nine Tri 7s 7-20 and 2-300 er however these planes are registered in the Netherlands to the Dutch km holding company only operate with KL flight numbers KLM Crews and operate flights to Taiwan mainland China and elsewhere so they're like any other km plane inside there is absolutely no difference between km Asia airplanes and other km planes and the service is exactly the same as on other km flights and since km also operates their regular non-asia branded planes to Mainland China as well as Taiwan I fail to see any point as to why the brand is still around in the end I thought it might simply be a brand recognition thing in Taiwan but nope klm's Taiwanese website shows the regular logo with a crown and the title Royal Dutch Airlines after at least 6 hours of research for all I can tell km Asia Only still exists as a livery if I'm wrong in that or if you know why they keep this Livery and brand around please let me know in the comments because I'm genuinely curious anyway after this lengthy tangent it's time to board our flight km's Boeing 7200 feature Collins Aerospace Diamond parallel seats up front and business class with economy class having an economy Comfort section up front with better leg room the yt_comments.text: Subang Airport was Kuala Lumpur’s primary airport until KLIA opened, so that’s something. I find Asiana to be one of the better value Asian airlines. I first flew with them last year and they charged half of what Singapore Airlines was charging for Singapore-Seoul flights. I’m flying them again to Tokyo in 2 weeks time, first leg will be in the A350 again, so the upcoming video is really gonna pump me up for the trip. Even more exciting, my onward flight from Incheon to Tokyo will be on the A380! I have a goal of flying as many A380s as I can and this journey will kick start that endeavour. I hope to score a seat on the upper deck at check-in too. You were so lucky to get to fly their 747, I hope to do so before it retires 😊

yt_comments.text: Love the review, great as always! The reason CM does not offer Wifi is because the antenna on the top of the fuselage would create too much drag and can cause fuel problems on long flights like Montevideo or San Francisco. Before the MAX, the -800 sometimes needed to stop for fuel in Cancun or other places to continue the journey to SFO. As for the IFE, I have no idea why they got rid of it, I personally only use it for the map and flight details, but even having it there and not doing anything just makes me feel more comfortable. Saludos desde Panama!

reviews.transcript_full: Welcome aboard ANA's Business Class in the Boeing 787 All Nippon Airways (ANA) is Japan's largest airline The video features the full ANA Business Class flight experience  This includes the amazing Business Class meals The video offers stunning views of Greenland This ANA Boeing 787 flight takes us from Tokyo to Brussels Welcome to Tokyo Narita Airport, Japan’s main international hub  Around 40 million passengers pass through Narita each year Tokyo Narita Airport is known for its efficiency and organization ANA offers dedicated Business check-in at Narita Airport Narita is quiet early in the morning, as flights start around 6 AM All Nippon Airways has several lounges at Tokyo Narita Airport The main ANA lounge is located in Terminal 1 near Gate 52 The lounge is open to Star Alliance Business Class passengers The lounge is split into two sections, connected by a corridor The main section is busiest and features the primary buffet The second section stays quieter until later in the morning The ANA lounge at Narita features a modern, Japanese design Seating options include armchairs, sofas, and bar-style counters  The lounge's second section offers views of the airport's interior  Seating in the main section suits both solo travelers and groups Large windows offer a view of the airport's tarmac and runways The main buffet offers salads, hot dishes, and light snacks Japanese and Western dishes suit every taste The lounge's noodle bar is a highlight, serving ramen and udon This is the Boeing 787 Dreamliner that will fly us to Brussels All Nippon Airways is the world's largest Boeing 787 operator ANA has a fleet of 88 Dreamliners (average age: 9 years) ANA was the first airline to fly the Boeing 787 Dreamliner Our flight to Brussels departs from Gate 55 today The cockpit and cabin crew arrive at the gate The ANA cabin crew bows when passing through the gate Bowing is a sign of respect in Japanese culture I am one of the first passengers to board today's flight ANA has different Business Class configurations on its B787s This Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner features 48 Business Class seats The 48 lie-flat seats are arranged in a staggered 1-2-1 layout All Business Class seats have direct aisle access The 48 Business Class seats are spread over two cabins The forward cabin contains 26 Business Class seats The rear cabin holds 22 BusinessCclass seat 7A is my window seat for the 14 hour flight to Brussels The seat width on the Boeing 787 is roughly 21 inches (53 cm) The pitch of the Business Class seat is 62 inches (158 cm) I'll take a tour of the ANA Business Class seat after takeoff The cabin looks modern and is spotlessly clean A welcome drink is offered during the boarding process We're leaving the gate at 10 am (on time departure) The safety video is played as we taxi to the runway Tokyo Narita Airport has two main runways Runway 16R/34L is 4,000 m (13,123 ft) long Runway 16L/34R measures 2,500 m (8,202 ft) ANA's B787s use Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 or GE GEnx engines Have you ever flown with All Nippon Airways? ANA was founded in 1952 as Japan Helicopter & Aeroplane Co The carrier was renamed All Nippon Airways in 1957 ANA's first international flight was to Guam in 1966 Today, ANA serves 90 domestic & 60 international destinations All Nippon Airways joined Star Alliance in 1999 The airline has won multiple awards for safety and cabin service  I love the moment when the plane breaks above the clouds This is the 'smaller' Business Class cabin (with 22 seats) And this is the 'larger' Business Class cabin (with 26 seats) Let's have a detailed look at the ANA Business Class seat In front of each seat is an 18-inch touchscreen monitor Below the TV is an ottoman and some storage space for shoes Next to the TV is a hook to hang a coat Next to the seat is a large side table Above the table are a reading light, remote, and power outlets Below the side table is an electronic panel for the seat controls The tray table pulls out from the side of the seat While not cutting-edge, the seat feels very comfortable Once at cruising altitude, the captain gives a welcome message ANA’s Business Class amenity kit comes in an Ettinger pouch The kit contains travel essentials and Aveda toiletries A reusable bag is included for convenience during travel Slippers are provided ANA's bedding includes a bed pad, comforter, and pillow The bed pad is a version of Nishikawa Sangyo's Air Cyclone Each seat comes with noise-cancelling headphones Flight attendants come by passing out hand wipes All Business Class passengers get a voucher for free Wi-Fi Let's have a look at the menu on today's flight Top chefs create the onboard menus for All Nippon Airways Amuse bouche: matcha almond pie stick and marinated mussel  Starter: sea bream sushi, Japanese omelet and duck breast Kelp-cured masu salmon with egg yolk vinegar Steamed chicken with aromatic sauce Main course: simmered beef in arima sansho pepper sauce The beef is served with rice, miso soup & Japanese pickles  Dessert: matcha mousse, cheese, and fruits There are three lavatories in the plane's forward section The Business Class lavatories are stocked with toiletries High clouds rushing by reveal the plane’s incredible speed The seat converts into a flat bed at the touch of a button The bed has a length of 78 inches (198 cm) The sun sets as we cruise over Alaska It never gets completely dark this far north in spring The horizon glows long after the sun disappears The Boeing 787 features an 18-inch touchscreen at each seat The inflight entertainment (IFE) system is easy to use ANA's IFE offers a wide range of movies, TV shows, and music  The system includes about 150 movies and various shows The entertainment is selected via touchscreen or a remote  ANA's IFE is called 'ANA Sky Channel' ANA offers complimentary Wi-Fi to Business Class passengers A moving map shows the flight route in real time The flight takes a polar route due to Russian airspace closure Flights from Japan to Europe take longer due to this rerouting ANA will soon launch a new Business Class on the Boeing 787 The new Business Class seat will be called “THE Room FX” The design is inspired by ANA’s “THE Room” on the 777 Each Business Class seat will feature a full privacy door New tech will include Bluetooth audio and wireless charging We've reached the Beaufort Sea, the main sea north of Alaska  Snacks can be ordered from the menu throughout the flight Rice Bowl with beef Japchae ANA’s signature noodle dish: negi miso ramen Häagen-Dazs ice cream The flight path takes us across northern Canada and Greenland The views are spectacular as the sun rises again Enjoy the stunning scenery and music in the coming minutes We're leaving the Canadian mainland behind us The scenery gets even better as we cross the sea to Greenland About 80% of Greenland is covered in ice The ice sheet is the second largest on Earth In places, the ice is over 3 km (9,800 ft) thick Greenland is an autonomous territory of Denmark The views over Greenland's east coast are breathtaking  Glaciers slowly move toward the sea, forming icebergs Flying over Greenland offers truly unique Arctic views The clear weather conditions afford sublime views I kept the camera rolling because the views left me speechless A dinner is served two hours prior to touchdown Main course: tilefish, wild vegetables & yuba with dashi sauce Tasty tidbits: cabbage & sakura shrimp in dashi sauce  The dinner is served with miso soup & Japanese pickles We're approaching mainland Europe after 14 hours of flying We hit some moderate turbulence following a smooth flight Modern aircraft are designed to handle turbulence easily The coastline of the Netherlands comes into view We fly through beautiful cloud formations as we land in Brussels  My home town comes into view. Can you guess the name?  We're landing at Brussels Airport at 4:30 pm (on time arrival) Thx for watching my All Nippon Airways Business Class video

reviews.transcript_full: Is Singapore Airlines the world’s best Business Class airline?  Many travelers rank Singapore Airlines above Qatar or Emirates Let’s judge the seat, food, service & comfort on a real flight The 13 hour flight takes us from Singapore to Brussels Enjoy the full Singapore Airlines Business Class experience! We're arriving at Singapore Changi Airport Changi consistently ranks among the world’s best airports The airport is home to the world’s tallest indoor waterfall The Rain Vortex is 40 meters (131 feet) tall At night, the Rain Vortex glows with shifting colors and music The airport spans 4 terminals arranged in an inverted U-shape The airport connects to 400+ cities across the globe Singapore Airlines offers a dedicated Business Class check-in Changi Airport serves 70 million passengers annually Let's visit Singapore Airlines' SilverKris Business Class Lounge Located at T3, this is Singapore Airlines' flagship lounge The lounge is split into a left and right section upon entry Both lounge sections feature their own buffet & drinks stations Seating ranges from sofas and armchairs to dining tables Food quality exceeds that of most Business Class lounges The lounge's other section feels more intimate This part of the lounge has a buffet station with open kitchen The spirits selection includes several premium brands Live cooking stations serve noodles and pastas The buffet includes a mix of Asian and Western dishes Lounge amenities include showers, meeting rooms, and Wi-Fi The lounge is open 24/7 for eligible passengers Let’s head to the gate for our flight to Brussels A Singapore Airlines A380 is parked right next to our gate This is the Airbus A350 that will fly us to Brussels Singapore Airlines is the world’s largest A350 operator Singapore Airlines' crew arrives at the gate (please count them) I count 6 pilots and 26 crew members (!!!)  Is this the most staffed flight ever? :-) Usually, there are 13 cabin crew & 3 pilots on a long-haul flight It's time to board the aircraft Singapore Airlines’ A350 features 42 Business Class seats Spread over two cabins, the seats are arranged in a 1-2-1 layout 20A is my window seat for the 13 hour flight to Brussels The seat is one of the widest in the airline industry Seat pitch is 153 cm (60 inch) and width is 71 cm (28 inch) Center seats include a partition screen for privacy Let’s take a detailed tour of the seat prior to takeoff The seat controls are located in a panel in the armrest In front of the seat is a large 18-inch HD screen A small compartment with vanity mirror sits beside the screen The seat features an ottoman (foot rest) to the side A side console offers storage, power outlets, and a reading light Next to the console is the IFE remote and a small storage box The tray table is stored in the armrest The crew welcomes passengers with a drink and hot towel We have a full Business Class cabin on tonight's flight The pilot welcomes the passengers Have you ever flown with Singapore Airlines? Leave a comment We're leaving the gate at midnight (on time departure) The safety video is a beautifully produced film  The iconic Singapore Girl delivers the safety instructions Safety instructions are paired with Singapore’s landmarks The cabin lights are dimmed for takeoff The A350 is powered by Rolls-Royce Trent XWB engines We get a nice view of Singapore Changi Airport after takeoff Business Class amenity kits are available upon request The kit includes skincare items from Le Labo Slippers and socks are offered A large pillow and a soft duvet are provided as well Noise-cancelling headphones enhance the inflight experience Let’s take a look at the inflight menu World-class chefs design Singapore Airlines' menus Aperitif: a choice of drinks, served with mixed nuts Starter: marinated smoked salmon with capers Main course: herb-crusted roast lamb chops, garlic confit mash Dessert: Milo dinosaur cake We encounter moderate turbulence above the Straits of Malacca  The region around Malaysia and Sumatra is prone to turbulence Converging trade winds create big thunderstorms The A350 has three lavatories for Business Class passengers The lavatories are stocked with Payot toiletries Singapore Airlines' cabin crew assists in setting up the bed When fully flat, the bed measures 198 cm or 78 inches in length Legs are positioned at a slight angle in bed mode The IFE system is controlled using a handheld remote Singapore Airlines calls its IFE system KrisWorld KrisWorld includes hundreds of movies, TV shows, and playlists Singapore Airlines also offers free Wi-Fi in Business Class The flight can be tracked in real-time with an interactive 3D map Light bites are served upon request throughout the flight Mid-flight snack: Singapore carrot cake with prawns Breakfast is served 90 minutes prior to landing Breakfast service starts with a hot towel to refresh a little Breakfast includes sliced fresh fruits and flavored yoghurt Lobster Thermidor is served as a main course The captain announces the start of our descent into Brussels Singapore Airlines is one of the world’s most awarded airlines The airline’s story began in 1947 as Malayan Airways Its first aircraft was the twin-engined Airspeed Consul In 1966, it became Malaysia-Singapore Airlines, or MSA MSA split in 1972, creating two national airlines Singapore Airlines quickly emerged as a global carrier Singapore Airlines has often led aviation innovation It pioneered free meals, drinks, and headsets in Economy In 2007, it also launched the Airbus A380 into service Thx for watching my Singapore Airlines Business Class video

ITA Airways (seat, meals, service, entertainment, amenities) Welcome to the International Airport of the Maldives We're taken to the main terminal by a Four Seasons luxury car Check-in is smooth, with dedicated Business Class counters We’re taken by bus to the remote aircraft stand The new international terminal at Velana International Airport 
in the Maldives is officially set to open this summer The Maldives’ old terminal was built for 1.5 million passengers
but now serves over 2 million, causing major congestion The new Maldives airport expansion will ease congestion 
and handle the growing number of travelers This is the Airbus A330neo that will fly us to the Maldives
(aircraft registration: EI-TYC; named Stefano Baldini)  ITA Airways operates a total of 23 long-haul aircraft in its fleet:
11 Airbus A330-900neo, 6 Airbus A350, and 6 Airbus A330-200 ITA Airways' fleet has an average age of 5.7 years Have you ever flown with ITA Airways?
If so, what was your experience? Leave a comment ITA Airways' A330neo Business Class cabin is arranged in a 
1-2-1 configuration, giving each passenger direct aisle access 6L is my Business Class seat for the flight to the Rome The seat model is the Thompson Vantage XL,  
an excellent seat type used by several leading airlines What makes ITA’s version unique is the bespoke Italian styling Window seats alternate between true window seats (set closer
to the fuselage) and aisle-adjacent seats (set closer to the aisle) In the center section, seats are arranged in a paired layout, 
designed with couples or traveling companions in mind ITA Airways' A330neo Business Class cabin features a
stylish decor, reflecting Italy’s legendary design sensibility A hot towel and welcome drink are offered upon boarding Nineteen athletes, including Olympic and Paralympic
medalists, demonstrate the procedures in the safety video We're leaving the gate at 1 pm local time (on-time departure) We pass a Dreamliner of Neos, an Italian airline specializing 
in leisure travel and a competitor of ITA Airways Male Airport has 2 runways measuring 45 × 3,200 m
(148 × 10,499 ft) and 60 × 3,400 m (200 × 11,150 ft) ITA Airways' Airbus A330neo aircraft
are powered by Rolls-Royce Trent 7000 engines The Trent 7000 engine delivers a thrust of 72,000 pounds
(one engine has the push of 100 Ferraris racing flat out) This enables the A330neo to achieve a non-stop range
of up to 7,200 nautical miles (approximately 13,334 kilometers) We get some terrific views of the Maldives after takeoff The Maldives' islands and atolls
are the visible tips of an oceanic volcanic mountain range The Maldives has 1192 coral islands & sandbanks: 200
islands are inhabited & 140 islands are home to resorts Let's have a closer look at the
ITA Airways Airbus A330neo Business Class seat The seat features a 17-inch high-definition TV screen A spacious footwell is located under the TV Passengers can hang their jackets with a built-in hanger The seat's side cabinet keeps belongings handy
and also holds a modern, elegant light and the power ports The side table under the cabinet holds the entertainment 
handset and seat controls for easy comfort adjustments The seat's tray table is smoothly released via a simple latch Let's explore ITA Airways' Business Class amenities The kit is an elegant clutch in sustainable and reusable canvas,
and contains a dental kit, eye mask, socks, and earplugs Business Class passengers also receive a second kit: a soft 
cosmetics bag by international wellness company QC Terme The kit includes shower gel, shampoo, 
sanitizer, face cream, body cream, and hand butter Bedding includes a pillow, duvet and slippers Noise-cancelling headphones are also provided Let’s explore today's inflight dinner menu ITA Airways’ Business Class wine list features 
a curated selection of fine Italian and international wines Aperitif, served with mixed nuts Starter: pumpkin and parmesan cheese flan
with mushrooms and toasted pumpkin seeds Turnip greens Orecchiette pasta: Italian pasta dressed
with anchovies of Cetara, tomatoes and bread crumble Main course: braised beef cheek, 
accompanied by roasted cubed pumpkin and sautéed chard Fresh sliced seasonal fruit plate Dessert: tiramisu with coffee glaze and dark cocoa crumble ITA Airways' A330neo Business Class has 3 lavatories: one 
at the front, and two shared with Premium Economy at the rear With the push of a button, the Business Class 
seat reclines into a fully flat bed The bed measures 80 inches (203 centimeters) in length Let's explore ITA Airways' inflight entertainment The program offers the latest Italian movies, Hollywood 
blockbusters, TV shows and immersive music playlists ITA Airways offers Wi-Fi on its Airbus A330neo fleet The flight path takes us over Abu Dhabi We encounter some turbulence in the Iraqi airspace It's time for a midflight snack: assorted Italian cheese board

reviews.transcript_full:
This video features a spectacular seaplane flight in the Maldives Enjoy the Maldives seaplane flight and the magnificent views! The destination of the flight is Soneva Secret,
the Maldives' newest ultra-luxury resort Welcome to Male International Airport in the Maldives, where
Soneva hosts meet guests who arrive by international flight The Soneva hosts also assist guests with the check-in
at the airport counters to secure seaplane boarding passes The Maldives has two seaplane operators: 
Manta Air and TMA (Trans Maldivian AIrways) Next, guest are transferred to the seaplane terminal by a Tesla The drive to the seaplane terminal takes only 5 minutes The new seaplane terminal was inaugurated in October 2022 At the seaplane terminal, Soneva operates its own
lounge, where guests can wait for their flight to the resort The lounge’s interior reflects Soneva's signature eco-design Snacks (cheese, chocolates & ice-cream) and beverages
are served, and complimentary WiFi is provided The lounge also features a play room for children The lounge features a large outdoor terrace, with views of the
seaplane docks, which is the world's largest seaplane terminal Prior to boarding, passengers are escorted 
to a small room, where a safety video is played Soneva has its own fleet of luxurious seaplanes Maintained and operated by Manta Air,
the Soneva seaplanes offer a superior travel experience The Soneva seaplanes have only has 8 seats
(for comparison, a regular seaplane features 16 seats) Aboard the plane, leather interiors welcome passengers Twin Otter seaplanes have short take-off and landing abilities They have a range of 886 mi (1425 km)
and a cruise speed of 173 mi (270 km) per hour Have you ever flown onboard a seaplane in the Maldives?
If so, what was your experience? Leave a comment Flight time from Male to Soneva Secret is 75 minutes
(a stop-over is made at Soneva Fushi along the way) All pilots in the Maldives are commercially trained and
they fly the plane with bare feet or flipflops (so cool!) A seaplane flight in the Maldives is a breathtaking journey
as it offers some of the most incredible views in the world The first part of the flight crosses the North Male Atoll - home to
the airport and capital city Male - which consists of 50 islands The first hotel in the Maldives opened
in the North Male Atoll in 1972 and had only 30 rooms The seaplane is flying over the famous One&Only Reethi Rah
Resort, located on the outer edge of the North Male Atoll We're making a stop-over at Soneva Fushi to drop some guests Soneva Fushi is regarded as the first luxury hotel in the
Maldives, setting of the trend of luxury holidays in the nation Opened in 1995, Soneva Fushi is still one of the Maldives' best 
resorts, blending ultra-luxury with environmental responsibility Welcome to Soneva Fushi International Airport,
probably the tiniest airport in the world The stop-over at Soneva Fushi takes only 5 minutes The plane takes off at short distance from the resort
as not to disturb the guests on the island Here we go again ... We get a spectacular view of Soneva Fushi after takeoff Soneva Fushi is located in the Baa Atoll,
a designated UNESCO World Biosphere Reserve The Baa Atoll is home to 1200 fish species, including manta
rays, sharks, and an abundance of sea turtles and dolphins The Baa Atoll consists of 75 islands of which
13 are inhabited with a population of over 11,000 people Two luxury resorts can be seen in the distance:
Anantara Kihavah Villas and Four Seasons Landaa Giraavaru As the seaplane leaves the Baa Atoll, the Maldives' 
next atoll - the Raa Atoll - comes into view Surfers and sailors flock to Raa Atoll
for its excellent surf spots and idyllic sailing routes We get a nice view of Joali Being Resort from the air This is Joali Maldives, the sister resort of Joali Being We're leaving the Raa Atoll and now head towards the
Haa Dhaalu Atoll, the most remote atoll in the Maldives We get our first glimpse of Soneva Secret,
the Maldives' most exclusive resort Soneva Secret is located in the bluest lagoon I've ever seen The only resort in the Haa Dhaalu Atoll, Soneva Secret is set on
Dhipparufushi Island at the westernmost tip of the Maldives Soneva Secret features only 14 water & island villas; each villa
comes with a dedicated team of three (including a butler & chef) This is how the landing looks like from the cockpit ... From the landing site, it's 5 min by speedboat to the resort The resort staff is waiting for us on the beach 
(it feels like a scene from the White Lotus, only the real version)

yt_comments.author: @jcshobbiesandrecreation5873
yt_comments.text: We flew Chicago to Frankfort and back route in Jan 2024. Both legs were on the 747-800 and we were upstairs in business for both flights. I found both flights to be enjoyable. The planes were clean, the staff was some of the best I've encountered and every meal and drink onboard was great. With all that said, I'm really looking forward to trying out the new cabin on the 800's once it is in place. If these flights were daytime flights I'd give them 9 out of 10 but, because they were at night, both my wife and I tried to get a little sleep. I'm 6ft tall and have broad shoulders. My wife is 5'9. We both felt the shoulder area of the seats when in the bed configuration was too narrow. She is a side sleeper and she found it very difficult to get comfortable. I tried to get comfortable but eventually gave up and put the seat back in the upright but reclined position and was able to get an hour or so of sleep. I found the IFE to be pretty good but the screens were dim even when adjusted to their max brightness and showing their age. I still watched several good movies during my flights but did wish for a better screen. Can't wait until they update the 800's cabin.

chapters.title: Where the 747 is still in operation

yt_comments.author: @jckyu
yt_comments.text: I flew on Air China's 747-400 when I went back to China last year, from Beijing Capital to Shenzhen Bao'an (PEK-SZX). This route is among China's busiest, but that day only 110 passengers were onboard. The business class was fairly crowded, but in economy, Air China was literally ferrying chairs - cushy vintage airplane seats with a boxy shape that reminded me of Pan Am's 747s, which I have only seen in online pictures. The business class seats are angle-flat and exactly the same as Asiana's, as shown in this video. I was fortunate to book myself in business class on the upper deck, with my friend and I each occupying a window seat. The view from the upper deck was truly amazing; I've never seen the ramp from such a tall angle. The inflight meal, a mediocre Japanese-style rice bowl, was unremarkable, but the cabin crew was stellar. They seemed to know a lot of aviation geeks are flying this route and were quite welcoming to us, two young students who are obviously different from the other business people on the plane, who were either taking a nap or doing paperwork, while we were unsettled in our seats, eager to explore the rest of the cabin. So, the flight attendants invited us to tour the first-class section on the lower deck, where Air China has swivel-style seats, quite similar to American Airlines’ first-class product on their 777s. We also toured the galley area, where we saw the cassette-based IFE system. Sadly, the economy class movie screen has been retrofitted, using LCD TVs rather than CRT projectors. The cabin has lots of interesting details, such as a fixture on the wall that is a Chinese drawing on one side, and a mirror when flipped to the other side. Some research revealed that Air China is using these B744s as backups for Xi’s "Air Force One", and that’s the reason why they are still flying. The last time the plane I was on (B-2447) was used for governmental tasks was flying Kim Jong Un to Singapore, phew. Of course, the airplane will be remodeled for these tasks. Another interesting aspect of my flight was that my friend and I estimated the cost per seat using fuel burn information and found it to be even higher than what we paid for our tickets (about $350 per person). This confirmed our suspicion that Air China wasn't expecting these 747s to generate revenue, but rather they were in operation for political reasons.

reviews.title: 17 HOURS ON THE QANTAS A380 Business Class Review from Dallas to Sydney

yt_comments.author: @high-reshallucinations
yt_comments.text: Pretty good overall — a comfortable, sleep-focused flight rather than a “wow” luxury experience ✈ The big wins were the Qantas A380 business seat, mattress pad, quiet/smooth ride, and crew. He apparently slept about 9 hours, which is basically the holy grail on a 16h48m flight. The weak points were pretty clear: Food: dinner was decent, but snack/breakfast sounded poor — lots of commenters also thought the catering looked below business-class standard. Entertainment/tech: limited IFE and no Wi-Fi, so the product feels dated. Ground experience: denied Flagship Lounge access, then ended up in a crowded Admirals Club. So: great bed, great crew, mediocre food, outdated tech. For a 17-hour Dallas–Sydney flight, I’d call it a successful flight — just not a top-tier business class experience like Singapore, Emirates, Qatar, etc. 😄

yt_comments.author: @vijaymohaniyer
yt_comments.text: The emirates 380 business class feels more premium than this. Screen sizes are bigger and the meals look and taste better too. Sad that Qantas doesn't have wifi. They seem to be like the Air India of Australia 😂

yt_comments.author: @high-reshallucinations
yt_comments.text: Qantas chose Viasat, not Starlink, and its long-haul retrofit is moving slowly — especially on the A380. ✈ On that Dallas–Sydney QF8 A380, the main reasons are: 1. Qantas already committed to Viasat Qantas announced its international Wi-Fi rollout using Viasat’s next-generation satellite network, with A330, 787 and A380 aircraft to be progressively retrofitted. That means they are not simply installing Starlink like Qatar or United. 2. A380 retrofits are hard Qantas said older A380s are especially challenging because they were built before modern onboard internet infrastructure was common. Installing Wi-Fi means adding antennas/radomes and aircraft wiring — basically physical surgery on the aircraft roof. Qantas specifically said the A380 is the most challenging fleet to retrofit. 3. Qantas is doing it during maintenance, not all at once The first international Wi-Fi aircraft were A330s, mainly for Asia routes. Qantas said 787, A380 and A330-300 installations would follow later, so the A380 fleet is behind the smaller/easier aircraft. 4. Coverage over the Pacific is still a weak spot for Qantas Qantas’ own Wi-Fi page says international connectivity can vary, and it lists areas where coverage is not available, including the South Pacific Ocean — exactly the kind of region a Dallas–Sydney flight crosses. 5. Other airlines moved faster with Starlink Qatar Airways, for example, has already equipped nearly 120 widebody aircraft with Starlink and completed its A350 rollout. That is why Starlink feels “already here” on some airlines while Qantas still feels behind. So basically: Qantas bet on Viasat, the A380 is difficult to retrofit, and the Pacific coverage/rollout is lagging. Starlink may be faster, but switching providers is expensive and disruptive once an airline has contracts, hardware plans and maintenance schedules in place. Reuters also notes that changing satellite providers is costly because aircraft need provider-specific equipment and downtime for installation.

yt_comments.author: @high-reshallucinations
yt_comments.text: Other airlines moved faster with Starlink mainly because they had stronger urgency, easier rollout paths, and better timing than Qantas. 1. They picked Starlink early, while Qantas picked Viasat Qatar, United, Hawaiian and others committed to Starlink as their next big Wi-Fi upgrade. Qantas instead committed its international A330, 787 and A380 fleet to Viasat’s satellite network, so it is locked into a different hardware and provider path. 2. Starlink installations got faster after the first fleets Qatar is the best example. It said its Boeing 777 Starlink retrofit time dropped from three days to 9.5 hours per aircraft, letting it finish the 777 rollout in nine months, about 50% faster than planned. That kind of process improvement makes a rollout much faster once the airline, installer and regulator have the aircraft type figured out. 3. Some airlines made Wi-Fi a headline competitive feature United is using Starlink as a big customer-experience weapon. It completed Starlink installation on 300+ regional aircraft and said more than 25% of its daily departures had Starlink by February 2026, with plans for 500+ mainline aircraft by the end of 2026. 4. Regional/narrow-body aircraft are easier to roll out first United started with regional jets and then moved to mainline aircraft. That is easier than starting with huge long-haul widebodies. Qantas’ problem is the opposite: its most painful gap is on international widebodies, especially A380s. 5. Qantas’ A380s are especially difficult Qantas has said retrofitting older international aircraft is complex, and that the A380s are the most challenging aircraft in its fleet to retrofit. Even the first international A330-200 Wi-Fi retrofit took around three weeks in the hangar. 6. Starlink had momentum and hardware scale Reuters reported that Starlink now has contracts on more than 7,000 aircraft, and airlines are rushing to upgrade because fast/free Wi-Fi has become a premium-cabin expectation. Once many airlines choose the same supplier, certifications, installation know-how and supply chains improve quickly. So the simple version: Qatar and United treated Starlink like a strategic priority and scaled the retrofit fast. Qantas chose Viasat, has older hard-to-retrofit long-haul aircraft, and is moving more cautiously. 🛰✈

yt_comments.author: @high-reshallucinations
yt_comments.text: The weak points came from a few specific things: 1. Lounge issue: He was denied access to the American Airlines Flagship Lounge, likely because of the lounge’s alcohol access rules in the US. He had to use the Admirals Club instead, which was crowded. 2. Food inconsistency: Dinner was good, but the mid-flight snack and breakfast were weak. The waffles apparently tasted like a frozen meal, and commenters felt the food looked more like economy food served on nicer plates. 3. No Wi-Fi: On a nearly 17-hour flight, no Wi-Fi makes the product feel outdated, especially compared with other premium long-haul airlines. 4. Limited entertainment: The IFE selection was not strong enough for such a long flight. So the main cause was not the seat or crew — those were good. The weak points were mostly ground lounge rules, catering quality, and old tech/entertainment. ✈

reviews.transcript_excerpt: 09 Jul 2026 RAVE sets the scene for deeply immersive inflight experiences By Mary Kirby → Executives at seatback IFE specialist RAVE Aerospace have for many years talked to airlines about bringing more content, higher resolutions and larger screens to the aircraft cabin.

article_quotes.text: Executives at seatback IFE specialist RAVE Aerospace have for many years talked to airlines about bringing more content, higher resolutions and larger screens to the aircraft cabin.

The Brea, California-based firm’s portfolio certainly reflects that evolution; its 4K miniLED HDR 10+ Liquid Crystal Displays can now be sized up to 32 inches, and its latest embedded IFE systems feature massive cloud networked storage and powerful processing.

We think they can transport them someplace virtually,” Louis Poupard, RAVE’s staff product manager said at the Aircraft Interiors Expo in Hamburg, where, together with seatmaker Safran Seats, RAVE introduced the premium suite demonstrator Origin.

Made of micro-LED bendable panels, the Immersive Display Concept from RAVE that is at the core of Origin is complemented by advanced seating technology and Euphony headset-free audio from Safran Seats.

RAVE and Safran Seats are not alone in exploring how a deeply immersive IFE and engagement experience — as achieved with vast screen real estate and compelling content in a premium suite — can transform the passenger experience.

Origin’s reveal comes two years after Collins Aerospace and Panasonic Avionics at AIX 2024 unveiled MAYA , their next-gen business class seat concept featuring a 45” curved ultra-wide OLED screen from Panasonic.

In terms of screen footprint, RAVE used the equivalent of 17.5ft in the semi-enclosed Safran Seats suite — including real estate above the passenger’s head — to transport attendees to another time or place.

By enabling passengers to escape from reality beyond the aircraft, airlines can create “sticky, really cohesive experiences,” said the RAVE executive, confirming to RGN that the firm has “already filed a few patents” around this IFE/seat integration project.

article_quotes.text: AZAL reveals interior of new A321neo, uses IFE as differentiator - Runway GirlRunway Girl AZAL reveals interior of new A321neo, uses IFE as differentiator - Runway Girl Runway Girl Network uses cookies.

Based on the popular Comoda Materia Pack short-haul business class platform from Italian seatmaker Geven, the 12 recliners on AZAL’s A321neo offer generous legroom, a legrest and a cocktail table on the center console.
Each business class seat also features a 4K OLED HDR10+ IFE screen from Panasonic Avionics’ next-gen Astrova line.
But AZAL’s business class seats on the A321neo appear to represent a new seat/IFE integration project for the two suppliers, as Comoda is traditionally offered with screen sizes of up to roughly 16″.
Panasonic’s cloud-based Modular Interactive tool, which enables the airline to customize the IFE experience, is also being deployed on AZAL jets.

Image: Panasonic Avionics Universal power, fast-charging USB-C outlets, complimentary Viasat-powered inflight connectivity and wireless IFE round out the offering in business class on AZAL’s first A321neo.
Down back, the economy class cabin features 179 slimline seats.

AZAL is not offering seatback IFE in economy, but passengers can keep their devices charged with Astronics’ EMPOWER USB outlet in the seatback, and avail of free wireless IFE or paid access to the Viasat IFC.

reviews.transcript_full: Today, I flew on an Airbus 380 operated by Emirates, the world's premier luxury airline , for just $120 Even those with no interest in airplanes or airlines have likely heard of it at least once. Emirates is considered the undisputed best among the "oil money" Middle Eastern "Big Three " and is the world's largest operator of the A380. Emirates owns 120 of the 251 aircraft produced by Airbus, accounting for nearly half of the total. From the luxury in the skies featuring onboard showers and bars to the ultra-fast in-flight Wi-Fi "Starlink ," Emirates' A380 has a lot to show you today. Let's get started! Hello, this is Manager Woo. This is Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport. Since Bangkok is a top global travel destination, Emirates operates five flights daily; one of them is dedicated to the "Fifth Freedom" route between Bangkok and Hong Kong. EK384 and EK385 depart from Bangkok at 2:15 PM and from Hong Kong at 9:30 PM. I am off to my destination. I booked a one-way economy ticket to Hong Kong on Agoda for $120. Since the lowest fare for this route is in the 110,000 won range on Hong Kong Express, adding 50,000 won to book Emirates is by no means a bad deal. I will proceed with check-in at the S counter. Although there are self-check-in kiosks, I will check in at the counter because the line isn't long. Actually, one of the reasons I checked in at the counter was that I wanted to receive a ticket with this red logo on it. It is convenient because there is an escalator right next to the counter that goes up to the departure hall. Since I have to take a train to get to Gate S today , I will visit the lounge in the main terminal first. This is the Coral Business Lounge located near Gate D1. It has been open for about two years, so I heard the facilities are relatively clean and nice. You can enter using both a PP card and a The Lounge card. There is a shower room here, but it is not free, so if you need a shower, it might be better to go to the Miracle Lounge near Gate D5. Inside, the area is divided into a group space and individual tables. They have a good selection of drinks here, and the bar offers a variety of cocktails. I think this place would be good for people who like to drink, but the food here didn't really suit my taste. Should I say it tasted a bit like stainless steel? It had a slightly strong taste, so since I prioritize food over alcohol, I probably won't visit again. I then came to the Miracle Lounge near Gate D5. Many smokers visit here; you can grab a Zero Coke from the refrigerator right after entering and exit through the side door to smoke on the outdoor terrace. I noticed many people just come here and leave. Now, I will head to the gate. Gates starting with 'S' are located in the satellite terminal, so you have to take a train from the main terminal to get there, just like at Incheon Airport Terminal 1. This is my second time using this place; unlike the Incheon terminal, it is quite large enough to accommodate A380s, and since it hasn't been long since it opened, it is very pleasant. Today's boarding gate is S113. Since this is my first time flying on an Emirates A380, I took some photos of the plane from various angles. It has a sturdy front view with a width of 80 meters, the starboard side on the right where you can feel the height, and the port side on the left where the jet bridge connects. The jet bridge connects first to the upper deck where First and Business Class are located, and then to the main deck on the lower level where Economy is located. Two additional aircraft are being connected. With a wingspan of 36 meters alone, you can immediately feel how massive it is when standing next to a B737, which has a total width of this size. A Qatar Airways A380 had just pulled in at the opposite gate, so I went over to take a picture. Perhaps because its livery is split between gray and white, the all-white Emirates seems to look somehow larger. I have returned to the gate, and the flight attendants are giving a pre-flight briefing. This is a jumbo jet carrying over 20 crew members. Higher classes and membership tiers board first, and economy boarding begins on the lower main deck. That path on the right leads to the upper jet bridge for First and Business, while the Economy main deck is downstairs. Emirates is an airline I have a love-hate relationship with; I applied here several times when I was flying. With the resolve that "I will fly if I get accepted," I used Etihad and Qatar but never flew here, and here I am finally getting to fly it... The A380 is extraordinary starting with its door size, and heading upstairs... I’ll go past the stairs and head to my seat. This is the main deck, filled entirely with economy seats, and the seating arrangement is 3-4-3. The seats are made of fabric in bright pastel tones; to me, they reminded me a bit of the color of a Little Mermaid's fin . My seat today is 50C, an aisle seat in the very back row of the front cabin. The seat width is 18 inches, which is spacious and comfortable. The legroom is ample, even with the pockets packed full . When you recline the seat, the lower seat slides out to create a full recline, yet there is enough room for my knees not to touch the seat. The angle of the backrest is about this much, and the headrest is thick and adjustable up and down. I usually find leather headrests a bit uncomfortable, but since this is fabric, I used it comfortably . Even though it is a flight of less than three hours , headsets, cushions, and blankets are provided as standard. The cabin was so cold that I covered myself with it as soon as I boarded, and the temperature was just right. Now, an announcement is coming on saying, "We are closing the doors, so ground staff, please disembark." I will now verify the aircraft type using the safety card. The safety announcement plays along with the pushback. Over there. The male flight attendant who appeared reminded me a bit of the male lead from the Netflix series 'You.' All the flight attendants here looked like movie stars. 'I guess that's why I didn't make the cut' :(( I briefly had a metacognitive moment. Then an announcement came on saying that Starlink is available. After takeoff, I will check the Starlink speed. Power ports are located next to the monitors in each of the three window seats, excluding the aisle seat. The seat next to me was empty, so I just used it; you can consider there to be two ports for every three seats. Also, there is a USB-A charging port at every seat. Below the monitor is a remote control with a touch screen, and below that is the tray table... no, let's look at the cup holder first. The cup holder here is gimbal-style; the inner holder rotates, so they say it maintains a level position even if you recline the seat in front of you. But when I actually used it, it looked a bit scary. I'll show you later when I get my coffee. Returning to the tray table, it is semi-foldable and adjustable forward and backward. Even though it is a 13-year-old aircraft, the cabin environment and seats are generally clean. We have arrived at the runway, and we will take a look at the A380's heavy takeoff via the tail camera. Because the wings are so big, the landing gear retracting is obscured and hard to see. The overhead control panel is a bit high, so it is difficult to operate while sitting; you have to stand up to operate it, especially on the aisle side. Seat and flight information is displayed at the top of the monitor, and if you press 'I' in the bottom left, you can check the flight details and the aircraft you are currently on. Since the flight is only two hours long, I will diligently capture various things. First, if you go to the in-flight entertainment language settings, you can select from a whopping 14 languages, including Korean. This is the entertainment section, which boasts a vast amount of content that is considered the best in the world. There are sections by genre, and I will go into the latest movies to check for Korean subtitles. I checked 'Project Hale Mary,' but there are no Korean subtitles. Not all content has subtitles, and the content that does have Korean subtitles is... If you go back to the previous step and enter the Korean Movies section at the top, you will find a list. It seems they have separately categorized and stored content that offers Korean dubbing or subtitles. The headset for watching videos is good because it has cushions inside. Now, I will try connecting to Starlink. This is my first time using it, too. If you connect to Emirates Wi-Fi while in airplane mode, the window changes, and once you enter the main screen, the connection is complete. First, let's go into Netflix. I clicked on the "Manager Kim" video, and it loads almost immediately. The playback starting speed is wow... At this rate, it doesn't seem much different from doing it on the ground. Also, when I travel abroad, I usually use A.T. Baro Call; I wonder if it uses data for calls, because it connects as well. Let's check how fast Starlink speeds are at 39,000 feet. Wow , it keeps going up. Let's speed it up a bit. The download speed was 260 megabits per second, and the upload speed was 3.7 megabits per second . You can expect it to take about 30 seconds to download a 1GB video. I also tried connecting with my MacBook. I can watch live broadcasts of CNN, BBC News, and sports matches on the laptop's large screen. However... If I had to point out a downside, since it allows for work, it seems difficult to use the excuse that I can't check emails when flying on a business trip. I was sitting and replying to some emails when the meal cart arrived, so I turned it off immediately. I removed the cushion from my back, adjusted my posture, and will now reverently receive the meal. It is a flight of less than three hours, but the tray is overflowing. A flight attendant at the back even brought me a separate Zero Coke. The main course is chicken, served with cucumber salad for appetizer, blueberry chocolate cake for dessert, and bread. It comes with boiled carrots and mashed potatoes. I was a little disappointed that it wasn't rice, but everything tasted really good. The cabin is tidied up, and now I will go check the restroom. It is decorated luxiously with white and wood patterns, and the space is decent enough not to feel cramped. Even the lid has a wood pattern, and there are disposable toilet seat covers, so you can use it cleanly. Feminine toiletries are also placed under the mirror next to it, but I won't bother opening them. Above the sink, there is an air vent and a call light for the flight attendant, and the faucet below dispenses water automatically with just a touch of the temperature control, keeping it clean. It is set up so you can just wash your hands. Paper towels are right above it, making it convenient to use. Next to the sink, there is hand lotion and an Eau de Toilette spray; these are products from the Noir line by the British lifestyle brand 'The White Company'. The 500ml hand lotion was selling for 30 pounds, which is about 60,000 won in Korean currency. You can tell a lot of money was invested in various details. I came back to my seat and asked for a cup of coffee, but the flight attendant told me not to put it in the cup holder. As I showed you earlier, this holder rotates inward, right? If you insert the coffee, it adjusts the horizontal level like a gimbal, but I was a bit afraid to let go of it. So I just placed it on the table to drink . The monitor tilt works well so you can see the screen when you move over to the seat in front. With about 30 minutes left, the captain's announcement regarding the destination is coming on. The seat next to me is empty, and the legroom is spacious, so I was able to fold my legs and travel comfortably. I didn't show you the remote control; the touch sensitivity of the screen isn't exactly fast, but since I don't really need to use it much, I think it's fine. It is quite large, so when I held my iPhone up to it, [there is] a case It looks like it would be boiling if I took it off. Just like the captain's announcement, it has been raining continuously in Hong Kong , so I can see water passing outside the window. Since we are descending , the water is rising. Seeing the tail camera fog up due to the rain, I thought the rain was really intense. But then, just as the city of Hong Kong started to come into view, the rain stopped again. We are landing at Hong Kong International Airport. An announcement comes on telling us to stand up when the seatbelt lights go off, but everyone is in a hurry . We have about 500 people to disembark from this plane alone, so we really need to get going fast. Today was my first time flying on an Emirates A380, and it was also my first experience with Starlink, so I boarded with a lot of excitement. I have a lot to show you, but time is short, so the three hours seem to have passed in a rush. Actually, for the viewers to enjoy Emirates, you would need to fly Business or First Class to really appreciate it , but this is a small channel that hasn't been around for long, and it’s only fun to start from Economy and work your way up step by step, right?! However, I found Economy class to be excellent as well. I heard that they are currently upgrading the seats on all their aircraft as they add Premium Economy class . I don't know when it will happen, but for my next Emirates review, I plan to move up one class at a time on a retrofitted aircraft. I will not be entering Hong Kong; instead, I will be transferring to Incheon via Hong Kong Express. I will organize the review of the next section well and upload it as well. Thank you for watching the long video until the end.
