reviews.transcript_full:
Today I am adding a new airline to my 
list. My flight on All Nippon Airways   takes me from Sydney to Tokyo Haneda on 
their Boeing 787 Dreamliner. But with   JAL and Qantas also offering this exact 
route, where does ANA fit in? Stay till   the end because I'll show you how to fly this 
airline’s business class for less than 1000   AUD.
 
 
The check in line was completely empty   as I arrived just 90 minutes before my flight.
The baggage allowance in Economy is 2 checked   bags, each up to 23 kilograms — which is 
actually quite generous compared to most   carriers. Thanks to their partnership 
with VA, if you happen to have Velocity   Gold status or above, you get an 
extra 23kg of baggage allowance. After check in, it was through 
immigration and security,   and then a seriously long walk to Gate 53.
Unfortunately, the Velocity partnership with ANA,   doesn’t extend to lounge access - another 
casualty of the mis-mash of Velocity partnerships.  But by the time I got to the gate, 
it was already time to board anyway. The boarding process was impressively organised. 
In what I think is a first for Economy class,   ANA boards its window seat passengers 
board first. If you think about it,   this makes sense and should at least in theory 
reduce that awkward shuffle in the aisle.   ANA was the launch customer for the Boeing 
787. It has a fleet of 86 of these types   with many more on order. Today we are on 
the 787-9 specifically the international   configuration with 192 economy class seats. The 
seat configuration is the standard 3-3-3 layout. The disappointing part of this seat layout   is that they used to run a wider 2 4 2 
configuration, but this didn’t survive.   That leaves Japan Airlines the only one that 
has stuck with 8 across layout on the 787. At around 17 inches wide, today's 
seat is on the narrower side.  On the seat pitch front, at 33 to 34 
inches, it is among the best you'll   find in economy. The seat itself covers the 
basics well with a coat hook, USB C charging,   split seat pockets and AC power under the seat.   The footrest is a genuinely nice touch that 
you don't see on many economy products anymore. Amenities wise, you get a pillow and blanket 
— simple but appreciated on a 9 hour flight.  And after all those comments about seat width,   I lucked out today with two empty seats next to 
me, which made a very comfortable difference. We pushed back right on time as ANA treated 
us to their Pokémon themed safety video. One   of the most charming safety videos I've 
ever seen and very on brand for Japan. Shortly after takeoff, the crew came 
through with the pre meal service.  Wet wipes, a packet of rice crackers — which were 
actually really tasty — and some orange juice. The tissues on board are made 
from recycled green tea leaves.   It's a very Japanese touch and 
I thought that was really cool. Since this was my first flight with them,   I played it safe and went with a special 
option specifically the Hindu meal.  And right away, one thing 
stood out, the metal cutlery.  I don’t know about you, but for me, that's 
a mark of a premium airline even in economy. The tray itself was pretty substantial. 
Alongside the main there was a salad,   cheese and crackers, fruit and dessert. The 
main was a chicken curry with rice — fragrant,   well seasoned, decent portion. It actually 
reminded me of the meal I had on Malaysia   Airlines. Although thankfully I didn't spill 
this one. Overall, a solid meal service for   economy and better than I expected. Maybe I 
don’t need to order a special meal next time. After the meal service, the cabin windows were 
dimmed even though this was a daytime flight.  I took the cue and managed 
to get a few hours of sleep. Before that though I spent some time with 
the entertainment system. And this seems to   be a bit of a theme with Japanese airlines 
— the content library is well stocked, but   titles are displayed as lists rather than grids, 
which makes finding anything a bit of a chore.  On the plus side there was WiFi on board, and 
the messaging version was completely free.  On a day flight that was pretty valuable and 
it made the whole experience far more passable. In between the meal services, the galley was 
stocked with snacks and drinks that you could   help yourself to — water, juice, light snacks.
Here is a look at one of five lavatories in   Economy class. It was pretty clean 
as you would expect from a Japanese   airline. This one was fitted with a change 
table and of course, it came with a bidet. With around two hours to go, as we flew 
past Guam, the second meal service came   around — a snack box. Inside was a bread 
roll, some fresh fruit and dried fruit.   It was decent but honestly a bit light for 
a 9 hour flight. The second service could   have been more substantial — but this has become 
pretty standard across the industry these days. The rest of the flight was uneventful and we 
eventually began our descent into Tokyo-Haneda.  So where does ANA sit among the 
three airlines on this route?  Against Qantas, I think ANA wins pretty easily 
with a newer aircraft type offering a better   hard product and features like WIFI on board. 
Against JAL, it's a closer call. JAL still has   the edge in terms of seat comfort with their 
2 4 2 layout. The food and onboard services   were similarly good to each other while 
the IFE was equally bad in both cases.  Overall, ANA economy is a solid product 
and is a comfortable way to get to Japan.   But I probably won’t rate is as high as JAL. 
Let me know what you think in the comments. So, to that business class upgrade tip. ANA is 
a Star Alliance member and their flights can be   redeemed using other Star Alliance program 
including Avianca's LifeMiles program. I   paid 25,000 LifeMiles for this economy 
ticket flying out of Sydney. But here's   an interesting quirk — if you book from the 
Tokyo end, economy drops to just 20,000 miles   and business class exactly double that at 
40,000 miles. Buy those 40,000 miles during   a LifeMiles sale and you could be sitting in ANA 
business class for less than 1000 AUD. That is   the real sweet spot on this route. Just keep 
in mind that award availability is limited,   so always check this on the Aviance website before 
you buy — and never purchase miles speculatively.

reviews.transcript_full: Today I'm doing something brand new for this channel. My first flight review. We're flying Japan Airlines economy from Dallas Fort Worth to Tokyo Haneda. Now this wasn't even supposed to be our original plan. We were scheduled to be on American Airlines in premium economy, but that entire flight got cancelled. So instead, we were rescheduled and snagged the last three economy seats together on Japan Airlines brand new A3501000. And we're taking this flight to catch a cruise out of Yokohama near Tokyo. In this video, I'm going to show you what the boarding and service were like, how comfortable the seats were, and what you get in terms of entertainment and amenities, and of course, how the food stacks up. you're going to want to stick around to the end where I'm going to share my top three mustpack items for a long haul flight like this. And one thing you can probably skip if you're doing this exact flight. So, you'll have to let me know at the end of this video if you like seeing flight reviews or if you prefer when I stick to cruise content. I'd love to know your honest feedback. We're going to start today by talking a little bit about the boarding process. Boarding at Dallas Fort Worth Terminal D was super smooth. It was really organized. The gate staff kept things moving. In fact, they lined everybody up before the flight by your boarding number, which made things super easy, and there was just no chaos at all. They had so many different gate agents helping out. It was just really clean and easy. Once we were actually on the flight, the flight attendants were so welcoming and professional. They were helping passengers out with getting their bags overhead, getting people seated, and even offering to take photos. And this was a good thing because the flight at this point was starting to run a little behind. But somehow they managed to get everyone on in a timely fashion. Honestly, this whole boarding experience was one of the fastest and easiest and most pleasant experiences I have ever had on flight. Let's talk a lot about seats and comfort cuz I know this is a big one. So, we were in row 53, which is about halfway through the economy cabin. Now, the seats had adjustable headrests with side flaps and a pretty decent recline. It's about a 5 in recline according to the website. The leg room was fine until the person in front of you reclined which got a little bit tight around uh you know hour three or four especially for my six-foot husband. I felt really bad for him because he was in the middle seat. Now each seat had USB and USBC ports. They also had an AC outlet, a very handy cup holder. That was rare and so cool. And a tray table. But there is no device holder. So, you're definitely going to want to bring like a phone stand or something similar if you'd like to use your own device, but I just set mine up on the tray table and it worked out great. The AC outlet was in kind of a funky location. It was right beneath the tray table, and there was a headphone jack down there beneath the TV as well. You have to kind of look for it, but you'll find everything. They also provided wired headphones that were relatively comfortable in case you didn't bring your own Bluetooth or wired headphones for the flight. They're pretty soft and pretty cozy. I used them the whole time. Let's move on to the amenities and the storage. So, when you got to your seat, everybody had a blanket, a pillow, and headphones. And the blanket we never really ended up using, and I'll tell you why a little bit later. Pillow was very nice. It was kind of a longer lumbar pillow. It was a little more long and plush than the ones I'm used to seeing. The overhead bins were great. They had plenty of space and my large backpack even fit under the seat in front of me. They were also really lenient about taking bags on at DFW, which was great. We were able to take our full-size 20-in carryons and a personal item, and they gave us no trouble at all. But the seating overall, I would say it was nothing crazy fancy, but it was everything you need for a long flight in terms of amenities, especially in coach. It's about what you would expect. Let's talk about the in-flight entertainment, you guys. Every seat on this aircraft had a 13-in 4K screen with a really big selection of entertainment. They had movies. They had TV shows, music, live television, they had lots of Japanese comedy, and even an in-flight exercise routine. So, what do we actually watch? Well, I watched Goonies, which is kind of funny. And my husband actually got through three Japanese movies which he said were excellent. He was talking about them for a couple of days afterwards. So don't skip out on the Japanese entertainment. They have great subtitle choices. Now the coolest feature, if you ask me, on these crazy big entertainment screens, you guys, these things are really nice. Coolest feature was the aircraft camera. Now you can switch between the map view. There's even a cockpit view or even a chase cam of the plane in flight. This was especially cool during takeoff and landing. During landing, we actually saw the flight land from the perspective of the wheel that they put down, which was awesome. It's really neat, and I do highly recommend that you play around with it right when you get on the flight and turn it back on just to kind of see where you are. It's such a beautiful view. There's also this really cool feature on the screen. It's like a little timeline that shows when your meals are going to be served and when the cabin lights will dim. This is so clever because you're going to know exactly when to expect service without guessing. You can kind of plan your naps around this if you're the kind of person who can sleep on a plane. By the way, can you sleep on a plane? I cannot sleep on a plane. It's horrible. You can also peruse the food and beverage selections on the screen. We didn't have a choice really of meals. Like you couldn't order from the screen, but they would say, "Okay, here's choice one and choice two." And they showed all the beverages, which was really nice. The screen also had this little feature where you could look at the cabin layout in case you wanted to see maybe where your seat was or maybe you needed access to an accessible restroom or baby changing table. All of that was on this little map. Now, there is a feature on the entertainment screens. It's like a Bluetooth connect where you're supposed to be able to connect your Bluetooth device to the screen, but we couldn't get it to work and we kind of gave up because it just kind of sat there buffering and didn't work. So, I'm curious to know, we were talking about that plane camera before where you can see the outside of the plane. You can see what it looks like from the top. Would you use this or would you just stick with the window view? I'm curious to know if you think that's a neat new feature. Let's talk about food and beverage. I know this is a big one for everybody. Let's start with the first service. About 30 minutes into the flight, like really soon after takeoff, we got a snack and a full drink service. They gave us this little packet of delicious like trail mix. It was super good. Actually, it wasn't trail mix. It was like snack mix. Think of like a checkex mix or something. And it was delicious. And then at the 90-minute mark, the first full meal came out. You had your choice of Japanese chicken meatballs with rice or what they call the international option, which was like a small pasta, like an orzo dish with shrimp and mushrooms. And they both came with sides. So, you were going to be getting miso soup and a few other sides like they had like a barley salad and they had a spaghetti and they had a potato salad and you got real silverware. There was no bamboo. There was no plastic. I mean, this is beautiful real silverware to eat with or you could use the provided chopsticks. I thought one of the highlights was the little hogen ice cream that came out right after followed by some green tea and coffee. So that was meal number one. About 90 minutes in. Later in the flight, probably 5 hours later or so after everybody kind of did that major first sleep, they handed out little chocolate croissants. And then 2 hours before landing, we had breakfast. I thought this meal was great. They served a frittata. I think they said it was like leak and ham frittata. And that was served with some veggies, some fruit, and a small cheesecake like dessert. I thought that the meals were tasty overall, although they were really heavy on carbohydrates. I mean, that first meal was like rice or pasta with spaghetti, potato salad, and a barley salad. I would have loved to have seen a little grain salad or fruit or some more protein. Um, next time, in fact, I might even order a low carb option to see if I can get more protein on the flight cuz I think it just makes you really sleepy. So, what do you guys think about that? Do you like it when things are really high carb on a flight so you can kind of pass out or do you pre-order your meal? Speaking of meal service, there is one little detail that I wanted to share with you. If you were asleep for the meal service, they put a little pink sticker on the tray table right in front of you and that would offer you the opportunity to select a meal at a later time when you woke up. And it was really nice because I actually saw the flight attendants following up on this and walking by when the person woke up and saying, "Would you like a meal?" It was so nice. So, you guys heard the entree choices, right? You had the Japanese chicken meatballs or the international pasta. Which one are you picking? Let's talk about restrooms. I don't usually talk about restrooms that much on cruise ships or anywhere I travel, but Japan Airlines deserves credit for this one. They were spotless and they were stocked with seat covers. How nice is that? Seat covers on an airplane, hand towels, hand sanitizer. You even had like fancy pump soap. And it was easily the nicest economy restroom I have ever used. So, let's talk about the overall experience on the flight. I have to say this 13-hour flight went by pretty fast. The deplaning was smooth. Everything went wonderfully, and the luggage came out before we could even get through customs, immigration, and a restroom stop, which was super impressive. So, let's talk about the pros and cons. Pros of this flight, in my opinion, the friendly, professional service. The staff were elegant, friendly, professional, wonderful, just above and beyond, and they kept it together for that full 13-hour flight. The cabin was clean and elegant. I really liked the design. I thought it was gorgeous. And I loved the entertainment system. Those 4K 13-in screens were really nice and helped you to not get bored. I also really appreciated the generous luggage allowance. I'm sure that this varies by airport, but it really made a difference for us. Some of the cons for this flight, I felt like the cabin ran a little bit warm. Normally, I'd be bundled in a blanket and wearing my sweater. I didn't touch either of those items the entire time. Maybe it's just me. Also, I'm not a huge fan of the the Japan Airlines website or app. I didn't find it was userfriendly. I couldn't find my boarding pass. Had to email my boarding pass to myself. No big deal. But just after being accustomed to flying American, I found it a little bit confusing. And then one thing that I thought was kind of weird, and maybe somebody out there, maybe you know the answer to this, but the entire bulkhead section of the economy class stayed empty through the whole entire flight. In fact, they had reserved seats on these uh reserved signs, I should say, on the seats, which I thought was really strange because I'm sure that there was a tall traveler on that flight who would have loved to have that front row, but it just remained empty. Maybe they're saving it for people with children. I'm wondering if anybody knows the answer to that. Definitely drop me a comment if you do. So, was Japan Airlines economy a letdown or a pleasant surprise? I got to say, it was definitely a pleasant surprise. The service felt elevated. The flight was comfortable and the food was way better than I expected. Now, there's three things I would recommend that you pack for this flight. I would take a long charging cable to make sure that you can get to that actual cable location. That' probably be smart. But definitely take some chapstick in case your lips tend to get dry in the air. I think that we all kind of got a little chapped on our flight and that's one thing you might want to take. And I would also recommend you bring some proteinbased snacks with you. Maybe some jerky, maybe some protein trail mix, whatever you can find. One thing you can absolutely leave at home, it would be a bulky layer. You don't really need your warm winter coat. If you're flying summer or spring, I would say on this aircraft, you might end up getting hot. Again, that might just be my personal opinion. So, what is the longest flight that you have ever been on and how did you pass the time? I want to thank everyone so much for joining me on this first flight review. I hope you enjoyed it. If you liked it, check out our Japan playlist for more travel and cruise content. Be sure to subscribe and give us a like. Those thumbs ups really, really matter.

I was in the row in front, which had three seats with my seat being an aisle seat. >> As this was an overnight flight, a blanket was provided on each seat as well as a small pillow. However, the wing headrests were far more useful for sleeping than the pillow. Like other airlines, this can be adjusted up or down and the wings folded. The seat does recline, but just beware of people behind you when doing so. Now, the seat itself did feel cramped, especially for a long haul flight. It had 31 in pitch, which is what some lowcost airlines have. The width of the seat isn't great either. It's 19 in. During meal service, I found the elbow room to be inadequate. You essentially have to eat with your arms tucked by your side. The seats had the usual reading lights. However, you'll notice that there were no air vents, which I found bizarre. Not sure why this is the case, but something so simple it was solely missed. The lack of features continue with the inflight entertainment. Firstly, there were no plug sockets that I could find. There was only a USBA connector. This meant that I couldn't charge any of my devices as all mine were USBC. You're given these earphones to use and can take them away with you, too. >> The inflight entertainment is similar to what is found on BA. In fact, it might even be made by the same company. The content isn't too bad and had a number of movies and series. It isn't Emirates level of variety, but is enough for most people. If you wish to mirror your phone content on screen, ensure you download the Lufansa companion app before takeoff. One of the more pleasant parts of the inflight entertainment to use was the maps app. Once loaded, it was relatively responsive and offered different view points to choose from. One thing that may not be obvious is that the reading light is controlled from an on-screen button. There are no physical buttons for this. One last frustrating thing about the inflight entertainment was there was no search and the menu was all in alphabetical order. Even if you set a different order, it would revert back to alphabetical order when you go back into the menu. This meant there was endless scrolling. Now we come to meals on board. As this was a late flight leaving at 11 p.m., most people had decided to skip meal service and go to sleep. To start, we were given a bottle of water and a cracker mix. Due to halal dietary requirements, I had ordered a special meal. The meal was actually rice and veg and vegetarian since there were no meat items in it. The salad wasn't great, but the rice and veg with riter sauce were actually good. The prior wasn't great being rock hard to eat. The dessert was semolina. I questioned whether I should have it or not as I didn't want stomach problem since it was a milk based product and I was unsure how long ago it would have been made. Meal number two was breakfast as we landed early in the morning. It was basically paratha and dal. They essentially gave me a vegetarian or Indian meal even though I requested a halal meal. I would have been happy with any kind of halal meat. I think Lufansa Catering need to look at what passes as a halal meal because this isn't quite good enough. The only other part of the cabin you'll visit is the toilet. This is what it looks like. It's a pretty standard setup like in most other economic cabins across many other airlines. I do wish airlines could make this slightly bigger as it would go a long way to making it a comfortable visit. The toilet doubles up as a baby changing room too and has some helpful hooks on the doors. Can't really speak much about the service as I didn't see any other than the meal services, but I guess since it was a night flight, constant service in the cabin isn't expected. The flight landed on time in Rio despite leaving 25 minutes late. So, this is what premium economy is. A lot more space. >> Goodbye. >> Bye-bye. >> Hello. >> Hello. Oh, bye-bye. >> And we're off. >> So, what did I think of my first longhaul Lufansa flight? Well, my main takeaway was that I definitely can't do 12 hours in that seat. So, we'll definitely try for an upgrade on the return leg. Lufansa as a national carrier would naturally be compared to BA or even Emirates. In my opinion though, it is on par with BA and the equipment even feels similar to BA. In fact, take a look at their inflight entertainment. They both look identical. Where Lufansa falls short is the lack of plug points and poor meal options. I get that this was a special ordered meal, but halal does not equal vegetarian. Even though a vegetarian meal can be halal, I would have preferred something that was meat-based or even fishbased, but that wasn't even an option when pre-booking a meal. This is where the likes of the Middle East Airlines shines with their food options. However, Luftza isn't all bad. The main reason I chose it was because it had the best times connecting from Birmingham airport and would get me into Rio without too much wasted time in layovers. It was also the cheapest option for the dates I was looking at, although the tickets were still a pricey £1,000. The question you might be asking is, would I or should I fly Lufansa again? Yes, as I said in my last video about their short hall economy, it does exactly what it says on the tin and gets me from A to B without any drama or fuss. reviews.transcript_full: Tonight I'm flying China Airlines A350 business class between Sydney and Taipei, a quick overnight run, and honestly one of the most comfortable ways to cross this route. My flight was scheduled for 10:10 p.m. Sydney time, and it pushed back right on time. Before boarding, I stopped by the SkyTeam Lounge at Sydney Airport, but for some reason it was absolutely packed that night. [music] So, I didn't stay long, and I basically skipped food and drinks there. On board, China Airlines A350 business cabin is a 1-2-1 layout, so everyone gets direct aisle access. The cabin feels spacious, and even with the middle overhead bins removed, there was still plenty of overhead luggage space, >> [music] >> which is always a nice surprise on a full flight. Service from the cabin crew was top-tier throughout, >> [music] >> and I really appreciated the cabin temperature, comfortable, not too warm, and not freezing, [music] which makes sleeping so much easier on an overnight flight. The travel kits were excellent, >> [music] >> a pair of slippers and a Moschino vanity kit with genuinely good quality skin care items, plus a really cute Moschino luggage [music] tag, which I actually want to keep. I also loved the little table lamp. It's a small detail, but it makes the whole space feel more premium and cozy. Because it's an overnight flight, >> [music] >> I mainly slept. I didn't spend much time with the entertainment system, but I did notice one thing missing. There are no external cameras, so you can't watch the outside view from different angles like on some other airlines. That said, they do offer free Wi-Fi, and the speed [music] was good enough for messaging, including photos and using most of my usual iPhone apps without issues. After departure, dinner was served with an entrée, soup, and main course. I chose the seafood, and it was honestly delicious, especially since I hadn't eaten much before boarding. The drinks list was impressive, too, and I had a glass of Laurent Perrier Brut Millésime 2015, a vintage champagne you don't see every day. It was absolutely divine. I got about nearly 6 hours of sleep, then woke up for a Chinese-style breakfast, which I really enjoyed. We arrived in Taipei at around 3:45 a.m., about half an hour early, great for punctuality, but not ideal if you're actually going into the city. At that hour, hotels aren't ready for check-in, and public transport is limited, so it can be inconvenient unless you're transferring to an early morning flight. On the way back, departure was 10 to 12 at midnight, [music] and I used the China Airlines Lounge at Taoyuan Airport T2. Compared to the SkyTeam Lounge [music] in Sydney, the food and drink here were much better. It felt like a proper preflight meal. Because it's such a late departure, I prefer to eat before boarding and go straight to sleep. I asked the crew to move my main meal to the morning and cancel the original breakfast, and that plan worked perfectly. After takeoff, I slept really well, nearly 7 hours, which is exactly what I want on a flight like this. Finally, I need to talk about the seat. The seat itself is very comfortable for sitting, and the overall personal space is great. My only real critique shows up in bed mode. When you go fully flat, the seat base stays firm and flat, but then your body can feel the inward curve on the backrest section, which creates a small gap behind your lower back. It's uncomfortable to lie on an uneven bed, but not a deal-breaker. I believe a thin mattress pad would probably fix it completely. Overall, China Airlines A350 business class between Sydney and Taipei is a really solid product. Great service, a comfortable cabin, strong food and drinks, and reliable Wi-Fi, just with that one small bed mode gap that I hope they'll address with a mattress pad in the future. Thanks for watching.
